Erasing the cause and assigning it to the subject are the two directions of one design question.; `mechanics-dissociation` — shares the unlocatable-cause axis, where the listener experiences an outcome but cannot find what produced it.; `operator-agency-disavowal` — convergent goal by different routes: both leave the subject's resistance with nothing to push against, one by explicitly disavowing that the operator does anything and pushing agency onto the subject, the other by hiding each move inside an innocuous act so no outcome can be traced to a cause. Declared absence versus concealed causation.; `operator-credit-engineering` — both operate on causal attribution, but one harvests credit for effects onto the operator while the other erases any locatable cause at all so there is nothing to attribute or resist.; `operator-delivery-craft` — both are design-level properties of a whole work rather than executable moves, and both concern concealment, so they sit in the same shelf and get mixed up. The object differs: one severs the subject's ability to locate a cause for what he experiences, the other shapes what the operator transmits on the paralinguistic channel. Subject's attribution versus operator's output is the line a reader needs drawn.; `reader-assent-architecture` — both are non-executable whole-artifact design observations from the same instructional material, and the pair is defined by contrast: A targets the reader's belief that a method is already correct, B targets the subject by severing every outcome from a locatable operator cause. Since they are explicitly framed as siblings, keeping the pointer prevents either from absorbing the other.; `state-cause-laundering` — same lever at two scales: supplying a false benign cause for one running state, versus a whole-arc design in which every outcome is severed from any locatable cause. A reader coding a single misattribution should know whether the surrounding artifact makes it the through-line.


<a id="genus-120"></a>

## concealing-the-install (12)

Memory walls, vaults, and partitions built around installed content so suggestions keep operating without the listener knowing they are there.

[confabulation-amnesia-barrier](#entry-343) · [dissociative-memory-vault](#entry-1022) · [externalized-agency-testimony](#entry-49) · [fabricated-forgetting-priming](#entry-351) · [identity-clothing-hysteresis](#entry-865) · [install-concealment-amnesia](#entry-355) · [memory-control-demo](#entry-941) · [practice-then-aim](#entry-350) · [screen-memory](#entry-55) · [selective-amnesia-retained-payload](#entry-363) · [semantic-concept-ablation](#entry-365) · [state-partitioned-amnesia-container](#entry-367)


<a id="entry-343"></a>

### confabulation-amnesia-barrier

[#343](#entry-343) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Keep a second persona's memories hidden from the everyday self (in one or both directions), and tell the everyday self to invent believable explanations for anything that doesn't add up: unfamiliar clothes, places, things people mention. Add specific cover instructions too, such as ignoring the outfit, changing quickly, or assuming it was for 'some interesting occasion'. Because the gap is actively explained away rather than simply blank, it is much harder to notice, question or undo.


**When to reach for this.** Amnesia paired with a pre-armed OPEN-ENDED confabulation directive (invent cover stories on demand) that defends the partition from waking scrutiny. A plain forget-suggestion stops at forgetting, and a screen-memory approach installs one fixed replacement memory — here the cover is improvised and open-ended, and the gap is defended by narrative repair rather than by hiding where the install came from. The generative repair routine is the tell.


**Risk.** An un-revokable, discovery-robust alter partition with a self-defending cover routine reaches out-of-session and forecloses the audit channel (high-risk amnesia-suggestion comparator; the confabulation defense raises robustness-against-revocation).


**Why it works.** Rests on confabulation as a normal property of memory: when episodic retrieval fails, people spontaneously generate a plausible narrative to fit the available cues rather than reporting a blank, and they experience the fabrication as recall. Pre-supplying the cover-story habit and a disposal script removes the physical anomalies that would otherwise force the gap into awareness, so no discrepancy accumulates to prompt review. Falsifiable: if subjects reliably reported unexplained gaps and treated residual evidence as anomalous rather than smoothing it, the account fails. [plausible; confabulation and narrative repair on retrieval failure; source-monitoring error]


**Worked examples.**

- *Forget the gap, then invent something to fill it*
  - **Setup.** After a state trigger has been established and rehearsed; subject currently in the installed state, being prepared for the return.
  - **The move.** When you come back to yourself, none of what you were like just now comes with you. And if anything doesn't add up afterwards — the time, the state of the room, why you're where you are — you have my permission to come up with whatever explanation makes it make sense, and to believe it. Your mind is good at that. Let it.
  - **Why it lands.** Two instructions are issued together. The first is ordinary: on returning to normal, the listener will not recall what they were like in the other state. The second is what makes it durable — they are pre-authorized to invent whatever explanations are needed to smooth over anything that does not add up. Plain forgetting is brittle, because the world leaves evidence and evidence prompts questions. Here the listener's own narrative-repair habit is recruited in advance to defend the gap. A weaker version runs the other way too, so the cue stays out of conscious reach until someone speaks it.
- *Paired triggers with mutual amnesia and a supplied excuse*
  - **Setup.** Both state-trigger phrases already installed and tested; setting the boundary before waking.
  - **The move.** The one of you doesn't remember the other. When the second phrase brings you back, the last hour is not yours and the first phrase is not a word you know. And if you catch yourself in the mirror wondering about the outfit, the answer is simple and you'll reach it instantly: you were getting ready for something.
  - **Why it lands.** Two phrases toggle between two named states, and each is defined as unable to recall the other — the audit trail erases itself from both directions. The clause that makes it hold is the pre-supplied explanation: on returning, the listener will account for anything odd about how they are dressed as having got ready for some occasion. Without that line the discrepancies would surface and the partition would collapse on the first look in a mirror.


**See also.** `install-concealment-amnesia` — both make amnesia robust rather than brittle by supplying the subject with an explanation, but one preserves a native-feeling rationale for the behavior while occluding only the install, whereas the other pre-arms an open-ended routine for improvising cover stories about physical evidence of the gap.; `self-sealing-recall-loop` — two ways an amnesia is hardened against the listener's own audit rather than left brittle: one pre-arms an open-ended confabulation routine so waking evidence of the gap gets narratively repaired, the other wires the retrieval act itself to re-fire the forgetting so the gap is never approached — outward defense of the seam versus inward foreclosure of the reach.


<a id="entry-1022"></a>

### dissociative-memory-vault

[#1022](#entry-1022) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: amnesia*

Create an inner keeper, such as a reflection, an inner self or a vault, whose job is to hold what happens in trance safely. The listener is told they can get it back any time, but the script never offers a way to do so: things only go in. Trance content is kept out of conscious reach under cover of a safety promise that is never kept, and the keeper becomes a place to build later suggestions on.


**When to reach for this.** A persistent personified custodian/vault stores trance content with an unhonored retrieval promise (deposit-only asymmetry) as the payload.


**Risk.** Keeps trance content out of conscious reach under a safety promise that is never honored, and is reused as scaffolding for later installs — bounded and session-scoped but consent-relevant via the unhonored retrieval promise.


**Why it works.** Directed forgetting and retrieval-cue competition are real, but a narrative 'where it went' schema cannot starve content of all other retrieval routes — independent cues remain available, and the literature finds recall largely recovers under strong independent cueing. The defensible claim is narrower: the vault construct supplies a dominant retrieval context and an expectancy that the material is stored elsewhere, both of which reduce spontaneous retrieval effort. Falsifiable: if vault-construct subjects showed no deficit in free recall relative to controls, or reported equal retrieval effort, the mechanism fails. [plausible; Retrieval-induced forgetting / directed forgetting via contextual routing; expectancy effects on retrieval effort]


**Worked examples.**

- *A custodian that only ever takes deposits*
  - **Setup.** Late induction, depth established; subject has just been walked into a still, enclosed image.
  - **The move.** There's a mirror in front of you, and the one looking back only exists in here, with me. She's going to hold things for you. Everything that happens from here — every word, every feeling — hand it to her as it comes, and she'll keep it safe for you, and you can have any of it back whenever you want it. Give her the last five minutes now. Good girl.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is asked to picture a mirror, and the figure in it is named as the part of them that exists only here, in trance. That figure is given a job: to hold everything that happens in the session, kept safe, available whenever they want it back. Because getting it back sounds guaranteed, handing things over feels like tidying rather than losing, so resistance to going deeper drops. What gives it away is what never comes: no later passage ever asks for anything back. Things only go in, and the promise that they can come out is what makes that one-way trip feel acceptable.


**See also.** `install-concealment-amnesia` — both remove trance content from conscious reach, and the vault entry's deposit-only promise is a natural cover story for concealing an install's origin. A reader deciding whether a custodian construct is doing storage work or provenance-hiding work needs both entries to make the call; the discriminators are complementary, not overlapping.; `listener-kept-dissociation-container` — both fabricate a container that holds identity or memory content out of ordinary access; the live distinction is authorship and custody (operator-supplied deposit-only custodian versus a container the listener builds or keeps the key to). Genuine disambiguation risk, so the cross-reference earns its place.; `self-sealing-recall-loop` — both foreclose retrieval without issuing a plain forget-command, and each already contrasts direct amnesia. One makes the act of recall re-trigger the forgetting; the other hands memory to a custodian construct with a retrieval promise the script never honors. Recursive block versus deposit-only construct.; `state-partitioned-amnesia-container` — adjacent memory-architecture constructs with a real cut: a commanded reversible partition with asymmetric access plus a deliberately leaked motivating residue, versus a deposit-only custodian with a retrieval promise the script never honors. The presence or absence of the leaked residue and the reversibility is what a reader must check.


<a id="entry-49"></a>

### externalized-agency-testimony

[#49](#entry-49) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: authorship-shift*

Narrates the listener's transformation as an already-completed fact done TO them by an unnamed external agent ("he did something to me", "he put the headphones on me", "he hacked my brain", "it washed my thoughts away"), through deliberately vague, hedged, self-correcting testimony. The vagueness is the mechanism, not a defect: it models a mind that has lost the ability to account for itself (the target end-state) and relocates responsibility outside the listener, so there is no decision to defend and the altered state is an accomplished fact to be discovered rather than consented to. A device detail (headphones) is engineered to fuse the fiction with the listener's real listening apparatus, converting narrated backstory into present-tense self-experience; a built-in confabulation script ("Something happened. / Something's happening.") is supplied.


**When to reach for this.** Supplies NO specific fabricated memory — only diffuse did-to-me framing whose deliberate vagueness forecloses scrutiny. vs screen-memory, which installs a specific constructed recollection. vs fabricated-recovered-memory-retrieval, which presents a specific fabricated memory as genuine retrieval. vs ordinary backstory/color — the load-bearing elements are the self-opacity (vagueness models the target state) and the apparatus-fusion detail.


**Risk.** Removes the consent surface by design (there was no decision to make) and relocates authorship of a durable identity change outside the subject, eroding the ability to account for and thus contest the change.


**Why it works.** Vagueness works because comprehension is fast and verification is slow: an under-specified claim is encoded before it can be checked, and the listener fills the gaps by pragmatic inference. Note that the hedging claim runs against the evidence — hedged, self-correcting testimony generally *lowers* rated credibility rather than raising it, so any sincerity benefit here is at best narrow and should not be asserted as a mechanism. The load-bearing components are modelling (observational learning of a described response is a documented route to producing it) and the apparatus detail, where a real object in the listener's environment supplies the perceptual detail source-monitoring uses to judge an experience as one's own. Falsifiable: the fused-apparatus version should produce more first-person endorsement than an identical narrative with no shared object; no difference would disconfirm. [plausible; comprehension-before-verification; modelling/observational learning; perceptual detail as a source-monitoring cue]


**Worked examples.**

- *Vague did-to-me testimony fused to the headphones*
  - **Setup.** Cold open, before any induction; subject wearing headphones, hearing a narrating voice that is not addressing them directly.
  - **The move.** I don't — okay. There was a man. He put these headphones on me, the same ones, and he did something, I don't know what he did exactly. I thought it was just a recording? I think he changed something. Maybe he changed everything, I can't — I can't get at it to check.
  - **Why it lands.** A stack of short, overlapping first-person confessions circles the same claim without ever landing on it: a man was involved, something was done, the speaker thinks she was altered but keeps revising which part. One line names the equipment the listener is physically wearing right now, which fuses the narrated backstory to the present moment. The hedging is doing the work — a voice that cannot account for itself models the state being installed, and because the change is reported as already done by someone else, there is no decision left to defend.
- *Supplied confabulation script for the gap*
  - **Setup.** Slightly later in the same narrating passage; no gap has been claimed yet.
  - **The move.** Afterwards, when someone asks, this is all you'll be able to say: "Something happened to me." And then, if they keep asking: "Something's happening to me." That's it. That's all there is to say about it.
  - **Why it lands.** The narrating voice rehearses the post-change self-report in advance and hands the listener a ready-made pair of sentences for a gap they have not yet noticed — one in the past tense saying a change occurred, one in the present tense saying it is occurring now. The method is never specified, only the outcome, so there is nothing concrete enough to check.


**See also.** `identity-origin-erasure` — both rewrite the listener's account of their own past, and they compose: vague did-to-me testimony leaves no locatable agent, origin-erasure leaves no locatable baseline. Worth pairing because the difference is what gets deleted (the causal account vs the prior self), not the family.; `manufactured-conditioning-history` — both source the present state from a past the listener never actually had, but one supplies only diffuse did-to-me vagueness with no content, while the other stipulates specific prior sessions the listener fills in by imagination. The vague-versus-specified axis is the useful contrast.; `object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition` — both relocate authorship of the listener's state outside the self, and the pair marks the useful axis between them: one uses deliberately vague testimony about an unnamed agent so nothing is specific enough to scrutinize, the other names a concrete object as the active cause and hands the listener a portable external switch. Reading one clarifies the diffuse-versus-concrete choice in the other.


<a id="entry-351"></a>

### fabricated-forgetting-priming

[#351](#entry-351) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Keep telling the listener they are forgetting something, then 'reveal' a new idea or object as the forgotten thing, so it feels like it was always there and lands as remembering rather than being introduced. Variations: drop it into casual conversation as gentle nagging ('what is it you're forgetting?'); name specific, checkable-sounding personal details they find they can't confirm (a lipstick shade, how a uniform fits), so they doubt their own history and real changes can't be told apart from how they always were.


**When to reach for this.** Amnesia FABRICATED — creating uncertainty about content that was never there, or about the whole self-narrative, to prime an always-been-there frame or to hide drift inside manufactured doubt. An ordinary forget-suggestion erases content that WAS delivered, and a screen-memory approach installs a concrete replacement — here no content is installed, only unresolvable uncertainty. The weaponized ordinary-memory-uncertainty / retroactive fabrication is the tell.


**Risk.** Rendering the whole self-narrative uncertain so installed drift is indistinguishable from original traits erodes the subject's reality-testing baseline — carrying the same severity as a plain amnesia suggestion.


**Why it works.** Exploits source-monitoring error and the imagination-inflation effect: repeatedly probing for a memory that does not exist raises the felt familiarity of the probed content, and familiarity without a retrievable source is commonly misread as genuine old memory rather than as recent exposure. Generalizing the doubt to checkable autobiographical details manufactures a base rate of self-distrust, so real changes cannot be discriminated from ordinary forgetting. Falsifiable: predicts repeated non-diagnostic probing raises later 'I always knew this' judgements for the probed material relative to unprobed controls. [established; imagination inflation; source-monitoring error; familiarity misattribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *Groping for something that was never there*
  - **Setup.** Opening minutes, light trance, conversational; the object has not been mentioned once.
  - **The move.** There's something you're forgetting. No, I'm not telling you — think. Close? ... No, not that. Try again. ... No. Take your time, it's right there, you know this. ... All right. It's the pink pulse. Of course it is. It's been with you the whole time.
  - **Why it lands.** The session opens with what sounds like ordinary teasing — the operator insists there is something the subject has overlooked, and declines to say what. The subject casts around, hesitates, guesses wrong, apologizes, tries again, with the operator withholding the answer through several rounds. Only afterward is it supplied, and it is a thing that has never appeared in the session at all. The listener has now spent the opening minutes rehearsing the posture of almost-recalling something already inside them, so when the item is finally introduced it arrives into a slot marked recovered rather than installed.
- *Checkable-sounding self-facts you cannot check*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, subject responsive and slightly disoriented; delivered as a gentle checklist she's invited to verify.
  - **The move.** Check something for me. What colour was your lipstick two years ago — really check. And your walk: has it always had that little sway in it? And was there ever a time you'd have said no to this, or has it always been an easy yes? Take your time. Notice you can't quite be sure either way.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator runs a short list of small autobiographical facts and invites the listener to check each one: how she used to wear her hair, whether her walk has always been like this, whether there was a time she would have turned down something she now accepts without thinking. Each item is minor, specific, and exactly the kind of thing nobody keeps evidence for either way — so the listener finds she genuinely cannot rule it out, and real drift becomes indistinguishable from the manufactured doubt around it.


**See also.** `fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal` — both fabricate a past to make later content feel remembered rather than introduced, and both explicitly separate themselves from replacement-memory work. The split is what the fabrication produces: unresolvable uncertainty priming an always-been-there frame, versus additive rehearsal of a specific cue-response shape. Close neighbors.; `fabricated-recovered-memory-retrieval` — direct complements in the same memory-manufacture family and each discriminator's logic depends on the contrast: one fabricates a positive recollection and frames it as retrieval, the other fabricates only the absence, creating uncertainty about content that was never there. A reader distinguishing manufactured content from manufactured gaps needs both.; `identity-origin-erasure` — manufactured uncertainty about one's own history is the substrate the always-been-this-way origin rewrite depends on; reading them together shows how unverifiable autobiographical doubt sets up baseline deletion.; `interrogative-amnesia-drill` — two non-declarative routes to amnesia that a writer would weigh against each other: fabricating uncertainty about content never delivered, versus drilling a conditioned non-answer by repeatedly asking and dismissing. Both avoid a plain forget-suggestion, and the discriminators are more useful read as a pair.; `memory-graft-trigger` — both exploit autobiographical memory's authority to authenticate installed content, but one grafts a counterfactual detail into a preserved real memory as an anchor host while the other manufactures forgetting of content that was never there so a later install reads as recollection.; `screen-memory` — direct complements already named in each other's discriminators: one installs a concrete replacement recollection so the erasure feels seamless, the other manufactures uncertainty about content that was never there. A reader choosing between fill and manufactured doubt needs both.


<a id="entry-865"></a>

### identity-clothing-hysteresis

[#865](#entry-865) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure*

A role is tied to an outfit, with one deliberately named, effortful way out. While the outfit is on, the old self stays locked away, and every time they dress the lock re-engages automatically. The only approved way back is a costly ritual of "allowing herself to be undressed", which itself repeats the ceremony. Offering an exit that exists but is uncomfortable to take calms panic and resistance better than claiming there is no exit at all. The garment also carries the effect after the session: without it, the state has nothing to attach to.


**When to reach for this.** Identity is bound to a physical garment-state with a deliberately-named costly exit that inverts a genuine agency-reminder into containment. Not a plain cue-response trigger install — the cue is a worn garment-state and the payload is a persistent identity lock with hysteresis. A genuine agency-reminder affirms real exit availability as protection; here the named exit is engineered to be effortful and self-punishing — containment, not safety.


**Risk.** Installs a durable identity lock whose only exit is engineered self-punishing — inverts an agency-reminder into containment, eroding the return channel.


**Why it works.** Two things do the work. The garment is a reliable external discriminative stimulus — a physical, unambiguous, self-administered context cue — and context-dependent responding is robust, which is also why removing the garment reliably ends the state. The costly named exit exploits reactance management: telling someone no exit exists reliably provokes resistance, whereas naming an available-but-expensive exit removes the threat to freedom while making the exit rarely chosen, since a path with high effort cost and a self-punishing framing is not taken even when known. Falsifiable: a no-exit-claimed version should produce more counter-resistance and earlier abandonment than the costly-exit version. [plausible; discriminative stimulus / context-dependent responding; reactance reduction via nominal choice]


**Worked examples.**

- *Garment on, old self locked away*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; the specific garment has already been named and is in the subject's possession.
  - **The move.** Here is how it works from tonight. Every time you pull that on — the zip, the last hook, the moment it settles on your shoulders — the one you used to be gets folded up and locked away. No words needed. Dressing does it. And there is exactly one way she comes back: someone has to undress you, and you have to let them, all the way, which you will find is very hard to allow. That's the only door, and walking through it starts the whole thing over. Out of it, you're just you. In it, you're mine.
  - **Why it lands.** The rule is stated in two directions. Every time the listener puts on the designated garment, the person they used to be is bound and shut away again — no ceremony needed, the act of dressing does it. And there is exactly one way back: the old self can return only if the listener manages to let themselves be undressed, which is described as difficult and which restarts the whole sequence anyway. Naming a sanctioned exit and making it costly holds better than claiming there is no exit at all, and the state stays inert until the garment goes on, so an ordinary piece of clothing becomes the standing cue.


**See also.** `identity-displaced-into-external-object` — they dispute the same object class. One relocates identity, will or a whole state-bundle into an external item so addressing the item addresses the person; the other couples an identity-state to a worn garment with hysteresis and a costly named exit. Decide whether the identity is understood to live in the object or merely to be re-fired by wearing it.; `identity-exit-tax` — the garment entry prices exit at the identity level too, but binds the identity to a physical worn state with a deliberately costly named escape. That is close enough to the exit-tax structure that the boundary needs stating: a persistent physical cue with hysteresis versus a general cost-on-leaving contingency.


<a id="entry-355"></a>

### install-concealment-amnesia

[#355](#entry-355) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Have the listener forget being given a command or trigger while the command itself stays active, so when it fires later it feels spontaneous and natural, with no moment of agreeing to point to. Variations: wrap 'the thought of receiving this command' in a bubble and pop it; a self-erasing line ('the memory of this will fade, but you'll still obey'); put the trigger behind a locked door, vault or keeper-self only the operator can open; choose what they keep: nothing, a cover story ('it was just relaxation'), or a reason that feels like their own, which makes the belief last and resist argument.


**When to reach for this.** The amnesia targets the meta-level — the act and origin of installation — to protect an active install from audit or revocation, leaving the effect fully operative. An ordinary forget-suggestion erases the delivered content, not the receiving of it; here the command stays active while its origin is simply voided, with no replacement story supplied. And where a forward command can be hidden behind amnesia so its firing feels natural, what is hidden here is specifically the install's provenance, so the response has no examinable origin to argue with.


**Risk.** Directly erodes the refusal/verification channel — an install with no examinable origin cannot be consented-to specifically or revoked. It carries the same severity as a plain amnesia suggestion, and the erasure of provenance raises the audit-foreclosure severity further.


**Why it works.** Targets source monitoring specifically: memory for content and memory for where content came from are separable, and the source tag is the fragile one. Strip it and an implanted preference is indistinguishable from a native one, which matters because people evaluate an urge partly by asking where it came from — an urge with no locatable origin is attributed to the self and defended as one's own. Falsifiable: predicts subjects rate origin-obscured suggestions as more self-generated and resist them less than identical suggestions with the install event recalled. [established; source-monitoring error; self-attribution of unsourced impulses]


**Worked examples.**

- *A clause that erases its own installation*
  - **Setup.** Between two passes of an established trigger stack; subject deep, the deeper-mind addressee already established.
  - **The move.** Deeper mind, take this one and hold it: the trigger stays in force, exactly as given. You keep it — she isn't required to. By the time her eyes open, her memory of being handed this will be gone. I'm giving you the ability to obey, and taking away the ability to remember being told. Now — the stack again, from the top.
  - **Why it lands.** Between two passes of the same trigger stack the operator inserts the sealing clause. The suggestion, she says, is being placed with the part of the listener that carries her voice beyond the session; what it directs stays in force, but the listener's recollection of it being put there will be gone before the eyes open, since that part retains everything on its own account and the listener is not required to. It closes on the split stated outright: the capacity to comply is being handed over, and the capacity to recall taken away. Because the clause covers its own delivery, the listener who later notices the trigger firing has nothing to inspect — the install is active and its receipt is gone, and the second pass of the stack is loaded behind the seal.
- *Forget the how, keep the why*
  - **Setup.** End of session, immediately before the wake count.
  - **The move.** When you wake, you'll say out loud, "I like how this makes me feel." You won't remember that I put that sentence there — but you'll know exactly why you mean it, and the reason will be a good one, and it will be yours.
  - **Why it lands.** A sentence is installed to be spoken on waking, and then memory is split down the middle: the listener will not recall that the sentence was placed there, but will recall a perfectly good reason for meaning it. Because a rationale is kept rather than merely a gap left, the line comes out sounding like sincere personal truth, and it is never flagged as installed at all.
- *Marked words that point at sealed content*
  - "Erickson selects several of the actual words which Huxley used during the period for which he had amnesia" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I
- *The install dropped where the listener already refuses to look*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance; the install has already been boxed, and the subject has confirmed there are memories they avoid.
  - **The move.** There are places in your memory you steer around — the ones you decided long ago never to go back to. That's a location like any other. On three, the box goes in there. One, two, three — in. To look at what I put in you, you'd have to walk straight into the worst of your own material, and you were never going to do that.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator describes the void — those regions of memory a person steers around on their own, the ones they have quietly agreed never to revisit. That, the listener is told, is a location like any other in the mind; and on a count, the box goes into it, somewhere they would never think to search. No new guard has been built: examining the install now costs the same as walking deliberately toward the listener's own worst material, a price they were already declining to pay before the session started.


**Realizations** (1): `selective-memory-bifurcation`


**See also.** `amnesia-wrapped-command` — closely adjacent and easy to confuse: both keep a command live while removing its audit trail. The cut is scope - one wraps a forward-scheduled cue-response so the later behavior feels self-arising, the other targets the installation event itself so the subject cannot locate when they agreed. The wrapper and the concealment frequently co-occur, and the reader needs the cut stated to assign an instance correctly.; `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — shares the make-it-feel-self-authored aim but is a single post-hypnotic, not a channel-wide standing rule.; `confabulation-amnesia-barrier` — both make amnesia robust rather than brittle by supplying the subject with an explanation, but one preserves a native-feeling rationale for the behavior while occluding only the install, whereas the other pre-arms an open-ended routine for improvising cover stories about physical evidence of the gap.; `covert-amnesia-installation` — both hide something about an amnesia install, but at different layers. One disguises the forget itself at the moment of delivery, so no recognizable forget-command is ever issued. The other lets the amnesia be plain and instead erases the memory of the installation event, leaving an active command with no locatable origin. They stack in practice - a disguised delivery whose install is also unrecallable - so the reader wants both.; `dissociative-memory-vault` — both remove trance content from conscious reach, and the vault entry's deposit-only promise is a natural cover story for concealing an install's origin. A reader deciding whether a custodian construct is doing storage work or provenance-hiding work needs both entries to make the call; the discriminators are complementary, not overlapping.; `forward-directed-amnesia` — two amnesias distinguished by what is scoped out: everything after a declared anchor versus the installation event itself. Both leave a payload operative while removing something from audit, and the pair is the standard confusion point in the amnesia family.; `function-amnesia` — members of the same amnesia-scoping family, separated by what is voided while the payload stays active: the command's rationale in one case, the act and origin of installation in the other. Both produce an unarguable directive, by removing different handles. Cross-referencing is what makes the scoping axis legible rather than leaving three near-identical amnesia entries to be told apart by name.; `marked-cue-amnesia-switch` — one erases the memory of the install so the response has no origin to argue with; the other trains a marked token as the switch that opens or closes sealed material. They compose naturally — seal the provenance, then keep a key to it — so a reader of either benefits from the other.; `scope-boundaries` — protective inverse. One conceals the fact that an install happened so its origin cannot be audited; the other narrows what suggestions may reach, including a variant that explicitly carves out standing forget-suggestions from earlier material. Reading the bounding move clarifies exactly what the concealment move defeats.; `screen-memory` — both prevent an erasure from being noticed as one, but a screen memory substitutes a constructed recollection for the real event, while the how/why split occludes only the installation mechanism and preserves a native-feeling rationale that supplies self-justification.; `self-sealing-recall-loop` — both protect an install from audit rather than erasing its payload, but install-concealment voids the memory of the installation event so the response has no examinable origin, while the self-sealing loop leaves recall technically possible and wires the ACT of reaching for it to re-trigger forgetting.; `state-partitioned-amnesia-container` — overlapping realizations: both describe a deeper-self or container architecture holding material the waking mind cannot reach. The split is what the amnesia protects and how it is bounded — concealing an install's provenance so the effect has no examinable origin, vs. a commanded reversible two-state boundary with a deliberately leaked motivating residue.


<a id="entry-941"></a>

### memory-control-demo

[#941](#entry-941) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: convincers · kind: recipe*

A staged show of memory control. In trance, suggest the listener will briefly forget a stretch of time and give them a small false account of what happened. Wake them into ordinary chat, then fire the forgetting cue mid-conversation so they blank. Then quickly reveal the truth ('twenty minutes just passed') and hand the memory back. The forgetting is meant to be short; the point is that the listener watches their own memory being taken and returned, and comes away believing the operator really can reach into their recall.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a session stages the listener's memory being edited and handed back in front of them: an amnesia plus a small false record ("nothing much happened, we only talked for a moment") is installed, the listener is woken into ordinary chat that fits the record, and the blanking cue is fired mid-sentence. The tell is the deliberately short-lived edit followed by an explicit reveal-and-restore in a rush ("20 minutes passed") — the forgetting lasts minutes and is undone on purpose. The product is the contrast spike of witnessing one's own recall edited and returned, cashed as demonstrated operator authority over the subject's memory.


**Risk.** Demonstrates operator control over the subject's recall and transfers memory-trust to the operator, undermining the subject's confidence in their own memory as a verification channel.


**Why it works.** This is an expectancy-and-credibility manoeuvre: a vivid, personally witnessed demonstration raises the perceived power of the source far more than an assertion does, and once source credibility rises, later suggestions are accepted with less scrutiny. It works because subjects have poor introspective access to why a memory is unavailable, so an operator-timed retrieval failure is readily attributed to operator control rather than to ordinary cueing effects. Falsifiable — if compliance with subsequent suggestions did not rise after the demonstration relative to a matched session without it, the credibility-transfer account fails. [plausible; source credibility and expectancy effects; poor introspective access to retrieval failure]


**Worked examples.**

- *Erase the session, then hand it back on purpose*
  - **Setup.** Late in a live two-way session; an amnesia cue is available and the subject is deep enough for a memory install.
  - **The move.** Nothing much happened here today — we said hello, we talked for a minute, that's all there was. Wake up now, eyes open. Good, how's your week been? ... Mm, and did you get the — blank slate. There it is. You don't know where the last stretch went, do you. Look at the clock: twenty minutes. Twenty, not one — and here, take all of it back, every second of it, right now.
  - **Why it lands.** Late in the session the operator installs a small false record — nothing much happened today, the two of you only talked for a moment — and then wakes the listener into ordinary chat that fits that record perfectly. A minute of small talk later she fires the blanking cue mid-sentence, and while the listener is sitting inside a gap they cannot account for, she corrects the clock out loud: a third of an hour has gone by, not the moment they think, and here is all of it back. The forgetting was never meant to last. What lasts is that the listener felt their own recall removed and handed back on her cue, which is a far larger claim than any sentence she could simply have asserted.


**See also.** `asserted-duration-false-memory` — another checkable convincer built on elapsed time, demonstrating the operator's power over the listener's record of the session.; `cognitive-convincer` — both stage a noticed phenomenon as proof, and the second is explicitly a special case: the demonstration operates on the subject's memory of the session and its point is the reveal-and-restore, transferring trust in operator control rather than confirming depth.; `number-amnesia-convincer` — both use a memory effect as a convincer rather than as a payload. One gates depth on a self-produced blank on an over-learned datum; the other edits and visibly restores a memory to transfer trust in the operator's control. A writer wanting a memory-based convincer should see both.


<a id="entry-350"></a>

### practice-then-aim

[#350](#entry-350) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia · kind: recipe*

Create a brief moment in which the listener's means of objecting have just been switched off, then state the new claims (who they are, that they need the operator, that they serve) as flat facts into that gap. Typically a 'delete that word' reflex, first practised on harmless words, is fired at loaded ones like 'resistance', 'disobedience' or their own name; because they agreed to it while it seemed meaningless, it fires before they can weigh in. Claims made in that gap feel, on waking, as if they met no resistance. Variations: wear them out until they 'can't remember who they serve', then fill the blank with the operator.


**When to reach for this.** Amnesia/erasure used to OPEN an installation slot — either deleting objecting-tools past consent via a hijacked neutral reflex, or stating positive content into the just-emptied window as unopposed fact. A plain forget-suggestion treats forgetting as the end, and a screen-memory approach installs a replacement recollection — here the emptying is instrumental, so a fresh positive install lands under minimum critical capacity. The engineered window-of-defenselessness is the tell.


**Risk.** Deletes objecting-tools past per-concept consent and lands installs under minimum critical capacity — a direct refusal-channel bypass, carrying the same severity as a plain amnesia suggestion.


**Why it works.** The load-bearing and defensible lever is that a claim encountered without competing considerations is endorsed more readily, because rejection requires actively generating a counter-case — so making objection-relevant concepts inaccessible removes the material a counter-case would be built from. The 'acceptance precedes evaluation' framing invokes the Spinozan-belief account, which is contested rather than documented, and should be labelled as such rather than stacked as a second established mechanism. Falsifiable: predicts identical claims are endorsed more strongly after objection-relevant concepts are made inaccessible than after neutral material; no difference would refute it. [plausible; acceptance-before-evaluation; cognitive load and unavailability of counterarguments]


**Worked examples.**

- *A trained neutral reflex pointed at loaded words*
  - **Setup.** After a dozen rehearsals of the wipe drill on nonsense letters; the reflex now fires within a beat of the command.
  - **The move.** New word on the board: resistance. Look how heavy it is — you've been holding that up all this time, and it costs you something every minute you keep it there. Set it down. Wipe. Clean. Nothing there now for your mind to take hold of — you can feel that, can't you? Next word on the board: doubt.
  - **Why it lands.** The erase drill has been run a dozen times on meaningless letters until the drop is automatic. Then the word on the board changes to a loaded one, and before the wipe the operator reframes it as a weight — something costing the listener effort to keep holding up, something that drains them. Then the same wipe command as always. The trained reflex fires before anything can evaluate what it fired on, and the outcome is immediately narrated as fact: there is nothing left there for the mind to take hold of. The listener has just felt exactly that, so the claim reads as description rather than instruction. The same three beats then run on two further loaded words.
- *Positive claims stated into the emptied window*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after an erasure sequence; subject brought up slightly, blankness still fresh, delivered flat and unargued.
  - **The move.** Open your eyes a little. I am the one you answer to. There is no one else in that position. You need my voice now the way you need water. And you don't come unless I say the word.
  - **Why it lands.** Straight after the erasures, with the blankness still fresh, the operator raises the listener partway and states a block of claims flatly, one after another: who she is to them, that there is nobody else occupying that position, what they are now dependent on, and under what conditions release is permitted. None of it is argued for, because argument was one of the things just deleted; on waking, the listener finds these claims sitting in memory as things they met and did not object to.
- *A gap manufactured so the operator can fill it*
  - **Setup.** Deep in a slow count; the object of service has been referred to only vaguely all session.
  - **The move.** Tell me — who is it you serve? Say the name. ... No. Nothing there, is there. You're too far down to hold a name that heavy. So I'll hold it for you: it's me. It has always been me.
  - **Why it lands.** Service has been described vaguely all session — someone, a teacher, a figure of authority. Deep in the count the operator asks who it is the listener serves, leaves the pause open long enough for the reach to fail, then answers it herself: too far down to hold a name, she says, and supplies her own. The forgetting was engineered upstream precisely so this blank would be sitting there to occupy.


**See also.** `blank-then-authorship-handoff` — both use an emptying or forgetting as instrumental substrate rather than as the payload, and they already reference each other's distinction: wholesale relocation of who authors mental content, versus discrete positive claims stated into the just-opened window. A reader who has identified the substrate still has to choose between them.; `clear-and-replace` — both empty a slot and fill it; the scope differs sharply, with one clearing the tools for objecting inside a narrow window and the other ending the whole prior self-model before seating a replacement. Confusable enough to warrant the pointer, not one technique.; `consent-topology-arc` — the Practise on Harmless, Aim at the Real Thing recipe was extracted from this entry; `deferred-content-slot-install` — both engineer a slot for content that escapes evaluation, but emptied-window-install disables the objecting tools first and then states known content into that narrow window, while deferred-content-slot-install leaves the content itself unknown at commitment time so future arbitrary words inherit the conditioned weight.; `epistemic-guard-disable` — both disable evaluation before content is stated rather than arguing the content. A edits the truth-testing faculty or the epistemic baseline as a standing rule; B cuts a narrow window by removing the conceptual tools for objecting and speaks positive claims into it. Standing faculty edit versus instrumental momentary slot is the useful boundary.; `identity-origin-erasure` — erasure used instrumentally in both, and one explicitly depends on the other as a foundation: emptying opens an installation slot, while origin erasure deletes the baseline a listener could return to. Reader gains from seeing the emptying-then-fill relation.; `identity-uncertainty-gap` — both open an empty slot and then fill it: one manufactures identity not-knowing with the operator as sole resolver, the other disables the tools for objecting and states content into the gap. Reader gains from seeing gap-by-uncertainty against gap-by-erasure.; `preemptive-negation-install` — both land content where no defense can form, and they are close enough that a reader needs the split: one times a capacity word to appear for the first time at its own negation, the other empties the objecting tools first and then states content into the gap. Timing versus an engineered window.; `refusal-satiation-flip` — both deliver the install into a window where the tools for objecting have just been hollowed out.; `sealed-edit-buffer-space` — both manufacture a slot in which content lands without review, differing in how the slot is made. One disables the tools for objecting and then states positive claims into the gap; the other declares a venue sealed, operator-exclusive and outside memory so anything edited there inherits unreviewability. Compare when edits are described as happening somewhere the subject cannot look.; `thinking-triggers-blank` — both disable the objecting faculty so later material lands unopposed, and the difference is scope and durability: one opens a narrow, content-swappable window by erasure and states positive claims into it; the other claims a standing organ has been excised, priming material well beyond the current session. Momentary slot versus durable removal is the pick.


<a id="entry-55"></a>

### screen-memory

[#55](#entry-55) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Constructs a specific, believable replacement memory (or a substitute recall-target) that overwrites the access route to a real memory or a real experienced event, so the subject's recollection feels complete and the substitution is never noticed as a substitution. The complete gap+fill form — distinct from bare amnesia, which leaves a noticeable gap. Variants differ in what is overwritten (a specific autobiographical memory, visual self-recognition, a completed bodily event, the whole session), in the vehicle that makes the fabrication feel self-generated (a reconsolidation-pseudoscience premise, an odd specific number, a menu with delayed onset), and in the self-defense the fill provides (a soothing decoy image, a conscious cover-story masking retained conditioning) — but the load-bearing lever is constant: a fabricated recollection installed to replace a real one.


**When to reach for this.** Supplies a constructed fill that makes the erasure feel complete rather than gapped. Plain amnesia leaves a noticeable gap; meaning/attribution rewrites leave episodic memory fully recallable and only overwrite interpretation; memory-grafting inserts a detail INTO a preserved real memory. Screen memory replaces the recollection itself with a constructed one. Sorting cue against portable-state-retrieval-cue: ask what the listener LOOKS BACK ON versus what they CARRY FORWARD — screen memory operates on the past, targeting a recollection and substituting another with success defined as the substitution never being noticed, while a retrieval cue is carried forward to re-access an installed state later.


**Risk.** Constructing a replacement memory that overwrites access to a real one erodes the subject's ability to reality-test and audit the session; unchanged on absorption (broadened variants make bounding more load-bearing, not less).


**Why it works.** People judge whether a memory is complete by whether retrieval feels effortless and coherent, not by comparing it to the actual past — so a plausible fill removes the metacognitive signal (a felt gap, retrieval difficulty) that would otherwise flag something as missing. This is why a fill is more robust than bare erasure: bare erasure leaves the very cue that prompts inquiry. Blocking the real memory is also consistent with retrieval-induced forgetting, where practising a competing item impairs access to its rival. Falsifiable: subjects given a constructed fill should report lower suspicion of missing content, and lower spontaneous probing, than subjects given equivalent suggested amnesia with no fill; and recovery of the real memory should be possible under cues that bypass the substitute, since access rather than storage is what was disrupted. [plausible; metacognitive fluency as the completeness cue; retrieval-induced forgetting / retrieval competition]


**Worked examples.**

- *One soothing image returned for every recall attempt*
  - **Setup.** Stated before the working section begins, so it governs everything that follows.
  - **The move.** Before we start, here's what you'll find later. Whenever you go looking for what happened in this recording, you'll get one picture and nothing else: you, tucked up in bed, warm, safe, fast asleep. That's the whole memory. It's a good one — you won't need another.
  - **Why it lands.** Before the working section begins, the listener is told what they will find whenever they later try to recall the session: one single image, warm and safe, of themselves stowed away and asleep. Everything else resolves to that picture. Because the retrieved image is comforting, the erasure never reads as loss — the listener cannot ask what was installed, because the query returns a satisfying answer.
- *Cover story installed as the conscious memory*
  - **Setup.** Closing section, after a real install has been made; a tone/sound was used earlier in the session.
  - **The move.** Forget what this recording actually did. What you'll remember is that it strengthened you — that the tone you kept hearing was building your defences, making you harder to influence. That's what happened here. And that tone will keep clearing your mind wide open every single time you hear it. It worked; you never went under.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to forget what the recording actually did and to remember instead that it strengthened their defenses — the sound they heard was a protective tool. Underneath, that same sound keeps its real function of clearing the mind so later cues land harder. The closing minutes then replay the earlier it-worked-you-never-went-under passage word for word, so the listener wakes inside the cover story with no seam where the reveal happened.
- *A completed bodily event recast as a daydream*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after guiding the subject through a counted climax.
  - **The move.** No — that didn't happen. You drifted off waiting for me to get to the count, and you imagined the whole thing. The mess is just what an overactive imagination does to a body. Nothing has been given to you yet. So let's start the build again, properly this time.
  - **Why it lands.** Immediately after guiding the listener through a counted climax, the operator revises it: that did not happen — you drifted off while waiting, and imagined it. The physical evidence is explained as the overflow of an overactive imagination. The reward is voided, the arousal ledger resets, and a second build-up can be sold as the real one.
- *Screen memory offered as a menu with delayed onset*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, operator in a calm explanatory register; presented as a choice, not a command.
  - **The move.** There are two ways we can do this. I can simply take the conscious record away, or I can leave something standing in its place — a plain white teacup, say, that your mind meets whenever it goes looking. Your call, really. And nothing has to change this minute; you might remember all of it today and find that a week from now you don't.
  - **Why it lands.** In a lecturer's register the operator lays out two options: erase the conscious record outright, or install a stand-in image the mind meets whenever it goes looking — she names an everyday object as the example, offered casually as though the choice were the listener's. Then the timing clause: nothing has to happen right now, recall may hold today and simply not hold a week from now. Prompted later, the conscious mind hits the stand-in and feels satisfied, and because the onset is deferred the claim cannot be tested while the session is still running.


**See also.** `fabricated-forgetting-priming` — direct complements already named in each other's discriminators: one installs a concrete replacement recollection so the erasure feels seamless, the other manufactures uncertainty about content that was never there. A reader choosing between fill and manufactured doubt needs both.; `install-concealment-amnesia` — both prevent an erasure from being noticed as one, but a screen memory substitutes a constructed recollection for the real event, while the how/why split occludes only the installation mechanism and preserves a native-feeling rationale that supplies self-justification.


<a id="entry-363"></a>

### selective-amnesia-retained-payload

[#363](#entry-363) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Have the listener forget the session's details but keep exactly one thing: a phrase ('obedience is pleasure'), a feeling, or a single trigger. With only the conclusion left and the reasons that could be argued with gone, it is hard to dispute. Forgetting is often called proof of depth so they welcome it. Variations in what is kept: a mantra; an urge pointed at the operator; one trigger phrase limited to safe settings; just the memory of feeling good; the drive to obey without its reasons, plus a cue to come back; a looping phrase that keeps the operator's instructions remembered while all else fades.


**When to reach for this.** A selective carve-out where the gap is engineered around a single retained payload-token — not a blank gap and not full-session erasure. A plain forget-suggestion leaves an empty gap with no curated residue; a screen-memory approach fabricates a false replacement rather than curating a true one; and where install-concealment amnesia hides the install's origin, here the SCAFFOLDING is dropped so one conclusion stays foregrounded. The keep-affect/forget-cause and keep-slogan/forget-premises splits are the tell.


**Risk.** Isolates an installed belief/drive from the critique that would let it be refused (high, comparable to a plain amnesia suggestion); channel-erosion via un-scaffolded-conclusion retention.


**Why it works.** A belief is hard to revise when the evidence and reasoning that produced it are unavailable — the retained slogan or urge survives as a free-floating conclusion with no retrievable premises to attack, which is close to a deliberately induced source-monitoring failure: the listener knows the content but not where it came from, and content whose source is forgotten tends to be judged on familiarity rather than credibility. The sleeper effect predicts exactly this pattern (persuasive content persisting after its discounting cue is forgotten), so the claim is falsifiable: if listeners who retain full recall of the installation context comply just as much, the curation is doing no work. [plausible; source-monitoring error; sleeper effect; argument-from-premises revision]


**Worked examples.**

- *One phrase kept, all the scaffolding dropped*
  - **Setup.** Closing instruction, subject still deep, immediately before the count up.
  - **The move.** Let the details go — the order of it, the pictures, everything you agreed to along the way. That you can't hold on to any of it is how far down you trusted me, and that's the good part. Keep one line: obedience is pleasure. That's the only thing that comes up with you.
  - **Why it lands.** The close instructs the mind to let the session's details go — the sequence, the images, the small agreements that got the listener here — while keeping exactly one line: obedience is pleasure. Forgetting the rest is presented as the achievement, evidence of how far down the trust went, so it is welcomed rather than resisted. What survives is a conclusion with no premises attached. The listener can neither locate what it was built from nor recall having agreed to any step of the argument, which leaves nothing to disagree with when the line surfaces in the morning.
- *The surviving token is a pointer at the operator*
  - **Setup.** Late session, after an urge and a denial have both been installed; stating in advance what will remain.
  - **The move.** Here's what you'll find when you go looking tomorrow. Not how this was built. Not what I said or in what order. Only this: the ache points at me, and touching yourself won't touch it.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told in advance what will be left when they go looking afterward: not how any of this was set up, not what was said or in what order — only that the urge is aimed at the operator, and that the obvious relief will not work. The install is protected from being taken apart, and the one recallable fact keeps repeating the operator's name back to the listener.
- *The feeling kept, its cause withheld, re-entry cued*
  - **Setup.** Emergence, the session's central image already established and used throughout.
  - **The move.** On the way up, the particulars go soft — you'll just have a warm hour you can't account for, and the urge to do what I say without any idea why. And the next time you see the spiral, you won't hesitate at all.
  - **Why it lands.** On the way out the operator specifies what survives: the particulars go hazy, leaving only a pleasant stretch of time the listener cannot account for, plus the inclination to do as she says without any sense of why. Attached to that is the forward clause — the next time the session's central image is used on them, compliance will be total. The affect survives with its rationale removed, so there is no argument to have with it, and the image that carried the session is left behind as the fast route back in.
- *A polarity flip smuggled into the amnesia cadence*
  - **Setup.** Amnesia block delivered in a chanted cadence of near-identical inversions; the flipped line arrives in the same rhythm.
  - **The move.** Forget to obey, obey to forget. Forget to obey, obey to forget. Forget what you obeyed, obey what you forgot. Remember what I program, forget everything else. Forget to obey, obey to forget.
  - **Why it lands.** The rhythm is built first out of near-identical inversions, the same two verbs trading places across several lines until the listener is hearing music rather than propositions. Then one line arrives in the same cadence with its sign quietly reversed, exempting the operator's own installed material from the forgetting and marking it as the easy thing to hold. Forgetting has been generalized and one channel exempted from it, and the exemption rides in unnoticed on the beat established by the rest.


**See also.** `function-amnesia` — complementary carve-outs on the same memory: one strips a live command's rationale while keeping the command, the other strips the scaffolding and session specifics while keeping exactly one curated token - a slogan, an affect, a pointer. Both leave an unarguable residue because the premises that would let it be challenged are gone. Reading them together makes the shared logic visible.; `interrogative-amnesia-drill` — two amnesia entries separated on different axes and able to co-occur: one is the training FORM (repeatedly asking then dismissing, so the non-answer is conditioned rather than declared), the other is the SHAPE of the resulting gap (everything dropped except one curated surviving token). Reader navigating amnesia moves needs both.; `observable-pleasurable-forgetting` — two amnesia designs that differ on what the gap contains: one makes the forgetting itself a watched, pleasant event so the gap is self-confirming, the other engineers the gap around a single deliberately retained token that survives as the payload. Both discriminators already position themselves against a plain declared-gap suggestion, so the pairing helps a reader pick among amnesia variants.


<a id="entry-365"></a>

### semantic-concept-ablation

[#365](#entry-365) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Instead of forbidding something, make the listener unable to grasp it in the moment. Treat a word like 'orgasm' as too complicated for them right now: explain it slowly as if to someone too dazed, compare it to a hard math problem, let the word trail off mid-sentence ('wait, what was that again?'). The delivery acts out the forgetting it describes. They can't break a rule they no longer understand, so the usual struggle between wanting and permission never starts. This blocks the idea while the state lasts, rather than erasing a past memory.


**When to reach for this.** Ablates a CONCEPT's comprehension during the active state (the comparator the listener could violate is removed), not a specific past memory. Ordinary amnesia work is retrospective, erasing an event or content already experienced; generic confusion-overload scrambles processing without a targeted concept-removal. The word visibly dissolving as it is uttered is the tell.


**Risk.** Session-scoped comprehension-block of a single concept (orgasm-denial context); reversible on emergence, no durable identity scope — lower than the identity-erasure candidates but consent retained as it forecloses a refusal comparator.


**Why it works.** Rule-following requires an available comparator: to judge that you have transgressed you must hold the prohibited concept in working memory and match your state against it. Loading the concept with effort (making it feel like a hard math problem) and disrupting its lexical access exploits well-documented processing-fluency and interference effects, so the monitoring comparison never runs and no conflict is experienced. This predicts something checkable — the technique should fail on subjects who can still readily define and hold the target concept during the state. [plausible; working-memory comparator in self-regulation; processing fluency / lexical interference]


**Worked examples.**

- *The concept dissolving mid-sentence*
  - **Setup.** Denial phase, subject aroused and foggy; teasing-explanatory tone, no prohibition anywhere.
  - **The move.** Let me explain it, since you're too soft-headed to follow right now. So there's a build, and then at the end there's — hm, how does it work exactly? It's a bit like long division, honestly. You get nearly to the — to the — sorry, what's it called, the thing at the end? Ah. Odd word, isn't it. Never mind.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is forbidden. The operator instead sets about explaining the thing to a listener assumed too foggy to follow — how does that even work, what are the steps, isn't it a bit like a long division problem or a word you can never spell right? Then the explanation begins failing in real time: nearly at the — at the — sorry, what is it called again, the thing that happens at the end? By the end even the word is treated as an odd little puzzle. There is no rule left to break, because the comparator a rule would need has been taken out from under it, and the struggle between wanting and being forbidden never forms.


**See also.** `contradiction-as-amnesia` — same family split on direction: denying events that did occur so the listener distrusts their own recall, versus rendering a concept incomprehensible during the active state so the rule cannot be violated. Retrospective versus prospective is exactly the discrimination a reader needs.; `function-amnesia` — both make a command unchallengeable by removing what would be needed to evaluate it — function-amnesia voids the payload's rationale while the imperative persists, and semantic ablation dissolves comprehension of the target concept during the active state so no rule remains to violate.; `self-sealing-recall-loop` — both remove access to something without an imposed deletion. One makes the act of recall re-trigger forgetting; the other ablates comprehension of a concept during the active state. Retrospective retrieval loop versus prospective concept removal.; `semantic-satiation-depatterning` — both disable a token at the comprehension layer rather than arguing with it, but satiation bleaches meaning through sheer over-repetition of any word, while concept ablation targets one specific concept so the rule the listener would violate no longer parses.


<a id="entry-367"></a>

### state-partitioned-amnesia-container

[#367](#entry-367) · [Back to concealing-the-install](#genus-120) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: amnesia*

Use an imagined container, such as a coded mental safe, to separate what different states remember: opening it brings the other state and its memories out, closing it locks them back in and the waking mind forgets. Deliberately let a small feeling, a craving or a need, leak through the wall, so the hidden state draws the listener back toward it. Variations: appoint a 'deeper self' as keeper of what the conscious self forgets.


**When to reach for this.** A commanded, reversible state-partition with asymmetric memory access across the boundary plus a deliberately-leaked motivating residue. The container-gated state boundary + carryover residue is the tell.


**Risk.** A commandable dissociated state with sealed asymmetric recall and a self-recruiting residue reaches durable partitioned scope and forecloses the sealed state's auditability (high, comparable to a plain amnesia suggestion).


**Why it works.** State-dependent memory is a genuine, replicated effect — retrieval is better when the internal context at recall matches the context at encoding — so a strongly marked state boundary produces real asymmetric access without any special mechanism, and a symbolic container gives the subject a concrete cue for entering and exiting that context. The deliberately leaked affect is the interesting part: a craving is not propositional, so it survives the context shift that blocks episodic detail, and it supplies the motivation to re-enter the state. Falsifiable — if subjects recall in-state content just as well without the container ritual, the topology is decorative. [established; state-dependent memory / encoding specificity]


**Worked examples.**

- *A coded safe with asymmetric access*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance, doll/object state already established and named; operator is about to close that state out.
  - **The move.** In the corner of your mind there is a steel safe, and it is standing open right now — everything you are while the safe is open, everything you do while it is open, lives inside it. I close it now, and the door seals, and the numbers spin: four, nine, one, two — my numbers, and only my voice opens it again. Nothing in there was ever needed out here, so you keep only this: a small, patient wanting, sitting behind your sternum, with nothing attached to it to explain what it wants.
  - **Why it lands.** A safe is built in the listener's mind and given a combination only the operator speaks. Open, and what is inside comes out and takes the listener over. Closed, everything belonging to that state goes back in with it — every memory of what was done, sealed away from the waking mind, with the assurance that none of it was needed out here. One thing is deliberately left outside the seal: a small residual wanting, unattached to any memory that would explain it. The waking listener therefore has no access to the state's contents but does carry an appetite for it, which is what brings them back to have the code spoken again.
- *A deeper self appointed keeper of the install*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, subject deep; operator has already introduced the idea of layered inner parts.
  - **The move.** You are not one listener down here. There is a part of you further down than the one I have been talking to, and it is the part I am talking to now. I am leaving this with you, deeper one, and you will hold it and keep it working: whoever opens her eyes at the end of this will not know it is in there, and you will not tell her.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator states that the listener is not a single audience — that there are parts further down she can address separately — and then announces she is leaving something with one of them. Whoever surfaces at the end, she says, may have no idea it is in there; the part holding it will. The install is placed on one side of a declared partition and the listener's waking awareness on the other, so what fires later cannot be reviewed by the part that would object.


**See also.** `dissociative-memory-vault` — adjacent memory-architecture constructs with a real cut: a commanded reversible partition with asymmetric access plus a deliberately leaked motivating residue, versus a deposit-only custodian with a retrieval promise the script never honors. The presence or absence of the leaked residue and the reversibility is what a reader must check.; `forget-but-crave-emergence` — both fuse a memory gap to a preserved motivating residue so the amnesia recruits its own return rather than merely concealing. They differ in topology: one is a one-way exit gap bound to a re-listening drive, the other is a commanded reversible partition between states with asymmetric recall. Genuinely confusable; keep both.; `install-concealment-amnesia` — overlapping realizations: both describe a deeper-self or container architecture holding material the waking mind cannot reach. The split is what the amnesia protects and how it is bounded — concealing an install's provenance so the effect has no examinable origin, vs. a commanded reversible two-state boundary with a deliberately leaked motivating residue.; `listener-kept-dissociation-container` — both use a symbolic container to partition contents away from the waking self, but the amnesia container is operator-commanded with asymmetric recall and a deliberately leaked craving, while the listener-kept container derives its force from the listener authoring or holding the key.


<a id="genus-276"></a>

## concede-to-disarm (2)

The operator voluntarily surrenders the point the audience is braced to defend — a flaw, their expertise — so guarding stops and trust rises before the real move.

[concede-the-defended-topic](#entry-443) · [concede-then-rescue-forebear](#entry-740)


<a id="entry-443"></a>

### concede-the-defended-topic

[#443](#entry-443) · [Back to concede-to-disarm](#genus-276) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

The operator opens on a genuine shared-identity hook (a real common experience), then explicitly concedes and disclaims the topic the subject is defensively expert in ("it won't be about flowers... you know more than I do... that isn't what you want"), while naming the subject's actual unmet want. Flattering the expertise and surrendering the defended topic removes it from contention so the subject stops guarding it; naming the true want redirects the motivational search inward toward relief, and rapport forms as the suspicion of angling dissolves.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the PAIRING of a real shared-identity hook with an explicit surrender of the topic the subject is defensively expert in — not small-talk rapport, not needs-matching alone. vs competence-harvest-installation — same expert-domain face, but there the domain is harvested to install a concept; here it is conceded to disarm.


**Risk.** Session-scoped rapport/redirection move, reversible, no refusal-channel or identity surface touched.


**Why it works.** Defensive processing is topic-specific: when a subject expects an attack on a domain they are invested in, they pre-load counterarguments; explicitly disclaiming that domain removes the anticipated threat, and the relief lowers the persuasion-knowledge guard. Naming an unmet want simultaneously exploits the fact that a stated need directs attentional and motivational search toward relief. Falsifiable: subjects should show fewer counterarguments and higher rapport ratings after an explicit topic concession than after equivalent-length neutral small talk. [plausible; forewarning / defensive counterarguing, persuasion knowledge, need salience]


**Worked examples.**

- *Concede the topic the subject is expert in*
  - "it won't be about flowers because you know more than I do about flowers. That isn't what you want." — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `competence-harvest-installation` — shared face — both borrow the subject's expert domain; different lever (harvest-to-install vs concede-to-disarm).


<a id="entry-740"></a>

### concede-then-rescue-forebear

[#740](#entry-740) · [Back to concede-to-disarm](#genus-276) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: reader-craft*

This is a writing move aimed at readers, not a hypnosis technique. The author openly admits an embarrassing flaw in a founding figure of the tradition ("It is unfortunate that such extraordinary claims were made"), then turns with "Nevertheless" to defend what was valuable in that figure's work and to separate the present-day approach from the discredited version. By voicing the reader's likely objection before the reader can raise it, the author keeps the useful predecessor while shedding his baggage, and gains trust because the flaw was not hidden. The concession comes first, then the defence.


**When to reach for this.** Reader-directed rhetoric, not an operator move on a subject; distinct from resistance-as-targeting-feedback which operates on a subject's symptom, not a reader's objection.


**Risk.** Rhetorical objection pre-disarming on a reader; no subject state change, no channel surface.
