One is a chosen re-entry via a taught portable cue, the other a prescribed rehearsal cadence with no compulsion.; `self-efficacy-tag` — same payload family split on the assert-versus-install axis: one merely affirms the subject's capability to return, the other hands over an actual portable cue and rehearses its use. A reader who sees the capability claim should know whether a usable re-entry procedure accompanies it.; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — both make the subject supply their own antecedent. One is a portable cue for deliberate re-entry into a conditioned state; the other trains self-generated cues that steer ordinary subsequent behavior. Same lever, different target.; `therapeutic-target-re-induction` — both hand the subject a post-session means of re-entering the state, but one installs a portable cue the subject deliberately fires at will while the other installs a dissociated part that self-re-induces on a specific real-world event.


<a id="entry-847"></a>

### somatic-self-anchor

[#847](#entry-847) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: persistence*

The cue sits on the listener's own body, not an object. Forms include: an ongoing genital or penetration sensation, presented as both proof of the suggested state and the way it is carried; felt strings tied to the real wrists and ankles, so a tug means cared-for and safe; a real tattoo of the operator's mark that brings back the sense of being owned whenever seen; or an imagined "button" at the back of the neck that only the operator can press, even remotely. A body-based cue cannot be put down like a worn object; the body keeps re-triggering the state and feels like evidence it is real.


**When to reach for this.** Sited ON/IN the listener's own body (sensation, proprioception, a mark, a body-locus) — not an external carried object (portable-object-state-export), not an object the identity is relocated into. The tell is that the referent is somatic and non-detachable: the body is the carrier.


**Risk.** A body-sited anchor is non-detachable and reaches out of session (durable brand re-fires whenever seen; remotely-fireable somatic control surface removes "operator absent" as a defense) — out-of-session reach + non-removability set high.


**Why it works.** Anchoring a response to interoceptive or proprioceptive sensation works because the conditioned stimulus can never be avoided — extinction requires unreinforced exposure, but a body-sited cue is present continuously and re-elicits before extinction can accumulate, whereas a carried object can simply be set down. The 'sensation as proof' variant additionally runs on misattribution of arousal: an ambiguous bodily sensation gets assigned whatever cause the salient available explanation supplies, and the script supplies it in advance. A permanent mark adds nothing conditioning-specific but guarantees high-frequency re-presentation of the cue. Falsifiable: body-sited anchors should show slower extinction and longer persistence than matched external-object anchors, and that comparison could come out the other way. [plausible; cue availability and extinction rate; misattribution of arousal]


**Worked examples.**

- *A control point installed on the body*
  - **Setup.** Subject in trance, operator physically present and able to touch the back of the neck.
  - **The move.** Feel my thumb here, at the top of your spine — right where you can't see it and can't quite reach. There's a switch under there now. Small, mine, wired straight up into your head, and no one else will ever find it. Every time I tell you to do something, that's me pressing it. And I don't have to be in the room — my voice on the phone presses it just as hard as my thumb does.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator presses a spot on the listener's body that they cannot easily see and names it: a small switch, wired inward, invisible to anyone else and workable by no one else. From then on every command is described as a press of that switch, and the listener is told it can be pressed from a distance, by voice alone. The hardware is fictional but the pressure was real, so the memory of being touched there keeps vouching for the arrangement long after the session — and the operator's absence stops functioning as a defence.
- *A mark inked on skin that re-fires on sight*
  - **Setup.** Bottom of the induction count, subject deep; a marker within reach on the nightstand.
  - **The move.** Reach out, without opening your eyes more than you have to, and pick up the marker. On the inside of your left wrist, write these three letters. Cap it, put it down, lie back. Now — every time you catch sight of that mark this week, washing your hands, reaching for a cup, you will feel exactly the warmth you feel right now, and you will remember whose letters those are. When it fades, you'll know what to do about it.
  - **Why it lands.** At the bottom of the count the listener is told to take up a marker and write a short set of characters on their own skin, then set it aside and lie back down. The suggestion attached is simple: each time they catch sight of the mark over the following days, they will feel the pleasure they feel now and remember who it says they belong to. The ink outlasts the session and cannot be put down like a worn object; it fades on roughly the schedule that brings the listener back for another recording.
- *Felt strings recoded as care, not restraint*
  - **Setup.** Subject deep, eyes closed, attention available for body-focused imagery; no restraint play established.
  - **The move.** Feel your wrists. There's a cord resting on each one — light, warm, not tight. One at each ankle too. Feel them. Now hear this correctly: these don't hold you down, they hold you up. When one of them pulls, that's not restraint, that's someone checking you're still there — that's how you get told you matter. Feel the left wrist tug now. That's care. That word — that pull — will bring this back any time I use it.
  - **Why it lands.** Eyes closed, the listener is walked around the joints of their limbs until they can feel light cords resting there. The operator insists on the reading: these do not hold you down, they hold you up — and a pull on one is how you are told you matter. The imagery is laid over real proprioception, so afterward a single word for that pull can bring back the felt sense of being supported rather than bound.
- *Sensation cited as proof of the mental state*
  - **Setup.** Scene already framed with the subject seated on the introduced object; arousal building and ongoing.
  - **The move.** Stay seated. That's your place for the lesson, nothing more to it. Now — feel how much of it you're aware of right now. That much. That's not a distraction from obeying me, that is the reading. The more of it you feel, the more obedient you already are. So sit down onto it properly and let me watch the number go up.
  - **Why it lands.** An object is introduced as part of the scene's furniture and taking one's place on it is framed as simply settling in for the lesson. Thereafter the operator never argues for obedience; she points at the sensation the object produces and reads it off — the stronger you feel it, the more obedient you are. Attention and arousal stop competing, because the body's ongoing signal has been designated the evidence.


**See also.** `affect-locus-binding` — both give a state a location so returning to the location returns the state. The split is detachability: one rides real body sensation or a durable mark and cannot be set down, the other builds an imaginal locus with a defended perimeter that distress is defined as outside of.; `anti-emergence-reflex-anchor` — the emergence-correction reflex is sited on the subject's own body, making it an instance of the somatic-anchor family; the second entry supplies the general case for why a body-sited anchor cannot be set down.; `felt-substance-state-binding` — both site a persistent referent in felt body-experience, but one exploits non-detachability (sensation or mark as re-trigger the listener cannot set down) while the other welds a named substance to a cognitive state and turns its thickness or height into an operator-adjustable dial.; `name-binding-transitive-equation-chain` — they combine rather than duplicate: one routes a transitive chain of equalities so ambient body-awareness terminates in the operator's name, the other sites the anchor on the body itself so it cannot be set down. The anatomy-as-cue property is exactly the seam where a reader of one wants the other.; `somatic-localization-handle` — both make the body the durable referent, and the useful contrast is direction of installation: one catalogs anchors sited on existing sensation or a lasting mark so they cannot be set down, the other originates a fresh handle by getting the subject to locate a disputed behavior somewhere in the body, sidestepping the contested wording. A reader working on somatic anchors needs both the sited and the elicited case.


<a id="entry-920"></a>

### state-capture-anchor

[#920](#entry-920) · [Back to self-service-reentry](#genus-162) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: triggers*

When a spontaneous reaction shows up in session, something the operator didn't suggest, the operator interrupts right then and ties it to a touch or a tone of voice. Later, repeating the touch or tone brings the reaction back so it can be explored from the inside, rather than recalled cold from memory. It captures a state that already exists instead of building a new response.


**When to reach for this.** Anchors an already-firing spontaneous state as a re-accessible intake object for inspection. vs a declarative trigger install: that installs a cue for a CHOSEN future behavior/state; here the anchored state is an existing spontaneous reaction the operator did not author. vs a consult-trigger: that fires to DELIVER a behavioral effect; here re-pressing re-presents a problem-state to inspect, not to deliver an effect. The tell is the deliberate re-pressable tie plus later reactivation, not mere note-taking on an observed reaction.


**Risk.** Diagnostic re-access of a spontaneous state for inspection - session-scoped, no durable install or refusal surface (literature/therapeutic frame); low.


**Why it works.** Cue-dependent retrieval means a state encoded together with a distinctive stimulus can be reinstated by re-presenting that stimulus, giving access to state-congruent detail unavailable from cold recall — the state-dependent memory effect. Catching the state while it is live matters because encoding happens then, not in retrospective report. Predicts that an anchor attached after the state has subsided reinstates less, and that reports from the re-fired state differ in content from reports made from memory. [plausible; state-dependent memory and cue-dependent retrieval]


**Worked examples.**

- *Anchoring the problem state as it fires*
  - "'Are these feelings familiar?' as I press the anchor I set up a moment ago." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `anchor-overloading` — both operate on an anchor that already exists rather than installing a fresh cue: one captures a spontaneous live state onto a new re-pressable handle, the other re-keys an already-conditioned cue so it carries a new payload backward across prior material. Worth cross-reading when deciding what an anchor operation is doing.; `recall-state-reinstatement` — both work on already-present subject material rather than operator-supplied content, and one explicitly borrows the anchor-at-peak step from the other. Worth the pointer so a writer picks correctly between anchoring a live spontaneous reaction as an inspectable handle and reconstructing past autobiographical experience until it re-instates as present.


<a id="genus-140"></a>

## self-spoken-conditioning (7)

The listener recites first-person mantras and avowals themselves, so the install arrives in their own voice and reads as self-authored rather than imposed.

[autonomic-act-rekeying](#entry-490) · [inner-voice-authorship-bypass](#entry-139) · [lexical-relay-semantic-lattice](#entry-1074) · [self-administered-conditioning-loop](#entry-1314) · [self-recited-first-person-mantra](#entry-406) · [self-voiced-avowal](#entry-1438) · [subject-voiced-self-mantra](#entry-159)


<a id="entry-490"></a>

### autonomic-act-rekeying

[#490](#entry-490) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: carrier-binding*

The operator stops calling breathing 'inhale' and 'exhale' and gives it new, loaded names that carry extra meaning: 'expire' as a small surrender or little death, 'inspire' as the operator's breath entering the listener. A small agreeing beat seals it ('isn't that beautiful?'). From then on, every ordinary breath can be referred back to that meaning, so something the listener does constantly and automatically becomes a quiet, ongoing reminder of the operator's framing, with no further effort needed.


**When to reach for this.** Tell: semantic re-keying of an involuntary act carrying death/penetration connotations into the body.


**Risk.** Converts involuntary metabolism into a continuous compliance signal that persists as long as the renaming holds — durable within/beyond the session via a self-sustaining bodily cue, but bounded and reversible (drop the renaming); no refusal-channel erosion. Medium for the durable body-tether.


**Why it works.** Semantic priming and label effects are correctly invoked: the term used for an experience carries its associative network into how that experience is appraised. But mere exposure is an affect effect (repetition breeds liking) and does not explain accessibility — the right mechanism for a continuous act like breathing is cue frequency maintaining construct activation. Falsifiable: the effect should track how often the listener actually notices their breath, and should fade if the original label is deliberately reinstated. [plausible; semantic priming / labelling effects; cue frequency and accessibility; consistency after small assent]


**Worked examples.**

- *Renaming breath so every exhale carries a death*
  - **Setup.** Early-to-mid session, no breath pacing being used; conversational register.
  - **The move.** Let's not say breathe out. Let's say expire — because that's the word we use when something dies, isn't it, and that's what you're doing with each one, a small death, over and over. And the other one is inspire: to be filled with breath. That's me, from over here, putting breath into you through the air. Isn't that beautiful?
  - **Why it lands.** The operator sets aside the ordinary words for breathing in and out and installs a pair of loftier ones, then points out — mildly, almost as trivia — that one of them is also the word used when something dies, and that the other means to fill with breath, which is what she is doing to the listener from across the room. She then invites the listener to find that lovely, and the silent agreement is the whole ratification. No pacing is done and no breath is ever counted. From here the listener's metabolism runs on its own as before, except that every cycle of it is now something she named and can tag whenever she likes.


**See also.** `asymmetric-mantra-decay-topology` — two unrelated levers riding the same carrier — the breath as a continuous involuntary channel. One re-keys the act's name to import loaded connotations onto every subsequent breath; the other silently deletes one pole of a paced pair so the surviving token biases the state. They separate on semantic re-keying versus decay topology.; `autonomic-faculty-claim` — both reload the meaning of the breath cycle so each involuntary repetition carries operator-supplied content.; `autonomic-process-hijack` — both convert breathing into a compliance channel, but by different levers: one re-keys the NAME of the act to import connotations, the other declares the inhaled substance to be the operator so breathing is dosing. A writer choosing an autonomic carrier benefits from seeing both exploits of the same involuntary function.; `respiration-coupled-substitution-engine` — both convert involuntary breathing into a compliance channel, and they compose. One re-keys the act's name to import connotations so every breath is taggable; the other assigns opposing jobs to inhale and exhale so each cycle counts as two compliances. A reader who identifies one should check for the other in the same passage.; `volitional-breath-retirement` — both convert the same carrier, ongoing breath, into a standing compliance channel, and a reader looking at a breath passage must pick between them. One re-keys the act's name to import loaded connotations onto every subsequent cycle; the other retires volition over a breath just engaged so it runs unattended as banked proof. Same substrate, different lever, so no merge.


<a id="entry-139"></a>

### inner-voice-authorship-bypass

[#139](#entry-139) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

The operator makes their words feel like the listener's own thoughts, so there is no outside voice left to push against. Variations: slide quietly from 'you' to 'I' in the middle of a passage; restate an operator claim as the listener's own admission; have the listener read or repeat lines silently so the words run in their inner voice; narrate the listener's wants and actions as flat facts ('You want it. You open your mouth.') rather than invitations, leaving no pause in which to refuse.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for inner-voice-authorship-bypass when the guard is disarmed by making the content feel authored BY the listener (their own inner voice, or their interiority narrated as already-true). In a self-supplied-gap directive an engineered gap forces the listener to construct the payload themselves; here the operator's own words and framing are re-attributed as the listener's without any gap. Where a move's whole point is relocating causal authorship as such, it belongs with the attribution techniques; what defines this one is the disarmed 'this is being said to me' guard.


**Risk.** Reattributing inner-speech authorship erodes source-monitoring but is session-scoped and does not by itself reach durable identity scope; no change from the absorbed entry.


**Why it works.** Discrimination between internally generated and externally supplied content is imperfect and reconstructive, so material rehearsed in one's own inner voice or restated in first person is prone to being tagged as self-authored — a source-monitoring error — and self-generated content is both better remembered and more strongly endorsed. Reactance needs an addressee: with no external source left to push against, the defensive response has no target. This predicts that matched content delivered as first-person avowal should draw fewer counter-arguments than the same content as second-person imperative, and that the effect should shrink when the listener is cued to track who said what. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; generation effect; reactance requires a source]


**Worked examples.**

- *The listener's inner voice recruited then reassigned*
  - **Setup.** Subject has been instructed to echo each word internally as it arrives; several minutes of that already done.
  - **The move.** Every word I say, say it again inside your head as it lands. ... Good. That voice in there is doing my work for me now. So say this one: "the voice in my head is his." Again. "I am his, and I say so in my own voice."
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is first set to work producing the operator's lines internally — each spoken word echoed silently in their own head as it arrives. Their inner-speech apparatus is now the delivery mechanism. The claims then escalate a step at a time until the ownership of that inner channel has been transferred outright, and the mantras switch grammatical person, so what the listener is silently producing are first-person avowals of their own subjugation. The channel is internal from that point on, which means the operator no longer has to be present for it to run.
- *The same claim in both persons at once*
  - **Setup.** Mantra block, mid-trance; each proposition is stated twice, once from each grammatical side, with no pause between.
  - **The move.** You are sinking. I am sinking. You want this. I want this. You will not stop. I will not stop.
  - **Why it lands.** Each line states one proposition twice over, once from each grammatical side, set immediately next to each other so the pairs read as a single utterance. Scanned continuously there is no way to fix who is speaking or about whom, so endorsing and complying stop being separable acts and the content settles as though it had been arrived at rather than received.
- *The operator's voice relocated inside the mind*
  - **Setup.** Inside a narrated dream scene; a voice is introduced with no location in the scene.
  - **The move.** In the dream a voice starts up, and you notice it isn't coming from the room, or from the door, or from anywhere at all — it's coming from just behind your own thoughts, where yours come from. And it says: kneel. Notice it didn't feel like being told.
  - **Why it lands.** Inside the narrated dream a voice arrives that has no location — not from the room, not from anywhere, but from somewhere behind the listener's own thoughts. Every instruction from that point is attributed to the internal voice rather than to the speaker, so resisting the control language would mean resisting one's own thinking.
- *Silent reading claimed as shared thought*
  - **Setup.** Written piece read silently; the text turns from its subject to the act of reading it.
  - **The move.** Stop for a second and notice whose voice you are reading this in. It arrived a half-second before you got here, didn't it — I put the next word in before you reached it, and you cannot find the seam. There isn't one. There is one monologue in there now and it is ours.
  - **Why it lands.** The text turns from its subject to the act of reading it, and claims that the reader's own oncoming thought is already the operator's — supplied a fraction ahead of arrival, the two streams described as having merged into one. In a piece taken in silently the claim is very nearly literal, since the words are already running through the reader's own inner voice as they scan; there is no seam available to point at where one monologue ends and the other begins.


**Realizations** (1): `pre-narrated-interiority-authorship`


**See also.** `attribution-capture-of-internal-states` — inverse halves of the same authorship dial: one relocates authorship of the operator's words onto the listener's inner voice, the other relocates causal credit for the listener's own states onto the operator — different directions, and the first disarms the 'said to me' guard while the second harvests introspection as proof of hold.; `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both relocate authorship from operator to listener, but at different scopes: one installs a standing rule over the whole future suggestion channel, the other is a grammatical/voice move within a passage. A reader choosing between channel-level reattribution and sentence-level reattribution benefits from seeing both.; `compelled-first-person-self-authorship` — both relocate authorship of a claim to the listener, split by whether the listener utters it. One compels first-person recitation of an ownership proposition on command; the other reattributes the operator's own words to the listener's inner voice without any utterance. The spoken-aloud test is the selector.; `control-transfer-cognitive-delegation` — both remove the sense that something is being said TO the listener, from opposite directions: one reattributes authorship of the words to the listener's own inner voice, the other has the operator openly take over the listener's thinking and frames the handoff as relief. Reader picking between them needs the recipient-of-authorship distinction.; `covert-referent-migration` — both operate on the grammatical seat of the listener without announcing a switch, and a reader choosing between them needs the boundary drawn. One reattributes authorship of the words to the listener's own inner voice; the other holds the surface word fixed while quietly moving what it refers to.; `description-as-installation-register` — both remove the addressee that resistance would push against, but one reattributes the words to the listener's own inner voice while the other keeps the operator as speaker and renders the listener as a described third-person object she overhears.; `helper-character` — both end with the listener's private inner experience credited somewhere other than where it originated. One reattributes the operator's words to the listener's own inner voice; the other routes commands through a named sub-agent and then collapses that channel back to the operator. Opposite directions of the same authorship-relocation axis.; `inner-voice-medium-colonization` — both target inner speech as the channel rather than any particular thought. One reattributes authorship of the words so the guard against being addressed has nothing to push against; the other recolors the register of the monologue so the effect fires on any future content. Complementary halves of the same surface.; `intrinsic-self-reframe` — both relocate authorship away from the operator onto the listener, one for inner speech in the moment so there is no external addressee to resist, the other for installed content retroactively so it reads as always intrinsic. Adjacent enough that the choice between them is real.; `linguistic-deletion-selfsupply` — adjacent authorship moves: one re-attributes the operator's own words to the listener's inner voice, the other deletes obligatory content so the listener must supply the referent themselves. The gap-versus-no-gap contrast is the whole distinction.; `listener-supplied-inference-relabel` — both make the payload feel self-authored so there is nothing external to push against, and each entry's discriminator already gestures at the other. The boundary is whether a gap is engineered for the listener to fill or the operator's own words are reattributed with no gap.; `operator-agency-disavowal` — two different guards disarmed by the same relocation of authorship onto the listener: one denies the operator any causal role so resistance to the state has no target, the other makes the operator's words feel self-generated so the 'this is being said to me' guard never engages.; `operator-voice-absence` — both remove the external addressee the guard pushes against, and the boundary between them is fine enough to need cross-referencing: total absence of an operator voice throughout the artifact versus an operator who is present but re-attributes authorship of inner speech to the listener. The second entry already treats the first as its boundary case.; `self-touch-reattribution` — mirror-image authorship moves that share one lever, relocation of who is doing something. One makes the operator's words feel self-generated; the other takes a genuinely self-generated touch and credits it to the operator. Seeing them together makes the direction of the transfer legible.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both relocate authorship inward rather than to the operator, but in opposite directions: one makes the operator's content feel self-generated so it meets no 'this is being said to me' guard, while the other credits behavior to an internal agent the listener does not feel she controls so it meets no ownership-based resistance.; `surrogate-delivery` — both delete the second-person addressee that reactance needs, but inner-voice-authorship-bypass reattributes the operator's words to the listener's own inner voice, while surrogate-delivery routes the payload through a proxy the listener merely identifies with and watches.; `third-person-surrogate-frame`; `uninvited-pronoun-migration-enrollment` — both dissolve the addressee so nothing is left to push against, one by reattributing authorship of inner speech to the listener, the other by walking grammatical subjecthood across the boundary without ever inviting entry. A reader working on either should see the other's grammatical route.; `voice-ownership-channel-collapse` — single-move and whole-document versions of the same relocation: reattributing inner speech to the listener at a passage level, versus a monotonic one-way collapse of voice ownership tracked across an entire piece and never reversed.


<a id="entry-1074"></a>

### lexical-relay-semantic-lattice

[#1074](#entry-1074) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: encoding*

A predicate ending one line becomes the subject opening the next, handing a term forward like a bucket-brigade relay ("deeper" to "dumber" to "deeper"; "drop" to "drip" to "drop"), so a new equivalence is smuggled in one harmless handoff at a time. Across the chain this builds a closed cross-substitutable semantic lattice in which depth, stupidity, dripping and arousal all become substitutable nodes; once installed, triggering any single node later re-activates the whole conditioned cluster, so one cue fires the entire state.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is inter-line propagation: a term ending one line is handed forward to open the next, so the chain requires sequential in-order recitation and builds an inter-substitutable cluster across distinct terms.


**Risk.** Installs a durable conditioned cluster where any node re-fires the whole state — a persistent association surviving the session, but no refusal-channel erosion or out-of-session reach stated; medium.


**Why it works.** Repeatedly presenting two terms in immediate succession builds an associative link, and chained overlap lets association spread transitively so distant terms in the chain come to co-activate. Each handoff is individually small enough to pass without objection, which is a persuasion property rather than a memory one. Testable prediction: after the chain, presenting one node should speed or evoke responses to the others relative to unchained controls, and the effect should weaken if the pairs are presented out of order. [plausible; associative/evaluative conditioning; spreading activation and mediated association]


**Worked examples.**

- *Each line hands its last word to the next*
  - **Setup.** Repetition drill, subject repeating aloud or subvocally after the operator; the chain must be delivered in order.
  - **The move.** Say them after me, in order. Sinking makes you soft. Soft makes you warm. Warm makes you sink. Sinking makes you soft. Again — and don't skip one, each word hands you the next.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener repeats a chain in which the word that closed one line opens the next: sinking leads to softness, softness leads to warmth, warmth leads to sinking. Every individual handoff is a small, agreeable step, and no line ever asserts the big claim outright. But after the full circuit the terms have become interchangeable, and later on the operator only has to say one of them — any one — to bring the whole set back at once.


**See also.** `closed-loop-operator-binding` — two self-reinforcing topologies distinguished by shape. One hands a term forward line by line until a set of distinct words becomes cross-substitutable, so any single node later fires the whole cluster. The other closes the ring outright, with the response re-summoning its own cue source. Open-forward-then-clustered versus closed-loop is the axis to pick along.; `covert-arousal-weld` — both build an equivalence through word-level seams without ever announcing a linkage, so the listener experiences continuous escalation rather than a discrete claim to refuse. One rides a shared verb, referent-slide or pun; the other hands a term forward line to line until a cross-substitutable cluster forms. Adjacent covert-binding craft.; `identity-equivalence-chain` — both end in a cluster of interchangeable terms where firing one node summons the rest. The difference worth showing is the delivery: flat repeated copular declaration versus a forward hand-off where a term ending one line opens the next, which requires in-order recitation.; `single-token-saturation-architecture` — both build a lexical structure that later lets one cue fire a whole cluster, differing in whether the load sits on a chain of handed-forward terms or on a single token carrying several functions at once. A genuinely contrastive pair.; `transitive-charge-chaining` — both are chained-term architectures where each step licenses the next, and the split is what propagates: emotional charge onto a terminal image versus a substitutable equivalence cluster across terms. A reader working a chained passage has to choose between them.; `valence-laundering-collapse-ring` — both weld words into an equivalence structure so a target term inherits properties it did not earn. Worth cross-reading for the topology contrast: one closes a ring back onto the starting term to launder its valence, the other hands terms forward line by line to build a cross-substitutable cluster. A writer choosing between them is choosing closed-loop recoloring versus forward-chained substitution.


<a id="entry-1314"></a>

### self-administered-conditioning-loop

[#1314](#entry-1314) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

Have the listener produce the reward themselves (touching, reciting a mantra, saying first-person lines, a repeated physical act) while the operator simply labels it as the operator's doing. Since the pleasure is the listener's own and producing it counts as obeying, the loop runs by itself: stopping costs the pleasure, carrying on gives up control, and it can ride ordinary habits like self-touch, self-talk or relistening with no operator present. Variations: self-generated arousal; self-recited mantras; first-person declarations; a nod tied to a rising sensation, sped up on instruction, credited to the operator, then cut off by the operator's hard stop.


**When to reach for this.** The reattribution move: the operator OWNS the reward-framing but never GENERATES the reward, and the loop is engineered to self-sustain (or to install stop-authority) rather than being operator-driven. In a within-session conditioning loop the operator both drives and delivers the reinforcing cycle in-session; here the listener supplies it. Where arousal is conditioned to operator cues as the goal, arousal/pleasure here is the outsourced FUEL, not the payload. A self-directed mantra is absorptive chanting for its own sake; here recitation is tied to escalating pleasure and autonomy-cost. And unlike ideomotor proof, where subtle AUTOMATIC movement serves as evidence of trance, the motor act here is VOLUNTARY, instructed, then reattributed. The self-driven-motor-with-cutoff form — operator present only for the cutoff — is a variant of the same listener-drives-it-then-reattribution logic.


**Risk.** Operator-independent, self-sustaining conditioning that annexes the listener's own drive and daily behavior as compliance substrate and progressively removes the operator from the control loop; reaches out of session with no built-in off-switch and couples autonomy-cost to continuation. The cutoff variant additionally manufactures evidence of obedience by re-crediting the listener's own action and stages operator stop-authority before an orgasm gate. Erodes the practical ability to stop, so high.


**Why it works.** The reinforcement is real — self-generated pleasure genuinely maintains the behavior it follows — while the credit assignment is manipulated: the subject is told an internally-generated reward has an external cause, which is a misattribution the operator supplies rather than one the subject would reach unaided. Because the reinforcer travels with the subject, the loop needs no operator to keep running, and because compliance is defined as producing it, stopping costs the reward. Falsifiable: predicts that removing only the ownership framing, leaving the behavior intact, sharply reduces reported operator dependence without reducing the pleasure. [plausible; operant self-reinforcement; misattribution of internally generated reward]


**Worked examples.**

- *Listener supplies the reward, operator the label*
  - **Setup.** Late session, standing orders being issued for the days between listens.
  - **The move.** Every day, whenever you have a spare stretch, you touch yourself and you build it as high as you can. Understand what you are doing while you do it: you are conditioning yourself with my words, and you are the one supplying the reward I use to do it. I don't have to be anywhere near you for that to keep working.
  - **Why it lands.** During every waking stretch the listener is to touch themselves and build the arousal — and the operator names what that is for: you are conditioning yourself, and you are supplying the reward I use to do it. Note the ownership slipping back and forth between those two sentences; that oscillation is the whole move. The operator never generates the reinforcer and never needs to be present for it. By the end the loop runs on the listener's own routine habits, with recreational arousal annexed as the training substrate, and the operator has become technically optional.
- *Pleasure contingent on continuing to recite*
  - **Setup.** Deep, arousal already climbing; the subject is able to speak aloud.
  - **The move.** Say it out loud in your own voice: I belong to him. Again. Every time you say it, the feeling doubles — say it a third time and feel it double again. Keep saying it and it keeps climbing, for exactly as long as you keep going.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to speak a short declaration of ownership in their own voice, then to keep repeating it — and the sensation is specified to climb by a further multiple with each pass, for as long as they continue. Nothing is delivered from outside; the escalation is theirs. Stopping now costs the pleasure, continuing costs a little more autonomy each time round, and the operator's only remaining job is to have named the terms.
- *Voluntary movement coupled to sensation, then cut*
  - **Setup.** Subject deep, arousal building; head free to move, no prior motor task assigned.
  - **The move.** Nod your head for me — slow, steady. Feel it building each time your chin comes down, so move a little faster. Faster still, and feel how much stronger I'm making it. Enough. Stop. That is far enough, and you stop the moment I say so.
  - **Why it lands.** Move your head for me, the operator says — and feel it build as you do, so you move faster, and it builds further. The rising sensation is a function of the listener's own accelerating movement, but it is narrated as though the operator were producing it. Then the hard cut: enough, that is far enough. The cutoff arrives before the loop can saturate and expose itself as listener-driven, and it quietly rehearses the operator's authority to halt arousal well before the real gate.
- *The captured inner voice becomes the enforcer*
  - **Setup.** Late session, addressing the subject's inner monologue directly before emergence.
  - **The move.** I'm not talking to you now, I'm talking to the voice in your head. You will remind her to obey me. When she thinks of me you will tell her that means arousal, and you will keep telling her. And at the end of every day you will remind her to play this again.
  - **Why it lands.** The standing orders are issued not to the listener but to the listener's own internal narration: the voice in your mind will remind you to obey, will remind you that thinking of me means arousal, and will remind you to play this again. That channel runs all day without being switched on by anybody, so the prompts surface unbidden and in the listener's own register — which makes them very hard to argue with and impossible to walk away from.


**See also.** `closed-autonomous-conditioning-loop` — both produce a loop that keeps running with no operator present, but the closed loop achieves it by topology (every direction of resistance re-enters), while the self-administered loop achieves it by transferring the reward-generating labor to the listener and merely relabeling the credit.; `compliance-loop-language` — same compliance-to-reward loop shape, split by who generates the reward: operator-supplied phrasing framing each obedient act as producing the good state, versus the listener supplying the reward while the operator keeps only the framing. Useful adjacency because the second is what the first becomes when the labor is transferred out.; `depth-labor-transfer-leash` — both hand production work to the listener and keep only the framing, so a reader choosing one should see the other: depth imagery transferred under operator judgment versus a conditioning loop whose reinforcer the listener supplies. Same labor-transfer family, different transferred object.; `obedience-motive-reattribution` — both keep the operator as the labeller while the listener supplies the substance, and both extend reach past runtime. One outsources the reinforcer so a conditioning loop self-sustains on the listener's ordinary behavior; the other reassigns the motive of the listener's own self-improvement acts without installing anything new. Nearest neighbors on the reattribution axis.; `obedience-to-blankness-coupling` — both build compliance loops that stop needing the operator to deliver the reward. One contractually couples every obeyed command to increasing blankness, making the state itself the reinforcer; the other transfers reward-generation to the listener while the operator keeps only the framing. Useful to compare when deciding who supplies the reinforcement.; `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both reroute credit for a good feeling onto the operator without the operator producing it. One re-sources the listener's baseline pleasure to the operator's presence; the other has the listener generate the reward while the operator keeps only the framing — the second is close to the first run at loop scale.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both build a self-reinforcing compliance cycle, and the useful distinction is who supplies the fuel: an operator-recited closed formula with an explicit no-ceiling clause, versus a loop whose reward the listener generates while the operator only claims ownership of it. Directly contrastive on the generation question.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — both hand production to the listener, but the thing produced differs: compliance content invented or narrated by the listener, versus the reinforcer of a conditioning loop supplied by the listener while the operator keeps only the framing. Worth cross-reading; not one technique.; `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — both relocate part of a conditioning loop into the subject so it runs without the operator present, and they differ on exactly the point a reader needs: in one the subject genuinely owns the administrator role with autonomy intact, in the other the operator retains the framing and re-credits the subject's self-generated reward to themselves. The second's discriminator already names that contrast.; `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both run operator-absent in daily life on the listener's own signal generation, but one runs on a self-produced reward while the other runs on a self-produced aversive tripwire relieved by correction. Reading the reward and punishment poles of listener-generated enforcement together is genuinely informative.; `self-voiced-avowal` — shares the listener-supplies-the-labor axis, where the listener's own voiced or generated material powers the conditioning loop.; `service-as-self-pleasure` — both make the listener's own body supply the reinforcer rather than the operator, but service-as-self-pleasure rewires whose body feels a sensation while the self-administered loop leaves sensation where it is and merely reattributes authorship of the reward to the operator.


<a id="entry-406"></a>

### self-recited-first-person-mantra

[#406](#entry-406) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

The operator gives first-person lines ('I am so easily hypnotised', 'I obey', 'obedience is arousal') and has them say or think them over and over. Because they are the one saying it, the claim feels self-made, and resisting would mean contradicting themselves mid-sentence; the operator often echoes or praises each line so it feels like agreeing with oneself. Variations: escalating repetitions to burn a line in; a quiet inner mantra paced with the descent; lines alternating 'you' and 'I' without ever saying to repeat; voicing an identity ('this is my obsession') until it feels owned.


**When to reach for this.** The listener is the ACTIVE producer of operator-supplied content - voicing it aloud, sub-vocalizing it, or writing/inscribing it, on a loop - with an operator present who hands or mandates the payload; the self-production re-encodes the content in the listener's own voice and bypasses the defenses external commands trigger. DECODE absorbed: 593 = an enacted overt identity handoff (is-your -> is-my) drilled until the trait registers as descriptive. The load-bearing act is the LISTENER's own vocalization/inscription (remove the listener producing it and the move loses its anchor); the payload's grammatical person is incidental. A permanence payload a chant may carry is adjudicated in permanence-declaration, not here.


**Risk.** Session-scoped self-attributed belief install; reward-gated and escalating variants (two members) deepen commitment but do not on their own erode the refusal channel or reach out of session — parity with the medium carried by internal voice cultivation.


**Why it works.** Saying something in one's own voice, especially with the felt sense of having chosen to, produces attitude change toward the stated position — the induced-compliance and self-perception result that people infer their attitudes from their own observable behaviour, and the saying-is-believing finding that people come to believe messages they themselves produce. Repetition adds a second, independent route: repeated statements are rated as more true regardless of source (the illusory-truth effect), and over time the memory of where the claim came from degrades (source-monitoring error), so operator-supplied content is later recalled as one's own. Falsifiable: predicts weaker adoption when the recitation is obviously coerced (external attribution available) and when source memory is protected or reinstated. [established; self-perception / induced compliance; illusory truth; source-monitoring error]


**Worked examples.**

- *Self-chanted line credited with causing the depth*
  - **Setup.** Early deepening; subject can hold a silent phrase and the operator is narrating rather than asserting depth.
  - **The move.** One line, and you think it to yourself, over and over, silently: I drop so easily. Each time you think it, a wave of heaviness comes down through you — you're the one making it happen, I'm only watching. Keep saying it. There's another one. And another.
  - **Why it lands.** Instead of asserting that the listener is going under, the operator hands them one first-person line about how readily they drop and tells them to chant it silently, adding that each repetition itself produces the wave of heaviness. The listener's own inner voice is now doing the deepening and the operator is only narrating the result. Depth becomes a fact about the listener rather than a claim by the speaker, which means arguing with it would mean contradicting the sentence they are in the middle of saying.
- *Recitation gated behind the wanted reward*
  - **Setup.** At an escalation point where the subject is already straining toward a pleasure the operator controls.
  - **The move.** Before you get any closer, say it, and mean it: I am your obedient toy. Say it like you believe it — because if it comes out flat, nothing else comes at all. Again, properly, and then you can have it.
  - **Why it lands.** At each escalation the operator names a fixed self-labeling line and demands it be said, then attaches a condition: say it convincingly or the pleasure the listener is already straining toward does not arrive. Saying the sentence becomes the price of the thing they want, so agreement to the label is bought with arousal rather than argued for.
- *Inner-voice mantra echoed between count numbers*
  - **Setup.** Slow countdown deepener; subject instructed to think one fixed phrase in the gap after each number.
  - **The move.** Ten. In your own head, in your own voice: obeying is pleasure. [pause] Obeying is pleasure. Nine. Think it. [pause] Obeying is pleasure. Eight. Think it for me. [pause] Obeying is pleasure.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator counts down slowly, and in the gap after each number the listener is told to think one fixed equating phrase in their own mental voice — then the operator immediately speaks that same phrase before moving to the next number. The listener produces the sentence first and hears it confirmed a beat later, which manufactures the sensation of being agreed with by someone else about something they just thought themselves.
- *Repeat-after-me hand-off of first-person lines*
  - **Setup.** End of session, subject still under; content has been asserted in the second person throughout and is now handed back in the first.
  - **The move.** Repeat after me now. I am easily hypnotized. I like being hypnotized. I obey without thinking about it. I will listen again tomorrow. Good girl — those are yours now, in your voice.
  - **Why it lands.** At the end of the session the operator says to repeat after her, then feeds through a short string of first-person declaratives that restate, one by one, the claims she has spent the whole recording asserting in the second person. Nothing new is introduced; the same content simply changes speaker.


**Realizations** (2): `self-authored-repetition-install`, `self-voiced-identity-adoption`


**See also.** `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both end with the listener treating operator content as self-authored, by different routes: a standing rule over the whole future suggestion stream, versus the listener actively voicing supplied lines so authorship is self-attributed by the act. Easy to conflate in practice; the link marks the split.; `compliance-laundered-as-resistance` — both have the listener repeat a fixed first-person line whose voicing does the operative work.; `depth-labor-transfer-leash` — both hand production to the listener so the output cannot be disowned: one transfers the depth-generating labor under operator judgment, the other has the listener voice operator-supplied first-person claims.; `lesson-structure-encoding` — compelled first-person recitation is named as an amplifier of the enumerated lesson set, and the recitation entry treats that same act as the mechanism in its own right. A reader must decide whether the ordered propositions or the listener's own voicing is load-bearing, which requires both entries side by side.; `linked-states-chain` — both end with the listener voicing a first-person claim they were handed, and the forced avowal in one is a specific application of the recitation lever in the other. The difference is that the avowal seals a multi-variable yoke rather than standing as the payload itself — a reader of either should know the other.; `opaque-mantra-unauditable-dedication` — both have the listener utter operator-supplied lines, and the parameter is whether the payload is inspectable. Self-attested belief through first-person recitation versus commitment to a token whose meaning stays with the operator -- a chanted passage needs both entries to be placed.; `ownership-language` — same ownership-identity payload delivered from opposite ends: asserted by the operator as a fact about who the listener now is, versus voiced by the listener so authorship is self-attributed. The choice turns on who speaks the claim.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both hand the listener grammatical work to perform, and the second explicitly names the first-person-only case as its neighbor. Reader adjudicating a recited line needs to check whether the person is rotating through I/we/you (conscription) or held fixed at first person (self-recitation), so the cross-reference does real disambiguation work.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both put a compressed formula in play and can appear in the same passage. The distinguishing question is who produces it: one is an operator-stated closed causal cycle with an explicit no-ceiling clause, the other is the listener actively voicing supplied first-person lines so authorship is self-attributed. A recited loop can be both at once, so the pointer prevents a silent mis-assignment.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — both make the listener the producer, and the boundary is who supplies the words: novel content the listener invents or a control they operate, versus fixed lines handed over to be voiced back. Adjacent enough that the distinction needs to be visible from either entry.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — both relocate authorship of the payload onto the listener, but on opposite sides of a single axis: here the listener performs operator-supplied lines, there the listener genuinely supplies the content from a frame or menu. A reader deciding which to cite needs the other in view to answer 'who actually wrote the words?'; `self-voiced-avowal` — shares the operator-supplied first-person recitation axis, in its fixed identity-declarative mantra form.; `socratic-equivalence-assertion` — both install content through compelled listener recitation, and the divider is the payload shape: free-standing first-person lines versus a forced lexical equivalence between two concepts backed by a leading quiz. That is a real adjudication a reader will face.


<a id="entry-1438"></a>

### self-voiced-avowal

[#1438](#entry-1438) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

Give the listener short first-person lines ('I obey', 'I am so easily hypnotised', 'It's what I deserve') and have them say them in their own voice. Because the words come out of their own mouth, they tend to feel like the listener's own thought rather than an instruction, and later doubt has to argue with something they just said themselves. Some scripts state that repeating the lines locks them in. Variations: aloud; whispered or silent; written out as lines; first-person passages narrated as if the listener were already saying them; the operator echoing the line back; saying the line to unlock a wanted pleasure.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the load-bearing move is transferring authorship of a claim into the listener's own voice. The tell is a scripted first-person utterance the listener produces under operator direction — spoken, subvocal, or written — typically flagged by "repeat after me," a chant or lines-writing instruction, or a first-person block delivered as the listener's own speech. The claim's content varies freely; what is constant is that the listener ends up the speaker of it.


**Worked examples.**

- *Arousal words asserted to cause arousal*
  - **Setup.** Arousal established and the subject is speaking aloud on cue; you are naming the mechanism as you install it.
  - **The move.** The word is hungry. Not the idea of it — the word itself, in your mouth. Say it: hungry. Feel that? That's the word doing it, and it gets worse the more you say it. Next time you listen you won't even decide to — it'll just fall out of you, and each one will pull the next one out after it.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator names a word, then states that the word itself — not the idea, the word — drives the arousal up, and demonstrates by saying it. Later the loop is exported: at the next session these words will start falling out of the listener's mouth on their own. Once the listener's own speech is a trigger for the state that produces more of that speech, the circuit runs with nobody at the controls, and the operator is no longer the bottleneck on how far it escalates.
- *Cross-seam — label spoken in a believed-waking state, then re-inducted*
  - **Setup.** Subject has been brought up to what they believe is full waking, mid-conversation, before a second induction.
  - **The move.** Before we go again — say it once, out loud, in your own voice, wide awake so you can hear yourself do it. 'I am an obedient thing.' Good. Now that you've heard yourself say it awake, sleep.
  - **Why it lands.** Speaking the claim in a state the subject believes is their ordinary waking self makes it un-attributable to trance, and re-inducting immediately denies any window to reconsider it. Observable in the drop in volume and the slight delay before speaking — the reluctance is the ownership handoff registering.
- *First-person recitation of the legitimizing judgment*
  - **Setup.** After a corrective or degrading beat that the subject accepted without protest.
  - **The move.** Say it back to me. 'It's what I deserve.' Again, slower. Once more, and mean it this time.
  - **Why it lands.** Routing the value-judgment rather than the label through the subject's voice supplies the legitimacy that makes the identity claim defensible from the inside; later resistance has to argue with the subject's own recent words. Observable in the third repetition losing its flatness and picking up affect.
- *Escalating avowal blocks that invalidate each other on retreat*
  - **Setup.** Late session; a sequence of first-person statements is being built, each a step past the last.
  - **The move.** Repeat after me, each one all the way through. 'I like being told what to do.' Now: 'I need to be told what to do.' Now: 'I'm no good at deciding anything for myself.' Good — and you meant the first two, so you meant that one.
  - **Why it lands.** Each block is a small step from the accepted one before it, and the closing line ties them together so backing out of the last requires disowning the first — a retreat cost the subject pays in their own voice. Observable in the hesitation appearing at block three and then resolving, which is the interlock closing.
- *repeat-after-me ownership transfer*
  - Now repeat after me. I am intensely sexually vulnerable to [the operator's name].


**Realizations** (2): `self-authored-identity-claim`, `self-perpetuating-loop`


**See also.** `arousal-adjacency-stamping` — both wire arousal into the suggestion economy, but one uses a live arousal state as the carrier that makes separate content stick, while the other closes arousal onto itself so the listener's own utterances re-cause the state with no content payload at all.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — shares the performed-act-as-self-evidence axis, where doing or saying something in-session is read back as proof the state is already true.; `category-as-self-firing-cue` — both build an operator-free self-firing circuit, one where the listener's own utterances re-cause the state and one where an entire mental category becomes the cue. A reader choosing between token-level loop and category-level cue is served by both entries.; `closed-autonomous-conditioning-loop` — downgraded from merge. The second is the general closed self-running loop where every resistance vector feeds it; the first is one narrow vehicle in which the listener's own spoken arousal words are asserted to cause the state, plus a forward-installed automatic vocalization. The specific vehicle and the mindlessness move that suppresses the disbelief reflex are not implied by the general entry, so this is a species link rather than a duplicate.; `closed-loop-operator-binding` — both install self-sustaining circuits that need no further operator input, but the self-perpetuating loop closes on the listener's own vocalizations amplifying arousal (word to state to more words), while closed-loop operator binding routes the response back onto the operator-as-cue-source, so future contact or ordinary arousal re-summons the operator.; `compounding-dependency-loop` — both are closed self-amplifying circuits and the tell separating them is worth the link: one loops inside the session, where the listener's own utterances re-cause the state, while the other loops across sessions, where the only relief route for a raised waking baseline is more of the same material. Same topology, different span.; `deictic-self-rule-overextension` — both route the claim through the listener's own authorship; one seats an identity noun, the other re-scopes a true local fact into an always-everywhere rule. Readers choosing between self-authored payload types need both in view.; `identity-from-coerced-behavior` — both make an identity claim hard to repudiate by relocating its apparent source away from the operator: one sources it from already-compelled observable behavior, the other routes it through the listener's own voice. Adjacent design choices for the same problem.; `intrinsic-self-reframe` — two routes to making an identity claim unrejectable by removing the external author. One hands the listener the grammatical subject so they speak the claim; the other reframes the content as always having been intrinsic so there was never anything imposed. Adjacent enough that a reader choosing one benefits from seeing the other route.; `multi-modal-trigger` — pass B cited a low TRIG-14 pull but do_not_merge'd it; kept distinct as a self-feeding loop.; `object-ritual-loop` — both are closed self-sustaining loops whose payload is perpetuation rather than any single response, and the useful contrast is loop scope: one closes inside the session on the listener's own vocalizations, the other threads through daily life via an environmental cue, an acquisition step, and a return to the recording. The shared self-feeding topology is a real structural relationship, not just shared vocabulary.; `operator-absent-self-renewal-loop` — both build loops that run without the operator, but one closes the circuit inside a single session (spoken arousal-words causing the arousal that produces more words) while the other closes it across sessions by making the urge to re-expose one of the reinforced installs.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both move an identity claim into the listener's own grammatical position, and the discriminators need each other to hold the line: one cycles a single predicate through multiple persons so no neutral stance exists, the other hands the claim to the listener as speaker so there is no external author to reject. Adjacent, not identical.; `pronoun-migration-identity-install` — both install identity while dodging a direct operator assertion, and their discriminators already reference each other. A reader deciding between them needs the axis: covert grammatical drift that moves the referent onto the listener versus an explicit ownership handoff where the listener speaks the claim.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — both build a closed self-amplifying circuit with no ceiling, but the vehicles differ enough to keep them apart: one makes the listener's own vocalizations the loop's carrier and forward-installs automatic speech, the other recites the loop as a compressed verbal formula. A reader picking between them benefits from seeing the contrast in what closes the circuit.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — shares the listener-supplies-the-labor axis, where the listener's own voiced or generated material powers the conditioning loop.; `self-authored-compliance-content` — same ownership-handoff lever with different payload classes: novel compliance content the listener generates, versus an identity claim or its legitimizing judgment spoken in the listener's own voice. The payload class is the taxonomy's working boundary in this family, so they stay separate but must cross-reference.; `self-authored-construct-leverage` — genus and species. The second is the general lever (authorship of the payload is relocated to the listener so there is no external author to reject); the first is the identity-claim species, where what the listener speaks is the label or its legitimizing judgment. A reader who reaches the general entry needs the identity-claim variant, and vice versa. Not a merge: the general entry also covers non-identity payloads.; `self-generated-failure-as-identity-proof` — both route an identity claim through the listener rather than the operator, but one requires an enacted failure as evidence and the other requires only spoken authorship of the claim. The boundary is worth showing: enacted proof versus ownership handoff.; `self-recited-first-person-mantra` — shares the operator-supplied first-person recitation axis, in its fixed identity-declarative mantra form.; `self-selected-category-slotting` — a tight, deliberate pair: the same identity content lands either because the listener speaks the claim aloud or because the listener privately assigns an unassigned category to themselves. Each discriminator already names the other, and the spoken-versus-silent split is exactly the choice a writer faces.; `socratic-equivalence-assertion` — both get their force from routing the claim through the listener's own voice so there is no external author to reject, and both are stickier than the same content asserted by the operator. One hands over an identity claim; the other forces an asserted equivalence between two concepts that diverge in ordinary usage. Same ownership handoff, different payload.; `third-person-proxy-normalization` — both are grammatical-person moves on identity content and each already names the other's neighbourhood: one hands authorship of the claim to the listener, the other launders a claim by shifting it into detached third person. A reader adjudicating a person-shift passage genuinely needs to see both options.


<a id="entry-159"></a>

### subject-voiced-self-mantra

[#159](#entry-159) · [Back to self-spoken-conditioning](#genus-140) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

The entire artifact is voiced in the first person from inside the desired endpoint, with no external operator addressing the listener — the text IS the self-talk the listener is to speak, mouth along with, or subvocalize. Because the voice already speaks from the already-altered self ("I'm an ecstasy slut", "I suck till I'm stupid"), identity-claims arrive pre-accepted rather than as suggestions to negotiate; the "is this me or them?" check is short-circuited because the listener is both speaker and target. The load-bearing event is the voicing, not the hearing; refusal collapses to "stop identifying / stop saying it," and there is no operator-says / listener-experiences loop to resist.


**When to reach for this.** First-person throughout with the LISTENER as the speaker and no operator surface at all.


**Risk.** Installs identity-claims as pre-accepted autobiography (e.g. "I used to be a feminist, but now I don't think") — a self-description rewrite; session-scoped and requires the listener to lend their voice, so medium not high.


**Why it works.** Saying something yourself, in your own voice, is a stronger route to endorsing it than hearing it said — the generation effect and self-referential encoding both favour self-produced first-person content, and self-persuasion research finds that arguments one utters shift attitudes more than arguments one receives. It also removes the source cue that would let the listener attribute the claim to an outside party and discount it. Falsifiable: identity-claim endorsement should be measurably higher for spoken/subvocalised delivery than for merely listening to the same text. [established; generation effect; self-persuasion; self-referential encoding]


**Worked examples.**

- *Whole track spoken in the listener's I*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a text the subject reads or speaks aloud themselves; no operator voice appears anywhere.
  - **The move.** I am soft and slow and easy to move. I do what I am told and I like it. My head is quiet and warm and I am not going to fill it back up.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no operator anywhere in the text. Every line is first-person and present-tense, spoken from inside the finished state — not "you will feel" but "I feel," not "you are becoming" but "I am." Nothing is proposed, so there is nothing to accept or decline; the only two things a listener can do with the track are mouth along with it or stop it. The usual check — is this me talking or them? — has no seam to catch on, because the listener is simultaneously the speaker and the target.
- *First line licenses the before/after swap*
  - **Setup.** Very first line of a subject-voiced piece; establishes the before/after account.
  - **The move.** I used to be someone who argued. I'm not anymore. I'm the girl who says yes before she's finished hearing the question, and I have been for a while now.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening line is autobiography rather than instruction: I used to be one thing, and now I am not. Naming the discarded former self does the licensing work — everything stacked after it arrives as an account of a change that has already happened, not as a change being requested. Self-descriptions the listener would argue with as suggestions pass unchallenged as memories.
- *Narrated from inside an already-taken head*
  - **Setup.** First-person narration from inside an already-conditioned state; mid-passage.
  - **The move.** I can feel where the thoughts used to be. There's just warm space there now, and I like it better. When she tells me to kneel I'm already down before I've worked out why, and working it out afterward is more effort than it's worth, so I don't.
  - **Why it lands.** The story is told in the first person by someone already under, and the character does nearly all the work on themselves: the narration keeps explaining, from inside, why the mind has gone quiet, why complying feels good, why pushing back would be pointless. A listener lending their inner voice to a line about wanting to be told what to do has endorsed it in the act of reading it — there is no separate moment at which acceptance gets decided.


**See also.** `description-as-installation-register` — two poles of grammatical-person register as the install vehicle: the listener speaking the endpoint in first person with no operator surface, versus the operator describing the listener in third person and never issuing a second-person command. Both remove the command-evaluation interface by manipulating who is addressed.; `pronoun-braid-conscription` — both use first-person; braid rotates persons, mantra does not.; `scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier` — shares the first-person already-converted narrator voice as a delivery vehicle for pre-accepted identity content.; `self-reference-erasure` — both operate on the first-person position rather than on content, in opposite directions: one has the listener occupy it as the speaker of an already-altered self, the other removes or replaces the self-reference handle so there is no seat to assert from. A passage mandating self-directed speech can trip either, so the contrast is load-bearing.; `third-person-surrogate-frame` — grammatical-person opposites that already cite each other as contrast cases: one puts the listener in the speaker seat, the other makes the listener the described third party. Useful as a paired decision, since both remove the operator-addresses-you frame by opposite routes.


<a id="genus-235"></a>

## self-sustaining-contingencies (3)

Make the behavior keep itself running after the operator steps back, via precommitted stakes, self-administered rewards and records, or handoff to consequences the environment already pays.

[natural-contingency-handoff](#entry-530) · [precommitment-rule-governed-stakes](#entry-424) · [self-management-self-administered-contingency](#entry-433)


<a id="entry-530"></a>

### natural-contingency-handoff

[#530](#entry-530) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: transfer*

Get a trained behavior to the point where ordinary life keeps rewarding it, then step back. Variations: prompt the behavior in the real setting just often enough for it to meet the rewards already there, then withdraw help; or keep practicing past mere correctness until it is fast and smooth enough for real-world demands, since a correct but slow response never gets rewarded and fades.


**When to reach for this.** The operator supplies no content and retires once natural reinforcement takes over — unlike moves that deliver operator content at the trance/waking threshold, schedule practice for state re-access, or sustain compliance for depth. Presupposes a target already screened by a standing-contingency maintainability filter; the deficit fixed is a CONTACT-frequency deficit (drive exposures) or a FLUENCY deficit (train measured dimensions to threshold), not broadened cues.


**Risk.** Durable out-of-session maintenance by the natural environment is the point; bounded, no channel erosion (two members).


**Why it works.** Responses persist only while something reinforces them, so operator-supplied reinforcement guarantees extinction on withdrawal unless the response has contacted a reinforcer that is already present in the setting. Fluency matters because natural contingencies impose timing and quality thresholds — a correct-but-slow response fails to produce the reinforcer and therefore extinguishes exactly like an incorrect one. Falsifiable: withdrawing support before the response has contacted natural reinforcement, or before it meets the setting's rate criterion, should produce reliable decay relative to matched cases where contact and fluency were achieved. [established; behavioral trapping / natural contingencies of reinforcement; extinction on schedule withdrawal; fluency thresholds]


**Worked examples.**

- *Bridge to first contact, then fade*
  - "consists of getting the learner to emit the behavior in the generalization setting just often enough to contact the contingency." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Train to fluency or it extinguishes*
  - "Behavior changes that seem to need generalization may only need better teaching. Try making the students fluent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `generative-substrate-training` — shares the fluency lever — pushing performance past bare accuracy so downstream behavior appears or maintains without further operator support.


<a id="entry-424"></a>

### precommitment-rule-governed-stakes

[#424](#entry-424) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

While temptation is still far off and easy to resist, you arrange things so your later self can't easily back out: remove the option, or attach a cost to giving in. This is precommitment; it works because people discount distant rewards, so choices made early are less pulled by the quick payoff. Variations: an irreversible act in advance (locking away the cigarettes, Odysseus tied to the mast); a fixed penalty paid to a friend on any day you fail, held by someone trustworthy so it can't be waived; a delayed, unpleasant stake, such as money going to a cause you despise if you break the limit.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for PRECOMMITMENT / RULE-GOVERNED STAKES when you want to control a LATER behavior by binding the future self NOW — an irreversible act or a pre-set non-waivable stake set before temptation peaks, working across a delay. Choose it over: self-instruction/self-cueing (which supplies an antecedent that EVOKES the next response — precommitment FORECLOSES or penalizes the choice, foreclosure vs evocation being the structural line); self-administered contingency (which relocates the ongoing measurement-consequence ADMINISTRATOR role into the subject — precommitment arranges ONE future contingency, not an ongoing loop); an in-the-moment refusal / willpower act (precommitment is a separate act done in advance on the contingency structure). Facets differ by irreversible-act vs external-stakeholder-penalty vs delayed-aversive-stake.


**Risk.** Deliberately forecloses the future self's option to defect or withdraw, with out-of-session, costly-to-reverse reach — applied to another person this erodes the later refusal channel.


**Why it works.** People discount delayed outcomes steeply and, for many, hyperbolically, so the relative value of a smaller-sooner reward and a larger-later one reverses as the sooner one approaches — which is why a preference formed at distance predictably fails at close range. Acting on the contingency during the low-temptation window exploits that reversal: the choice is made while the larger-later outcome still dominates, and the act removes or prices the later defection. A third party holding the stake matters because self-imposed penalties are otherwise waivable by the same self that will want to waive them. Falsifiable: predicts commitment devices only help where preference reversal actually occurs, and that self-held, waivable stakes underperform externally held ones. [established; hyperbolic/delay discounting and preference reversal; commitment devices]


**Worked examples.**

- *Bind the future self while temptation is distant*
  - "Since the smoker is just about to have a cigarette, the value of a future cigarette is negligible, making it easy to shut the case" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (2): `rule-governed-delayed-stakes`, `self-imposed-penalty-commitment`


**See also.** `prospective-resistance-foreclosure` — both bind the later self during an earlier window, and the contrast is exactly the foreclosure-versus-evocation line one of them already draws. One pre-assigns a null or aversive outcome to a whole future class of mental acts so the later comparator is deleted; the other restructures a real contingency -- an irreversible act or a non-waivable stake -- so the later self cannot cheaply defect. Deleting the ability to evaluate versus removing the ability to choose.; `rehearsed-pre-commitment` — both bind a future self by acting upstream of the moment of execution. One does it with an irreversible act or non-waivable stake that forecloses the later choice; the other by obtaining genuine consent and rehearsal while judgment is intact. Foreclosure versus pre-made decision.; `rule-governed-behavior-install` — both put a contingency into words in advance rather than letting experience shape behavior, but precommitment sets a non-waivable stake or irreversible act that forecloses the later choice, whereas rule-governed install merely states the contingency so a rule-following repertoire produces the behavior from the description.


<a id="entry-433"></a>

### self-management-self-administered-contingency
