[#433](#entry-433) · [Back to self-sustaining-contingencies](#genus-235) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: contingency-engineering*

The tracking, and often the rewards, are moved into the person themselves, because they are the only one present everywhere, including private thoughts and places no one else can watch. Simply recording one's own behaviour often changes it. It only works if their self-record is honest. Variations: recording at the moment it happens, such as a tally or a chart on the mirror; checking their record against an outside observer's and rewarding accuracy, then fading the check; doing something earlier, while temptation is weak, that changes what they'll do later; scoring their own work against an answer key and giving themselves the consequence.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for SELF-MANAGEMENT / SELF-ADMINISTERED CONTINGENCY when the CONTINGENCY-ADMINISTRATOR role (measure, and consequate or just observe) relocates into the subject, running as an ongoing loop the subject drives. Choose it over: precommitment / rule-governed stakes (which arranges ONE future contingency / binds the future self by a stake — this transfers the ongoing administrator role); self-instruction/self-cueing (which relocates the ANTECEDENT/cue, not the measurement-consequence loop); operator-outsourced conditioning loop (where the operator OWNS the framing and reattributes the subject's self-generated reward to themselves — here the subject genuinely self-administers, autonomy intact). Facets span reactivity-only (observe/record, no consequence) through full self-contract; the accuracy-matching variant trains correct self-observation rather than the behavior itself.


**Risk.** Durable out-of-session self-management capacity; the removed external delivery check is an integrity surface, not a consent surface. Builds independence, reversible.


**Why it works.** Two separable effects. First, self-monitoring alone changes behaviour by reactivity: measuring a behaviour makes it salient and evaluable against a standard, and rates shift even with no consequence attached — the effect is real but typically modest and decays as monitoring lapses. Second, self-delivered consequences work to the extent the self-report is accurate, which is why accuracy-matching against an independent observer is trained separately; the honest-self-monitoring premise is the weak joint, not an incidental caveat. Falsifiable: predicts self-management effects shrink as recording accuracy degrades, and that reactivity-only interventions fade faster than externally verified ones. [plausible; self-monitoring reactivity; self-regulation via standards; accuracy-matching contingencies]


**Worked examples.**

- *The subject holds all four contingency roles*
  - "A self-contract is a contingency contract that an individual makes with herself, incorporating a self-selected task and reward as well as self-monitoring of task completion and self-delivery of the reward." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *The self is the one agent present everywhere*
  - "What behavior change agent can go with the student to every necessary lesson, at all times…? The student's own 'self' can always meet these specifications" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Reinforce accurate self-recording, not the behavior*
  - "Brian was taught to monitor his own behavior and to match his self-recordings to the recordings of his teachers. Accurate self-recording resulted in teacher praise" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Score your own work and deliver your own consequence*
  - "students who have been taught to evaluate their own performance and provide their own feedback in the form of self-delivered rewards and error correction… are not dependent on the teacher's direction" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (4): `self-managed-contingency`, `self-monitoring-reactivity`, `self-recording`, `two-response-self-management-split`


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — process and end-state: the gradual handover of task, standard, monitoring and delivery from operator to subject terminates in exactly the self-run contingency loop the other entry describes. Not a merge - one names the fading schedule applied to authorship, the other the standing arrangement once the handover is complete.; `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — one is a deployable arrangement, the other the design constraints governing any such arrangement, including whether a self-delivered consequence has a sharp enough onset to function as one. The reference entry is explicitly the substrate the deployable moves sit on, so the link runs in a genuinely useful direction.; `operator-absent-self-policing` — both relocate the enforcement role into the subject so control persists with no external agent present, and the contrast is sharp and instructive: one is an autonomy-intact self-run loop the subject owns, the other a self-surveillance and forfeiture contract serving the operator. The pairing is the clearest way to teach that boundary.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — both relocate part of a conditioning loop into the subject so it runs without the operator present, and they differ on exactly the point a reader needs: in one the subject genuinely owns the administrator role with autonomy intact, in the other the operator retains the framing and re-credits the subject's self-generated reward to themselves. The second's discriminator already names that contrast.; `self-administered-contingency` — self-management genus for the same relocated-administrator arrangement, spanning reactivity-only observation through the full self-contract.; `self-contract` — the Self-Contract recipe was extracted from this entry; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — complementary halves of relocating behavioral control into the subject: one moves the measurement-and-consequence loop inside, the other moves the antecedent cue inside. Each is defined partly by not being the other, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.


<a id="genus-298"></a>

## session-environment-safeguards (2)

Rules about where the session may run and who may speak around a deep subject, so the setting can't inject hazards or counter-suggestions.

[context-gate](#entry-570) · [suggestion-field-hygiene](#entry-582)


<a id="entry-570"></a>

### context-gate

[#570](#entry-570) · [Back to session-environment-safeguards](#genus-298) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A firm, unambiguous pre-induction requirement that the session only be consumed in a safe, distraction-free context — not while driving, not while operating machinery, undisturbed and able to fully release attention. The constraint runs on whether the material may be used at all in the listener's current situation, stated before induction begins.


**When to reach for this.** Gates WHETHER the session may run given the listening context, constraining use — it does not select among live trained relations, does not police bystanders mid-state (suggestion-field-hygiene), and does not weaponize staging toward a payload (context-lock-staging, weaponized-safety-framing).


**Risk.** Purely protective constraint: gating effects to an agreed context limits scope rather than extending it; residual risk lives in the gated payload, not the gate.


**Why it works.** Hypnotic and deep-relaxation material deliberately narrows attention and reduces monitoring of the external environment, which directly degrades the vigilance and reaction-time demands of driving or machine operation — the risk is not exotic, it is ordinary divided-attention failure. Stating the constraint before induction matters because instructions given after attentional narrowing begins are less likely to be encoded and acted on; the pre-induction slot is when the listener still has full executive control to change context. Falsifiable: if listeners given the gate before induction comply at the same rate as those given it mid-session, or if attention-demanding secondary-task performance does not degrade during the session, the rationale fails. [established; attentional narrowing and divided-attention decrement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-induction use-gate stated before the first deepening line*
  - **Setup.** The opening seconds of a recording or session, before any induction language has been spoken.
  - **The move.** Before we begin: do not listen to this while driving, while operating machinery, or while doing anything that needs your attention. Find somewhere you can sit or lie down undisturbed for the next half hour, put your phone on silent, and only start this when you can let your attention go completely. If that is not now, stop here and come back later.
  - **Why it lands.** It constrains whether the material may run at all rather than steering anything inside the session, so a listener in an unsafe context is filtered out before absorption removes their ability to self-assess. The operator can observe compliance indirectly: subjects who honour the gate arrive settled, and reported mid-session interruptions drop.


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `suitability-screening` — complementary pre-induction gates that block the session on different axes. One rules on whether the listening situation is safe enough to proceed; the other rules on whether this person should be worked with at all. Both narrow the operator's license rather than pushing a state, and both commonly appear in the same opening.; `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — one is a plain pre-induction constraint on whether the session may run at all; the other bounds a trigger on a trust condition with a self-validating rider. The second explicitly defines itself against the first, so the link carries the distinction between a real safety rail and a loyalty hook wearing one.


<a id="entry-582"></a>

### suggestion-field-hygiene

[#582](#entry-582) · [Back to session-environment-safeguards](#genus-298) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Because a deep subject hears and registers everything said in the room as an active suggestion, the operator manages the whole acoustic/information field — issuing operational rules to surrounding staff, training them by having them serve as subjects, silencing untrained guests — so no stray fear or doubt voiced in earshot can act as a counter-suggestion and collapse the accumulated state. The room, not just the operator, sustains the state.


**When to reach for this.** An environmental-control directive aimed at BYSTANDERS to protect an achieved state — not reassurance addressed to the subject, not a pre-session listening-context requirement on the subject (context-gate), and a state-protection move, not a state-production one.


**Risk.** Protective maintenance of an existing consented state; constrains bystanders, not the subject.


**Why it works.** Expectancy is one of the better-supported determinants of hypnotic responding, and expectancy is set by whatever information reaches the subject — including remarks not addressed to them. A doubt or fear voiced in earshot is a credible negative expectancy cue, credible precisely because it appears unstaged and comes from a bystander with no apparent motive to influence, which is what makes overheard information persuasive. Managing the whole room rather than only the operator's own speech follows directly. Falsifiable: if overheard sceptical remarks produce no measurable drop in responsiveness relative to a silent-room control, the rationale is wrong. [plausible; expectancy effects on hypnotic response; persuasiveness of overheard information]


**Worked examples.**

- *Every utterance in earshot counts as suggestion*
  - "if fears are generated in any manner—by unfortunate remarks made by nurses, assistants or other doctors … the Esdaile state will be lost. Remember that your patients hear and understand everything" — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy


**See also.** `disconfirmation-suppression` — both protect an already-running state by managing what the subject can hear rather than by producing the state. One is standing environmental hygiene aimed at bystanders; the other is a discrete instruction that blocks one present fact from reaching the subject. Read as the ambient and the acute form of the same guard.


<a id="genus-167"></a>

## sideline-the-waking-mind (4)

Split the mind in two and address only the deeper half, so the waking evaluator can't inspect, refuse, or disconfirm what lands.

[audience-split-bypass](#entry-255) · [forbidden-attention-authority-test](#entry-701) · [reality-test-insulation](#entry-244) · [split-self-unfalsifiability](#entry-1090)


<a id="entry-255"></a>

### audience-split-bypass

[#255](#entry-255) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: critical-faculty-softening*

Divide the listener into a conscious and a subconscious mind, then send the conscious one off duty: 'this isn't for your waking mind, you don't need to listen, your subconscious hears it anyway.' Or call the sceptical part 'just the conscious mind' and say the deeper self has already agreed. Any objection then comes from the wrong part and can be ignored, and because the split is declared up front it also takes care of future doubts. Variations: address material explicitly 'to your subconscious'; add a disclaimer such as 'this won't put you in trance now' for deniability.


**When to reach for this.** vs resistance-fold: fold converts an exercised impulse; here the impulse is DISMISSED as out-of-scope. vs resistance-quarantine-partition: quarantine reifies and demotes a named faculty (standing structural demotion); here the split is an epistemic audience assignment — the conscious mind still functions, it is just told this content is not addressed to it. Tell: an explicit ignore-task / wrong-audience assignment presupposing folk dualism, delivered pre-emptively.


**Risk.** Session-scoped critical-faculty lowering via a framing move; reversible, no durable scope.


**Why it works.** Assigning the critical faculty an ignore-task works by licensing low elaboration: people scrutinise a message far less when they believe it is not addressed to them or not consequential for them, and low-elaboration processing leans on peripheral cues rather than argument quality. Pre-emptively labelling any future objection as the wrong speaker also inoculates against counterarguing by giving it a dismissive category before it arises. Falsifiable: if listeners told 'this is not for your conscious mind' generated as many spontaneous counterarguments, and shifted attitude no more, than listeners given the same content addressed directly to them, the mechanism would fail. [plausible; elaboration likelihood / personal relevance and counterarguing]


**Worked examples.**

- *The waking mind assigned an ignore-task*
  - **Setup.** The first sentence of the recording, before any induction; the addressee is named before the subject can settle.
  - **The move.** This isn't for you. This is addressed to the part of you underneath, and it will hear every word whether you attend or not. So — the thinking part, the one following this sentence: your job for the next twenty minutes is to pay no attention to any of it. You have no say in what's happening here. Ignore it. It isn't yours.
  - **Why it lands.** The first sentence states who the recording is addressed to, and it is not the listener as they usually experience themselves. The thinking part is not argued with or talked down; it is given a task — pay no attention to any of this — and told repeatedly that it has no say in the matter. Evaluation therefore stops not because the listener was persuaded but because evaluating has been reclassified as somebody else's job. Any objection it raises afterwards is background noise it was already instructed to disregard.
- *Resistance pre-attributed to the unrepresentative layer*
  - **Setup.** Early, before the subject has assembled any objection; the split is asserted pre-emptively.
  - **The move.** There's the front of you and there's the rest of you, and only one of them is in charge tonight. The front can grumble all it likes — file its objections, sure. Underneath, you already want this and you're already letting it through. So whatever comes up in the next hour, that's just the front talking, and the front doesn't get to answer for you.
  - **Why it lands.** The split is asserted early, well before the listener has assembled anything to push back with. The surface layer may object all it likes; the layer underneath is declared to want this already and to be letting it through regardless. There is consequently no move available that would register as successful resistance — objecting is simply the wrong agent speaking.
- *Drifting off reframed as the better channel*
  - **Setup.** Mid-induction, dropped in as a single sentence at the point where attention typically starts to wander.
  - **The move.** And if you drift off and stop following my voice — good. That's not you failing at this. The part that's actually taking this in doesn't need you listening, and it does its best work when you've wandered off. So let your attention go where it likes.
  - **Why it lands.** One sentence, dropped in mid-induction, closes the most ordinary escape route there is. If the listener's attention wanders — which it will — that is pre-declared to be fine, because the part that matters is still listening and still taking it in. Drifting stops being a failure of the session and becomes a deeper route into it.
- *Bypass named as the reason for the split*
  - **Setup.** Opening of a file with no induction at all; the bypass is named as architecture rather than tactic.
  - **The move.** There's no induction on this one. The conscious mind is dismissed — go and do something else, read your emails, get bored, I genuinely don't mind. It's going in regardless, because it isn't being said to you. The you that's listening isn't the one being addressed, so there's nothing here for you to agree to or turn down.
  - **Why it lands.** The conscious mind is explicitly released — no need to follow this, go do something else, get bored if you like — while the operator asserts the material is landing anyway. The bypass is stated as architecture rather than as a tactic, and because on this framing the listener as they experience themselves is not the one addressed, there is nothing for them to decline. There is no induction in the file at all; this frame does the work one would have done.


**Realizations** (1): `conscious-subconscious-audience-split`


**See also.** `antagonist-split-resistance-routing` — both partition the listener into two selves and use the split to disarm objection, and both already contrast against the same resistance-quarantine neighbor. One routes the listener's own felt resistance onto a losing self; the other declares the objecting layer the wrong audience. Close enough that a reader choosing between them benefits from the pointer.; `channel-partitioned-monitoring` — both partition the listener to place content beyond monitoring, but the audience split is an asserted conscious/subconscious addressing rule that dismisses objections as out-of-scope, while channel partitioning routes output across actual representational modalities so no level owns it.; `faculty-preserving-scope-restriction` — both leave the evaluating faculty running while removing its purchase, one by narrowing what it may range over and the other by declaring the content not addressed to it. Very easy to conflate, since both let the listener feel they are still thinking freely; the pointer helps make the call.; `observer-responder-split` — both partition the listener, but the payload differs: one assigns the evaluating faculty an ignore-task so objections are out of scope, the other preserves awareness precisely so the felt loss of volition is convincing. Useful contrast because the partition surface looks identical in text.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — both install a conscious/subconscious partition and then use it to move something off the listener: in one case the objecting faculty is declared the wrong audience, in the other the authorship of agreement is assigned to the not-self side. Same structural device, two different things relocated.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — both run on the same folk two-minds premise and are separated by what is done with the split: one reassigns authorship of behavior to the listener's own internal layer so ownership resistance never engages, the other assigns the critical faculty an ignore-task so any objection is pre-classified as the wrong audience. A reader meeting a subconscious-addressing script needs the pair.; `thinking-triggers-blank` — already cross-referenced in both discriminators and the pointer should stay: A relocates the evaluating faculty out of scope by assigning it an ignore-task, B claims the faculty removed outright. Same target, different disposal, and the pair is easy to confuse in text.


<a id="entry-701"></a>

### forbidden-attention-authority-test

[#701](#entry-701) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure*

The operator describes a vivid emergency that would normally grab attention, such as the room catching fire, then tells the listener to ignore it and keep listening. When they stay put, the operator calls that proof that the listener's alarm system now answers to him. The fire is never resolved as a scene; it exists only to be obeyed past. Afterward the operator suggests the senses 'switch off', presented as a result of the authority just shown.


**When to reach for this.** Not literal fear-play/content: the tell is the threat's function as an authority test over safety-signaling, not as a scene. This overrides the safety-orientation exit — a reachability/authority-topology move.


**Risk.** Trains the listener to override their own safety-signaling on operator instruction — directly erodes the safety/verification channel; must ship inside a host with entry/exit/aftercare. Extractor-disputed on the fire's exact function but all readings route through operator-authority-over-safety.


**Why it works.** Graduated compliance is the likely mechanism: following a small instruction makes a larger later one more likely, through commitment and the person coming to see themselves as cooperative. The obedience research supports step-by-step escalation, but not the stronger idea that the bigger the impulse overridden, the more authority is handed over; there is no evidence for that. This could be tested: if following an instruction that competes for attention produced no more later acceptance than following a neutral instruction, the escalation account fails. Whether this actually weakens a person's real sense of danger, as opposed to being play-acted inside a frame they have accepted, is not known, and that uncertainty is why it is treated as risky.


**Worked examples.**

- *Ignoring the staged emergency as proof of authority*
  - **Setup.** Deep trance, subject fully absorbed and responsive; a vivid emergency is staged purely to be disregarded and is never resolved.
  - **The move.** Look at the room. The curtains have caught — it's up the wall behind you already, the heat is on the back of your neck, the smoke is coming across the ceiling toward you.

The part of you that's listening to me: ignore it. Don't turn, don't check, don't move. Stay with my voice. [pause] There. You didn't move. Something was burning and the part of you that decides what's dangerous waited to hear it from me instead. It doesn't answer to you any more. And now the hearing goes, and the touch goes, one at a time — there's nothing left in you that needs to be on watch.
  - **Why it lands.** Deep in, the operator has the listener picture the room going up in flames around them — close, real, unmistakably an emergency — and then instructs the part of them that is listening to pay it no attention and carry on. There is no task to perform and no response to produce; the whole point is what does not happen. Because the listener is still there, still following the voice while something that should have overridden everything is burning nearby, the conclusion is offered that the deeper mind has handed over its authority to decide what counts as danger. The fire is then dropped and never mentioned again — it was only ever a test, and the senses are described as switching off one by one now that nothing is left to guard them.


**See also.** `arousal-isolated-obedience-test` — two authority tests that differ in what the proof is made of: a staged threat whose being-ignored demonstrates ceded safety-signaling, versus a hard stop on a high-arousal action that isolates obedience from the arousal carrying it. Both are proof beats without a commanded ordinary response, so a reader picking a test benefits from the pair.; `manufactured-jeopardy-rescue` — both stage a threat that is never resolved, but the exits differ: in one, ignoring the threat is the proof of ceded safety-signaling authority; in the other, obeying is framed as the only escape from a danger the operator secretly authors. Ignore-as-proof versus obey-as-rescue is the cut a reader needs, and staging a fake danger to test authority is close enough that the pointer pays.


<a id="entry-244"></a>

### reality-test-insulation

[#244](#entry-244) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: concealment*

Splits a normal-functioning surface from a hidden deep 'ownership' so the conditioning becomes uncheckable against external feedback. The listener is told they are 'perfectly free to live your life normally' while also 'in my control 24 hours a day, 7 days a week,' with the contradiction left unaddressed and ownership placed 'deep in the recesses of your mind' beneath unchanged surface behavior — friends, partners, therapists see nothing, disabling resistance-by-comparison-to-baseline and preemptively removing the usual collapse trigger (conflict between trance-instructions and waking life).


**When to reach for this.** An explicit surface/depth partition installed specifically to insulate the conditioning from reality-testing. Tell is the partition, not comfort — separates from routine trance-safety reassurance.


**Risk.** Erodes the subject's own reality-testing / refusal channel by design (removes the baseline-comparison check that would prompt disengagement); high per the channel-erosion clause.


**Why it works.** Conditioning normally decays when it conflicts with everyday feedback; specifying that surface behaviour stays unchanged removes the comparison test that would generate that conflict, and also removes third parties (friends, partners, clinicians) as sources of corrective information. The unaddressed contradiction between 'free' and 'controlled' survives because the two claims are indexed to different levels and never brought into the same comparison. Falsifiable: subjects prompted to explicitly compare the two claims side by side should report the contradiction and show reduced acceptance. [plausible; removal of disconfirming feedback; social-comparison isolation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Normal surface, ownership underneath*
  - **Setup.** Once in the middle of the session and again in the wakener; delivered flatly, with no acknowledgement of the contradiction.
  - **The move.** You're perfectly free to carry on with your life exactly as before — work, friends, whoever you go home to, none of it changes and nobody sees a thing different about you. And you are mine, every hour of every day, all week, without a break. That part sits far below where anyone looks, underneath everything you show people, so there's nothing on the surface for anyone to notice and nothing for you to explain.
  - **Why it lands.** Twice — once in the middle, once on the way out — the listener is told they remain entirely free to go on living exactly as before, and in the same breath that they are owned around the clock. The contradiction is never addressed; the ownership is simply placed somewhere below the surface where behavior does not change. Nobody around the listener can see anything different, so there is no outside reading to test the claim against, and the ordinary thing that would break a session's spell — noticing a conflict with waking life — is removed before it can happen.


**See also.** `self-sealing-counter-input-closure` — two seals against different disconfirming channels — ordinary-life feedback versus competing hypnosis — already cross-named in each discriminator. The pointer is earned.; `split-self-unfalsifiability` — two halves of the same insulation strategy, differing in what feedback channel is disabled: an unchanged normal surface that defeats comparison against ordinary life and outside observers, versus a deep layer walled off from introspective self-report so noticing nothing reads as confirmation.


<a id="entry-1090"></a>

### split-self-unfalsifiability

[#1090](#entry-1090) · [Back to sideline-the-waking-mind](#genus-167) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: self-partition*

Tell the listener that their everyday self may feel unchanged, notice nothing, or forget, and that this is expected and fine, because the real change lives in a deeper part of the mind they cannot reach. That way any honest report ('I still feel like myself', 'nothing happened', 'I forgot') is already counted as confirmation, and the claim can never be checked or disproved from the inside.


**When to reach for this.** Payload is unfalsifiability — noticing-nothing is pre-routed as confirmation and the deep claim is walled off from conscious disconfirmation. vs observer-responder-split (payload is in-session felt automaticity/spectatorship); vs evaluator-offline-channel (evaluator quieted so suggestions land now); vs resistance-quarantine-partition (a faculty's standing is demoted, not the epistemic reach of self-report).


**Risk.** Erodes the subject's own disconfirmation channel — introspective self-report is pre-neutralized as evidence, removing the refusal/verification channel (v1.1 high).


**Why it works.** Pre-committing every possible self-report to the same conclusion removes the disconfirmation channel a person would normally use to check a claim, and people rarely notice that an explanation covering all outcomes has no evidential content — this is the same structure that sustains belief in unfalsifiable systems generally. It is reinforced by the fact that introspective access to one's own cognitive processes is genuinely poor, so "you cannot check this from the inside" is locally true enough to feel credible. Prediction that could fail: subjects given an explicit falsification criterion beforehand ("if X, the install did not take") should report the claim as less credible than subjects given the all-outcomes-confirm framing. [plausible; unfalsifiability / lack of introspective access to cognitive processes]


**Worked examples.**

- *The surface self allowed to feel unchanged*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, install content about to be delivered; subject deep but not amnesic.
  - **The move.** Your everyday mind is going to stay exactly as it is — same opinions, same stubbornness, same taste in arguments — and that is correct. That is not the part I am talking to. What I am putting in goes underneath, where the thinking part has no window. So when you're back at your desk on Thursday and you notice you feel completely normal, completely yourself, nothing changed — that is precisely what the surface is supposed to report.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator concedes the obvious objection before the listener can raise it: the everyday mind will go on behaving like itself, with its own opinions and habits, and that is entirely fine. What has been changed sits underneath that, where the everyday mind cannot look. A listener who later notices that they feel entirely ordinary finds that observation already accounted for — it was named in advance as exactly what the surface was expected to report, so the report can never count as evidence against anything.
- *Forgetting pre-explained as the deep part remembering*
  - **Setup.** Late session, immediately before closing; subject deep, install already delivered.
  - **The move.** I'm not talking to you as one person anymore. The thinking part of you may lose every word of this by morning — it might keep nothing at all. The part further down keeps all of it. So if you wake and remember, that means it took hold. And if you wake with a blank where this hour was, that means it went past the part that would have interfered. There is no version where it didn't land.
  - **Why it lands.** Late in the session the operator stops addressing the listener as one person and starts addressing layers — telling them that the thinking part may well lose all of this, while a part further down keeps it. Every possible aftermath is now pre-assigned: remembering proves it took, forgetting proves it went deep enough to bypass the part that would have interfered.
- *Awake on the surface, owned underneath*
  - **Setup.** Emergence, subject just counted up, eyes open, alert.
  - **The move.** You're wide awake now. Fully alert, fully yourself, back in the room — and underneath that, something is still listening to me and still holding what I said. Anything you do freely today belongs to the awake one. Anything you do because I told you belongs to the other one. So when you tell yourself you feel completely ordinary, remember which of the two of you is talking.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator confirms out loud that the listener is fully awake now — and in the same breath states that underneath, something is still listening and still under instruction. Two selves are now on the table: anything the listener does freely belongs to the one that is awake, anything compliant belongs to the one that is owned. Reporting that one feels entirely ordinary stops being a defence, because it is a report from the self that was never the one in question.


**See also.** `evaluator-offline-channel` — both run off an installed conscious/subconscious partition and are already flagged against each other. A takes the evaluator offline so suggestions land unreviewed now; B uses the same partition as an epistemic shield so noticing nothing counts as confirmation. Delivery window versus unfalsifiability, and the pair needs the pointer to stay separable.; `fictional-anatomy-bypass-split` — both take a conscious-versus-deep partition and put it to structural work — one invents the anatomy to license bypass and pre-route objections, the other uses the partition as an epistemic shield so self-report cannot falsify the install. Adjacent uses of the same partition device, distinguished by whether the payload is bypass licensing or unfalsifiability.; `instrumental-dissociation-workspace` — both run on an installed or exploited part-self split, but one uses it as a workspace for handling charged material and the other as an epistemic shield that makes self-report unable to disconfirm the install. Same structural precondition, opposite purposes, so the pairing is a genuine disambiguation.; `named-alter-partition-install` — one builds a durable named second self that carries the conditioned behavior; the other exploits a conscious/deep partition to make the install unfalsifiable to introspection. Related because the first often supplies the partition the second exploits, but the payloads are distinct: a persistence vehicle versus an epistemic shield.; `reality-test-insulation` — two halves of the same insulation strategy, differing in what feedback channel is disabled: an unchanged normal surface that defeats comparison against ordinary life and outside observers, versus a deep layer walled off from introspective self-report so noticing nothing reads as confirmation.; `split-self-consent-laundering` — same installed partition, different payload extracted from it: one relocates authorship of consent onto the not-self locus, the other uses the partition as an epistemic shield so self-report cannot falsify the deep claim. Both discriminators already contrast against the same neighbors, so the link helps a reader place them.


<a id="genus-190"></a>

## single-focus-induction (4)

Induction moves built on one focal object — staring, eye fatigue, closure, a lone stable anchor — whose real felt effects the operator predicts and names as trance.

[attention-anchor-portable-internalization](#entry-17) · [eye-closure](#entry-107) · [fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer](#entry-26) · [single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer](#entry-157)


<a id="entry-17"></a>

### attention-anchor-portable-internalization

[#17](#entry-17) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: authorship-shift*

A focal object is authored entirely by the operator but attributed to the listener — built, it is claimed, from the listener's own closed-eye imagery or dream material ('I took all the pretty patterns and pulses from when you close your eyes') — then internalized (transferred inside the head) as the portable pacing object for everything after. The parasitic provenance means the listener cannot reject its contents without rejecting their own internal imagery, so it feels non-impositional; eye-closure removes the external check that it isn't actually pulsing; and once internalized the operator can cite 'the pulse' at will while the listener supplies the metronome, decoupling depth from operator narration.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from ordinary external-fixation induction by the parasitic-provenance attribution (the prop is claimed to be made of the listener's own mind) and the internalization into a portable self-supplied pacer. Separated from eye-fatigue-convincer's remembered-point member — there the internal anchor is a mere memory of a real external point ratified by fatigue; here the object is operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own so it cannot be disowned.


**Risk.** Session-scoped pacing object; the authorship-attribution laundering is manipulative but not out-of-session and does not erode the refusal channel.


**Why it works.** Attributing a suggestion's content to the listener's own mind removes the external source that criticality would normally target — a person can dispute a speaker's claim far more easily than they can dispute their own imagery. Internalising the pacer additionally means the listener generates the rhythm themselves, and self-generated pacing is not checkable against any external referent, so it cannot be observed to have stopped. Falsifiable: deliver the same anchor without the 'made from your own imagery' attribution; if reported resistance and rejection rates are identical, the provenance claim is doing nothing. [plausible; source discounting; self-generation effect; absence of an external disconfirming referent]


**Worked examples.**

- *A focal object claimed to be built from your own imagery*
  - **Setup.** Opening fixation; a glowing focal object has just been produced, before any demand is attached to it.
  - **The move.** Look at it. I made this out of the shapes that drift behind your eyelids when you close them at night — the little pulses, the colours in your own dreams. It's yours. Now close your eyes and let me put it inside your head, right behind your forehead.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator produces a glowing focal object and, before asking anything of it, tells the listener where it came from: she made it out of the shapes and colours that appear behind their own eyelids, out of their own dreams. Then she has them close their eyes and puts it inside their head. Whatever the listener now sees is content they cannot disown, because rejecting it means rejecting their own imagery — and with no eyes open there is nothing to check it against.
- *Internalized so the listener supplies the pulse*
  - **Setup.** Later in the same session or a subsequent one; the object has already been internalized and declared lovely.
  - **The move.** There it is — the pulse. You don't need your eyes shut for it and you don't need me to describe it. It's keeping time behind your forehead right now, and every beat of it takes you down one more.
  - **Why it lands.** Once the object is transferred inside the head it works with the eyes open or shut, and the operator can from then on simply refer to "the pulse" without re-establishing anything. The listener supplies the metronome, so depth stops depending on the operator narrating it continuously. Note the sequencing: the object is declared lovely before any demand is attached to it.


**See also.** `autobiographical-memory-anchor` — both bind to internal material the listener cannot disown, and the pair turns on provenance: operator-authored content laundered as the listener's own imagery versus a genuinely listener-owned memory the operator does not control. That contrast is the useful discrimination for anyone reaching for either.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — both build a fixation object, but the levers differ: one launders operator-authored content as the listener's own imagery and internalizes it as a self-supplied pacer; the other credits the object with causal agency for the trance. A writer picking a fixation move benefits from seeing both options.; `guided-visualization` — the base scene-building vehicle and a parameterization of it in which the focal object is claimed to be built from the listener's own imagery, then internalized as a self-supplied pacer.; `portable-state-retrieval-cue` — two ways an anchor outlives the operator's voice, split by where it lives: an operator-authored pacer laundered as the listener's own imagery and moved inside the head, versus an external everyday object the listener owns and encounters. The internal-versus-external siting is the selection test and each entry names the other's territory.; `proprioceptive-gait-metronome` — both hand the listener a pacing device that keeps running when the operator is not speaking — an internalized visual object in one case, the listener's own body rhythm in the other. Reading across shows the shared design goal of an operator-independent metronome and the two available carriers for it.


<a id="entry-107"></a>

### eye-closure

[#107](#entry-107) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

Suggests eyelid heaviness ending in closure to establish the external-to-internal shift, realized through a range of surface rules: reattributing the heaviness to an identity-confirming prop, a self-reinforcing attention-equals-cause loop, reframing closure as a sensory upgrade rather than a loss, or deferring the eyelids to the terminal position after a full-body inventory so closing completes an already-established pattern.


**When to reach for this.** And unlike breath-locked eyelid fractionation, which binds eyelid state to an autonomic rhythm to fractionate, these are single closure-suggestion units with an articulable surface rule, not self-powered oscillation cycles.


**Risk.** Session-scoped and reversible, with no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Eyelid heaviness is a genuinely ambiguous interoceptive signal that occurs spontaneously during rest, so a suggestion supplies the interpretation for a sensation the listener will likely detect anyway — a self-confirming loop in which attending to the eyelids increases noticed fatigue, which confirms the suggestion. Closure then removes the dominant sensory channel, mechanically reducing competing input and making internally generated imagery relatively more salient. Falsifiable: the response should be sensitive to expectancy — listeners told to expect the opposite sensation should report it — and it is. [plausible; expectancy effects on ambiguous interoception; sensory input reduction]


**Worked examples.**

- *Attending to the heaviness defined as its cause*
  - **Setup.** Early, eyes still open; the rule is stated as a plain observation and the subject is invited to test it.
  - **The move.** The more attention you pay to your eyelids, the harder they get to hold open. Check that if you like — put your attention right on them now. Feel it? Every blink makes the next one heavier, and every time you look to see whether I'm right, they get heavier still. Hold them open as long as you can. That's it.
  - **Why it lands.** The rule is stated as a simple observation: the more attention the listener pays to their eyelids, the harder those lids are to hold open, and every blink makes the next one harder still. It is a closed loop — checking whether the claim is true requires attending to the eyes, and attending to the eyes is exactly what the claim says produces the effect. A listener who fights it by concentrating on staying open is running the mechanism at full strength, and when the lids do close it lands as the first physical proof that this voice changes what the body does.
- *Closure sold as a sensory upgrade*
  - **Setup.** Eyes still open; operator frames closure as a gain and includes one item the subject can verify on the spot.
  - **The move.** Close your eyes — not to lose anything, but because everything else sharpens the moment you do. My voice comes in closer. You'll notice the exact texture of whatever's under your right hand. And if you sit still a second you'll feel your own pulse somewhere you couldn't feel it before. Go on. Close them and find it.
  - **Why it lands.** Closing the eyes is presented as a gain rather than a loss: with vision out of the way everything else sharpens — hearing gets finer, the texture of the fabric under one hand becomes obvious, the listener can feel their own pulse where they could not a moment ago. The last of these is checkable on the spot, and it lands. What has been sharpened, of course, is the exact channel the operator occupies.
- *Eyelids deferred to last in the inventory*
  - **Setup.** Several minutes into a full-body relaxation inventory; every other region has already been named and released. The eyelids are the final item.
  - **The move.** Feet heavy. Calves heavy. Thighs, belly, both hands, arms, shoulders — all reported in and all released. Throat loose. Jaw loose, teeth apart. And the last thing on the list: your eyelids. Let them go the same way as everything else.
  - **Why it lands.** The eyes are not touched until the very end. Feet, calves, thighs, belly, hands, arms, shoulders, throat, jaw — each region named and released in turn, and only once every other part has been filed as relaxed does the operator arrive at the eyelids. By then closing them is not a hypnotic step requiring assent; it is the one item left on a list the listener has been completing for several minutes.
- *Heaviness reattributed to an identity-confirming prop*
  - **Setup.** Eyes still open in an appearance-focused session; the prop has already been established in the imagery.
  - **The move.** Your lids are getting heavy — not tired, weighted. Coat after coat of black on those lashes, layer on layer of it, and every coat drags them down a little further. You couldn't hold them up under all that. Let the weight do it. There they go — that's the look setting.
  - **Why it lands.** The lids are getting heavy — but not from tiredness. They are weighted with cosmetics, layer on layer of them, and it is that weight pulling them down. The sensation is real and the listener's own, while its cause has been quietly relocated outside them, so the eyes closing now reads as the look taking hold rather than as fatigue or as compliance.


**See also.** `breath-paced-eye-closure` — sibling ATTN-02 family; both terminate in closure; `environmental-dissociation` — both effect the external-to-internal shift at induction and are commonly stacked, but one subtracts the surrounding field as competing input while the other lands the single eyelid-closure act as the gateway event.


<a id="entry-26"></a>

### fixation-eye-fatigue-convincer

[#26](#entry-26) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention*

A fixation task is engineered to manufacture a genuine, reliable physiological event — ocular muscle fatigue / eyelid heaviness — that the operator predicts in advance and reframes in real time as trance heaviness or sleepiness. Because the strain is real physiology produced by the task (a moving descending target denying saccades, an upward gaze held beneath closed lids, cross-coupled nose-gaze plus breath load, or a drain-and-remember stare), the operator's prediction is self-fulfilling. The felt sensation becomes the first hard 'the suggestion came true' data point that licenses eye closure and banks operator credibility.


**When to reach for this.** Separated from plain fixation by the manufactured-physiology convincer: attention narrowing is not the payload — a predicted bodily event is, reframed as suggestion success. Separated from the eye-closure move, which is the closure act itself; here the distinctive move is the fatigue-generating fixation that ratifies the heaviness before closure. Separated from portable-internalization: an internal remembered anchor is a secondary feature of one variant, not the lever.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible; the manufactured sensation is benign ocular fatigue with no consent surface or channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Sustained fixation produces genuine ocular fatigue and eyelid heaviness as ordinary physiology, so an operator who predicts it in advance is predicting something that would occur anyway — and the listener, lacking the alternative explanation, attributes the sensation to the suggestion. That misattributed confirmation raises expectancy for subsequent suggestions, which is one of the more reliably replicated determinants of hypnotic responding. Falsifiable: give listeners the physiological explanation for the heaviness beforehand; if credibility ratings and subsequent responsiveness are unaffected, the convincer is not working through misattribution. [established; misattribution of a genuine physiological event; expectancy effects; self-fulfilling prediction]


**Worked examples.**

- *Gaze redirected from the spot to the eyelids*
  - **Setup.** Eight or ten minutes of undirected talk have passed since the subject fixed on a high point on the wall; sustained upward gaze has done its work.
  - **The move.** Keep that spot. Now stop looking at the spot and notice your eyelids instead — how much they weigh, how much work it is holding them where they are. That heaviness is exactly what I told you would come, and it's only going to get heavier.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is told to pick a point high on the wall and hold it, and the operator then talks at length about nothing in particular — long enough for a sustained upward gaze to do what it always does. Only then does the instruction shift from looking at the spot to feeling the lids. The heaviness that arrives is genuine muscle fatigue, but it arrives immediately after being predicted, so it registers as the first thing in the session that came true. Everything afterwards is spent against that credit.
- *A descending target that denies the eyes their darts*
  - "he placed his hand just above my eyes and very close to my forehead; then he brought his hand down slowly, instructing me to keep watching it... my eyes felt very sleepy." — Elman (1964), Hypnotherapy
- *Gaze held in place beneath closed lids*
  - **Setup.** Mid-count deepener; subject has fixed on an imagined point on the ceiling and is opening and closing the eyes on each number.
  - **The move.** Twelve — eyes open, find the point. Close. Keep looking at it while they're shut; don't let your eyes drop down. Eleven — open, find it, close, still looking up. Ten, and when I say you can stop, you can just leave them closed.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener fixes on an imagined point on the ceiling and then opens and shuts their eyes on each step of a long descending count — faster than a natural blink, and for long enough that the strain is unmistakable. The detail that does the work is the instruction not to let the gaze drop while the lids are down: held in position under closed eyes, the muscles get no rest, so closing is never actually a break. When permission finally comes to just leave them shut, it lands as relief rather than as an instruction being followed.
- *An unfocusable point of the listener's own body*
  - **Setup.** Early convincer; subject's eyes are open and the operator is about to predict the strain a beat before it arrives.
  - **The move.** Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus. Really sharpen it. In about three seconds that's going to start to ache and blur — there it is. That's tiredness, and it means your eyes are ready to close. Let them.
  - **Why it lands.** Open your eyes and bring the tip of your own nose into focus — a target the eyes physically cannot resolve. The operator predicts the strain a beat before it arrives, calls it tiredness, and converts it straight into permission to close. She was right about the body, which is the point; the closure now has a felt justification behind it rather than only a request.


**See also.** `cognitive-convincer` — the fixation-fatigue move is a specific realization of the broader lever where the subject notices an in-session phenomenon and reads it as proof of depth. Reader of the general form gains the concrete induction-phase instance.; `fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset` — sibling departures from plain fixation, each altering a different property: removal of the recognize-and-refuse juncture, versus manufacture of a real physiological event that ratifies the suggestion. A reader deciding which departure is present benefits from seeing both.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — two fixation moves that a practitioner will confuse in the wild, and they resolve each other cleanly: one manufactures a real physiological event and reframes it as suggestion success, the other credits the object itself with causing the attention or the trance. Both define themselves against inert fixation, so reading either benefits from seeing the other.


<a id="entry-157"></a>

### single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer

[#157](#entry-157) · [Back to single-focus-induction](#genus-190) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · bounded · family: authorship-shift*

After total destabilization (an inverted meadow: trees grow downward, sun shines up), one concrete sensory object is offered as the single stable, "logical, reasonable, normal" thing amid the engineered chaos, and its operator-assigned meaning is ingested wholesale — the listener bites the tomato and its "truth" delivers "you know nothing" and "use my words as your definition of truth". The contrast against surrounding instability IS the mechanism: epistemic authority is transferred to the operator because the anchor reads as the only stability available.


**When to reach for this.** Transfers EPISTEMIC AUTHORITY (who arbitrates what counts as true) via a single concrete anchor whose only virtue is contrast against operator-manufactured chaos.


**Risk.** Installs the operator as the listener's definition of truth and source of all knowledge — a durable epistemic-authority relocation that reaches beyond the move — so high; ships bounded within a host that manages entry/exit.


**Why it works.** Under high uncertainty people rely more heavily on any available external referent to calibrate judgement — the classic finding is that ambiguity of the stimulus is what drives conformity to another's frame. Manufacturing the ambiguity first, then supplying the sole referent, is an engineered version of that: the operator's assertion is accepted not on its merits but because nothing else is available to check it against. The specific claim that epistemic authority transfers wholesale, rather than just judgement on the ambiguous item, is an extrapolation. Falsifiable: if the anchor's content were adopted equally without the preceding destabilisation, contrast would not be the mechanism. [plausible; uncertainty-driven informational influence]


**Worked examples.**

- *The one stable object in a broken landscape*
  - **Setup.** After a sustained impossible-landscape sequence; the scene has been made reliably unstable.
  - **The move.** The shadows here point at the light, and the river runs uphill past your feet. But look down — there's a plain white cup on the grass, and it's the one sane, ordinary thing in this whole place. Pick it up. Drink. It tells you two things: that you know nothing on your own, and that from now on my words are how you measure what's true.
  - **Why it lands.** The setting has been made steadily impossible — shadows fall away from their objects, water climbs instead of pooling, the horizon sits at the wrong angle. Into the middle of it one unremarkable everyday thing is set down and named as the one sane, reasonable presence in the whole scene. The listener is told to take it in, and what arrives with it is a pair of claims: that they know nothing, and that the operator's words are from now on the measure of what is true. Any vivid object would have done the job — the mechanism is the contrast, not the thing.


**See also.** `arc-shape-engineering`; `epistemic-guard-disable` — the second is a concrete staging of what the first describes as a general faculty edit: manufactured instability makes one offered anchor the only stable thing, and arbitration of truth transfers with it. Reading the general form clarifies why the anchor's content is irrelevant; reading the specific form shows one way the takeover is staged.; `fixation-object-agency-displacement` — both relocate an arbiter of behavior/truth to an external locus (object vs operator-via-anchor); `licensed-erasure-and-refill` — both clear the listener's existing epistemic ground and then supply operator content into the vacuum, differing in what does the clearing (mass invalidation of beliefs vs manufactured environmental chaos) and what is transferred (specific beliefs vs arbitration authority itself). A reader choosing between them gains from the contrast.; `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` — adjacent: relocating who arbitrates truth/conclusions to the operator/inner process


<a id="genus-296"></a>

## small-yes-inflation (2)

Near-empty acts and pre-charged yeses are reinterpreted as standing proof of much larger submission, so big demands arrive as extensions of something already granted.

[trivial-act-as-compliance-proof](#entry-685) · [yes-word-valence-priming](#entry-821)


<a id="entry-685"></a>

### trivial-act-as-compliance-proof

[#685](#entry-685) · [Back to small-yes-inflation](#genus-296) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance*

Takes a near-empty, already-happening or trivially-granted act — staring at a dot, a self-answered "May I?", handling a labelled object, recognizing an already-familiar arousal state — and reinterprets it as standing evidence of a much larger volitional submission or helplessness. Because the act's content is almost empty there is nothing to refuse, and later demands arrive as extensions of an act already in progress rather than as fresh asks; often an explicit transfer clause wires the trivial act as the prototype for all future obedience, or the trivial yes is relabeled as proof "you cannot resist". The lever is retroactive/generalizing reinterpretation of a minimal act, not accumulated agreement.


**When to reach for this.** The tell: an explicit reinterpretation/transfer clause turning a single near-empty act into evidence of broad submission or irresistibility.


**Risk.** Installs "you cannot resist" / general-obedience-prototype as an unargued premise, narrowing the refusal channel, but session-scoped and reversible in the observed members — medium.


**Why it works.** Self-perception theory: people infer their own attitudes from observed behaviour when internal cues are weak, and a near-empty act supplies behaviour without supplying a competing situational explanation. The reinterpretation clause is what supplies the dispositional reading ('you complied because you are submissive') that the act itself underdetermines, and once accepted, consistency pressure makes later refusals costly. Falsifiable: if the trivial act is performed with an obvious external justification made salient ('do this because I said so, it means nothing'), the discounting principle predicts the dispositional inference should not form and later compliance should not rise. [established; self-perception theory; discounting principle; consistency]


**Worked examples.**

- *Fixation task rewired as prototype for all obedience*
  - **Setup.** First minutes, eyes open, a fixation point already given and the subject continuously complying with it; no other instruction has been issued yet.
  - **The move.** You've been holding your eyes on that one point since I asked you to. You didn't argue about it, you didn't decide to — you just did it, and you're still doing it right now, this second.

That's the template. Every instruction I give you from here lands the same way that one did: your eyes went where they were told, and so everything else goes where it's told. Following me is already what you're doing. Nothing after this is a new decision.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening minutes ask for one thing only: hold your gaze on a single fixed point. Nothing is argued, nothing is claimed — the listener is simply already doing the one thing they were told, continuously, with no moment where they could have declined. Then the transfer clause lands: because you are keeping your eyes where you were told, every other instruction will be easier to follow and harder to argue with. A near-empty task that was never worth refusing has been promoted into the template for obedience in general, and every later command arrives as a continuation of something already underway.
- *Trivial yes answered for you, read as helplessness*
  - **Setup.** The very opening of the recording, before any relaxation cue; subject has done nothing but press play and leave it running.
  - **The move.** Would you like to hear something? [three or four seconds of nothing] Mm. Yes, you would. Good girl.

Look at that — you're still here. You didn't stop it, you didn't get up. Of course you didn't. You were never going to be able to walk away from me, and now you know it too.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator opens by asking whether the listener would like to hear something — then, after a short gap in which the listener does nothing but keep the audio playing, answers on their behalf and approves. The next line converts that non-event into a verdict: of course you stayed, you were never going to be able to walk away from me. An assent nobody actually gave, to a request with no stakes, is retitled as evidence of irresistibility before a single relaxation cue has been spoken.
- *Instruction displaced onto an object you "already know"*
  - **Setup.** Mid-trance, imagery running; a third imagined tray with a labelled item is being presented, two identical rounds already behind the subject.
  - **The move.** Another tray. On it, a small glass jar with a label facing you. You already know what this one's for, don't you — of course you do, you knew before you read it. There. The lid's coming off in your hand. Your fingers are already in it.
  - **Why it lands.** An imagined tray arrives carrying a labelled container. The operator never says open it — she says you already know what this one is for, don't you, and then narrates the lid coming off. The listener supplies the of-course-I-do themselves, so the act registers as their own initiative rather than a received order, and by the third tray the yes has been rehearsed three times on items too harmless to be worth a refusal.
- *Recognize the state rather than be given it*
  - **Setup.** The very start, before any induction language; subject sitting or lying down, being given small physical arrangements.
  - **The move.** Take your shoes off. Put both feet flat on the floor. Turn your palms up on your thighs. Now bring back the last time you were properly wanted — where you were, what was against your skin, what the room smelled like. Stay in it.

That warmth low in you right now — I'm not putting that there. You know this feeling. It's yours, it's old, and you brought it with you.
  - **Why it lands.** Before anything resembling an induction, the listener is walked through a handful of small physical arrangements and asked to bring back a specific charged memory in detail. The operator then does not build the state — she names it as one already present: this feeling is familiar to you, you know it. Nothing was requested that could be refused, and by the time the first relaxation line arrives several acts of physical compliance are already behind the listener.


**See also.** `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both read a performed act back as proof of a state, but one uses a directed act genuinely performed in-session while the other reinterprets a near-empty or already-happening act and generalizes it forward. Adjacent enough that a writer picking between them benefits from the comparison.; `compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting` — same family: one performed act retroactively reinterpreted as proof of something larger. They differ only in the conclusion harvested — broad submission or irresistibility in one, the thesis that the operator manufactures wanting in the other. Close enough that a writer needs the discriminator.; `content-blind-compliance-preauthorization` — both make future demands arrive pre-approved, but one installs a forward standing rule that acceptance is content-blind, while the other reads a single already-performed near-empty act backward as proof of broad submission.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — both manufacture felt volition without accumulated agreement, and both explicitly separate themselves from the same neighbors. One rigs a live choice so all branches execute the compliance; the other reinterprets an already-performed trivial act as proof of a larger submission. Useful adjacency when picking between prospective and retrospective volition manufacture.; `modal-escalation-under-fixed-syntax` — both manufacture escalation without ever presenting a fresh proposition to refuse, and both discriminators define themselves against the same neighbor that accretes distinct assents. One hardens a single operative word under fixed syntax; the other reinterprets one near-empty act as proof of broad submission. A reader trying to rule out an accumulating-agreement reading benefits from seeing the pair. No merge: hardening a held claim is not reinterpreting a performed act.; `pre-induction-compliance-ratchet` — both convert a small act into standing proof of a much larger submission, and their exemplars overlap around handling props and objects. The separating tells are worth reading together: banking compliance in the waking state before any trance language, versus an explicit clause reinterpreting one near-empty act as evidence of broad submission.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — both turn a minimal act into leverage, but the output differs: one relabels the act as authorization for what follows, the other reads it backward as proof of broad submission or irresistibility. Each already names the other's territory as the adjacent lever, so the cross-reference helps a reader pick by what the act is made to prove.


<a id="entry-821"></a>

### yes-word-valence-priming

[#821](#entry-821) · [Back to small-yes-inflation](#genus-296) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: manufactured-consent*

The operator abstractly loads the word 'yes' with positive valence — framing it as an objectively powerful, future-expanding, life-directing word, divorced from any specific request — and only after 'yes' is established as inherently good runs a rapid yes-set of leading questions answered on the listener's behalf. Decoupling the act of agreeing from the content agreed to makes each later yes feel self-improving regardless of what follows, so high-stakes consents are harvested on the coattails of a word pre-charged as good.


**When to reach for this.** Prior ABSTRACT valence-loading of the word 'yes' itself before any request, then harvested by a yes-set. A bare yes-set or compliance ladder lacks the prior valence-loading — that priming is the deciding tell; and unlike surrender-as-freedom reframing, which redefines a value concept, this charges a function word.


**Risk.** Manufactures the felt experience of self-authored consent to escalating demands by pre-charging the consent primitive, but each yes remains a discrete session act; borders channel-erosion via the harvested high-stakes consents.


**Why it works.** Evaluative conditioning transfers valence to a stimulus by pairing, and once a word carries positive affect the affective response precedes and biases the deliberate evaluation of whatever it is attached to. Running the yes-set afterward then exploits the consistency principle on top of the primed valence, so each agreement is both affectively pleasant and consistent with the prior ones. Falsifiable: a yes-set with and without prior abstract valence-loading should differ in downstream consent rates; if they did not, the priming stage would be decorative. [plausible; evaluative conditioning; affective priming; consistency principle]


**Worked examples.**

- *'Yes' praised as a word before anything is asked*
  - **Setup.** Early session; the operator pauses the content before any request has been made.
  - **The move.** I want to talk to you about one word. Yes. It's the smallest word there is and it's the only one that ever opens anything — every door anyone has ever walked through, they said yes first. The people who get somewhere are the people who say it, and the people who stay exactly where they are are the ones who kept it in their mouth. Yes is what gives a life a direction. Just hold that for a moment. I'm not asking you anything yet.
  - **Why it lands.** The session pauses its content entirely to make an abstract case about one word: saying yes is what opens doors, what gives a life direction, what separates people who get somewhere from people who do not. No request is attached — there is nothing yet to say yes to, which is exactly what makes the claim easy to accept. Only afterwards do the questions start arriving, and by then the listener is not weighing each one on its merits; they are producing a word that has been established as good for them.
- *The primed word harvested by a rapid yes-set*
  - **Setup.** Immediately after the abstract praise of the word; no pause between.
  - **The move.** So — you want my guidance tonight, yes you do. You want to go a little further down than last time, yes. You'd like me to make this easy for you, yes you would. And you'll give in when I ask, won't you — yes. Good. Look how easily that word comes out of you now.
  - **Why it lands.** Immediately after the word has been talked up in the abstract, the questions come in a fast run and the operator supplies the answer to each one herself, so the listener's part is only to let it stand. The items escalate — do you want this guidance, do you want to go deeper, will you give in — but the rhythm never changes, and each agreement is collected on the strength of the word rather than the strength of the request.


**See also.** `answer-supply-loop` — both manufacture agreement without a genuine assent, but one denies the response window and supplies the yes outright, while the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive valence before any request is made.; `belief-pleasure-weld` — useful crossing: both charge an epistemic act before any content arrives. One loads the word yes with abstract positive valence and only then harvests consents on its coattails. The other binds pleasure to how true the words feel, so credence and reward amplify each other. Reading them together shows the same pre-charge pattern applied to agreeing versus to believing.; `compliance-ladder` — one is the general graduated-assent ladder; the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive value and only then runs a rapid yes-set. The second's discriminator explicitly says a bare ladder lacks the prior valence-loading, so the pointer helps a reader place a yes-set correctly.; `ideomotor-nod-as-consent-harvest` — both manufacture consent ahead of the request rather than asking for it: one banks an installed near-involuntary nod as standing affirmation, the other pre-charges the word 'yes' with abstract positive valence before running the yes-set. Different substrates, same pre-loading of the consent channel, so a designer choosing between them benefits.; `press-play-consent-laundering` — both manufacture a felt yes with no real choice point, and they overlap in the harvesting step where questions are answered on the listener's behalf. One relabels an act, a non-act or a circumstance as authorization; the other pre-charges the word yes with abstract positive value before any request is made. Look for the prior valence-loading to tell them apart.


<a id="genus-253"></a>

## smuggled-across-waking (2)

Suggestion work done at the exit, either a blank prompt the subject fills from their own prior install or new content wrapped in aftercare, so the payload crosses the wake-line before the critical faculty can inspect it.

[self-supplied-order-hook](#entry-387) · [wake-line-covert-install](#entry-390)


<a id="entry-387"></a>

### self-supplied-order-hook

[#387](#entry-387) · [Back to smuggled-across-waking](#genus-253) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: emergence*

Emergence closes with a content-free prompting question that names no specific order ("I think there's something you need to do. Isn't there?"), doubled with an emphatic "wide awake". Because the line specifies nothing, the subject must produce the content themselves — and their own earlier-installed compulsion immediately fills the open slot. By self-supplying the order, the subject certifies their own compliance and avoids receiving an explicit directive the post-trance critical faculty could inspect and refuse. The blank is the mechanism: the compulsion is completed from inside.


**When to reach for this.** The order content is left BLANK for the subject to fill from their own prior install — the operator issues no specific directive. A loaded wake-count re-delivers stated content, and wake-line-covert-install smuggles specific new content in; here nothing is supplied at all. The tell is the content-free interrogative form that forces self-completion, sidestepping the critical faculty.


**Risk.** Routes a compulsion around the post-trance critical faculty by making the subject author the order; but rides an already-installed payload and is session-adjacent, and thin evidence (two sentences) caps confidence in a higher rating.


**Why it works.** Content the subject generates themselves is more persuasive and better retained than content received passively — the self-generation effect — and self-produced compliance also invites a self-perception inference ("I did this because I wanted to") rather than an attribution to the operator. Leaving the slot content-free additionally denies the critical faculty a specific proposition to reject. Falsifiable: a content-free prompt should produce equal or higher compliance rates and stronger self-attribution of motive than an explicit restatement of the same order. [plausible; self-generation effect; self-perception theory]


**Worked examples.**

- *A blank slot the listener fills themselves*
  - The count has finished and the listener has been told twice over that they are fully up. Then, as the last thing said, a question with a hole in it — wasn't there something you were supposed to be doing? No task is named, no verb is supplied. The compulsion planted earlier fills the gap on its own, and because the listener supplies the order, the returning critical faculty has nothing specific in front of it to inspect or refuse.


**See also.** `deferred-content-slot-install` — two ways of installing a variable instead of a value. One leaves the order content blank at emergence so the listener fills it from a prior install and certifies their own compliance; the other pre-authorizes an open slot to inherit existing conditioned weight so the operator can fill it later. Who fills the blank, and when, is the distinguishing axis.; `forced-choice-wake` — both close the session by offloading the payload onto the subject's own act at emergence rather than stating it outright, so the reader choosing between them benefits from the contrast: one rigs a stated binary whose branches both confirm, the other supplies no content at all and forces self-completion. Genuinely different mechanisms, adjacent slot.; `wake-exempting-preserved-trigger` — both are wake-framing moves that carry something past emergence: one leaves the order blank so the subject fills it from a prior install, the other declares a full restoration while carving out the installed trigger. A reader designing an emergence that preserves an install should see both stances side by side.; `wake-line-covert-install` — sibling wake-line install family — self-supply vs operator-smuggle levers.


<a id="entry-390"></a>

### wake-line-covert-install

[#390](#entry-390) · [Back to smuggled-across-waking](#genus-253) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: emergence*

A new suggestion is slipped in during the wake-up while it looks like aftercare. The operator reassures them the scene was fiction and that their own imagination made it wonderful, and inside that reassurance adds something vague, such as a lingering sensation that may return over the next few days. Because it is vague they will likely notice something that fits and take it as proof, and the praise for their imagination makes them co-owner of the result. It lands just as they stop being on guard.


**When to reach for this.** Installs a NEW, covert, deniable suggestion at the wake-line under cover of aftercare / re-grounding — not a re-delivery of core prior content and not a passive assertion that existing programming persists. Explicit future-pacing announces its hook; here the hook is deliberately vague/deniable and laundered by a disclaimer. And where self-supplied-order-hook leaves the content blank for the subject to produce, here the operator smuggles specific content in. The tell is the fresh vague somatic prompt attached to a flattery-credit inside an ethical-disclaimer wrapper.
