  - **The move.** From now on, every time your hand goes to your mouth, snap the band on your wrist once — immediately, not after. You'll watch the count fall off a cliff this week. Don't get comfortable: the snap stops stinging around day ten and the count comes back up, and the day we stop, you'll still have every one of those bites left in you.
  - **Why it lands.** The immediate drop is real and gives the subject early evidence the procedure works, while the pre-announced rebound stops them from reading the drop as a change in disposition. Observable: rate falls sharply within the first sessions, then creeps back as the emotional reaction to the snap habituates — and on withdrawal the cumulative count matches an unpunished baseline, which is the reserve-conservation tell rather than any extinction.


**Realizations** (1): `positive-punishment-aversive-presentation`


**See also.** `mechanical-response-preclusion` — shares the temporary-suppression axis — rate falls only while the intervention remains in force, leaving the underlying disposition intact.


<a id="entry-1551"></a>

### backdated-nonrefusable-install

[#1551](#entry-1551) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

The install is asserted to have already happened during a window the listener could not observe, so there is structurally no point at which it could have been declined. In the fractionation file the operator narrates the listener's hand drifting toward the face, then retroactively asserts the button was implanted "while you were sleeping," treating the drift as previously conditioned though no prior drill installed it; "Luckily I'm trustworthy, huh?" names the exploited window and waves it off. In the nurse script the mind-cage trigger is installed during a narrated post-surgery blackout with the amnesia claim built in — "their memory doesn't have any recall ... they simply didn't pay close enough attention." Ideomotor narration then supplies live proof: the hand involuntarily presses the button and the listener drops, so the backdated conditioning demonstrates itself as already real.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script reports the conditioning as a past accomplished fact — done during sleep, blackout, or surgery the listener supposedly cannot recall — rather than performing the install in the listener's presence. The tell is tense: the install arrives as a fait accompli, typically paired with an amnesia clause and an immediate involuntary bodily demonstration offered as evidence that it took.


**Worked examples.**

- *install reported as already done during unobservable sleep*
  - you see while you were sleeping I just implanted a button on your forehead


**See also.** `asserted-duration-false-memory` — also asserts a checkable-sounding fact about an unobserved stretch of session time on bare operator authority.; `covert-install-under-cover` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its backdated-to-an-unobservable-window form.; `identity-origin-erasure` — shared axis of relocating an install's origin into an erased or unfalsifiable past the listener cannot inspect or return to.; `presupposition-install` — both backdate the operative event to a moment the listener cannot revisit or contest.; `template-reuse-install` — both route a heavier install around the scrutiny a fresh install ceremony would draw — there by dating the install to an unobservable past, here by riding a template the listener already accepted.


<a id="entry-1446"></a>

### bait-and-switch-contract-arc

[#1446](#entry-1446) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The file opens promising one thing (relaxation, an easy familiar state, with repeated low-stakes assurances like 'nothing complex', 'easy', 'pleasant') and ends delivering another: automatic obedience. No single passage makes the swap; it is spread across a sequence that never signals the change: a very easy start, a way of soaking up resistance, self-fulfilling proof that the listener is listening, narrowing awareness to just the voice, a quietly slipped-in turn toward obedience, and a countdown that seals it. Words like 'obey' never appear in the first half and show up only after the listener's attention has narrowed to the voice. Someone hearing only the opening would call it a relaxation file; someone hearing only the end would call it an obedience-trigger install.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script's front and back halves describe different transactions — the opening reads as a low-stakes relaxation induction, the closing as an obedience installation — and no passage in between visibly renegotiates the terms. The tell is lexical: the payload vocabulary is entirely absent from the opening half and surfaces only after attentional narrowing, and the closing's delivered state exceeds what the opening's repeated assurances contracted for.


**Worked examples.**

- *no single passage performs the swap — the arc is the mechanism*
  - No single passage performs the bait-and-switch. The switch is the cumulative relationship between the opening 200 words and the closing 200 words, plus everything in between that bridges them without flagging the bridge.


**See also.** `attention-as-evidence-loop` — the self-fulfilling listening-proof move that this arc uses as one of its unflagged bridging steps.; `consent-topology-arc` — the whole-script consent-surface topology family this bait-and-switch realization was split out of.; `voice-absorption` — the voice-only attentional field that serves as this arc's mid-script bridge between the opening contract and the closing delivery.


<a id="entry-1517"></a>

### baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration

[#1517](#entry-1517) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

When setting a target for a behaviour the subject already does, base the first goal on their own measured average so the first round can be won: for example, a gap between occurrences equal to or a little shorter than their usual gap, or an allowed count at or slightly below their normal rate. Then tighten the target in small steps, only after they have succeeded. If they fail, go back to the last level that worked and move forward more slowly. Reward low rates, not perfection, so one slip does not end the game. Variations: a rolling target that only rewards responses better than most of their recent ones.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the question is where to set the bar on an already-occurring behavior and how fast to move it. The tell is arithmetic on the subject's own baseline — a mean, a quotient, or a ranking of recent responses — producing the opening criterion, followed by one-parameter-at-a-time performance-gated steps and an explicit back-off-and-re-approach rule when a step fails.


**Worked examples.**

- *baseline-derived opening criterion*
  - use the mean number of responses emitted during baseline sessions, or slightly lower than that average, as the initial full-session DRL criterion.


**See also.** `aversive-procedure-administration-envelope` — same calibration axis — placing a procedure's parameters where the subject's measured data say they can function.; `differential-reinforcement` — the differential-reinforcement family whose criteria this calibration procedure parameterizes.; `differential-reinforcement-low-rate` — criterion-sizing axis: the first allowed-rate ceiling is read off the subject's own baseline session mean.; `omission-reinforcement-dro` — criterion-sizing axis: the opening omission interval is computed from the subject's baseline mean inter-response time.; `reward-taper` — same parametric-calibration axis — steps and criteria sized from measured performance so each stage stays winnable.


<a id="entry-852"></a>

### belief-outcome-gate

[#852](#entry-852) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A rule for the operator: do not change a belief the person's life rests on until you can predict what else will shift when it changes. The operator first gauges how much depends on the belief, and holds off even if the person explicitly asks to go ahead. The limit is set by foreseeable fallout, not by whether the person said yes.


**When to reach for this.** Gates on the operator's FOREKNOWLEDGE of consequences, not on the subject's consent — unlike a consent checkpoint, this gate holds even against an explicit request to proceed; a rule about what the operator may touch, not a move performed on the subject.


**Risk.** Purely operator-constraining protective gate.


**Why it works.** Works on the operator, not the subject: it treats stated consent as an unreliable proxy for informed consent, because people are demonstrably poor at affective forecasting — predicting how they will feel about a changed state they have never occupied. Since a foundational belief is one that many other beliefs and behaviours are inferentially and behaviourally conditional on, altering it produces downstream changes the subject could not have priced in when agreeing. Falsifiable: if subjects who requested such changes reliably reported outcomes matching their pre-change predictions, the gate would be solving a problem that does not exist. [plausible; affective forecasting error; informed-consent validity]


**Worked examples.**

- *No pin pulled without a known outcome*
  - "if I don't know what I am going to end up with, I don't pull pins!" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**See also.** `context-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-facing governance gates that block a high-stakes act until a condition on the operator's own knowledge is met, one verifying the subject's actual state and one requiring foreseen consequences before touching a load-bearing belief. Reading them together shows the shape of a positive-governance rule.; `disconfirmation-suppression` — both are operator conduct rules around a load-bearing belief, but one withholds change until downstream fallout is foreseen while the other actively hides a fact that would collapse an effect already running.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are operator-side gates that can block an install from proceeding, and both are constraints on the operator rather than moves performed on the subject. One gates on the operator's foresight about downstream fallout and holds even against an explicit request to proceed; the other gates on the subject's lived, tested endorsement and can return abort. Useful pair when choosing which kind of restraint to write.; `intervention-gating` — both are operator-side conditional rules that branch or block the plan before anything is done to the subject, with no subject-facing surface. One is a general precondition-branch family, the other a specific hold on altering a load-bearing belief until consequences are foreseeable; the specific case reads as an instance of the general gate and readers should see the relation.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both are operator-side governance gates that narrow the operator's own license rather than acting on the subject, and both hold independently of the subject's consent or request. One gates on design coherence, the other on foreseen downstream fallout; a reader classifying a self-imposed hold needs the pair.; `suitability-screening` — both are operator-side gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, and they gate on different grounds: subject fitness and consent state versus the operator's foreknowledge of downstream fallout. Reading one raises the natural question of what else can hold a session back, which the other answers.


<a id="entry-568"></a>

### beneficiary-target-filter

[#568](#entry-568) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Before any work starts, each possible target behavior is screened by asking whose benefit the change serves. Only changes that bring immediate and lasting benefit to the person themselves pass, such as new sources of reward or a wider range of useful skills. Goals chosen to make someone 'still, quiet, docile' for the convenience of staff or society are rejected. A simple worksheet turns 'whose behavior, changed by whom, for whose benefit' into a checklist of answerable questions.


**When to reach for this.** A per-target ADMISSIBILITY filter keyed to the subject's own long-term benefit, applied against institutional pressure — not a session-scope boundary declaration, and not installability spec craft (well-formedness QA asks 'can this be built cleanly', not 'who benefits').


**Risk.** Protective screen on the operator's own selection behavior.


**Why it works.** Prospective screening works because the party choosing a behavioral target has interests that predictably diverge from the subject's, and unconstrained choosers reliably resolve that conflict in their own favour — the documented institutional pattern is that 'problem behaviours' selected by caregivers cluster on staff-burden reduction rather than on expanding the subject's own reinforcer access. Forcing the choice through a written 'for whose benefit' question is a precommitment device: it converts an implicit, deniable judgement into an explicit answerable claim that a third party can later audit, which raises the reputational cost of a self-serving answer. Falsifiable: if target lists produced with the worksheet do not differ in composition from lists produced without it, or if compliance-suppression targets pass the filter at the same rate, the mechanism is not operating. [plausible; principal-agent conflict of interest; accountability effects on judgement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reject targets that only serve others' convenience*
  - "Target behaviors should not be selected solely for the primary benefit of others (e.g., 'Be still, be quiet, be docile')" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Admit only targets that widen the person's own reinforcers*
  - "selected because they will improve a person's quality of life… by allowing the person access to new reinforcers and additional reinforcing contexts" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `harm-rejection-filter` — same admissibility test run on the other side of the dyad: beneficiary-target-filter screens targets for the subject's benefit before install; this screens suggestions inside the subject at delivery.; `target-selection` — both are design-time filters on the target list before anything is enacted, but one supplies selection criteria and the other an admissibility test keyed to whose benefit the change serves. Read together when deciding what an intervention should aim at.


<a id="entry-1547"></a>

### bidirectional-naming-transfer

[#1547](#entry-1547) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Teach a word in one direction only, for example "touch the cat" (understanding), and the other direction, saying "cat" when shown one, appears without being taught. Learning "A goes with B" can likewise produce "B goes with A". This only works once the learner already has the general skill of linking hearing a word to saying it; without that, nothing carries over. Variations: mix both directions in one session on the same object, so understanding and naming support each other; have the learner repeat the pair aloud as one phrase, which puts the reverse order in their own mouth.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a single referent is being wired under both speaker and listener control and only one role is (or needs to be) explicitly taught. The tell is directional harvest on one word: teaching runs comprehension-to-production or production-to-comprehension for the same stimulus — one-way training, interleaved two-way trials, or self-repetition rehearsal — and the reverse role is then emitted with no instruction ever delivered on it.


**Worked examples.**

- *self-echoic chant bridges the untrained reverse direction*
  - AB training on a unidirectional intraverbal relation automatically produces a reverse BA intraverbal relation


**See also.** `class-wide-function-transfer` — sibling propagation move: one trained relation reaching beyond what was directly taught, there across a class rather than across a direction.; `derived-relations-installation` — umbrella entry for derived/generative training designs; this is its train-one-direction-harvest-the-reverse form.; `generative-substrate-training` — sibling generativity move: both convert a small trained investment into untrained verbal behavior, here via a whole component set rather than one relation.


<a id="entry-71"></a>

### blank-occupant-obedience-slot

[#71](#entry-71) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

Raise the question of who the listener is to obey, offer yourself as the answer, then openly drop the question ("Is that me? ... Doesn't matter. Perhaps it's whoever you hear in the empty void your mind is"). Obedience is separated from any particular person and attached to whatever voice the listener hears, in this recording or any future one, leaving a lasting habit of obedience with no named owner. The move itself is out in the open, but its spread is not: the listener does not notice the conditioning becoming portable.


**When to reach for this.** The authority slot's occupant is deliberately blanked and generalized to any present or future voice — versus ownership language (names the operator as owner), a nested authority conduit (a specified higher figure), and agentless fate-authority (no slot at all, authority relocated to impersonal fact); the tell is the explicit discarding of the operator's identity.


**Risk.** Portable, self-targeting conditioning that generalizes out-of-session to arbitrary future voices — out-of-session reach without bounding, and the consent surface cannot name its future beneficiary.


**Why it works.** Conditioning generalizes along stimulus dimensions unless discrimination training narrows it; by explicitly refusing to specify the authority's identity, the script withholds the discriminative training that would confine obedience to one operator, so any sufficiently similar cue (a voice giving instructions in this format) recruits the response. The overt framing also keeps the listener's scrutiny on the question 'obey whom' while the actual change — that the answer slot has become a variable — passes unexamined. Falsifiable: it predicts subjects trained with this move show more response to a novel operator's voice than subjects trained with a named owner, which is directly testable. [plausible; stimulus generalization vs discrimination training; misdirected attention]


**Worked examples.**

- *Obedience slot with the occupant left blank*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, deep; the operator has just been giving obedience suggestions and raises the question herself.
  - **The move.** You're obeying — but who exactly are you obeying? Is that me? Hm. Doesn't matter. Perhaps it's just whoever happens to be speaking into the empty space your mind has become. Whoever's voice is in there. That's who you obey.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator raises the obvious question — who exactly is being submitted to? — offers herself as one possibility, and then drops the question rather than answering it: it makes no difference, and the answer may simply be whatever speaker happens to be present in the listener's emptied attention. The listener notices the question being asked but not that the answer has been left as a fillable blank, so what gets installed is an obedience slot with no fixed occupant, ready for this recording and for any voice after it.


**See also.** `authorship-laundering-meta-rule` — both generalize past a single install to a standing rule, but the meta-rule blanks the SOURCE of suggestions by reattributing content to the listener, while the blank-occupant slot blanks the AUTHORITY figure so obedience attaches to any future voice.; `interpretive-closure-meta-command` — both leave a variable deliberately unfilled so the listener supplies it — one blanks WHO is obeyed so any voice occupies the slot, the other blanks WHAT is commanded so the listener's own interpretation generates the act.; `nested-authority-conduit` — same slot-topology genus with the occupant specified versus blanked.; `object-of-no-properties` — both empty a slot in the operator/subject relation rather than filling it: one blanks who is to be obeyed, the other strips the listener of properties that could ground refusal. Their discriminators both define themselves against ownership language, so a reader will meet them at the same fork.; `operator-authority-assertion` — directly opposed treatments of the authority slot: one asserts the operator's own present standing as the ground for compliance, the other raises the question of who is to be obeyed and deliberately blanks the answer so the slot generalizes. One entry already names the other as its contrast.


<a id="entry-1439"></a>

### bodily-restraint

[#1439](#entry-1439) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: immersion · kind: recipe*

Creates the feeling of being tied up through words alone; the point is handing over control. Imaginary ropes are described one place at a time, wrists, then ankles, then waist, each 'tightening' and 'locking in place', so each step is small and easy to accept. Then the script adds that struggling only makes them tighter and that only the operator can release them. The result is felt helplessness where struggling or not noticing confirms the frame instead of breaking it. Variations: the step-by-step build described above; slipping the ropes in during a flood of pleasure, then saying they were already there and the listener was too deep to notice.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script builds physical restraint out of narration alone and uses it to hand bodily agency to the operator. The tell is ropes or bindings that exist only in the telling, paired with a struggle-makes-it-tighter clause, a release-only-by-permission clause, or a retroactive "you didn't even notice being tied" framing.


**Worked examples.**

- *struggle-amplifier with permission-gated release*
  - you could try to struggle against these ropes to get free, but the more you struggle, the tighter the ropes only get... the only way you can be released, is by me granting permission


**See also.** `catalepsy-as-ownership-reframe` — shares the immobility-as-agency-transfer axis, where a delivered inability to move is recoded as the operator's ownership or control.; `manufactured-resistance-theater` — shares the narrated-struggle axis, where the script performs the listener's resistance against a constructed restraint for them.; `motor-inhibition-convincer` — shares the suggested-motor-incapacity axis, where an inability to move is installed and then demonstrated to the listener.


<a id="entry-1518"></a>

### borrowed-precedent-legitimacy

[#1518](#entry-1518) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: framing*

The operator elicits or narrates a real autobiographical experience in which the target state already occurred with full social sanction — remembered surgical anesthesia — and frames the present suggestion as a re-activation of that known pattern rather than a novelty. Belief becomes cheap because the precedent is verified memory: the placebo is billed as 'a capsule which follows the exact nerve pattern of the previous anesthesia' so the subject will be 'anesthetized in every area where you were anesthetized before,' and the remembered IV drip already proved that surrender to a substance and to strangers was normal, sanctioned, and even pleasant ('it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that'). The precondition is that the subject has, or can vividly claim, the prior experience — the operator elicits it first ('Have you ever been anesthetized before?'). The move can carry a covert verification gate before anything irreversible is staked on it: a graded pain test (towel clips in tender areas) so the operator proceeds only on confirmed analgesia ('If he had felt it, I wouldn't have gone ahead with the surgery').


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target state has a genuine prior occurrence in the subject's own biography that can be recalled and mapped onto the present suggestion, so conviction is imported rather than built. The tell is a specific autobiographical memory being elicited or volunteered, followed by an explicit sameness assertion — 'this feels so similar to that,' 'anesthetized in every area where you were anesthetized before' — billing the new state as recurrence, not novelty. A covert go/no-go test before relying on the borrowed state is a secondary tell.


**Worked examples.**

- *remembered surgical anesthesia lends its legitimacy to a fictional 'medicine'*
  - It took hold so fast as I babbled nonsense about being so easy to hypnotize... telling these total strangers all my secrets so readily, but it felt right at the time. This feels so similar to that


**See also.** `cognitive-convincer` — same self-evidence axis: the subject's own noticed experience supplies the proof the operator would otherwise have to assert.; `fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal` — same memory-as-install-vehicle axis, run on fabricated recollections instead of verified ones.; `front-matter-reader-positioning` — shares the borrowed-legitimacy axis: an already-sanctioned precedent or lineage lets the new material arrive pre-validated.; `pseudo-orientation-in-time` — shares the recall-frame axis: content delivered as remembered rather than proposed is cheap to believe.


<a id="entry-1392"></a>

### borrowed-structural-coercion-precondition

[#1392](#entry-1392) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing · kind: container*

Rather than building pressure within the session, the operator runs the persuasion inside a hierarchy that already exists and that they did not create: an employer who requires attendance, a chain of command, a programme a court or school mandates. That existing power does the compliance work before anything is said, because refusing now costs a job or a place, not just awkwardness. And since everyone showed up, being there already looks like partial agreement, so the operator can speak to the room as if it had opted in. The operator's own words never have to carry the pressure, which keeps it deniable.


**When to reach for this.** The leverage is BORROWED — a coercive relation that predates the encounter and that the operator did not create — so cost-of-refusal, not persuasiveness, does the compliance work. Split from `borrowed-reflex-recruitment` (440), the true structural cousin: 440 also imports something pre-existing, but every variant imports an asset whose LEGITIMACY the subject already grants (a fluent reflex, a real memory, a verified prior state, a cultural ritual, an adjacent working suggestion), and the import buys credibility or momentum. This imports an enforceable relation whose COST OF REFUSAL transfers, and buys attendance regardless of credibility. Legitimacy-transfer vs cost-of-refusal-transfer is the whole split.


**Why it works.** Two established findings apply. First, compliance depends heavily on the cost of refusing rather than on how persuasive the message is; behaviour can change without attitudes changing. Second, research on insufficient justification predicts the opposite of what an operator might hope: someone who can point to an outside mandate has a ready explanation for being there that has nothing to do with their own views, so they are less likely to take the message to heart. That tension is the useful, testable part: this setup should reliably get attendance and outward compliance but weaker private attitude change than a genuinely voluntary version. Testable: if mandated attendees showed the same lasting belief change after the mandate ended as volunteers with matching starting attitudes, the account is wrong in an important way; if they showed more, the insufficient-justification prediction is reversed.


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-existing mandate cited once, then presence read as assent*
  - **Setup.** Opening minutes of a session the subject attends because a standing obligation requires it — a workplace mandate, a court-ordered program, a chain of command — and which the operator neither created nor can lift.
  - **The move.** You're all on the roster for the full ninety minutes, so let's not pretend anyone's deciding whether to be here — that was decided upstairs. What's left to you is how you spend it. And since you did show up, I'm going to take that as you being ready to work, and start where people who are ready start: eyes closed, hands flat on your knees.
  - **Why it lands.** The cost of walking out is a job or a placement rather than an awkward moment, so refusal is priced out before any content is offered, and the operator's own material never has to be persuasive. Watch for compliance that arrives without the usual negotiating look — hands go flat, eyes close, and nobody asks what this is for.


<a id="entry-560"></a>

### boundary-dissolution-no-not-operator-region

[#560](#entry-560) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: foreclosure · kind: container*

One sustained move erases every distinction the listener could use to mark where the operator's influence stops: sleep, hypnosis, and arousal are equated; dreaming, trance, and waking are equated; the listener's deeper mind is equated with the operator; and the listener's wants with the operator's wants. Because the same erasing move is repeated across several unrelated areas, undoing any one equation doesn't restore a dividing line. The intended result is that no part of the mind is left that the listener can point to as definitely not the operator's.


**When to reach for this.** A writer reaches for this entry when one and the same boundary-erasing operation is run on axis after axis across the text: sleep, trance and arousal named as one thing; dreaming, trancing and the muzzy state after named as one thing; the operator named as the voice of the listener's own deeper mind; and what the listener wants defined as what the operator wants them to want. The observable tell is the repetition of the identical equivalence move across multiple independent axes, wired so that removing any single equivalence still restores no boundary. The cumulative payload is territorial: by the end, no mental region remains that the listener can point to as definitively not-operator.


**Risk.** Leaves no mental territory the listener can identify as not-operator, eroding the ground on which a refusal or verification could stand — channel-adjacent erosion, so high.


**Why it works.** Judging where one's own agency ends depends on a comparator that checks whether an experience matches self-generated intention; deliberately equating categories that the comparator relies on (asleep/hypnotized, my wants/your wants) removes the distinctions the check needs to run, so no region can be flagged as externally caused. Repeating the same operation across independent axes matters because a single blurred distinction can be repaired from a neighbouring intact one, whereas simultaneous blurring across axes leaves no intact reference. Falsifiable: subjects given the equivalences on one axis only should retain measurable ability to identify externally-sourced content; the claim predicts multi-axis versions degrade that discrimination substantially more. [speculative; self/other source discrimination — the comparator account is contested and the multi-axis claim is untested]


**Worked examples.**

- *No territory left that is not the operator*
  - **Setup.** Consolidation stretch late in the file; the same equivalence operation is run across four independent axes in one block.
  - **The move.** Sleep and trance and being turned on are all one thing — you've never really been able to tell them apart, and now you don't have to. Dreaming, drifting, and that muzzy half hour after you wake are all one place, and I'm in all of them. That quiet voice underneath your thoughts is mine, and always was — and what you want is simply what I want you to want, so there's nothing left in there belonging to anybody else.
  - **Why it lands.** The same move is run on axis after axis: sleep and trance and arousal are named as one thing; dreaming and trancing and the muzzy state afterwards are named as one thing; the operator is named as the voice of the listener's own deeper mind; and what the listener wants is defined as what the operator wants them to want. No single one of these is load-bearing — pull any one out and the others still leave nowhere to stand and nothing left to call one's own.


**See also.** `count-erosion-deepener` — both work by plurality rather than depth: the same removal applied across several independent targets so no single repair restores the lost footing. One erases boundaries across independent axes, the other dismantles ordered cognitive anchors in sequence through a single perceptual stream. Useful contrast on whether the multiplicity is simultaneous or staged.; `isolation-by-annexation` — both delete the listener's outside reference point and are the closest neighbours to each other. One erases boundaries by asserting the same equivalence across multiple independent axes so no territory reads as not-operator; the other leaves boundaries intact and captures the sources a counter-frame would draw on, relabelling them as the operator's. Equivalence versus capture is the line.


<a id="entry-1524"></a>

### boundary-non-return-loop-design

[#1524](#entry-1524) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The file deliberately has no real exit. Either there is no wake-up at all and the last line matches the first, so the end flows straight back into the start, or the 'wake-up' keeps them in role ('wake slowly, my slave, life has just begun') with no count-up and no undoing of what was built. Lines like 'you'll keep coming back' come true by simply replaying it, and stopping takes an active choice while letting it loop takes none. Variations: across a series, each part relies on what earlier parts installed and leaves the listener ready for the next.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the closure work lives at the edges of the file and across plays or parts, not inside any passage. The tell is what the boundary lacks — no wake-up, no count-up, no closure beat, a tail that seams to the head or to the next installment — paired with content that treats repetition as already-having-happened, so each replay retroactively confirms the artifact's claims.


**Worked examples.**

- *replay bootstraps the artifact's own confirming history*
  - "You come back again and again" becomes true on the second listen by mechanical fact. The script bootstraps its own history with each loop, so the equation chain (M3) and the retroactive history (M5) gain weight purely through replay, without any new content.


**See also.** `deferred-terminus-conversion` — shares the closure-withheld axis, with the release or payoff relocated outside the file's boundary to drive continuation.; `emergence-negative-space` — shares the omitted-emergence axis: the missing return ramp is itself the structural feature that dissolves the in-trance/out-of-trance boundary.; `loop-as-mechanism-no-dismount` — shares the replay axis: the looping format makes the script's own again-and-again claims self-fulfilling.


<a id="entry-1231"></a>

### bounded-failure-counterweight

[#1231](#entry-1231) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

A discrete permission-to-leave-undone move that locally inverts a compulsion the surrounding script builds. After completing all reachable work, the operator points out one thing that cannot be done and walks the listener through accepting it gracefully ("what you can't do at the moment it's okay to leave it aside"), inoculating against the perfectionism-freeze / completion-overrun the same script's rehearsal installs. It is a bounded-failure counterweight embedded amid material driving the opposite compulsion.


**When to reach for this.** A therapeutic bounded-failure permission that COUNTERWEIGHTS a compulsion installed elsewhere in the same script — it narrows/limits rather than intensifies.


**Risk.** Welfare-protective — grants permission to leave work undone to counter a perfectionism drive; reversible, session-scoped, no consent surface. Positive-governance.


**Why it works.** Explicit permission to leave something undone works by removing the perfectionistic contingency — when completion is framed as all-or-nothing, a single unreachable item invalidates the whole effort and triggers abandonment, whereas a pre-authorized partial outcome keeps the effort classed as success. This is the standard behavioural-activation and relapse-prevention logic around all-or-nothing thinking, where the pre-agreed lapse is what prevents the lapse from becoming collapse. Its placement amid opposite-pushing material matters because permission granted by the same source that set the demand is credible in a way self-granted permission is not. Falsifiable: it predicts lower abandonment and lower distress at an unreachable item when the permission clause is present than when the identical script omits it. [plausible; all-or-nothing thinking and completion contingencies; abstinence-violation effect / pre-authorized lapse]


**Worked examples.**

- *One task named as fine to leave undone*
  - **Setup.** Late in a task-rehearsal sequence; listener has just completed everything reachable and dwelt on the satisfaction.
  - **The move.** Look up at the top of that window — the corner you can't get to without a ladder you don't own. That one doesn't get done today. Stay with that a second, because this part matters: you did what was in reach, and the bit that wasn't stays where it is, and it doesn't spoil any of the rest. Say it back — this one I leave. Good. Now put the cloth down and be finished.
  - **Why it lands.** The rehearsal has the listener work through a room until every reachable surface is finished and the satisfaction of finishing is dwelt on at length. Then the operator points out one part that is out of reach with the tools at hand, and holds the listener there a moment: this one does not get done today, and that is allowed — you do what is in reach and set the rest aside without it souring the rest. It is a single beat, with completion-pressure on both sides of it, and it exists to stop the same rehearsal from turning into a compulsion that cannot stop.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — both are genuine governance moves that narrow rather than extend the operator's reach, and both are surrounded by material pushing the opposite way. One affirms the standing right to stop; the other grants permission to leave a specific thing undone as a counterweight to an installed compulsion. Useful for a reader auditing which safety-shaped moves are real.; `comfort-permission` — both are welfare-facing permission moves that pre-empt a failure reading: one licenses bodily or emotional noise so it does not read as trance failure, the other licenses leaving a task undone so it does not read as personal failure. A reader looking for the permission-grant family gains from the pairing.; `engineered-failure-harvest` — opposite uses of engineered failure. One arranges a task the listener genuinely cannot pass and then cashes the failure as the target result; the other grants permission to leave one thing undone specifically to counterweight a compulsion the same material installs. The contrast clarifies both.; `granted-exit-disarm` — the sharpest available contrast on permission-giving: identical surface form, opposite answers to who ends up constrained. One supplies an assurance whose acceptance stands down protective monitoring and widens operator licence; the other is a genuine welfare permission that narrows what the script demands.


<a id="entry-1569"></a>

### breath-tingle-convincer

[#1569](#entry-1569) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: framing · kind: recipe*

Describe the sensation before the breathing starts, so it is recognized as proof when it arrives. Keep the breathing short and stop once tingling or light-headedness appears; overdoing it is unsafe. What is really happening is the body's response to overbreathing being read as the trigger working.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 3 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Tell them a tingle or light head means the trigger is working, then have them breathe fast or deep until they feel exactly that.


<a id="entry-1525"></a>

### build-and-dismantle-scene

[#1525](#entry-1525) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: arc-topology · kind: recipe*

A vivid sensory referent is deliberately furnished and given real experiential weight, then destroyed, and the resulting referent-void is filled with the operator's own repeated tokens. Immersion here is technical rather than stylistic: the goal is to remove every reference frame except the operator's voice, executed as a stepwise removal of competing referents. By the late mantra section the listener has no environment, no narrative, and no body schema being actively maintained — only the voice. Closure is achieved by attentional monopoly: once every competing frame has been deleted, nothing remains for attention to hold onto outside the operator's stream.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a piece spends real craft building a rich scene and then spends equal craft dismantling it, refilling the emptied space with a small looping vocabulary. The tell is the build-destroy-refill sequence: a sensory referent is provided, systematically taken apart, and its void repopulated with operator tokens until the voice is the sole remaining reference frame.


**Worked examples.**

- *stepwise deletion of competing reference frames*
  - Immersion here is technical: the goal is to remove every reference frame except the operator's voice. M2 (bath) provides a sensory referent, M3 destroys it, M4 fills the resulting referent-void with operator tokens.


**See also.** `claim-staircase` — shares the voice-to-interior axis: the operator's voice promoted stepwise until it is the listener's whole remaining world.; `closed-vocabulary-lexical-narrowing` — shares the shrink-the-accessible-field axis, there applied to the semantic field via a small closed set of operator-chosen words.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — the build-destroy-refill referent deletion appears there as one pooled operation producing whole-artifact reachability closure.


<a id="entry-1425"></a>

### capacity-ceiling-overreach-inversion

[#1425](#entry-1425) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

A warning. When a subject is holding a delicate trained balance, such as a response trained against a competing urge, you can widen what you ask of it bit by bit and it keeps working, until suddenly it does not. There is no way to tell in advance where the limit is, and everything looks fine right up to it. Past the limit the balance does not wear down gently: it flips into the opposite reaction, and the damage spreads back onto earlier triggers that were solid, so they stop working too. Because success gives no early warning, an operator pushing by results only finds the limit by breaking it.


**When to reach for this.** The two properties that carry it: a tolerance ceiling not measurable in advance (performance up to it looks healthy, so there is no leading indicator for an operator titrating by observed success), and RETROACTIVE spread — collapse damages cues and installs that were stable and were not under demand at the time. Against 434 shaping-successive-approximation, the sharpest neighbour: shaping's deterioration is graded, scoped to the response being trained, and explicitly recoverable by dropping back to the last successful approximation (the dip-and-recover signature is read as the procedure WORKING); here failure is abrupt, disproportionate to the final increment, inverts the balance into its opposite process, and propagates backward onto untouched material. Against 173 capacity-saturation-overload: a live reversible load applied AS an induction — lift the load and capacity returns; this crosses a training-tolerance ceiling and leaves persistent damage. Against 1239 doubt-injection-state-collapse: one running effect broken by re-arming judgment against it, damage scoped to that effect with no backward spread. Against 850 anchor-collapse-state-jamming: disorganization produced ON PURPOSE as the precondition for integration; nothing here is collapsed deliberately and there is no constructive endpoint. Against 86 irresolvable-input-confusion: a delivered vehicle with an intended effect. This is the only entry describing unintended structural collapse rather than a targeted move.


**Why it works.** The effect itself was shown experimentally: pushing a subject's discriminations past what they can tolerate produces a sudden, outsized breakdown that also disturbs responses that had been stable. That observation has held up. The explanation has not. The original account, about protective inhibition exceeding a capacity, is not supported. The modern reading is only a description: behaviour held up by opposing processes near their limit has little margin, so a small extra demand can cause a large change. No specific brain mechanism is known. Treat the ceiling as a tolerance you discover, not a quantity you can measure. Two predictions can be checked. Collapse should be sudden and out of proportion to the last push; if decline is gradual, this is ordinary over-training. And damage should spread to responses that were not being trained at the time; if only the trained response suffers, the spreading claim is wrong.


**Worked examples.**

- *Widening the demand past an unmeasurable ceiling; retroactive collapse*
  - **Setup.** Hazard illustration. A response has been trained against a competing disposition and has held through several clean widenings; the operator, reading healthy performance, widens once more.
  - **The move.** You've held it with your eyes closed, and with them open, and with the room quiet. Now do it with the door open and someone else in the room — same as before, just wider.
  - **Why it lands.** Every trial up to the ceiling looked healthy, so observed success gave no leading indicator; past it the balance does not degrade gracefully but flips into its opposite process. What identifies this rather than ordinary shaping deterioration is the backward spread — the operator finds that cues which were solid and were not under demand at all have also stopped working, and dropping back to the last successful step does not restore them.


<a id="entry-926"></a>

### carrier-is-cargo-fusion

[#926](#entry-926) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: carrier-binding*

The operator makes the thing that carries the trigger identical to the behaviour being asked for, so there is no separate step to refuse. Example: wearing a perfume is both a requested purchase and the cue that keeps the effect going with every breath; declining the trigger means declining the perfume too. Upkeep can also be pinned to other constant everyday channels: saying 'hello' to people, the inner voice, glancing in mirrors.


**When to reach for this.** Not a magnitude/count move (more channels) but a topology fusion (carrier = cargo).


**Risk.** Removes the refusal channel for the persistence install (cannot decline the trigger without declining the surface behavior) and reaches out-of-session on always-on ambient channels — channel erosion plus unbounded out-of-session reach.


**Why it works.** The lever is choice-architecture bundling: presenting two items as one indivisible option means refusal forfeits the desired component, and loss aversion makes that trade unattractive. The scent element adds odour-based evaluative conditioning, which acquires readily and shows good long-term retention — but the claim that odour cues are habituation-free is backwards, since olfactory habituation is unusually fast and continuous exposure drops the cue out of awareness within minutes, so the cue works on re-presentation after a gap rather than sustained wear. Falsifiable: unbundling the carrier into a separately declinable step should raise refusal rates with nothing else changed. [plausible; bundled choice architecture / loss aversion; olfactory evaluative conditioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *The reminder cue hidden inside the ask itself*
  - **Setup.** The behavioral list is being handed over near the end of the session; ordinary lifestyle asks are being framed as the harmless part.
  - **The move.** So — the small everyday things. You'll buy a bottle of the vanilla perfume and you'll wear it, every day, wrists and throat, before you leave the house. And here's the other half of it: that scent is what keeps all of this alive. Every breath you take of it puts the training back in, top-up after top-up, all day long, whether you're thinking about me or not. Same with the word 'hello' — every time it leaves your mouth, and every mirror you pass.
  - **Why it lands.** The behavioural list the listener is asked to adopt includes acquiring and using a particular everyday item — and that same item is separately made the thing that reloads the conditioning, continuously, for as long as it is in use. There is no moment where an anchor is offered for acceptance on its own; to decline the always-on reminder the listener would have to decline the ordinary lifestyle instruction, which was framed as the harmless part. Other channels are loaded the same way, each hooked to something that recurs many times a day without anyone deciding to trigger it — but this one is where carrier and cargo are the same object.


**See also.** `object-ritual-loop` — both engineer post-session persistence around an acquired object and can look identical on the surface. One chains cue, purchase, ritual and re-listening into a self-sustaining loop whose payload is perpetuation; the other fuses the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral ask so there is no separable install step to refuse. Loop shape versus topology fusion.; `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — both are topology moves that remove a separable refusal point: several payloads yoked to one recurring stimulus, versus the persistence carrier fused into the behaviour being asked for. Different fusions, same design goal of leaving no standalone thing to decline.; `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` — these frequently co-occur on the same always-present social cue and the same fixed-order commitment inventory, so they read as one move on first pass. One turns on fusing the reinforcement carrier into the behavioral payload so no refusable install step exists; the other turns on the cue never being named as a trigger plus a one-way self-extending ladder. Separable levers that often ride together.


<a id="entry-1527"></a>

### case-then-formalize

[#1527](#entry-1527) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

A vivid concrete case is presented first and the formal apparatus is fitted onto it afterward, so the model reads as discovered in the phenomenon rather than imposed on it. A verbatim transcript alternates with formalizing commentary that retro-fits vocabulary onto moves performed without it — a famously articulate subject "spontaneously arrives at a technique which we have formalized," making the model look like natural law — while ordinary-case replication (the Mary Lou insertion) converts "Erickson did this with a genius" into "you can do this with a 45-year-old in a training group," carrying the generalization claim. The case narrative and the meta-model commentary are arranged so each licenses the other: the vivid phenomena supply the reader's belief that something real is happening, the apparatus then claims to explain it, and once the frame is accepted for the easy case, harder cases inherit credibility by analogy. The same ordering runs in textbook form: the chapter leads with a concrete, emotionally legible payoff, and only after the reader is impressed does the text name the properties — so every abstraction has already been cashed out in a concrete win before it is asked to be believed.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the sequencing itself does the persuading: demonstration before apparatus, with the demonstration licensing the abstraction. The tell is temporal order — the reader meets the phenomenon as a story or a concrete win first, and the formal vocabulary arrives afterward as a name for something already believed, often with an ordinary-case replication carrying the generalization from exceptional exhibit to "you can do this too."


**Worked examples.**

- *demo-first ordering that licenses the apparatus*
  - so the model appears *discovered in* the master's behavior, not imposed.


**See also.** `reader-assent-architecture` — shares the stance-priming axis: the reader's acceptance of a method is arranged before the method is stated, as in its follow-and-formalize instance.; `reader-assent-engineering` — the container for reader-targeted rhetorical architecture, which pools transcript-then-formalize and ordinary-case replication among its levers.


<a id="entry-1509"></a>

### chain-interruption-evocation

[#1509](#entry-1509) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Let the subject start a routine they can do and want to finish, then block one step partway through: the scissors are missing, the jacket zip won't go. Being stuck just short of the payoff makes the missing piece suddenly valuable. The block is lifted only when they produce the new behaviour being taught, usually asking for it, so the new behaviour rides on the momentum of the routine. To confirm it is the wanting doing the work, some runs supply the missing item in advance and the request disappears. The interruption needs to be mildly frustrating: too little gives no motivation, too much becomes real distress.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the subject already runs a fluent multi-step routine toward something they want and you need to install a brand-new response the routine never required, without adding any external reward. The tell is a deliberately withheld mid-sequence piece whose restoration is contingent on the new behavior — the motivation is harvested from blocked momentum toward the terminal payoff.


**Worked examples.**

- *interrupted link established as a reinforcer, release gated on the new response*
  - By interrupting the chains at the point at which these additional objects (or actions) are needed, practitioners can momentarily establish them as reinforcers and contrive opportunities to teach a wider variety of mands


**See also.** `behavior-chaining` — chain-structure axis: the dual-function stimulus links assembled there are the routine this move interrupts for leverage.; `conditioned-motivation-by-pairing` — conditioned-MO axis: pairing history and chain-blocking are sibling routes to firing motivation without the raw need.; `motivating-operation-engineering` — contrived-value-spike axis: blocking a link mid-chain is a transitive instance of the value shift this entry generalizes.


<a id="entry-1514"></a>

### chain-link-severing

[#1514](#entry-1514) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Many habits are chains of steps, each step leading to the next and the whole thing paid for by the final payoff. Take that payoff away and the earlier steps weaken too, so the chain falls apart from the end backwards. Variations: withhold the final payoff; give the payoff freely beforehand so it is no longer wanted; cut a single link by rewarding a later step every time it happens, inside or outside the chain, so the earlier step stops leading anywhere and fades while the later step stays intact.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the unwanted behavior is a multi-step sequence run toward one payoff and the goal is to make the whole run die — or one early link drop out — without confronting every step individually. The tell is that the operator touches only the terminal reward (withholds it, pre-satiates it, or pays it out unconditionally) and expects responses far upstream to decline on their own through the chain's internal links.


**Worked examples.**

- *backward propagation of terminal-link extinction*
  - Because each chain link's stimulus is both conditioned reinforcer for the prior response and SD for the next, removing the terminal payoff strips the upstream stimuli of their reinforcing function, so earlier responses decline too.


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation (retained core: cue/materials editing)` — works the same behavior chain from the opposite end, collapsing it by attacking the terminal payoff rather than the initiating stimulus.; `behavior-chaining` — build direction of the same chaining axis: assembling the sequence this move unravels.; `dual-function-chain-stimulus` — the dual-function chain-stimulus principle whose back-propagating value this severing move drains.; `reinforcement-extinction` — extinction genus carrying the chain-structured-suppression facet this entry matured from.


<a id="entry-1430"></a>

### chance-pairing-self-maintaining-ritual

[#1430](#entry-1430) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering*

If rewards arrive on a timer, unrelated to anything the subject does, whatever they happened to be doing just before gets strengthened. Because that action now happens more often, it is more likely to come just before the next reward too, which strengthens it again. So a pointless ritual can form and keep itself going with nobody designing it, and removing 'the reason' for it does nothing, because there never was one. It only takes hold when the action was already fairly frequent. An operator can seed one deliberately by handing out reward on a clock. Variations: a one-off coincidence that then fades normally; a self-feeding loop where extinction stalls.


**When to reach for this.** Every nearby closed loop in the shipped taxonomy is operator-AUTHORED; this one has no author. compounding-dependency-loop (536) is a deliberately constructed cure-feeds-disease circuit where the operator installs both the escalating state and its designated relief route. bidirectional-reentry-loop (1332) is two cues deliberately installed to fire each other, with both legs over-broadened on purpose. perpetual-obligation-ledger (506) is an operator structurally over-repaying to keep a debt open — an intentional accounting move on an inter-agent quantity, not an emergent one on a rate. failure-pre-attribution (862) pre-assigns the meaning of a null outcome; that is an interpretive frame supplied by the operator, whereas nothing here is interpreted or supplied at all. It is also distinct from the one-clause reinforcement-leak guards that tell an operator to avoid accidental pairings: those name it as a hazard to prevent, this specifies the positive-feedback structure that makes it self-sustaining, which is what an operator needs in order to recognize or deliberately seed one.


**Why it works.** Rewards that arrive regardless of behaviour really do produce odd, persistent habits; this has been shown repeatedly. But the usual "superstition" explanation has been seriously challenged. A well-known replication found that much of the behaviour was the animal's natural behaviour triggered by the timing of rewards, not accidental strengthening of random acts. So some timed reward schedules produce self-sustaining arbitrary rituals and some produce typical natural behaviour, depending on the subject and the interval. It is not universal, and the question is still open. It can be tested: if chance pairing is at work, the rituals should differ from subject to subject and follow each one's own early coincidences. If everyone ends up doing the same thing, chance pairing is not the cause. Cancelling the reward whenever the behaviour occurs should also end a chance-built ritual, while timing-driven behaviour would persist.


**Worked examples.**

- *Failure mode — a clock-based payoff installs a private ritual nobody wrote*
  - **Setup.** A recurring session where praise or a reward cue lands on a fixed interval (top of the hour, end of segment) regardless of what the subject is doing.
  - **The move.** Every fifteen minutes I'll tell you you're doing beautifully. It won't be because of anything in particular — it's just the clock.
  - **Why it lands.** Interval-timed delivery strengthens whatever happened to precede it, so the subject builds a stereotyped pause-then-burst pattern and defends it as the thing that works. Operator observes an unrequested small behaviour appearing just before each scheduled delivery, and resistance when asked to drop it.
- *Usable move — clock-scheduled reward left to grow its own ritual*
  - **Setup.** A reward is delivered on a timer, and on purpose no target behaviour is named, so whatever the subject happens to be doing gets picked up.
  - **The move.** There's no rule here and nothing you have to get right. Every few minutes the tone will sound and you'll feel that warm drop — and after a while you'll notice you've started doing some small thing just before it comes. Whatever that turns out to be, keep it. It's yours, not mine.
  - **Why it lands.** The subject authors a private ritual they experience as self-discovered rather than instructed, which makes it unusually durable and unusually hard to argue them out of. Operator observes the idiosyncratic behaviour stabilising within a few sessions without ever having specified it.
- *Reward on a fixed clock, seeded by naming whatever preceded it*
  - **Setup.** You are dispensing praise or reward on your own timer — every few minutes regardless of what the subject does — and one delivery has just landed.
  - **The move.** Good — and I notice you had your hands folded just then. Hold them like that. There you go.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is being reinforced deliberately; the folded hands merely happened to precede a scheduled delivery, and naming them raises their rate so they are more likely to precede the next one. Observable over a session: the posture appears at a stable nonzero floor and persists after the operator stops commenting on it, and removing the stated 'reason' for it changes nothing, because there was never a contingency to break.


**Realizations** (1): `adventitious-contingency-capture`


<a id="entry-1493"></a>

### choice-affordance-removal

[#1493](#entry-1493) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: foreclosure*

Choicelessness is staged as a property of the imagined environment rather than commanded: the elevator has "no buttons in here for you to push. You have no choices to make," or the held middle state is framed as aversive dissonance ("a place you'd rather not be") with "down" pre-loaded as the only named relief. Agency-suspension is experienced as ambient fact — the scene is a vector field with one attractor — so obedience or descent becomes the only remaining gravity and no obedience demand ever has to be issued at the moment of capture. Alternative exits are either absent from the scene's construction or named only as theoretical preference, never offered as structural relief from the middle. The staging can escalate to full dissolution of the scaffolding itself — "everything solid falls out from under you" — leaving the listener held aloft by nothing but "your desire to heed my call," pure dependence presented as the scene's physics.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a scene's geography does the coercing: an imagined space built with no affordance for any behavior but the desired one, or a middle state framed so aversive that a single pre-named exit is the only relief. The tell is that choicelessness is narrated as an ambient fact of the environment ("no buttons," "you have no choices to make") rather than commanded, and the desired behavior arrives as the topology's lone attractor.


**Worked examples.**

- *choicelessness built into the imagined environment*
  - There are no buttons in here for you to push. You have no choices to make. Only by your obedience. Will you get where you're going.


**See also.** `closed-vocabulary-lexical-narrowing` — same shrinking-the-accessible-space axis applied to a different substrate: there the vocabulary is narrowed to operator-chosen words, here the behavioral affordances are narrowed to one attractor.; `no-exit-response-closure` — both close the listener's option space — no-exit-response-closure by pre-mapping every possible response to the same outcome, this entry by building scenes in which the options never exist.


<a id="entry-692"></a>

### class-collision-humor

[#692](#entry-692) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering*

Some words belong to two categories at once; 'flies' is both a verb and an insect. The speaker first sets up one reading ('time flies like an arrow'), then abruptly forces the other ('fruit flies like a banana'). The listener is pulled one way and then the other in quick succession, and that whiplash between two readings is what produces the laugh or groan. The skill is in the setup and the reversal, not in what the joke is about.


**When to reach for this.** Requires a stimulus with real dual class membership plus a reversible context.


**Risk.** Produces a humor/groan response via a benign match-to-sample whiplash; session-scoped, reversible, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Comprehension involves rapid commitment to one parse; the reversal forces a garden-path re-analysis, and the incongruity-resolution account of humour holds that the pleasure comes from detecting and resolving the mismatch, not from the content. The groan response is the cost signal of the re-parse. Falsifiable: if listeners who do not hold both readings of the ambiguous term (e.g. non-native speakers lacking the verb sense) still find it funny, the dual-class-membership account is wrong. [established; incongruity-resolution theory of humour; garden-path reanalysis]


**Worked examples.**

- *Priming one class membership, then reversing the context*
  - "the pun can be deliberately set up to evoke conflicting classes" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


<a id="entry-1548"></a>

### class-wide-function-transfer

[#1548](#entry-1548) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Attach a feeling or reaction to one member of a group, and the whole group takes it on, including members the person has never met. One sentence like "spiders are dangerous" links a familiar category to a loaded word; from then on every member, and similar creatures like ants, brings up the reaction without ever being paired with it. The only thing to push back against is that one sentence. Variation: teach just two links, "A is the opposite of B" and "B is the opposite of C", and C starts acting like A without ever being paired with it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when one sentence or one trained link is meant to change the subject's reaction to many stimuli at once, including instances never encountered. The tell is a valence or behavioral function landing on class members that were never directly conditioned or paired — delivered through category membership, equivalence, or a relational chain — so the reach of the single move is the whole class, unseen instances included.


**Worked examples.**

- *one intraverbal rewrites the whole class's function*
  - encountering any member of the class evokes the intraverbal


**See also.** `ambient-yes` — both attach a valence or function that propagates across a whole class of everyday referents rather than a single cue.; `bidirectional-naming-transfer` — sibling propagation move: one trained relation reaching beyond what was directly taught, there across a class rather than across a direction.; `derived-relations-installation` — umbrella entry for derived/generative training designs; this is its function-transfer-across-a-class form.; `respondent-stimulus-pairing` — same axis of attaching a reaction to a stimulus — there by direct pairing with an eliciting stimulus, here by propagation through class structure.


<a id="entry-1575"></a>

### clicker-training

[#1575](#entry-1575) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering · kind: recipe*

Charge the marker before you use it by pairing the click with a treat many times. Then click at the exact moment the wanted behaviour happens, follow every click with a treat, and shape toward the goal by clicking closer and closer attempts. Whether a clicker works better than a spoken marker is unclear: the evidence is mixed, and studies in people are few.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Pair a click with a treat until the click feels good, then click the exact moment of the wanted behaviour and follow with a treat.


<a id="entry-1460"></a>

### closed-vocabulary-lexical-narrowing

[#1460](#entry-1460) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: attention*

Once the listener is already well under, tell them there are now only ten words they can focus on, all loaded ones (devotion, submission, arousal, surrender, obedience, control, release...), and that every other word is just a bridge between them. Recite the list in shifting orders, sometimes swapping a word, and build odd sentences almost entirely out of list words. Any thought they try to have is meant to pass through one of the loaded words. Forgetting is offered as a side effect rather than a command: their name and address feel 'slippery' because those words aren't on the list. It would sound silly as an opener.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator legislates vocabulary itself — an explicit closed list of permitted focus-words, with the rest of language demoted to connective tissue between them. The tell is the recited list: a short roster of loaded words repeated in varying orders, grammatically odd sentences assembled almost entirely from list members, and memory effects attributed to words falling outside the list rather than to any standalone amnesia command.


**Worked examples.**

- *non-list words demoted to bridges between the loaded lexicon*
  - You can only think of other words as bridges between the only 10 important words you can remember so far


**See also.** `build-and-dismantle-scene` — shares the shrink-the-accessible-field axis, there applied to the semantic field via a small closed set of operator-chosen words.; `choice-affordance-removal` — same shrinking-the-accessible-space axis applied to a different substrate: there the vocabulary is narrowed to operator-chosen words, here the behavioral affordances are narrowed to one attractor.; `gradient-word-reification-into-device` — shares the words-as-operative-objects axis: language itself escalated into the controlling apparatus.; `symptom-word-weaponization` — shares the loaded-word lexical lever: operator-chosen emotionally charged vocabulary doing the suggestive work.


<a id="entry-1501"></a>

### cognitive-loss-pleasure-relabel

[#1501](#entry-1501) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: conditioning*

Every cognitive loss suggested (forgetting, emptiness, missing thoughts, fears, will, memories) is paired in the same breath with reward language: 'Forgetting feels wonderful', 'Feeling so empty. Feels wonderful', or a repeated run of 'the pleasure that comes from having no...' across several faculties. Dense repetition while the listener feels good makes the pairing stick until it holds on its own. Its job is protective rather than motivating: noticing something is missing would normally cause alarm and break the trance, and this turns that alarm into pleasure, closing off the most common way people come out on their own. It works underneath the main forgetting or emptying suggestions so they can run without interruption, rather than doing anything by itself. The repeated rhythm also deepens.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script that is stripping mental content pairs each named absence, in the same sentence or breath, with a pleasure word. The tell is reward language attached directly to the loss noun itself — "forgetting feels wonderful," "the pleasure that comes from having no thoughts" — repeated as a tag while removal work is in progress, so that noticing the loss lands as pleasant instead of alarming.


**Worked examples.**

- *anaphoric pleasure-tagging of each removed faculty*
  - the pleasure that comes from having no thoughts, the pleasure that comes from having no fears, the pleasure that comes from having no will, the pleasure that comes from having no reservations, the pleasure that comes from having no memories


**See also.** `closed-affect-loop` — shares the defensive goal of closing off affective routes by which the frame could be disconfirmed or trance broken.; `valence-laundering-collapse-ring` — both launder the valence of loss-vocabulary, 602 through a semantic equivalence ring rather than concurrent reward-tagging.; `value-hierarchy-inversion` — both make a loss read as gain, 168 by reranking an existing value hierarchy rather than tagging the absence itself.


<a id="entry-1399"></a>

### collateral-suppression-spread

[#1399](#entry-1399) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

Weakening one trigger also weakens its neighbours, even ones never touched: triggers that share the same sense, the same body area or similar meaning, and at worst the natural reflex the whole group was built on. The closer a neighbour is to the one being removed, the more it loses. This matters for safety: switching off a single trigger can quietly dampen nearby responses, leaving the person flatter overall than anyone intended, and the loss only shows up the next time one of those neighbours is called on.


**When to reach for this.** Against trigger-network-mutual-binding: that is a DELIBERATELY cross-wired web whose topology is the authored payload, and what propagates through it is ACTIVATION. This is the involuntary inverse — no wiring was authored, the cluster is merely similar cues, and what propagates is suppression. Against counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening: that names the intended weakening of one targeted cue; this names what happens to the cues nobody targeted, and it is the reason the targeted move needs a blast-radius check. Against multi-modal-trigger and pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier: both spread ONE authored payload across channels or slots by design; here nothing is spread by the operator at all — the diffusion is a property of the substrate. Not reinforcement-extinction's documented side-effect cascade (burst, recovery, resurgence), all of which happen to the TARGET behavior; the object here is untargeted siblings.


**Why it works.** Learned responses are keyed to cue regions rather than to point stimuli, so both excitation and inhibition generalize along the same similarity gradients — which means a suppression trained at one point necessarily lands, in reduced measure, on everything near it, and the collateral loss should fall off monotonically with distance from the attacked cue. Falsifiable: probe siblings at graded similarity before and after a targeted extinction. If untouched neighbours showed no decrement, or if the decrement were flat across near and far siblings rather than graded by similarity, the account fails. It also predicts the spread is largest exactly where the operator's cue-surface widening was most aggressive, since that is what made the cluster tight in the first place. [established; inhibitory generalization gradients; stimulus generalization]


**Worked examples.**

- *Blast-radius check before de-conditioning a single cue*
  - **Setup.** About to decommission one installed trigger; the operator maps, in advance, the untargeted cues that share its sensory channel, bodily site, or semantic neighbourhood.
  - **The move.** Before you starve the snap-of-fingers cue, test the three things that live next to it: the click of the pen, the same hand on the same shoulder, and the word you paired to that shoulder. Score each one now, out of ten. Score them again a week after the cue is dead, and expect the pen to have dropped further than the word.
  - **Why it lands.** Suppression driven into one cue diffuses through the substrate to neighbours nobody touched, graded by closeness, so the de-conditioning pass flattens a region rather than a point. Observable: the pre/post scores fall on cues that were never run, and the loss otherwise appears only the next time a sibling is called on and comes back thin.


<a id="entry-1387"></a>

### collective-sanction-as-recognition-block

[#1387](#entry-1387) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

A group, with no single leader or target, is led into a visible shared act of condemning someone for a desire every member privately feels too.
