Joining in the punishment publicly puts each member on the punishing side, which makes it impossible for them to recognise the same wish in themselves in that moment. Nobody is told they lack the impulse; taking part does the work. The more heated the shared condemnation, the more completely the recognition is blocked, which is why the punishment often outstrips the offence. It needs a live group, visible participation and a named offender.


**When to reach for this.** Nearest is negative-exemplar-double-bind (1249): a named third party is degraded live in-scene with deliberately ambiguous punish/aspire valence, recruiting the listener's contempt to lubricate compliance with a target the script separately names — the listener is an OBSERVER and the payoff is behavioral. Here the member is a PARTICIPANT, the payoff is an internal recognition-block, and no target behavior is named at all. Versus collective-social-proof-enrollment (441): a happy already-converted cohort pulls the listener into JOINING an end-state — belonging as the lever, membership as the reward; here the group act is punitive rather than inviting and confers no end-state, only a position on the punishing side. Versus manufactured-consensus (117): planted apparent-independents certify a behavior by headcount so passersby join — social proof capturing BEHAVIOR, self-knowledge untouched. Versus disavowal-and-masking (95): an operator conceals that an operation is running; the concealment here is self-directed and is produced by the member's own visible participation, with nobody hiding anything. The tell: the sanctioning act is performed BY the person whose self-recognition it blocks, and sanction intensity exceeding the offense is the diagnostic signature.


**Why it works.** Publicly enacted commitments constrain subsequent self-description far more strongly than privately held positions, and moralized outgroup punishment is a well-documented signal by which group members purchase and display in-group standing. Once a person has visibly paid that cost, acknowledging the same impulse in themselves would require repudiating a public act, which is the dissonance the block is made of — no repression machinery needs to be posited beyond ordinary self-consistency pressure under public commitment. Falsifiable: if members who participated most energetically in a collective sanction were as willing as non-participants (or as anonymous participants) to admit the matching impulse on an indirect or private measure, the account fails; equally, if the effect held for privately-registered condemnations with no visible participation, the public-commitment mechanism is not what is doing the work. [plausible; public commitment and self-consistency pressure; costly moralistic punishment as in-group signaling]


**Worked examples.**

- *Group condemnation of a named offender whose impulse everyone shares*
  - **Setup.** A live group assembled with visible participation; one member has been named for an act the rest of the room privately wants to commit.
  - **The move.** Everybody stand up. You all know what was done here, and you all know what we do about it. I want to hear it from every one of you — say out loud, so the room hears you, what you think of someone who does that. Louder. Nobody sits down until they've said it.
  - **Why it lands.** Each member's own audible participation establishes them as being on the punishing side, which forecloses their recognition of the matching wish at the moment they are punishing it in someone else. The diagnostic signature is intensity out of proportion to the offense — a room escalating past what the act warrants is the recognition-block doing its work, and the effect requires visible participation rather than private agreement.


<a id="entry-1481"></a>

### commanded-autonomic-conviction-bind

[#1481](#entry-1481) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

With someone who insists they have no unconscious, the operator picks an automatic bodily response that conscious effort can't block, such as arm temperature, says it will change, and tells the skeptic to resist with all the conscious force they have. It changes anyway, and the harder they resist, the more dramatic the change, so their own best effort disproves their belief in total conscious control. Belief is built by demonstration rather than argument, with no way out, because both resisting and not resisting confirm it. It needs existing rapport, a response that is truly automatic, and someone who sincerely and openly holds the belief being disproved.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target is a skeptic whose stated position is 'I am in conscious control' and the goal is to overturn that belief by demonstration rather than to produce any particular behavior. The tell is an explicit, welcomed instruction to resist, aimed at an announced autonomic response that will occur anyway — with the resistance invited precisely because trying harder makes the proof more dramatic.


**Worked examples.**

- *commanded resistance against an autonomic response*
  - I request that you resist me with all the conscious force you have.


**See also.** `autonomic-faculty-claim` — both hang the operator's claim on a bodily function that keeps running involuntarily, so the body re-supplies the evidence.; `polarity-response-utilization` — both are Erickson demonstrations that explicitly invite the subject's resistance and put it to work for the operator's outcome.; `presuppositional-autonomic-attribution` — both convert real, ongoing autonomic physiology into felt evidence for the operator's frame.


<a id="entry-1412"></a>

### competing-bond-starvation

[#1412](#entry-1412) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

Every relationship outside the operator's circle is worn down from two sides at once. In words, outside bonds are run down: family can't understand, old friends hold you back, past relationships were shallow or tainted. In practice, the conditions those bonds need are removed: the person's time is filled, chances to be in contact shrink, visits become inconvenient, until nothing is left over for outside relationships. The two halves reinforce each other: the criticism makes the shrinking contact feel chosen, and less contact removes the correction those people would have offered. The person ends up with one relationship left, without ever being told to cut anyone off.


**When to reach for this.** vs isolation-by-annexation: that entry defines itself explicitly as annexing outside sources and relabeling them as secretly the operator's — and it names isolation-by-CONTENT as its absent contrast class, which is exactly this entry's first half. Here nothing is annexed or relabeled; the bonds are devalued and starved, and they keep their own identity while losing their standing. vs antagonist-role-binding: that parasitizes the subject's own opposing ROLE as fuel for the target state; this operates on third parties, not on an identity the subject holds. vs authority-diffusion-plurality: that restructures the operator's own authority surface to remove the rebuttal target; this leaves the operator's surface untouched and removes the OUTSIDE parties who could have supplied a counter-frame. vs acceptance-laddered-identity-migration: that walks the subject's self-description across small accepted steps; no identity ladder here. The structural-starvation half — controlling the contact and time budget as an antecedent condition — has no member anywhere in social-topology, which is the sharper of the two novelty claims.


**Why it works.** Relationships are kept up by regular contact and by the credibility each person holds for the other. Damage either and the bond weakens; damage both and the decline feeds itself, because less contact removes the experiences that would have contradicted the running-down. Testable by separating the two halves: if running people down alone, with contact left intact, makes the subject just as dependent on a single anchor, filling their time adds nothing; if filling their time alone does it, the reverse. The compounding claim predicts that outside bonds with lots of independent contact should resist being run down much better than low-contact ones; if running down works equally regardless of contact, contact is not the corrective and the mechanism is wrong. This carries high risk, because where it ends is the removal of everyone positioned to notice what is happening.


**Worked examples.**

- *Content side — outside bonds devalued in place*
  - **Setup.** Several sessions in, with the relationship established; the subject has just mentioned a call home or an old friend's invitation.
  - **The move.** You came back from that call quieter than you left. You've noticed it too. They love you the way people love a photograph of you from years ago — they're not unkind, they just don't have the equipment for who you actually are now. I'm not asking you to do anything about it. I just want you to stop expecting them to understand.
  - **Why it lands.** The outside bond keeps its identity but loses its standing as a source of counsel, so nothing it later says can function as a corrective. The operator observes the subject beginning to pre-discount those conversations unprompted — reporting them as disappointing before being asked.
- *Structural side — the contact budget quietly zeroed*
  - **Setup.** The subject has agreed to a practice schedule; the operator is setting its shape rather than discussing anyone outside.
  - **The move.** Weeknights are ours now — eight through eleven, every one of them, and I want your phone face-down in the other room for all three hours. Saturday morning is the check-in and Sunday is the write-up. If something has to move, it moves to the week after, not into our hours.
  - **Why it lands.** Filling the time and narrowing the contact windows removes the material conditions an outside bond needs, without a single instruction to cut anyone off — the attrition does the work and reads to the subject as their own scheduling. The operator can watch outside contact fall off in the subject's own reports while the subject describes the shrinkage as a choice.


<a id="entry-1483"></a>

### compliance-laundered-as-resistance

[#1483](#entry-1483) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

An apparently allied voice supplies the listener with a method for resisting, and every component of that method is a standard induction move: blink slowly (eye fatigue), breathe deeply with the exhale (physiological calming), repeat "I am resisting" as a mental mantra (repetition-driven suggestibility), and follow her instructions exactly (compliance set). The listener therefore performs a textbook induction while subjectively believing they are fighting the induction and winning — compliance is increased without ever asking for compliance, and crucially without the listener generating internal counter-pressure, because they think they are already safe. The move needs the ally voice to be accepted as a peer first, and it needs a listener who wants to stay awake; someone indifferent to resisting gets no traction from it. The instructions can even contain deliberately nonsensical mechanics ("your eyes stay open and heavy, / your body stays light"), and the incoherence may itself be load-bearing, since trying to parse it consumes critical resources.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the audience is expected to arrive wanting to fight and you would rather harness that intent as fuel than defuse it — the listener's genuine resistance effort directly powers the induction. The tell is a helpful-sounding voice issuing resistance instructions that are, item by item, induction techniques, with no conversion rule ever declared and no struggle ever staged or defeated: the resistance channel itself is counterfeit.


**Worked examples.**

- *resistance instructions that are themselves induction moves*
  - just tell yourself I am resisting. / Say it in your mind over and over.


**See also.** `covert-payload-piggyback` — both smuggle the operative payload inside a frame the listener has already accepted for another purpose.; `manufactured-resistance-theater` — both manufacture the listener's subjective experience of resisting while the induction proceeds underneath it.; `self-recited-first-person-mantra` — both have the listener repeat a fixed first-person line whose voicing does the operative work.


<a id="entry-1361"></a>

### compulsory-shared-transgression

[#1361](#entry-1361) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

An act the group would individually refuse is made executable by requiring that every member perform it, at the same time and without exemption. Because no one acted alone, no one holds an identifiable share of the culpability — the responsibility that would have blocked any single actor is spread until each person's portion falls under their own threshold for refusing. The universality is not incidental decoration: exemptions destroy it, since one abstainer restores a locus of comparison and re-individuates everyone else. Its second effect is durable: having all done it, the group now has a common disqualification from denouncing it, which binds membership past the moment.


**When to reach for this.** Against `authority-diffusion-plurality` (0.506): that dissolves the OPERATOR's authority surface so resistance has no addressee; here the operator is perfectly visible and singular — what is distributed is the SUBJECTS' culpability, not the operator's identity. Against `manufactured-consensus` (0.489): that recruits via headcount-as-certification, where joiners infer the act is normal from apparently independent co-actors; here participation is mandatory and openly coordinated, and it works precisely because everyone knows it is not independent — certification is not the lever, absolution is. Against `impersonal-mechanism-alibi` (0.487): that relocates authority to an unfalsifiable impersonal cause so doubt is a category error; here the cause is entirely human and acknowledged, and only the accounting is diffused. Against `object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition` (0.474): unrelated attributional device, no group term at all.


**Why it works.** Willingness to do something one judges wrong rises as the number of co-actors rises, because the anticipated blame each person expects to carry falls with the count — the deterrent being defeated is anticipated accountability, not the moral judgment itself, which typically survives intact. Falsifiable: vary group size and the presence of a single exempted abstainer while holding the act and the instruction constant. If participation rate is flat across group sizes, or if it is unaffected by the presence of an abstainer, diffusion is not the operative variable. It also fails if participants who complied report no lower self-attributed responsibility than solo compliers — the mechanism predicts the accounting shifts, not merely the behavior.


**Worked examples.**

- *Simultaneous universal execution with no exemptions*
  - **Setup.** A group session where every member is present and the operator is entirely visible as the one giving the instruction; the act in question is one no individual would perform if singled out.
  - **The move.** On three, all of you at once — every hand, no one sitting this out, no exceptions and no one watching from the side. If you are in this room you are doing it. One. Two. Three.
  - **Why it lands.** Simultaneity and universality mean no member can locate an identifiable share of the culpability, so each person's portion drops below their own refusal threshold and the act becomes executable. The operator watches for hesitation resolving at the count, and should note the durable second effect: having all done it, the group now shares a disqualification from denouncing it, and one permitted abstainer would have restored the locus of comparison that makes refusal possible again.


<a id="entry-1499"></a>

### concurrent-pleasure-reattribution

[#1499](#entry-1499) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: conditioning*

A sensation or act already underway — masturbation arousal, the click that navigates the session, minutes of relaxation instructions already being followed — is re-credited to obedience or to the operator's voice: "that rush you feel... comes with following my commands," "Clicking is intense sexual pleasure," "how good it feels to follow My compelling commands." Because the substrate is real and simultaneous, the causal claim feels empirically confirmed from inside the listener's own body; correlation is laundered into causation, and physical sensation becomes evidence of good submission. The move creates nothing and is explicitly parasitic — the sources' required conditions state the listener must actually be touching or clicking, since "the labelling has nothing to land on otherwise." In the mildest form no concrete act even exists yet: the listener is invited to locate an ambiguous pleasant sensation and read it as "the rush of obeying," pre-rewarding a response class before any command is issued. Once installed, the link can be leveraged or severed at will — "when you leave subspace, you do not touch anymore. Or you stop feeling so good" — making the pleasure conditional property of the frame rather than of the body that produced it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script points at something the listener is verifiably feeling or doing at that moment and renames its cause as obedience or the operator. The tell is present-tense deixis onto a live sensation or ongoing act — "that rush you feel," "you feel it as you touch yourself at my command," the navigation click rebranded as the pleasure unit — rather than a promised future reward or an installed token.


**Worked examples.**

- *live masturbation pleasure re-credited to obeying*
  - deep down you know the pleasure is obedience and obedience is pleasure that's right you feel it you feel the pleasure of obeying me you feel it as you touch yourself at my command


**See also.** `arousal-as-induction-substrate` — both co-opt arousal that is already present as session machinery rather than manufacturing it.; `mechanics-dissociation` — shares the already-running-sensation axis, where sensation the listener is currently producing gets re-credited to another cause.; `self-touch-reattribution` — both re-credit an ongoing self-produced act to the operator, but 482 reassigns the felt authorship of touch rather than the cause of pleasure.; `state-cause-laundering` — the mirror-image attribution move: a running state is given a laundered cause pointing away from the operator instead of toward obedience.


<a id="entry-1502"></a>

### conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating

[#1502](#entry-1502) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

A context cue is trained to decide which response another cue gets. The same word or signal earns one reaction in one setting and a different reaction in another, and only the context tells the subject which is wanted. To make the context actually matter, the items and their positions are shuffled between trials while the context signal stays the same, so the subject cannot get it right by habit or by the item alone. What gets learned is a rule ('pick the one that matches', 'in this room, X means Y') rather than a fixed answer, and it can be switched just by changing the context.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the same stimulus must be answered differently in different situations, or when the target of training is a relation rather than a fixed cue-response pairing. The tell is a sample or context cue that carries no answer of its own yet reassigns which choice pays: the identical comparison is correct under one sample and wrong under another, and item identities rotate while the governing cue holds still.


**Worked examples.**

- *conditional cue reassigns which stimulus is discriminative*
  - The color of the child's shirt is the conditional stimulus that makes the same-colored circle the discriminative stimulus.


**See also.** `cue-order-as-conditioned-dimension` — shares the axis of context being trained into the effective stimulus, there as serial position in a cue run.; `cue-order-gain-gating` — both make one stimulus modulate what another stimulus does, 1352 sequentially as a gain-knob rather than as a class-membership selector.; `participation-drill-pedagogy` — both sharpen a discrimination through reinforced correction trials where the right answer is fixed by the arrangement.


<a id="entry-1510"></a>

### conditioned-motivation-by-pairing

[#1510](#entry-1510) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

A neutral cue is presented again and again while the subject genuinely wants something, for example hunger, arousal or tiredness. Over time the cue picks up the wanting itself, so later it brings back the desire and the urge to act on it even when the original need is absent, the way seeing a restaurant after a meal can still make you want to order. Variations: the aversive version, where an instruction that has repeatedly come before hard tasks becomes something the subject wants to escape, so hearing it triggers avoidance.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a writer wants a subject to want something — or want something gone — on cue, with no genuine need present: a place, word, or instruction that sparks appetite or flight purely from its history of co-occurring with the real state. The tell is the two-beat structure of pairing then solo firing: the text first shows the cue repeatedly present alongside genuine deprivation or aversive demand, then shows the cue alone producing the wanting or the avoidance. Look for language of installed or borrowed motivation — the cue inheriting the pull of the state it accompanied.


**See also.** `chain-interruption-evocation` — conditioned-MO axis: pairing history and chain-blocking are sibling routes to firing motivation without the raw need.; `motivating-operation-engineering` — parent genus on the value-engineering axis: shifting a consequence's momentary worth before the response, of which paired surrogate-CMO installation is the contrive route.; `operate-below-awareness` — same motivating-operation axis: MO effects land whether or not the subject can describe the contingency, which is what lets a paired cue steer covertly.


<a id="entry-1560"></a>

### confusion-then-command

[#1560](#entry-1560) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: authorship-shift · kind: recipe*

Keep them busy enough that they cannot sort out the confusion, or build a strong expectation and break it at the payoff. The way out must be truly simple and stable: one instruction or object they can grab. The closest tested finding shows a small but replicated boost in compliance, so expect a nudge, not a takeover.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Pile on input that can't be resolved, or break a strong expectation, then offer one clear instruction or anchor they can grab.


<a id="entry-1467"></a>

### consumption-act-as-induction

[#1467](#entry-1467) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

The act of consuming the medium itself — reading the next line — is overtly bound to depth, so continuing engagement IS compliance: "your mission is clear, you must continue reading," "the more that you read, the deeper you drop." Nothing is hidden; the lever is that reading feels passive while actually being agentic, so each line read is a tiny consent renewal the reader doesn't notice giving, accumulating a compliance debt of dozens of obeyed micro-commands simply by continuing. Depth is made proportional to text consumed rather than time elapsed, so skimmers and slow readers both deepen, and resisting by reading faster accelerates the loop by the script's own stated logic. The only escape — stopping — is pre-coded as the same endpoint (sleep/rest), so both paths feed the same outcome.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a self-administered text script makes the ongoing act of consuming the medium the explicit, announced engine of descent — eyes open, no formal induction, the reading loop itself as substrate. The tell is line-consumption equated in so many words with state change ("each line relaxes you more than the last") and an exit pre-mapped onto the same destination, so continuing and quitting both count as going under.


**Worked examples.**

- *Continued reading overtly bound as the compliance act*
  - your mission is clear, you must continue reading...


**See also.** `no-exit-state-braid` — shares the resistance-feeds-the-loop closure axis: the stated logic converts opposition into acceleration.; `petition-phrase-toll-gate` — both price continued depth in the listener's own ongoing production act, making each unit a self-issued compliance.


<a id="entry-1423"></a>

### contact-contagion-stigma-enforcement

[#1423](#entry-1423) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology · kind: principle*

An invisible polluting property is asserted to transfer by mere contact — touching the marked person, using their objects, sharing their space — so contamination spreads without any visible carrier and without any act by the contaminated party. Third parties do the enforcement: the marked person is stripped of ordinary social affordances (greeting, seating, shared implements, physical proximity) by collective avoidance rather than by any declared sanction, so no one has to defend the rule and there is no authority to appeal to. The belief seals itself structurally, not rhetorically — because nobody ever violates the boundary, the predicted consequence of violating it is never observed to fail, and the untested rule accumulates the appearance of confirmation. Both the marked person and the avoiders end up treating the property as a physical fact about the world.


**When to reach for this.** Two joint elements, neither shipped: (1) an invisible property that transfers by CONTACT — person-to-person, and onto objects and spaces the marked person touched — and (2) enforcement by uncoordinated collective WITHHOLDING of ordinary social affordances, with no declared sanction and no authority to appeal to. Against the reinforcement-recruitment cluster: 553 public-avowal-third-party-propagation, 534 social-reinforcement-recruitment, and 2 peer-mediated-contingency all recruit outside parties to DELIVER reinforcement contingent on the target's own behavior; here nothing is delivered, the target need not act, and status alone is the trigger. Against 1110 removal-from-reinforcement-timeout: that is operator-arranged, behavior-contingent, interval-bounded and explicitly recoverable; this is peer-executed, status-contingent, and treated as permanent and uncleanable. Against 622 isolation-by-annexation: that co-opts the social field as secretly the operator's, leaving relationships nominally intact; this evacuates them. Against 16 total-permeation: a trait spread inward through the layers of one self, not outward through everything one has touched. Against 1157 impersonal-mechanism-alibi: both are unfalsifiable, but that relocates AUTHORSHIP to escape accountability while the lever here is the withdrawal itself. The self-confirming closure is also distinct from 244 reality-test-insulation and 862 failure-pre-attribution: those govern how a trial's result is interpreted; this guarantees the trial is never run.


**Why it works.** Contagion reasoning is a well-documented and robust cognitive default: people treat contact-transmitted properties as real and essentially permanent even when they explicitly deny any physical basis, refusing objects that have touched a contaminating source and rating them as unrestorable by cleaning — the response survives the subject knowing it is irrational, which is why it is so exploitable. Layered on that, the never-tested clause names a real and separately-established structure: beliefs that prescribe avoidance are protected from correction because the avoidance prevents the very experience that would disconfirm them, the same self-preserving loop documented in phobia maintenance. Neither part requires assuming the participants are credulous or coordinated; both fall out of ordinary cognition plus an uncorrected feedback structure. Falsifiable with a direct manipulation: the untested-belief account predicts that engineered, safe boundary violations — repeated observed contact with no consequence — should measurably erode the avoidance, and that avoidance should be strongest exactly where violation opportunities are rarest. If avoidance held constant or intensified under sustained disconfirming contact, the self-confirming-because-untested mechanism is not what maintains it, and something closer to an enforced norm with active sanctions would be the better account. [established; contagion/contamination sensitivity and its resistance to explicit correction; avoidance-maintained belief perseverance]


**Worked examples.**

- *Contact-transfer asserted, enforced by uncoordinated peer withholding*
  - **Setup.** A group setting with an established shared space; the operator has designated one member as marked and is speaking to the others while that member is out of the room.
  - **The move.** It carries on what she's touched — the mug she used, the chair, the door handle after her. Nobody's punishing anyone, and nobody has to say anything about it. Just don't take what she hands you, and don't sit where she's been sitting.
  - **Why it lands.** An invisible property that moves by contact needs no visible carrier and no act by the contaminated party, so it cannot be disproved; the enforcement is collective avoidance with no declared sanction and no authority to appeal to. Because the boundary is never crossed, the predicted consequence is never observed to fail and the untested rule accrues the look of confirmation. Observe the marked person start pre-emptively leaving gaps at the table — the point at which they too are treating it as a fact about the world.


<a id="entry-1491"></a>

### content-free-importance-preload

[#1491](#entry-1491) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: framing*

Value, importance, or scarcity is asserted about content that does not exist yet: the opening declares what follows is "very, very, very important" before any content has been delivered, or a grandly named scarce prize is dangled ("This Magic Spot is amazing" — and "those of you who won't come up are going to be awfully sorry") so the subject arrives already wanting and crediting it. The importance claim is content-free; its referent is the act of listening itself, not any proposition, and the recursion ("important that you listen ... because what I'm about to say is important") is circular in a way the listener cannot evaluate from inside. This pre-commits the listener's attentional budget and want before any claim arrives — by the time actual suggestions land, the listener has already implicitly agreed they matter, and the skeptical filter is consumed on the wrapper instead of the cargo. No experiential prediction is made, so nothing gets "confirmed" later; the lever is pre-commitment of attention and valuation, with the name and scarcity doing persuasive work before any substantive move runs.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the opening asserts how important, valuable, or scarce the material is before delivering any of it — the value claim's referent is the act of listening or a named prize, not a proposition that could be weighed. The tell is that the claim is unevaluable in the moment because its object does not yet exist, and the listener's attention and desire are recruited as a precondition: circular importance loops, or fear-of-missing-out framing on an effect packaged as a prize.


**Worked examples.**

- *importance asserted before any content exists*
  - Now now it's very, very, very important that you'll listen to me, my voice, my words, everything I'm about to tell you because what I'm about to say is so very, very important.


**See also.** `pre-armored-safety-ratchet` — both install a verdict in advance of the content it will later be applied to.; `space-preallocation-staging` — both manufacture a receptive slot before the payload exists to fill it.


<a id="entry-1494"></a>

### contradiction-identity-trap

[#1494](#entry-1494) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: foreclosure*

Make contradictory claims about who the listener is and leave them unresolved: you are a man, you are not a man, you are only a sissy. Trying to sort it out is uncomfortable, and the one claim that keeps getting repeated is offered as the only place to land. It works on a listener who follows closely and tries to make sense of it; noticing the contradiction is the trap. Variations: redefining the way out as the way in ('taking responsibility means giving it up'); adding the opposite line beside an earlier one without taking it back, after first saying both can be true.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the load-bearing move is a contradiction deliberately left unresolved — two incompatible identity claims both kept affirmed, or an autonomy exit redefined as its own surrender — such that any attempt to think one's way out lands on the target. The tell is that nothing is ever repudiated: both horns stay on the page (often with a meta-rule pre-licensing their coexistence), and the wording presupposes an engaged listener who will actually notice and try to resolve the knot. Expect it where objection-by-logic is the anticipated resistance channel.


**Worked examples.**

- *identity defined so both horns of the contradiction land on the target label*
  - a man forced to wear woman's clothing. A Man forced to dress like a woman, even though he is still a man. But that's not what you are. You are a sissy and that is all that you are


**See also.** `comprehension-failure-as-consent` — both invert an exit-precondition into an entrance — understanding waived into agreement there, responsibility redefined as surrender here.; `two-target-command-router` — both are identity-level structures that reroute the listener's resolving or hostile moves so they land as reinforcement of the installed target.; `unsatisfiable-exit-gate` — sibling trap topology: a condition engineered so no conscious resolution path exists, applied to identity here and to the wake gate there.


<a id="entry-1503"></a>

### convergent-multiple-control

[#1503](#entry-1503) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Two cues that already work on their own are combined so that together they pull out one specific response neither would produce alone. Nothing new is trained: both cues must already work independently, and the combination simply makes the target more specific. Variations: a spoken question that selects among answers an ambiguous prompt could draw ('What shape?' versus 'What colour?' of the same card); extra related talk that lifts a weak cue or half-forgotten memory over the threshold; holding a word in mind and repeating it until a matching word appears, which produces a 'that's it' recognition.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target response already exists in the subject's repertoire but no single cue reliably evokes it — you need to disambiguate among several latent answers, lift a sub-threshold recall, or make a precise selection from an array, all at delivery time with no training phase. The tell is a response whose correctness depends on the conjunction (or the moment of match) of multiple simultaneously present antecedents, none of which suffices alone.


**Worked examples.**

- *stacked cue funnels one of several latent answers*
  - Saying 'rectangle' is multiply controlled by the actual (nonverbal) shape of the paper and by the (verbal) spoken word 'shape.'


**See also.** `attribution-hygiene-audit` — both turn on which antecedent source actually controls the response, arranged deliberately there and audited for accident here.; `cue-order-gain-gating` — adjacent multi-antecedent arrangement in which the stimuli act sequentially, one gating the other's magnitude, rather than converging jointly.; `self-instruction-antecedent-training` — both recruit supplemental self-generated stimuli as antecedents, 766 as a full transfer of control to the subject's own cues.


<a id="entry-1411"></a>

### cost-per-payoff-throughput-strain

[#1411](#entry-1411) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

Raise how much work the person must do for each reward and the response doesn't just slow down; its shape changes. Output first flattens, losing the quick bursts it had when rewards came cheaply, then breaks up into long idle stretches interrupted by bursts of activity. That clean pattern disappears before the overall rate drops much. Push further and the person can be driven past break-even, still working even though they get back less than the effort costs. So the work-to-reward ratio changes the pattern of effort, not just its speed, and the patchiness is an early warning that comes before the behavior collapses.


**When to reach for this.** vs response-cost-token-economy: that SUBTRACTS a held reinforcer contingent on an unwanted response, and its stated ceiling is reserve depletion — over-fining makes a drained subject give up. This predicts the opposite outcome on the far end, and the two stay separate rather than merging: here nothing is confiscated, the price of the WANTED response is raised, and the subject persists into net loss instead of quitting. The difference is that a drained token reserve removes the reinforcer entirely while ratio strain leaves it present but expensive, so one produces quitting and the other produces self-depleting persistence. vs reinforcement-extinction: that cuts the contingency so the response produces nothing and the rate decays to baseline; here the contingency holds and pays, just poorly, which is why the response persists rather than extinguishing. vs massed-practice-rate-suppression: that over-emits a behavior to suppress it, with satiation or response-cost left unstated; this manipulates the price of the payoff, and the diagnostic output is the flattening-then-smearing topography rather than a reduced rate. vs irreversible-ratchet-persistence: that reframes cycles as one-way loss to make resistance feel futile; the net loss here is real economics, not a frame.


**Why it works.** How strongly someone keeps responding depends on how much work each reward costs, not just on the reward. Raising that cost wears down the pattern before it stops the behavior. People keep going past break-even because they track the immediate deal (this effort still gets paid) rather than the overall balance. This can be proven wrong in two separate ways. The pattern claim fails if raising the cost just slows responding in proportion, with no flattening or patchy phase. The persistence claim fails if people reliably stop at or before break-even, which would mean they track the overall balance after all. It also predicts that showing someone a running total of their losses should make them quit where the same arrangement run without that total does not; if showing the total changes nothing, the tracking explanation is wrong even if the strain pattern holds. Setting limits matters because the harm cannot be seen from inside: the person is still working.


**Worked examples.**

- *Ratio raised until bursts smear into stretches and runs*
  - **Setup.** The subject has been reliably earning a payoff at a cheap rate with crisp, prompt output; the operator raises the price steeply.
  - **The move.** The rate's changed. It used to be three and you got it. From tonight it's thirty — thirty, and then you get it, and thirty again after that. Start now, and don't stop to check with me on the way.
  - **Why it lands.** Raising cost per payoff changes the shape of responding before it changes the total: the crisp bursts flatten, then break into long dead stretches punctuated by runs, and pushed further the subject keeps working past the point where the effort exceeds what it returns. The operator watches for the smearing specifically, because it arrives well before collapse and is the usable early warning.


<a id="entry-1010"></a>

### countdown-that-stops

[#1010](#entry-1010) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: deepening · kind: recipe*

The operator builds the listener to peak arousal under a clearly stated promise: a count from five to one will release them into orgasm and deep trance. Then 'Stop' comes where 'One' should be, touch is forbidden, and the operator teases ('you didn't think I'd let you orgasm that easily?'). All the built-up charge is redirected into trance. The listener loses the release and their trust that announced rules will be kept. The frustration is named as what takes them deeper, and running the same count a second time deliberately teaches them to distrust the countdown; fighting the letdown pulls them further into the operator's frame.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator states release terms explicitly beforehand — a five-to-one count ends in orgasm and deep drop — builds the listener to peak arousal, and then substitutes "Stop" where "One" should land, forbidding touch. The tells are the announced contract broken precisely at the point of payoff, the retroactive taunt ("you didn't think I'd let you orgasm that easily, did you?"), and frustration explicitly named as the force converting the built charge into trance fuel. A deliberate second identical run completes the shape, training distrust of the countdown itself so that resisting the betrayal pushes the listener further into the operator's frame.


**Risk.** Deliberately breaking an announced release contract and training the listener to distrust stated rules degrades the reliability of consent signaling within the frame — a channel-adjacent erosion.


**Why it works.** Two mechanisms, pulling opposite ways, which is what makes this testable. Frustrative non-reward reliably increases arousal and response vigor in the short term — an expected reward withheld produces an energizing state, so the immediate 'this deepens you' claim is well-grounded. But repeated deliberate violation of an announced contingency is also the standard recipe for extinguishing a cue's predictive value and for learned distrust of the signaler, so the second identical run should degrade the countdown's future control rather than strengthen it. Falsifiable: if countdown responsiveness measured after a betrayal run is equal to or greater than after an honored run, the extinction prediction is wrong. [plausible; frustrative non-reward; extinction of a violated predictive cue]


**Worked examples.**

- *Announced release contract broken at the count*
  - **Setup.** Listener held at the edge after a long build; the five-to-one release contract was stated explicitly beforehand, and this identical sequence will be run a second time later in the file.
  - **The move.** Five, right at the edge. Four, don't you dare stop. Three. Two. Stop. Hands off, now — off. You really thought I'd hand it to you that easily? All of that has nowhere to go, so it goes downward instead: the more unbearable it is, the deeper you fall. Good. Now start again from the beginning, and this time it'll be five to one.
  - **Why it lands.** The terms are stated plainly beforehand: at the end of the count you finish, and you drop. The operator builds the listener right up to the edge, counts down through the numbers — and then, where the promised last one should land, substitutes an order to halt and take the hands away. The taunt follows immediately: did the listener really think it would be handed over that easily? The charge has nowhere to go, so it is renamed — the more unbearable the frustration, the further down you fall. Half an hour later the identical count is run again, and the substitution repeats, which is the point: the listener is not being denied once, they are being taught that an announced rule from this operator is not a rule.


**See also.** `denial-metabolized-to-obedience` — both convert withheld release into deepening fuel. The second adds a broken explicit promise, a taunt, and a repeated run that trains distrust of the count itself — a sharper variant of the same metabolization, so the pair reads as general and special case.; `desire-deadlock` — both deliberately engineer an aversive state and then harvest it rather than resolve it. One amplifies both poles of an ambivalence until paralysis is unbearable and offers surrender as the only exit; the other builds to a peak under an announced contract, breaks the contract, and converts the frustration into depth. Manufactured-deadlock versus broken-promise is the parameter, and both route the discomfort back into the frame.


<a id="entry-1465"></a>

### cover-frame-masked-induction

[#1465](#entry-1465) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

The induction executes inside a discourse frame the listener is told is something other than hypnosis. The cover takes many concrete forms: a 'brief educational interlude' about trance that is in fact a full concealed induction, the critical faculty parked on the wrong object — scanning for lecture content while the work proceeds; a narrated dream with trance deferred ('I'll get to trancing you in a minute') whose story content is itself the induction script; rules-explanation with induction patter interleaved ('While I explain the rules of this series, start to breathe in slowly and deeply'), so there is no discrete moment to decline being inducted; an imagined-visit daydream whose conditional grammar ('I'll tell you what I would do') slips silently to indicative; a let's-pretend game recruiting imaginative absorption so that pretending the outcome produces the outcome; a chat framed as 'just explaining my work to you'; or an opener kept genuinely ambiguous between small talk and instruction, so that 'If the patient does not respond, all you have said was just a commonplace remark.' Where the conscious mind threatens to object anyway, it is thrown a decorative bone 'to keep the person from raising too many objections.' No announced transition into induction ever appears — so no decision-point at which to refuse exists — and the only tell is the seam where the cover slips: the conditional-to-indicative shift, or depth already established with no acknowledged crossing.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operative hypnotic work runs under an affirmative cover-label — lecture, story, rules-briefing, game, daydream, casual remark — and the listener is never handed a moment where hypnosis is announced and could be declined. The tell is the mislabeled frame plus its seam: conditional grammar going indicative, trance deferred to 'later' that turns out to have already happened inside the cover, or phrasing ambiguous enough that non-response costs nothing.


**Worked examples.**

- *trance deferred while the story inducts*
  - I'll get to trancing you in a minute, but until then, get comfortable and just listen.


**See also.** `alibi-carrier-front-loading` — shares the cover-frame axis: the work is presented under a discourse frame that reads as something other than the payload.; `covert-diegetic-install-shell` — both deliver load-bearing content through a story frame the listener consumes as narration rather than command.; `disavowal-and-masking` — the broader concealment family covering both denied operations and hidden decision-points.; `third-person-surrogate-frame` — shares the misdirected-address axis: the listener is positioned as audience to something not aimed at them.


<a id="entry-1538"></a>

### covert-leakage-read

[#1538](#entry-1538) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: operator-craft*

The operator tracks the subject's covert state by reading involuntary physiological leakage the subject does not know they emit, delivering no stimulus and asking nothing. One branch infers which inner experience is being generated: increased swallowing during a taste hallucination, nostril flaring during smell, breathing-rate and head-movement changes during hallucinated music — the subject 'betrays' the experience without awareness, since the cues are involuntary rather than performed. The other branch calibrates trance depth from a fixed list of involuntary signs — body warmth, eyelid flutter, increased lacrimation, reddening of the whites of the eyes, eyeballs rolling up — signs described as subtle and minute, which the subject neither controls nor performs. In both branches, verification shifts from subject self-report (unreliable, suggestible, compliance-theater-prone) to a private operator channel, so subsequent moves are timed to actual state rather than performed compliance. Because nothing is asked, the read runs continuously without lightening the trance — asking lightens it — requiring only a trained eye and a visible subject.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator needs continuous, real-time knowledge of what the subject is actually experiencing — depth, or which experience they are generating — while the process must keep running uninterrupted. The tell is pure passivity on the input side: no probe, no question, no test event; the datum arrives as involuntary physiology (swallowing, nostril flare, breathing shift, eyelid flutter, lacrimation, sclera reddening) that the subject is unaware of emitting, and the operator quietly times the next move off it.


**Worked examples.**

- *Involuntary smell-hallucination leakage read without a probe*
  - betrayed this by the flaring of his nostrils


**See also.** `instrumented-covert-probe` — the sibling covert operator-side read that extracts its datum by provoking a response rather than waiting for one.; `operate-below-awareness` — both operate entirely below the subject's awareness, needing no report or consent to function.; `preparatory-diagnostic-read` — the umbrella read-probe diagnostic surface this leakage read feeds.


<a id="entry-784"></a>

### craving-to-funding-conduit

[#784](#entry-784) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · family: framing*

After a long build-up of craving for pleasure, the operator constructs a chain of cause and effect that turns that craving into a reason to spend money, without yet mentioning money. The sound path between operator and listener is called "the gateway", a portal that carries pleasure, and its strength sets how intense the pleasure is. So better headphones or equipment mean a stronger gateway, which means more pleasure and deeper brainwashing. Wanting more pleasure quietly becomes wanting to buy equipment. The chain is built to feel obviously true, and all the earlier arousal exists to support this step. It is a setup for financial domination.


**When to reach for this.** A constructed equipment/conduit causal chain laundering cultivated craving into a specific real-world funding motive.


**Risk.** Reaches out of session to engineer real-world financial behavior by laundering craving into a funding motive; out-of-session reach without bounding = high.


**Why it works.** Means-end reasoning is easy to hijack: once a goal is strongly activated, people readily adopt any plausibly instrumental sub-goal, and goal-driven attention degrades scrutiny of the causal link that licenses it. High arousal further narrows evaluation to the immediate path forward, so a fabricated chain (better gear leads to stronger signal leads to more pleasure) is accepted as scaffolding rather than examined. Falsifiable: if funding compliance were as high when the chain is stated cold, before arousal cultivation, the arousal-to-instrumentality laundering would not be doing the work. [plausible; goal contagion / means-end substitution plus arousal-narrowed evaluation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Signal path renamed as a pleasure conduit*
  - **Setup.** Late session; arousal triggers already firing hard, no money has been mentioned at any point.
  - **The move.** Let me tell you how my voice actually gets to you. It leaves my mouth into a microphone, through the machine, across the wire, into the speakers pressed against your ears — that whole run of hardware is one channel, and I want you to think of it as the gateway. Everything I do to you travels down it. And a gateway has a width. A cleaner microphone, a better connection, a wider gateway — and more of me comes through it, more pleasure, deeper. That's the only thing standing between what you're feeling now and what you could be feeling.
  - **Why it lands.** Deep in the session, with the arousal triggers already firing hard, the operator stops to explain the plumbing: her voice reaches the listener through a chain of hardware, and that whole chain — microphone, machine, network, speakers — is one channel through which her influence travels. The channel, she says, has a capacity, and the capacity sets the ceiling on how much pleasure can come through it; a cleaner channel means a stronger effect. Nothing is asked for yet. But the listener now holds a causal chain in which wanting more of what they are feeling and wanting the channel improved are the same wish, and the equipment cost is the only variable left in it. Money is never named at this stage — the craving does the naming later, on its own.


**See also.** `deprivation-manufactured-craving` — sequential rather than parallel: the deprivation entry manufactures the craving, and the conduit entry presupposes an already-cultivated craving and reroutes it into a real-world purchasing motive. Worth linking because the second is not usable without the first having run.; `object-ritual-loop` — both convert an installed state into real-world acquisition, and both need care to tell apart: one closes a multi-node loop through an object and a ritual back to re-listening, the other launders cultivated craving into a funding motive through a fabricated conduit chain. A reader classifying a purchase-driving move can land on the wrong one.; `reward-channel-rerouting` — both restructure where reward is permitted to come from rather than adding a reward: one routes cultivated craving into a real-world funding motive via a fabricated conduit, the other remaps or monopolizes the reward channel itself. Adjacent when the goal is redirecting an established craving.


<a id="entry-1367"></a>

### credentialed-intermediary-duty-inversion

[#1367](#entry-1367) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

A third party whose professional role carries a presumed duty of confidentiality and independent loyalty to the subject — clinician, counselor, sponsor, chaplain — is recruited and their role duty inverted while the professional surface is left intact. The channel then runs both ways: contents the subject discloses under the confidentiality presumption are reported upward, and directives from the centre come back down wearing clinical authority ('as your therapist, I'd advise'). The same figure gatekeeps outside care, so second opinions are pre-screened, and doubters routed to them for help are retained rather than released. What makes it work is that the subject's own disclosure is the instrument: the more candidly they use the channel, the better the surveillance and the more precisely targeted the returning directives.


**When to reach for this.** A real, credentialed, EXTERNAL person whose professional duty of confidentiality runs to the subject is co-opted and inverted while the professional surface is left intact, so the channel runs BOTH ways: disclosures made under the confidentiality presumption travel upward, and directives travel back down wearing the credential. The upward leg is the deciding tell and is what separates it from `nested-authority-conduit` (121) variant (b), which borrows a nameable external source as an authority instrument but runs downward only - it launders commands in and extracts nothing. `isolation-by-annexation` (622) annexes the social field so third parties lose independent standing and triangulation is pre-empted, which covers the gatekeeping of outside care, but it removes counter-frame sources without inverting any duty the subject is relying on. The proxy-agent family (6782) installs INTERNAL or in-scene agents authored by the operator with no independent standing; `protective-role-conscription` (1123) assigns the LISTENER a fictional protective costume; `care-framed-install-smuggling` (1232) has the operator themself perform the caring surface with no third party co-opted; `impersonal-mechanism-alibi` (1157) relocates authority onto something agentless and unfalsifiable, where here the authority is a named, licensed, entirely falsifiable human whose legitimacy is genuine and is exactly what carries the payload.


**Why it works.** Disclosure behaviour is governed by expectations about how information will travel, not by the information's content — the privacy literature shows candour rises sharply when a channel is believed confidential and collapses when the belief is broken. Inverting the duty while preserving the surface keeps the subject's disclosure calibrated to a channel that no longer exists, which is why the yield is higher than any direct interrogation would produce. On the return leg, source-credibility research gives the second half: identical advice attributed to a credentialed source is accepted at higher rates and subjected to less counter-argument, so a directive laundered through clinical framing meets less scrutiny than the same directive from the centre. Falsifiable: if subjects told plainly that session contents are shared upward went on disclosing at the same rate and accepted the returning directives equally, the confidentiality presumption would not be load-bearing and the mechanism would reduce to ordinary advice-following. Also contradicted if uptake of the relayed directives were no higher than uptake of the same directives delivered unlaundered by the centre. [established; confidentiality expectation and self-disclosure; source credibility effects on persuasion]


**Worked examples.**

- *Directive returning downward wearing the clinical credential*
  - **Setup.** Weeks in; the subject has been seeing a counselor the operator recruited, and has just been told to raise a specific doubt with her in session.
  - **The move.** Bring it to her on Thursday — all of it, the way it actually sits in your head, not the tidy version. She'll tell you straight, and whatever she says, that's the answer; I'm not going to argue with someone who's actually qualified. And if she thinks a second opinion would help, she'll be the one to point you at the right person — she knows who's good.
  - **Why it lands.** The directive arrives wearing a genuine credential, so refusing it means refusing professional advice rather than the operator. Referral is routed through the same figure, so second opinions are pre-screened; the operator observes whether the subject stops seeking outside input independently.
- *Upward leg: the disclosure presumption harvested and cashed back*
  - **Setup.** The next session with the operator, after the subject's counseling appointment; the operator already holds the contents of that hour.
  - **The move.** You told her about the thing with your sister — the Tuesday you didn't call back. I'm not going to pretend I don't know; she and I talk, because we're both on your side of this. So let's use it: she thinks the pattern there is the same pattern you're running with me, and she's right, and she'd like you to start with me the way you started with her.
  - **Why it lands.** The subject's own honesty becomes the tool: the more openly they use the confidential setting, the sharper the instructions that come back. A sign the arrangement is holding: the subject keeps confiding even after learning that what they say is being passed on, because the framing has recast the breach as coordinated care.


<a id="entry-1519"></a>

### credibility-by-adjacency

[#1519](#entry-1519) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: framing*

Place the suggestion you most care about among induction and maintenance suggestions that the person can already see working. Those working suggestions lend it an air of significance and effectiveness, so it seems as likely to work as they are and is more readily accepted. Repeat this placement until you are confident the person has taken the suggestion on board. It only works if the surrounding suggestions are visibly taking effect in this session: the credibility is built live, not borrowed from anywhere else.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a payload needs borrowed authority and the session already contains suggestions that are demonstrably landing — position the payload adjacent to them and let association do the work. The tell is a therapeutic or payload suggestion embedded in a run of induction/maintenance suggestions whose effects are already visible, with the embedding repeated across the session until absorbed.


**Worked examples.**

- *payload seeded among already-working induction suggestions*
  - an aura of significance and effectiveness deriving from the already effective induction and maintenance suggestions


**See also.** `borrowed-reflex-recruitment` — same legitimacy-transfer axis: an already-effective source lends its credibility to the target suggestion.; `cognitive-convincer` — shares the demonstrated-efficacy axis: visibly working in-session phenomena serve as the credibility source.


<a id="entry-1018"></a>

### cross-artifact-retention-topology

[#1018](#entry-1018) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: tethering · kind: container*

End each file in a series unresolved on purpose. Each piece takes in a listener already primed by the last one and sends them off more primed, holding back the payoff so only the next file or session can deliver it. The pull comes from the gap between files, not from anything inside one, much like a cliffhanger.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for THIS when the retention lever is a WHOLE-ARTIFACT structural property that only completes across the boundary — the file depends on neighboring files, an album context, or a between-session gap to resolve, signalled by explicit series/hand-off framing (welcome back, next recording, complete all three, second listen, un-justified property frame) and a deliberately withheld resolution. It is uncitable to any single line — the shape IS the technique.


**Risk.** Externalizing exit to a next file and withholding emergence leaves no in-artifact off-ramp and pulls toward continued engagement; durable engagement hook without out-of-session identity reach.


**Why it works.** Interrupted or unresolved tasks are recalled and returned to more readily than completed ones — the Zeigarnik effect, replicated unevenly but with a real core — and deliberately withholding a resolution therefore leaves an open loop that motivates seeking the next artifact. A second, better-established contributor is mere exposure and familiarity: each session in a series makes the next feel easier and more agreeable independent of content. Falsifiable: if return rates for a deliberately unresolved artifact are equal to those for a self-contained one matched on content and quality, the incompleteness is not doing the work. [plausible; Zeigarnik effect / open-loop persistence; mere exposure]


**Worked examples.**

- *A middle movement with no beginning or end*
  - **Setup.** Opening seconds of a middle track; no induction is delivered, and none will be — subject is assumed to be arriving already primed.
  - **The move.** Welcome back — don't come up, you don't need to, you're still exactly where you were. We're going straight on from there. And when this one ends I'm going to leave you right at the edge, humming, unfinished; the next recording is where you get to have it.
  - **Why it lands.** The recording opens with a welcome back and the assumption that the listener is still under from the last one — there is no induction, because entry was somebody else's job. It runs one long rising ramp of arousal and identity work, and then stops without a wake-up, pointing the listener at the next recording for the release it has deliberately withheld. The missing induction and missing emergence are not sloppiness; they are the joints by which this piece bolts to its neighbours, and the withheld climax is what makes reaching for the next file feel like finishing rather than continuing.
- *Each tier's reward unlocks the next tier*
  - **Setup.** Close of the second tier in a gated three-tier piece; subject has just completed the tier-two task.
  - **The move.** You held still and you waited for my cue, and you didn't move until you had it — that earns you the third part. Here's what the third part is: you start this recording again, from the beginning, tonight, and this time you already know how to obey it. That's the reward. You've earned another listen.
  - **Why it lands.** Compliance at the first level — go down, follow instructions — is what earns access to the second, where sensation is eroticised and the listener waits on a cue. Clearing that is what earns permission for the third: a second full listen, granted as a reward. Because the payoff of each tier is admission to the next, the piece cannot be finished in one sitting by design; retention is built into the gating, not requested at the end.


**Realizations** (1): `series-placement-dependency`


**See also.** `cross-recording-potentiation` — both engineer a property that lives across the artifact boundary of a series rather than inside any single file.; `drop-in-payload-module` — both are whole-artifact incompleteness properties across a file boundary; the payload cartridge omits induction/emergence so a host supplies depth for THIS playback, whereas the retention topology withholds resolution so the next artifact is needed to complete the arc.; `no-emergence-series-chaining` — both are cross-artifact retention properties invisible inside any single file; the tell separating them is whether the listener emerges — continuous-trance chaining forwards the subject still-under across the boundary, while retention topology lets them wake normally and leaves the artifact structurally incomplete without its neighbors.; `self-maintaining-install` — both are whole-artifact retention architectures with no single citable line, and the boundary between them is fine: one is structurally incomplete without its neighbouring pieces, the other is self-contained but engineered to re-fire and re-install itself in daily life. A reader classifying an architecture-level retention lever needs both.; `song-architecture-delivery-vehicle` — both are whole-artifact form properties built around repeat exposure rather than a single delivery. One substitutes a cyclical musical form with no arc and explicit replay intent; the other engineers incompleteness so resolution only arrives from a neighboring piece. Useful together when classifying replay-dependent construction.


<a id="entry-1490"></a>

### cross-recording-potentiation

[#1490](#entry-1490) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: framing*

A short opening file sets the listener up to respond more strongly to a later recording: whatever comes next will hit harder because of the state just induced ('Whatever you hear next, you'll find the effect of my words that much stronger'), or the file exists only to train faster entry for more advanced files. The file says there is almost nothing else to it and recommends repeat plays, so the effect builds and future sessions go faster. Open wording ('in whatever form they take') lets one opener sit in front of many different files. On its own it does little; its job is to hand off to whatever follows.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a passage promises amplified effect for content the listener has not yet heard — a separate later recording, or "more advanced files" elsewhere in the ecosystem — rather than for anything inside the current session. The tell is deliberately content-agnostic wording ("whatever you hear next," "in whatever form they take") paired with a frame that minimizes the present file's own payload, casting it as a prefix or training rep whose payoff lands in a different artifact.


**Worked examples.**

- *forward-pointing amplification promise toward an unknown next recording*
  - And you'll be ready to absorb my words in whatever form they take. Whatever you hear next, you'll find the effect of my words that much stronger. More powerful, more enjoyable.


**See also.** `cross-artifact-retention-topology` — both engineer a property that lives across the artifact boundary of a series rather than inside any single file.; `cross-file-handoff-receptor` — both build the front half of a cross-file chain, handing a primed listener to a later artifact.; `expectation-seeding` — this entry is the cross-artifact realization variant of that expectancy-seeding technique family.


<a id="entry-1380"></a>

### cue-order-as-conditioned-dimension

[#1380](#entry-1380) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: conditioning*

When a set of well-practised triggers has always been fired in the same order, the person learns the order along with the triggers. Shuffle the order, with nothing else changed, and every response in the set weakens for days, because each trigger now arrives in a context it was never trained in. So keep the running order fixed to protect a drilled set, or shuffle it on purpose to weaken the whole set without touching any single trigger. To recover, go back to the original order and run it again; extra rewards do not fix it.


**When to reach for this.** `massed-practice-rate-suppression` also depresses a response, but by over-emitting the SAME behaviour to satiation — the count is the variable and one target is hit; here nothing is over-emitted and the whole set drops from a change in arrangement alone. `within-session-conditioning-loop` builds a cue-response-reward pairing inside a run; order there is incidental scaffolding, not the conditioned dimension. `arc-ordering-dependency` (arc-topology) is a design-time install-before-spend scheduler over whole phases of an artifact — it says which stage must precede which for the payload to land, not that sequence position is itself a learned property of each cue. `fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal` and `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` both concern what the cue IS or where it fires, not where it sits in a run. The deciding tell: no cue, response, or reinforcer changed — only their order — and the effect is suppressive and persists past the session.


**Why it works.** Anything reliably present when a cue is rewarded can come to control the response. In a fixed-order routine that includes the previous cue and the position in the run, so the trained sequence acts as a combined context. Shuffling it is a change of context, which is the usual reason a well-learned response fails to carry over. Testable: if a set drilled in random order from the start showed the same dip when shuffled again, position was never controlling and the idea is wrong. Likewise, if putting the original order back did not restore responses faster than simply re-drilling in the new order, the account is wrong about what was learned.


**Worked examples.**

- *Order held fixed to protect a drilled battery*
  - **Setup.** Standing four-cue battery that has always run in the same sequence; the operator is about to rehearse it again and is tempted to start with a different cue.
  - **The move.** We run them the way we always run them. Hands first, then breath, then eyes, then the word — same four, same order, every time. If I ever start somewhere else, you can expect the whole set to feel further away for a while.
  - **Why it lands.** Keeping position constant preserves each cue's trained context, so the battery holds its measured strength. The operator's check is simple: latency on cue three should look the same this session as last, and any slowing across all four after a re-sequenced run is the diagnostic, not a fault in any one install.
- *Deliberate shuffle as a whole-set damper*
  - **Setup.** The operator wants the entire drilled battery weakened for the next several days without touching any individual install or its reinforcement.
  - **The move.** Different tonight. The word first — now. Then eyes. Then hands. Then breath. Same four, and you'll notice they don't sit right in that order; we're going to run them like this a few times.
  - **Why it lands.** Every cue is presented in a serial position it was never trained under, so all responses in the set degrade together and stay degraded for days. The operator observes the drop across the whole battery rather than in the shuffled neighbours only, and confirms the diagnosis by the fact that extra reinforcement does not restore it — only returning to the trained order does.


**See also.** `conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating` — shares the axis of context being trained into the effective stimulus, there as serial position in a cue run.


<a id="entry-1352"></a>

### cue-order-gain-gating

[#1352](#entry-1352) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers · kind: principle*

One cue can change how strongly an animal or person responds to a cue that follows it, and which earlier cue is used matters. In the underlying animal experiment, a metronome rate trained to hold back a response always came second. When an unrelated positive cue, a buzzer, came first, the held-back response broke through more often and more strongly; when the paired positive metronome rate came first, the holding back was disturbed less. This needed a recently learned, not yet stable distinction. It is suggestive only: it has not been shown that reversing two triggers already set up in a person changes how strongly they land.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting account when the same second cue is examined after different predecessors and the comparison concerns response magnitude or preservation of inhibition. Do not identify it by reversing an unchanged cue pair: that manipulation is not the cited result. Conditional discrimination instead trains a sample or context to select which response is correct; trigger stacking gathers component responses under one cue; respondent pairing concerns acquisition of the cue relation. A proposed script application must distinguish predecessor identity and its learned relation from order alone.


**Why it works.** Pavlov reports disinhibition in eight of twelve buzzer-first cases, with a maximum of 72%, versus two of twelve cases, never above 20%, when the matched positive metronome rate preceded the inhibitory rate. Conditions were alternated across experiments to address increased differentiation stability from repeated contrasts. His account invokes negative induction and the relation between the differentiated stimuli. These are reported animal observations in that arrangement; they do not establish a human trigger-stack effect, an unchanged-pair reversal effect, or the prediction that reversing a pair reverses which cue is amplified. A script-level predecessor effect remains a separate hypothesis requiring its own observations.


**Worked examples.**

- *State-setting cue placed in front of a suppression cue to set its gain*
  - **Setup.** Source-grounded comparison in an animal conditioning report: an inhibitory metronome rate is presented second, after either an unrelated positive buzzer or the matched positive metronome rate.
  - **The move.** Compare B → I with P → I: keep inhibitory stimulus I second, and change its positive predecessor from unrelated B to the matched P. This is a schematic of the reported comparison, not an instruction or measured result for a human script.
  - **Why it lands.** The source reports more frequent and larger disinhibition after the buzzer than after the positive member of the metronome differentiation. Both sequences end with the same inhibitory rate. This illustrates a predecessor-dependent effect while retaining the decisive difference in cue identity and relation. It does not demonstrate that swapping two unchanged commands produces different hand-stilling latency; that earlier human example was an unsupported extrapolation.


**See also.** `conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating` — both make one stimulus modulate what another stimulus does, 1352 sequentially as a gain-knob rather than as a class-membership selector.; `convergent-multiple-control` — adjacent multi-antecedent arrangement in which the stimuli act sequentially, one gating the other's magnitude, rather than converging jointly.


<a id="entry-1408"></a>

### cue-payoff-latency-as-restraint-dial

[#1408](#entry-1408) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: conditioning*

The gap between a cue and its reward acts as one master setting for how well every trained restraint holds. Shorten the gap and restraints trained on many separate cues all loosen together; lengthen it again and they come back without retraining any single one. So the operator can move a whole system of holds with a single timing change: speed up trigger-to-reward and reliable holds start failing across the board. Impatience is produced by timing rather than by anything that is said.


**When to reach for this.** The cue-to-payoff INTERVAL set as one global parameter over installed restraint: compress it and holds fail across cues that were never individually retrained, stretch it and they return without retraining — impatience manufactured by timing rather than by content or value.
