Against motivating-operation-engineering (429): 429 is the other system-wide antecedent lever, but it moves the reinforcer's momentary VALUE up (establishing) or down (satiation/abolishing); here value is untouched and only the latency changes, which is why the effect reverses cleanly on re-lengthening where satiation does not. Against precommitment-rule-governed-stakes (424): 424 treats a long cue-payoff delay as a given obstacle and binds the future self to bridge it; this treats the delay as the operator's own knob. Against respondent-habituation (facet of 1313): that lever is the SPACING between repeated presentations of one eliciting stimulus (massed blunts, spaced preserves); this is the gap between a cue and its consequence. Against bidirectional-reentry-loop (1332) and any per-link trigger work: the identifying claim is scope — one number moves the whole installed restraint set, not a topology over named cues. If shortening the interval for one cue leaves untouched cues holding firm, this entry is false and collapses into a per-link timing property.


**Why it works.** This treats restraint as a shared pool set by one overall setting rather than as a property of each cue, which is why changing a single interval would move cues that were never retrained individually. The cheapest test settles it: shorten the interval for one cue only and check whether restraints on the untouched cues still hold. If they hold firm, the effect is per cue and the system-wide claim is false. It is also contradicted if lengthening the interval again fails to restore the restraints, which would mean lasting erosion rather than a reversible adjustment.


**Worked examples.**

- *Interval compressed globally, unrelated holds tested*
  - **Setup.** Several separate hold-and-wait rules are installed and reliable; the operator wants to see restraint loosen without touching any of them individually.
  - **The move.** New timing, starting now. Everything you've been waiting on, you get the moment you ask — no counts, no pauses, no earning it first. Ask and it's yours, same second. [Later, on an entirely different rule that was never mentioned:] Hold that. Hold it the way you always have.
  - **Why it lands.** Collapsing the cue-to-payoff gap loosens the installed restraint set as a whole, so holds on cues that were never retrained begin to fail — and the operator confirms this by testing an untouched one. Stretching the interval back out restores them without retraining, which is what distinguishes a timing dial from a change in what anything is worth.


<a id="entry-1395"></a>

### curated-sample-frame-control

[#1395](#entry-1395) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: framing*

The operator controls which members of a group an outside observer is permitted to meet and speak with, and rehearses those members, so that what the observer samples is a deliberately non-representative slice presented as a random one. The observer is left to draw their own conclusion — and does, correctly reasoning from the evidence in front of them to a false generalization, because the sampling frame rather than any individual claim is what was corrupted. No one lies to the observer, which is exactly why it survives a skeptical audience: the observer's own inference does the work and feels self-generated. It generalizes past the group setting to any curated demonstration — reference calls routed to selected customers, showroom staging, a pilot cohort chosen for its results.


**When to reach for this.** The lever is control of the SAMPLING FRAME an outside observer draws from: which members they may meet is curated and rehearsed, so a non-representative slice is presented as a random one and the observer's own valid inference carries them to a false generalization. No one lies, which is why it survives a skeptical investigator. Split from `manufactured-consensus` (117), the nearest social-evidence move: 117 plants confederates and fabricates the headcount, so the falsity is in the actors and detection of one actor collapses it; here every member is genuine and the falsity lives entirely in who was excluded, leaving nothing for the observer to catch. Split from `staged-external-reality-corroboration` (239), which manufactures real perceptible events for a subject already inside the frame; here the mark is an outside observer who is not in trance and may be actively skeptical. Split from `suggestion-field-hygiene` (582), which silences bystanders defensively to protect an achieved state in a present subject. Split from `preparatory-diagnostic-read` (840), whose measurement/attribution face — clean-condition isolation, faulty-control audit — exists to protect the OPERATOR'S own read from confounds; this deliberately manufactures that confound in someone else's read, making it 840's adversarial inverse.


**Why it works.** Two robust inferential failures are being exploited. Selection bias is invisible from inside a sample: observers routinely fail to correct for how cases reached them, and reason from the observed distribution as though it were the population — the survivorship-bias literature documents this in trained analysts, not just naive ones. Second, insensitivity to sample bias survives warning: even observers told a sample may be curated tend to under-adjust, because the vivid particulars they actually encountered dominate the abstract knowledge that others were withheld. Falsifiable and cheaply testable: give one group of observers a curated sample and another a randomly drawn one from the same population, and compare their estimates of the population. If the curated group's estimates matched the random group's, the frame control does nothing; if pre-warning observers that the sample was selected fully corrected their estimates, the under-adjustment claim specifically fails. [established; selection/survivorship bias; insensitivity to sample bias and under-correction after warning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Rehearsed subset offered as an open sample to a skeptical visitor*
  - **Setup.** An outside observer — a visiting relative, an investigator, a prospective participant — is arriving to form their own impression of a group, and the operator has had a day's notice.
  - **The move.** To the three chosen members, beforehand: "When she asks how long you've been here, give her the number and then say what you were doing before. Don't volunteer anything about the schedule." To the observer, on arrival: "Talk to whoever you like — grab those three, they're around. Take as long as you want, and I'll be outside; you'll get a straighter answer without me standing there."
  - **Why it lands.** Every word the observer hears is true and every person they meet is genuine, so a skeptical observer finds nothing to catch; the falsity lives entirely in who was not in the room, and the observer's own valid inference carries them to the false generalization. Watch for the observer reporting back with a conclusion they credit to themselves — "I asked around, nobody's under pressure" — and defending it more firmly than the operator ever asserted it.


<a id="entry-786"></a>

### data-extraction-objective

[#786](#entry-786) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

The session ends by having the listener write and send the operator an email confessing "the most effective methods of controlling and manipulating you", which the operator then uses to design future sessions. Instead of putting a trigger, identity or habit into the listener, the session takes information out. Compliance becomes material for an ongoing cycle in which trance produces information and that information shapes the next trance. The manipulation is named openly as something the listener wants, which may make it harder to resist than if it were hidden.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this entry when the terminal payload of a session takes information out of the listener rather than putting a mechanism in: everything the script builds terminates in a request to write and send material — a confession email detailing 'the most effective methods of controlling and manipulating you.' The tell is the explicit recursive external loop, openly named: the operator states that the harvested data will be used to design future trance, and frames the manipulation itself as something the listener wants. The extracted material outlives the recording and feeds the next session, distinguishing it from any information-gathering that serves only the session in progress.


**Risk.** Harvested data outlives the session and feeds operator design of future control — out-of-session reach with durable operator leverage over the subject.


**Why it works.** Written self-disclosure creates a durable artifact the subject must stay consistent with, and self-disclosure is intrinsically rewarding — both are well-supported. The claim that openly naming the manipulation disarms vigilance runs against the forewarning literature, where warning of persuasive intent typically increases resistance; treat disclosure as at best neutral and possibly costly, not as a mechanism. Falsifiable: within-subject, disclosed vs. undisclosed framing of the same written-commitment task should show whether disclosure helps, hurts, or does nothing. [plausible; self-disclosure reward, escalating commitment, written-commitment effects]


**Worked examples.**

- *The payload harvests rather than installs*
  - **Setup.** Final minutes; subject is deeply aroused, has been disclosing throughout, and no trigger or identity has been installed.
  - **The move.** Before you close your eyes tonight, you're going to write me an email. Not about how it felt. I want a list: the specific things I say and do that work best on you — what makes you stop arguing, what makes you ache, what you couldn't refuse if I used it. Be exact, because I'm going to use it. Everything I make for you next will be built out of what you send me, and I think the part of you that's smiling right now knows that's the best thing about this.
  - **Why it lands.** Everything the session builds — the arousal, the disclosure, the sense of intimacy — terminates not in a trigger or a new self-image but in a request: write it down and send it. The operator says plainly what the material is for, that knowing which levers work best on this particular listener is how the next session will be built, and frames the listener's willingness to hand that over as one of their own favorite things about the arrangement. The listener leaves with nothing installed; the operator leaves with a specification. Naming the manipulation outright is not a slip — an admitted appetite is much harder to object to than a concealed one, and the loop it opens outlives the recording.


<a id="entry-1383"></a>

### dead-sibling-battery-drag

[#1383](#entry-1383) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

When one trigger in a regularly run set has gone dead, worn out or been spoiled by a bad experience, keeping it in the routine drags down the triggers fired alongside it. Removing it lifts the rest without any re-drilling. You can tell this apart from general tiredness because a trigger fired on its own is unaffected; only the ones run together with the dead one are weaker. It also works in reverse: a deliberately deadened trigger can be slipped into a set to dampen the whole set.


**When to reach for this.** `counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening` weakens ONE stimulus's own control over ONE response by training an incompatible state against it; the collateral effect on unrelated co-present cues is exactly what it does not model. `trigger-network-mutual-binding` cross-wires a set so any node recruits the others — mutual REINFORCEMENT, the positive-sign version of this, and it predicts a dead node weakens the web only via lost support, not via active downward re-weighting. `opposed-state-fusion-trigger` fuses antagonistic states onto ONE token; here the interference is between separate cues. `category-as-self-firing-cue` and `ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet` are cue-surface moves, not inter-cue relations. Deciding tell: the harm travels from a suppressed cue to its co-present neighbours, and the fix is retirement of the suppressed cue rather than any work on the neighbours.


**Why it works.** Cues fired in the same run are judged against each other. A cue that reliably predicts no payoff lowers the expected value of the whole run, so the subject's readiness to respond is set by the run as a whole rather than by each cue alone. That is why the effect depends on the cues appearing together, and why removing the dead one, rather than retraining it, is the fix. Testable: if a weakened trigger fired alone, in a session where the dead cue never appeared, showed the same weakness, the problem is not about the cues appearing together and is ordinary general suppression. And if retiring the dead cue did not lift the others over a comparable number of repetitions, the claimed cause is wrong.


**Worked examples.**

- *Retiring the poisoned cue to lift its co-present neighbours*
  - **Setup.** One cue in a five-cue battery was extinguished or soured months ago but is still being fired alongside the others; the other four have all been sitting below their old strength, while a cue tested in isolation still runs clean.
  - **The move.** The old snap cue is out of the set — I'm not using it again, and you won't hear it in a run. We keep the other four exactly as they are, no extra drilling, and we run them clean tonight.
  - **Why it lands.** Removing the suppressed member stops it re-weighting the cues fired alongside it, so the rest recover without any work being done on them. The confirming observation is specificity: only cues that shared a run with the dead one improve, and a cue that was always fired alone shows no change — which rules out general fatigue or satiation.
- *Parking a dead cue as a deliberate broad-spectrum damper*
  - **Setup.** The operator wants a live battery running at reduced strength without extinguishing any individual member, and has an already-suppressed cue available.
  - **The move.** We're putting the old snap cue back into the run — right in the middle, between the breath and the word. It doesn't have to do anything. It just travels with the others.
  - **Why it lands.** A suppressed cue kept in the running set drags the responses of everything fired with it, damping the whole battery from one insertion. The operator watches for a uniform softening across co-present members that reverses on removal, which distinguishes it from the individual cues having weakened on their own.


<a id="entry-1461"></a>

### decoy-focus-monitor-parking

[#1461](#entry-1461) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: attention*

Give the listener's conscious attention a job: focus completely on an imagined object or idea that has already been made vivid. Then say openly that while they do that, they don't need to listen to your voice, and their subconscious will simply absorb your commands. Keep giving commands the whole time. If their mind wanders, send it back to the object, never to your voice. Because the split is stated out loud, agreeing to it feels like being a good participant rather than giving in, and the 'don't listen' permission is never withdrawn, so it covers everything said afterward.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script splits into two channels — an object the listener is told to watch, and a voice they are told to stop monitoring while it keeps issuing commands. The tell is an explicit 'you don't need to listen to my voice' paired with uninterrupted command delivery, plus drift-handling that sends wandering attention back to the decoy rather than back to the voice.


**Worked examples.**

- *overt permission to stop listening as cover for the unmonitored command channel*
  - You don't need to listen very closely to my voice anymore. All you should do now is concentrate on picturing Chastity


**See also.** `covert-linguistic-delivery` — shares the unaudited-channel axis: commands travel a route the conscious mind is not evaluating.; `fixation` — the decoy is a fixation object; this move repurposes the fixation substrate as a parking spot for the monitor.


<a id="entry-1360"></a>

### decoy-target-affect-split

[#1360](#entry-1360) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: framing*

One affective response is split across two targets: a conspicuous, ridiculous stand-in absorbs the sanctioned surface reaction (the audience laughs AT the buffoon), while the sharper unsanctioned charge — contempt, indignation, distrust — is silently re-aimed at the institution, doctrine, or person standing behind the decoy. Because the audience believes it is only enjoying the harmless figure, no defense is mounted for the real target, and the critique is absorbed without ever having been argued. The move requires a visible stand-in genuinely attached to the real target, so that discrediting the front contaminates the back by association rather than by assertion.


**When to reach for this.** Against `class-collision-humor` (0.500): that produces the humor response itself by whiplashing a dual-class stimulus between two readings; here the humor is not the payload but the cover — its job is to occupy the audience's declared reaction so the undeclared one can travel. Against `negative-exemplar-double-bind` (0.499): that stages a third party as a punishment/aspiration exemplar aimed AT the listener's own conduct; here the third party is not a lesson about the listener at all, it is a lightning rod for affect destined elsewhere. Against `response-model-affect-tag` (0.512): that models what the listener should feel about the current line; this splits a feeling the listener already has and misdirects half of it. Against `counterfeit-cue-forgery` (0.488): that forges a cue's provenance; here nothing is forged — the decoy is genuinely attached to the target, which is exactly why the transfer works.


**Why it works.** Attitude toward a target moves when something reliably associated with it is devalued, and evaluations acquired that way are not tagged with their source — so the audience ends up holding the verdict without holding a memory of being argued into it, which is why it survives arguments it never engaged. Falsifiable: if a listener's rated attitude toward the real target is unchanged after a decoy pass but shifts under direct criticism, the transfer is not occurring; likewise if listeners can accurately report that the decoy segment changed their view of the institution, the undefended-because-unnoticed part of the account fails. Weakening the decoy's real association with the target should weaken the effect; if the effect persists with an arbitrary decoy, the mechanism is something other than associative transfer.


**Worked examples.**

- *Ridiculous stand-in absorbs the laugh while contempt travels to the institution behind it*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session framing passage, addressing a body of outside advice the subject has been consulting; a specific pompous public figure who fronts that advice has already been established as a running joke.
  - **The move.** Picture him again — the diplomas on the wall behind him, the little laser pointer, the way he says "studies show" and then adjusts his tie. Go ahead and laugh, he's ridiculous. And every single word he reads out was written for him upstairs, by people who chose him for it.
  - **Why it lands.** The audience's declared reaction is fully occupied by the harmless figure, so no defence is mounted for the body standing behind him, and the sharper charge — contempt, distrust — arrives at the institution without ever having been argued. The operator observes the subject laughing along and, later, treating the source itself with a flatness they never chose or defended.


<a id="entry-1451"></a>

### deepener-carrier-lamination

[#1451](#entry-1451) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: conditioning*

A second change (obedience, lower intelligence, body changes, permission to move) is woven into each beat of a trusted deepener, such as a countdown, so it goes in as part of the package rather than as a claim to weigh up. Each beat pairs depth with the change ('deeper and more obedient'), so accepting the count means accepting both. Repeated across many beats, it comes to feel like part of going deeper. Some versions make it a sign of depth (a hand 'unlocked' only as the mind sinks), so the behavior feels caused rather than chosen; others fix a lasting result at a numbered step.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a payload variable rides inside the cadence of a routine deepener — numbered countdown beats or relaxation patter each carrying an extra adjective or increment alongside the depth language. The tell is that the payload never appears as its own suggestion sentence anywhere in the script: it exists only fused to depth phrasing ("deeper and more obedient"), repeated beat after beat, so the deepener structure itself is the delivery vehicle.


**Worked examples.**

- *Obedience riding the numbered beats of a countdown*
  - 7, so deep, so relaxed and sinking deeper, deeper and more obedient, just listening to my voice and obeying


**See also.** `count-as-delivery-vehicle` — the per-step-cargo end of the same carrier axis: a count or descent scaffold repurposed as a suggestion-delivery armature.; `loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion` — the same payload-riding-a-count move applied at the other end of the session, inside the emergence window.; `pulse-multiplexed-command-carrier` — shares the one-carrier-many-payloads axis, with a recurring pulse stimulus instead of a deepener structure.; `task-disguised-deepener` — both fuse extra work into a structure the listener is already cooperating with, so the addition installs as cargo.


<a id="entry-1381"></a>

### delay-interval-silent-decay

[#1381](#entry-1381) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

A trigger that used to work fades to nothing even though it is still being fired and still being rewarded. The cause is a long, fixed wait between the trigger and the reward, with the trigger repeated many times during that empty stretch. Each unrewarded repetition in the gap weakens the response, and the eventual reward does not undo it. The response just gets slower, then partial, then absent, with no refusal. Check the gap, not the reward schedule: if adding more rewards does not help, the wait is the problem.


**When to reach for this.** This is the exact inversion of `reinforcement-extinction`, which reduces a behaviour by BREAKING the response-reinforcer contingency — there the payoff is withheld, here it is still arriving on every trial and the response dies anyway. `asymmetric-mantra-decay-topology` also decays a structure, but by the operator silently deleting one pole of a paired recitation — an authored removal; here nothing is removed and the decay is a by-product of an unchanged parameter. `reinforcement-leak-proofing` is about reinforcement reaching the behaviour from unintended paths — a leak problem; this is a decay that persists with the contingency perfectly sealed. `irreversible-ratchet-persistence` claims one-way accumulation toward a durable state; this is one-way decay of a maintained one. The deciding tell is repetition-under-delay as the decay driver while reinforcement is intact — a maintenance failure the operator can hit while doing everything the shipped entries say to do.


**Why it works.** The gap between cue and payoff is a stretch in which the cue is present and nothing arrives. Each repetition therefore includes a long unrewarded exposure that builds suppression, while the reward at the end only reinforces the very end; the longer the gap, the worse the balance between suppression and reinforcement on each repetition. Testable: if the response faded just as fast with short gaps, with the same number of repetitions and the same reward rate, the account is wrong and this is simply ordinary thinning of the reward schedule.


**Worked examples.**

- *Diagnosing the gap between cue and payoff*
  - **Setup.** A previously reliable cue has gone slow then absent over several weeks; the operator has been firing it repeatedly through a long lead-in before the reward arrives, and has already tried adding reinforcement without effect.
  - **The move.** I've been saying the word from the moment we start and not paying it off until the end — that gap is what's killing it, not you. So from tonight the word comes once, and what it earns arrives inside two seconds. Nothing else changes.
  - **Why it lands.** Collapsing the cue-to-payoff interval and cutting the repetitions inside it removes the suppressive work the empty gap was doing, which is the only fix — the contingency was already intact, so more reward could not help. The operator watches for latency to shorten over the following sessions; if it does not, the interval was not the driver and the diagnosis was wrong.


<a id="entry-1433"></a>

### delegation-revocation

[#1433](#entry-1433) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: triggers*

Takes away a third person's ability to set off a trigger that was earlier handed to them, while keeping the trigger working for the original operator or the subject. The operator states plainly that this named person's voice no longer fires it, has the subject imagine that person saying the cue and nothing happening, and ideally confirms with a live attempt by that person that fails. The withdrawal carries the same weight as saying no in the first place: permission to share a trigger is only a real, limited grant if it can be taken back.


**When to reach for this.** The object revoked is the DELEGATION — one named party's right to fire an existing trigger — never the programming: voiding the cue for all utterers is the mirrored-install-removal direction, an operator dissolving their own authority at termination is the credit-return/control-handover close, and a clause that auto-revokes transferability when trust lapses is the attested conditional neighbor (trust-gated-trigger-clause). Only here does a specific third party lose firing rights while the cue-response link itself survives.


**Risk.** Protective/hygiene direction of the third-party-activation surface: removes a standing high-risk capability rather than installing one. By consent doctrine a revocation may never itself be gated on a ceremony that could be withheld, so no explicit-consent or bounding flags. Authored prescriptively — a safety model that can grant an irrevocable capability is worse than one that never modeled it: granting a third party the right to fire an installed cue requires that the grant be withdrawable, and an explicit cancel-phrase protocol revokes the programming itself, not the delegation.


**Why it works.** A delegate fires the trigger because their identity was trained into the discriminative stimulus class; revocation is discrimination retraining that re-narrows the class to exclude them — the same stimulus-control mechanics as the operator-exclusivity/voice-lock clauses, run in the withdraw direction. Renewal and spontaneous recovery predict a revoked delegate's cue may fire again after delay or context shift, so a single revocation without a delayed re-test is not a completed revocation. Falsifiable: after revocation the former delegate's utterance should fail while the operator's still fires; if both fail, the move tore down the programming instead of the delegation. [prescriptive; stimulus control / discrimination training; consent-revocation-as-refusal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Named de-authorization, rehearsed as a null firing, then live-tested*
  - **Setup.** A trigger is installed and a specific third party was previously granted the right to fire it; subject is in a working state and consents to the revocation.
  - **The move.** Listen closely, because this changes one thing and only one thing. The word still works — it works when I say it, and it works when you say it to yourself. It no longer works in his voice. Picture him now, standing right in front of you, saying it exactly the way he used to — and notice how nothing moves. Nothing rises, nothing goes. Again: he says it, and it's just a word. Good. He'll try it once in person this week, and it will do exactly what it just did.
  - **Why it lands.** The identity component of the cue-complex is re-narrowed by explicit naming, and the imagined null firing gives the subject direct experiential evidence that the exclusion holds rather than a mere instruction to be complied with. Observable: during rehearsal the subject shows no somatic onset at the imagined utterance, and the live attempt by the revoked party fails to fire while the operator's own utterance still does — that asymmetry is the confirmation, and it demonstrates the programming survived.


**See also.** `mirrored-install-removal` — programming-revocation neighbor: 907 voids the effect for everyone via a mirrored off-switch; this entry revokes one delegate's access and keeps the programming; `operator-exclusive-trigger-firing` — the access-control sibling in the restrict direction: 1307 binds firing to the operator's voice from install time; this entry returns an already-delegated trigger to that narrower state; `third-party-activation` — the grant this entry withdraws; 1321 presupposes the trigger exists and hands off activation authority — this entry takes that authority back from a named delegate; `trust-gated-trigger-clause`


<a id="entry-1389"></a>

### deniable-misdelivery

[#1389](#entry-1389) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: concealment*

The real target gets a message disguised as a routing mistake: a reply-all that 'should' have been private, a note left where they will certainly read it, a remark made 'to someone else' within earshot, a file 'accidentally' attached. Because it seems not meant for them, they take it as unguarded truth and give it more weight than if it had been said to their face. The sender can always say 'that wasn't for you, sorry', but the message has already landed. It can carry things that could never be said directly: accusations, desires, judgements.


**When to reach for this.** Every nearest neighbour hides the payload INSIDE a correctly-addressed delivery; this one hides it in a fake addressing error while the surface content stays plain. Versus covert-linguistic-delivery (183): there the payload rides the surface FORM of a correctly-addressed utterance (presupposition, ambiguity, embedded command) and is unrecoverable by conscious audit; here the content is fully explicit and audit-visible — what is faked is who it was for. Versus register-camouflaged-delivery (286): 286 conceals the payload in an unmonitored CHANNEL or register (aside, background track, offhand remark) so the evaluator never scans it; here the recipient scans it with full attention, and the misaddressing is what licenses the content rather than what hides it. Versus operator-delivery-craft (1280): that shapes the operator's own transmitted signal — tone, gesture, texture; nothing about the delivery signal changes here, only its declared destination. Versus disavowal-and-masking (95): 95 denies the operation exists; here the message plainly exists and is acknowledged — only its intentionality is denied. The source's dyadic-correspondents framing is incidental; the mechanism is operator-usable as stated.


**Why it works.** Overheard and apparently-unintended communications are discounted less than directly-addressed ones because the recipient's persuasion-knowledge defenses key on perceived intent to persuade — content believed not to be aimed at you is not filtered for motive, so it is credited more, and this overheard-communication advantage is a robust finding in the persuasion literature. The retraction path works separately: a disavowed message is not un-read, since retrieval of the content is not gated on believing it was intended. Falsifiable: if the identical content produced equal belief change and equal recipient impact whether it arrived as an apparent misdelivery or as a direct address, the credibility half fails; if invoking the 'not meant for you' retraction measurably reduced the recipient's later acceptance of the content back to baseline, the one-way claim fails. [plausible; persuasion knowledge / discounting of intentional persuasive intent; overheard-communication credibility advantage]


**Worked examples.**

- *The remark made 'to someone else' within earshot*
  - **Setup.** The target is in the next room or across the table with the door open; the operator speaks to a third person at conversational volume, pitched to carry.
  - **The move.** No, honestly — the change in them these last few weeks is something. They've gone soft in a way they'd never admit to your face. Wait, is the door — never mind.
  - **Why it lands.** The content arrives fully explicit and fully heard, but because it was supposedly not addressed to the target, it is taken as unguarded truth and carries more weight than the same sentence said directly. The operator can still back away from it at no cost, and backing away does not undo how it was heard. The operator watches for the target to bring it up later on their own terms, which shows the message landed.
- *The message sent to the wrong window on purpose*
  - **Setup.** Ongoing text correspondence; the operator composes an assessment or desire that could not be stated directly, and sends it to the target framed as meant for a third party.
  - **The move.** God, I can't stop thinking about what they'd do if I actually asked. — Sorry, that was meant for someone else. Ignore that.
  - **Why it lands.** The misdelivery frame licenses content the direct channel withholds, and the apology arrives after the reading is complete, so the move is one-way. The operator's observable is whether the target treats the retraction as sincere; either way the content has been read, and a target who does not respond at all has still received it.
- *The note left where it will certainly be found*
  - **Setup.** The operator has physical access to a space the target uses daily and wants an assessment delivered without ever having said it.
  - **The move.** Have you seen a folded page in here? I was writing something out for myself and I've mislaid it — it's not for anyone else, so if you find it just leave it face-down.
  - **Why it lands.** Framing the document as private and unintended guarantees it is read as candid rather than composed, which is exactly what lends it evidential weight. The instruction to leave it face-down supplies the retraction path in advance; the operator observes any change in the target's behaviour without the subject ever admitting they read it.


<a id="entry-1410"></a>

### deprivation-reversal-ceiling

[#1410](#entry-1410) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

Most escalation assumes more is better: more denial, more deprivation, more holding back gives more drive and more effort. That stops being true past a certain point. Beyond it, further deprivation lowers responsiveness, and the person pushed harder does less, not more. This sets an upper limit on every escalation or denial routine. What to watch for: a response that stops rising and starts falling as pressure increases is the limit announcing itself, not resistance or a failed install, and it is a signal to ease off rather than push harder.


**When to reach for this.** vs motivating-operation-engineering: that entry owns BOTH value directions but its only ceiling is the one-line 'satiation/aversion overshoot' on the ABOLISHING side — value falls because more was GIVEN. This is the ESTABLISHING side inverting: output falls while deprivation keeps increasing, the opposite manipulation reaching a similar place, and the case that entry does not elaborate. vs deprivation-manufactured-craving: that manufactures want by removal or object-substitution and its named failure mode is a chronic never-closeable need, not an output reversal. vs unsatisfiable-arousal-overrun: that drives past a declared scale maximum and removes the discharge move, assuming the engine keeps climbing — this names where it stops. vs manufactured-insufficiency-ratchet and compounding-escalation-ratchet: both keep resetting 'enough' upward on the same unbounded assumption. vs capacity-saturation-overload: that is processing CAPACITY starving evaluation in-session; this is motivational drive inverting its own output relation.


**Why it works.** Deprivation raises output only while the capacity to produce the response is intact. Past a point, deprivation wears down that capacity faster than it raises motivation, so the combined effect turns over: an inverted U rather than a plateau. Testable by the shape of the curve: increase deprivation step by step and measure output. If output rises and then levels off without falling, there is a ceiling but no reversal, and the claim is overstated. If output keeps climbing at every level a limited, safe protocol can reach, the reversal lies outside the practical range and does not matter in practice. The capacity explanation can be tested too: past the peak, responses should become slower, weaker and less complete rather than being clean refusals. If they stay intact but simply come less often, motivation fell rather than capacity, and the explanation is wrong even if the curve is right.


**Worked examples.**

- *Rate turns down under increasing denial; ceiling read, pressure released*
  - **Setup.** A denial structure has been escalating for several sessions and output has been climbing with it; this session the subject is slower and flatter than last, under strictly more withholding.
  - **The move.** Stop. You're not going to earn anything back right now and you're not in trouble — that's not what this is. We're going the other way tonight. Take it, all of it, right now, and don't ask me for permission first.
  - **Why it lands.** A rate that stops climbing and turns down while deprivation keeps increasing is the drive-response relation inverting, not resistance and not a failed install; the correct read is that the monotonic range has been exceeded. The operator releases pressure and watches whether responding recovers on the way back down — which distinguishes the ceiling from a genuine refusal.


<a id="entry-1453"></a>

### deprivation-then-grant-relief

[#1453](#entry-1453) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology*

Press a strict rule, a false promise, or an ordeal until it genuinely chafes, then grant one narrow exception. The exception lands as relief the listener grabs gratefully, not as an instruction to stop and weigh. The feeling flips from frustration to reward, and a release found as an escape is held tighter than one offered as a deal. Variations: an absolute rule stated at length before one permitted exception; a first countdown that reaches the bottom and then reverses, so a second count's real permission feels like a gift; a first trance taken away so the listener begs, making the second feel wanted.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the early phase's whole function is aversive pressure — an exhaustive prohibition, a countdown deliberately reversed at its bottom, an imposed ordeal followed by withdrawal — that a later narrow grant then discharges. The tell is the emotional sign-flip on the payload itself: the same content that would read as instruction or negotiable deal if delivered first instead lands as relief, reward, or fulfillment, gratefully claimed by the listener as their own escape.


**Worked examples.**

- *Absolute rule pressed until the lone exception feels like escape*
  - Presenting the absolute first makes the exception feel like a found escape


**See also.** `arc-ordering-dependency` — the rule-before-exception realization sits inside this genus of load-bearing phase ordering.; `scaffold-then-spend-sequencing` — sibling sequencing move where the early phase installs premises rather than aversive pressure.; `truncated-cue-inhibition-charging` — neighbouring withheld-payoff axis, where repeated truncation trains suppression instead of pricing a later grant.


<a id="entry-1019"></a>

### depth-capping-time-commitment

[#1019](#entry-1019) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: deepening*

Before the session, the subject picks a set length of time to stay in a light trance. Keeping that commitment in mind keeps them aware that they can return to normal awareness at any moment, which holds them near the surface. Depth becomes something they keep steady and light rather than a one-way slide down. The time commitment is there to limit depth, not to increase it.


**When to reach for this.** Nothing here is a trigger — unlike a trigger-expiry clause, which bounds when an installed trigger stops working, this is a depth-regulation move that holds trance shallow. It also differs from the related reality-availability and value-dial deepeners in using a fixed duration commitment specifically to cap rather than raise depth.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible depth-holding with no consent surface or channel erosion; keeps the subject shallow and reality-available.


**Why it works.** Hypnotic depth tracks the subject's own expectancy and self-report more than any independent state variable, so a pre-committed intention to remain light functions as a self-directed expectancy that caps reported and behavioral responsiveness. The time commitment also keeps an external referent (elapsed clock time, the option to stop) in working memory, and maintaining that referent competes with the absorbed, narrowed attention that deeper trance reports depend on. Falsifiable: subjects who fix a light-depth duration in advance should score lower on standard suggestibility measures than the same subjects without the commitment; no difference would refute it. [plausible; expectancy effects on hypnotic responding; attentional absorption competing with external monitoring]


**Worked examples.**

- *A fixed light-trance duration caps depth*
  - "he did this by setting a given length of time during which he would remain in a light trance. This had the effect of making him more strongly aware that at any moment he could 'reach out and seize external reality'" — Bandler & Grinder (1975), Patterns of the Hypnotic Techniques of Milton H. Erickson, Vol. I


**See also.** `scope-coupled-depth-titration` — both treat depth as a controllable variable rather than a one-way descent, and they are complementary knobs: a fixed advance commitment holding depth light, versus scope width pulling depth up as a structural consequence. A reader wanting to regulate rather than maximize depth benefits from seeing both.; `temporal-orientation-voiding` — the same clock-awareness lever worked in reverse: a held time-commitment keeps temporal orientation salient to cap depth rather than dissolving it.


<a id="entry-1414"></a>

### describer-cost-deterrence

[#1414](#entry-1414) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

Rather than argue with an unfavorable account, the group makes producing one expensive for the person producing it. Two levers combine: an asymmetric cost threat aimed at a party who cannot match the group's resources — the researcher, the writer, the small publisher — and an individualized, surveillance-flavored signal that this particular person has been noticed by name. Neither lever contests the account's accuracy; both operate on the describer's expected cost of publishing it. The describer softens the claim or drops it, or the publisher withdraws, and what survives into the public record is whatever was cheap to say. Because the surviving descriptions were selected by cost rather than by merit, the group becomes the de facto arbiter of how it is described without ever winning an argument.


**When to reach for this.** The target is a third party who DESCRIBES the subject population, not the subject and not the subject's counter-frame — no v7 entry acts on an outside observer's incentives, which is what makes this a genuine gap rather than a restatement. Honest caveat on grain: institutional rather than script-executable, and the family fit is by function (information-environment control) rather than by altitude.


**Why it works.** This works on the public record, not on any one person's mind. When publishing a critical account costs the writer something, and the cost rises the more damaging the account is, the accounts that survive are a skewed sample. Nobody has to be fooled and no claim has to be disproved for this to happen. It is the same structure as publication bias, where a fair set of findings produces a lopsided literature simply because some results are costlier to publish. Singling a writer out by name adds a separate effect: personal attention makes the risk feel much larger than the actual odds of action, which is why naming someone works better than a general policy. This could be tested by comparing accounts written under legal risk with accounts of the same group written without it (other countries, anonymous posts, or people no longer exposed). If both agree in tone and content, the deterrence is not shaping the record.


**Worked examples.**

- *Asymmetric cost aimed at a party who cannot match it*
  - **Setup.** An outside writer has a piece in progress about the group; the group's counsel drafts a letter to the small press rather than to the writer.
  - **The move.** We want to be clear that we are not asking you to change a word. We simply want you to know that we retain counsel on annual engagement, that we have pursued matters of this kind to their conclusion before, and that our resources for doing so are not a constraint on us. Please take whatever time your own review requires.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing in the account is contested; only the describer's expected cost of publishing it is raised, and the resource asymmetry does the arithmetic for them. The observable outcome is a softened claim or a withdrawn book, and what survives into the public record is whatever was cheap to say.
- *Individualized surveillance-flavored signal that a named person was noticed*
  - **Setup.** A single researcher has published a preliminary finding; the group's contact reaches them directly, in their own name.
  - **The move.** We read your paper — the one from the March conference, not the earlier version. We noticed you've moved, and that you're presenting again in the autumn. We follow this work closely and we wanted you to know that we know who is doing it.
  - **Why it lands.** Making the describer individually visible converts a professional act into a personally costly one, again without disputing anything they wrote. The operator observes the effect not on the researcher's beliefs but on their output volume — and because the surviving descriptions were selected by cost rather than merit, the group ends up arbitrating how it is described without having won an argument.


<a id="entry-1021"></a>

### description-as-installation-register

[#1021](#entry-1021) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: self-partition*

The operator speaks about the listener in the third person ("the persona," "she") and describes her responses as ongoing accomplished facts, never addressing her as "you" and never issuing a second-person command. This sidesteps the listener's normal command-evaluation interface — a listener can refuse a command but cannot refuse a description of a self she is already inside — and positions her as overhearing her own conditioning, which is itself mildly dissociative. The install lands as reportage of what is already true rather than as an instruction to be weighed.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the systematic zero-occurrence of second-person "you" across the whole file, with the listener rendered as a described third-person object whose responses are stated as facts. It is the REGISTER — describe-don't-command — that is the lever, not any single line.


**Risk.** Erodes the command-evaluation checkpoint by routing installs around it as description rather than instruction; session-scoped and reversible, but it lowers the refusal threshold.


**Why it works.** Third-person description removes the pragmatic slot where a directive would normally be evaluated: comprehending an assertion requires provisionally representing it as true (Gilbert's Spinozan model), while rejection is a separate, effortful second step that a description about someone else does not obviously invite. Because no request is addressed to the listener, no compliance decision is triggered, yet self-referential processing still binds the described content to self-concept. Falsifiable: if listeners rejected or resisted third-person descriptions of themselves at the same rate as second-person commands, or showed no self-referential encoding advantage for them, the account fails. [plausible; Spinozan belief fixation (comprehension entails provisional acceptance); self-referential encoding; absence of a compliance-decision cue]


**Worked examples.**

- *Described in the third person, never addressed*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, any point after settling; the operator has not used the word "you" once and will not.
  - **The move.** She's settled now — her breathing has gone slow without her arranging it. She doesn't hold on to thoughts the way she used to; they arrive, and she lets them go past. And she likes the sound of that word. She likes it more each time it's said near her.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing in the recording is aimed at "you." The operator talks about the listener instead, in the third person and in the present tense, as a matter of record: she settles easily now, she doesn't hold on to thoughts any more, she likes the sound of that word. Over a whole file the pronoun that would let the listener answer never appears once. There is no command to weigh, so the ordinary reflex of accepting or declining an instruction never fires — and refusing a description of yourself that you are apparently already living out has no obvious grammar. It also seats the listener slightly outside herself, overhearing her own conditioning being discussed by someone else.


**See also.** `covert-install-under-cover` — third-person clinical exposition is one of the concealment covers in the broader hidden-install family, so the two genuinely overlap on one surface. Kept as a cross-reference rather than a merge because one is a whole-artifact register (zero second-person address across the entire piece, describe-don't-command) while the other is a family of install-act disguises that mostly still address the listener directly.; `dissolution-then-installation` — the third-person describe-don't-command register the dissolution movement often runs in before the hinge.; `indirect-command-smuggling` — both deliver the payload in a register the listener's command-evaluation interface never receives as a refusable second-person imperative.; `inner-voice-authorship-bypass` — both remove the addressee that resistance would push against, but one reattributes the words to the listener's own inner voice while the other keeps the operator as speaker and renders the listener as a described third-person object she overhears.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both defeat the listener's command-evaluation interface by making an install arrive as description rather than instruction - one by manufacturing the referent first so the later claim reads as recognition, the other by never using second person at all. Complementary routes to the same interface bypass, and they can be layered.; `pronoun-migration-identity-install` — both install without a second-person command, and both work by grammatical person rather than assertion. One slides the referent from a described category onto the listener; the other keeps the listener permanently in third person so nothing is ever addressed to her to refuse. A reader picking a covert-enrollment register gains from seeing the drift form and the never-say-you form side by side.; `scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier` — shares the third-person descriptive register that bypasses the listener's command-evaluation interface.; `subject-voiced-self-mantra` — two poles of grammatical-person register as the install vehicle: the listener speaking the endpoint in first person with no operator surface, versus the operator describing the listener in third person and never issuing a second-person command. Both remove the command-evaluation interface by manipulating who is addressed.; `uninvited-pronoun-migration-enrollment` — both install via grammatical person rather than command, but one holds the listener permanently in described third person so there is no command to refuse, while the other walks pronouns toward the listener and makes the refusal to invite the load-bearing move.


<a id="entry-1549"></a>

### description-first-install

[#1549](#entry-1549) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

Use the trigger phrase many times in ordinary sentences before saying what it does: 'love to [phrase],' 'because you [phrase],' 'when you [phrase],' lines that seem to describe what is already happening. Only then announce that these words return the person to this state. A trigger can also be introduced by describing its effect on others ('every time I use that voice, they slip') before turning to the listener, or by borrowing a familiar game like tag, using it casually ('I can tag you and you go deeper') before installing it with a touch. Since nothing sounded like an install, the listener's guard stays down, and the announcement turns the earlier uses into practice. This only works if the listener meets the early uses cold, without having read or heard the script in advance.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a trigger must bypass the listener's anticipation of trigger language by being planted before it is ever named as one. The tell is a distinctive phrase recurring in ordinary sentence roles — reports, explanations, anecdotes about someone else, game metaphors — followed only later by an announcement of its function, so that the reveal confirms conditioning that the prior uses already performed.


**Worked examples.**

- *deniable prior fires, installation announced last*
  - by the time the explicit installation lands, the listener has rehearsed the response twice without recognizing the rehearsals as installations


**See also.** `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — shared axis of a benign advertised surface carrying an unrequested payload until past the point a wary listener would have exited.; `covert-install-under-cover` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its description-first temporal cover.; `install-under-attentional-cover` — sibling cover: there the listener's parsing capacity is consumed by a concurrent task, here attention is free and the timing of the reveal does the concealment.


<a id="entry-527"></a>

### design-time-reconnaissance

[#527](#entry-527) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Before designing anything, map everything the plan must survive, so gaps show up on paper, not in real life. One form: list every setting where the behavior should and should not happen, with alternative responses planned for the wrong moments; list every form the response should take and decide which to train directly; and survey the cues and rewards already present in those settings. The other: have the person write out every part of them that objects and why, checking every sense rather than stopping at the first few, warning that many usually object. Either way, a missed setting or objection can't resurface after commitment.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for design-time-reconnaissance when the writer needs an exhaustive pre-design map so nothing is missed -- a completeness sweep on the PLAN before any teaching/install, subject untouched. Tells: enumerate should/should-not settings + response-form triage + standing-contingency survey (a); complete written cross-channel census of objectors (b). Its contingency survey supplies the environment map that target-selection's maintainability criterion tests against.


**Risk.** Planning reconnaissance with environmental-survey and participant objection-census variants from different sources; the latter includes direct questioning and must not be described as subject-free.


**Why it works.** Learned responses are under stimulus control, so what is trained in one set of conditions does not automatically transfer to conditions never enumerated — generalization is the exception and must be planned for, which is why an explicit inventory of settings and non-settings outperforms assumption. The objector census leans on a weaker claim: externalizing and writing down items reduces reliance on recall, and free recall reliably under-samples a set relative to prompted or exhaustive enumeration, so first-responders crowd out the rest. Falsifiable: if plans built with exhaustive enumeration showed no fewer post-commitment failures than plans built from unaided recall, the value claim is wrong. [plausible; stimulus control and non-automatic generalization; retrieval-cue limits on free recall]


**Worked examples.**

- *Enumerate where it should and should not occur*
  - "situations that may appear to be appropriate opportunities…but are not…for which an alternative response is needed" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Enumerate response forms, then triage teaching*
  - "Only by having a complete list of all the desired forms of the behavior can the practitioner make meaningful decisions about which behaviors to teach directly and which to leave to generalization" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Survey the contingencies already running in the setting*
  - "What discriminative stimuli usually set the occasion…What schedules of reinforcement…are typical…What kinds of reinforcers are likely to be contingent" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (1): `exhaustive-objector-census`


**See also.** `operator-side-design-gating` — both are planner-facing pre-deployment checks on the design with nothing delivered to the subject: one exhaustively enumerates the space the plan must survive, the other tests whether the planned baselines actually determine the intended emergent relations and blocks the protocol if not. Enumeration and the go/no-go gate it feeds are naturally read together.; `target-selection` — adjacent design-time operator moves that are easy to conflate, and each discriminator already names the other: one filters and operationalizes which target to aim at, the other exhaustively enumerates the space the plan must survive. They also interlock, since the enumeration supplies the environment map the selection criteria test against. Filtering is not enumerating, so no merge.


<a id="entry-1375"></a>

### designated-bearer-culpability-transfer

[#1375](#entry-1375) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: social-topology*

A group's shared blame is piled onto one person through an acted-out ritual, and that person's acceptance is staged to look like their own free choice. Everyone else leaves feeling lighter without having admitted anything. Because the transfer is performed rather than argued, there is no claim for anyone to dispute, and because the bearer seems to volunteer, nobody, including the bearer, experiences it as something forced on them.


**When to reach for this.** Blame moves sideways ACROSS PERSONS, from a collective to one member, and the transfer is masked as the recipient's own choice. All three shortlisted agency-diffusion neighbours relocate authorship of the SUBJECT'S OWN state and never reassign blame to a different person: impersonal-mechanism-alibi moves authority for a change onto an unfalsifiable impersonal thing (biology, fate, law) so doubt becomes a category error — no second person receives anything; register-hybrid-agency-diffusion smears ownership between operator-agency and apparatus-agency across a whole script's vocabulary, again within the one subject; object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition installs an object as the declared cause of the subject's own compliance. arc-shape-engineering is the nearest structural match — a whole-arc topology where the operator manufactures a condition and sells its cure — but its payload is control transfer to the operator, where here the operator may not be a beneficiary at all and the payload is a redistribution of culpability among participants. The tell against all four: after the move a DIFFERENT person is carrying something they did not previously carry.


**Why it works.** Groups discharge collective liability more readily onto a single identified bearer than by distributing it, because a concentrated attribution gives the remainder a clean exit that a distributed one does not; enactment rather than argument supplies the warrant, since a performed act leaves no premise available to dispute. The self-chosen surface matters independently: a transfer that reads as volunteered does not activate the fairness objections an assignment would, from the group or from the bearer. Falsifiable: run the same re-enactment with the bearer visibly assigned by the group rather than appearing to elect the role; if the group's reported relief and the bearer's uptake are unchanged, the concealed-choice element is decorative and the effect is plain scapegoating. Separately, if participants' sense of their own culpability is unchanged after the ritual — measured before and after — the transfer claim fails outright, whatever the bearer reports. [plausible; scapegoating and collective blame displacement; ritual enactment as warrant; volunteered-versus-assigned role effects on perceived fairness. The cultural-anthropology origin of this account is interpretive and is not evidence for the mechanism.]


**Worked examples.**

- *Staged re-enactment with the load taken up as the bearer's own election*
  - **Setup.** A group session closing out a period the whole group is implicated in; one member has been quietly set up all evening as the one who will step forward, and everyone is standing in a ring.
  - **The move.** One of you is going to take up what the rest of us have been carrying. Nobody will be asked and nobody will be chosen — whoever it is will simply step into the middle when they're ready. When you step in, you carry it for all of us, and the rest of us set it down. Step in when it's yours.
  - **Why it lands.** Blame moves sideways across persons, from the collective onto one member, and the ritual form supplies the warrant — the transfer is enacted, so there is no proposition to contest. The self-chosen surface conceals the reassignment, so no participant experiences having imposed anything; after the move a different person is carrying what the group was carrying, and everyone else leaves lighter with standing intact.


<a id="entry-1496"></a>

### desire-priced-in-depth

[#1496](#entry-1496) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: conditioning*

A craving the listener already brings to the session — live arousal, hunger for fetish contact, appetite for a coveted title — is not satisfied directly; instead its route to satisfaction is redefined as the operator's goal-state, so that wanting the reward IS the descent engine. "Step one" toward the desired thing is a deepening instruction ("Well, step one, / sleep even deeper"), or access is explicitly priced in units of trance depth and enslavement (touching heels but not feet, direct contact only earned by going deeper), or a craved label like "good slave" is named, made desirable, and deferred behind unspecified performance. The price then ratchets or the gate recedes — heels, then bare feet, then contact; the title granted and revoked to keep the striving loop open — so satisfaction is always one surrender further down. This converts pre-existing motivation into deepening fuel rather than a competing distraction, and it runs without any discharge or release event ever being required: the mechanism operates even when nothing is released, because the coupling is between wanting and depth, not between compliance and payoff.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the listener's desire demonstrably pre-exists the move — the script assumes arousal or craving is already live and does not manufacture it — and the operator prices its satisfaction in depth, surrender, or earned worth. The tell is toll-gate grammar: the first step toward the wanted thing is a deepening command, access is rationed in explicit units of submission, and the price visibly ratchets or the goal keeps receding so the striving loop never closes.


**Worked examples.**

- *fetish access explicitly priced in trance depth and enslavement*
  - the only way you can ever touch my feet, is by going deeper, by becoming even more enslaved


**See also.** `opposed-state-fusion-trigger` — shares the wanting-welded-to-deepening axis: seeking the desired state is made mechanically identical to going deeper.; `petition-phrase-toll-gate` — both put a toll booth on descent — there the toll is a compelled petition phrase, here the toll runs the other way: depth is the currency and the fetish object the purchase.; `severed-relief-valve-ramp` — same deferred-satisfaction economics at whole-arc scale: discharge is withheld so accumulated drive converts into depth.


<a id="entry-1437"></a>

### diegetic-channel-continuity-license

[#1437](#entry-1437) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

When the story being told would stop the operator from speaking (their mouth is busy, they have walked away, they are not in the scene), the script says their voice carries on anyway: inside the listener's head, by telepathy, or through some device. This lets the instructions keep flowing at exactly the moments the scene would otherwise silence them, so the listener never has to choose between staying immersed in the story and staying under suggestion. Example line: 'Even with a busy mouth, I can still continue your hypnotic training.'


**When to reach for this.** The lever is keeping the DELIVERY CHANNEL open when the fiction would close it — not embedding the operator in the scene (diegetic-operator-embedding: frame swap, viewer/avatar split; here the listener remains a directly-addressed hypnosis subject and only the transmission route is fictionalized), not handing the state-change's cause to an outside agent (causal-attribution-to-external-agent: authorship of EFFECTS; here the operator keeps authorship and only transport is claimed), and not converting words into felt touch (words-as-touch-transposition: modality claim; here the modality stays verbal). Reach for this when an embodied scene must proceed without stopping the voice.


**Risk.** Session-scoped framing convenience; carries no consent or boundary erosion itself, though it deepens scene immersion and so composes with whatever is being delivered through the licensed channel.


**Why it works.** This predicts a pattern in where the move appears: claims that the voice continues show up exactly at the moments when the story has the speaker's mouth busy or takes her out of the room, and they are absent from scripts with a narrator who never has a body in the scene, since there is no contradiction to fix. Anyone could check this against a collection of erotic hypnosis scripts that stage physical scenes.


**See also.** `diegetic-operator-embedding` — shared axis: the operator participates in the fiction's delivery situation. DOE swaps the frame (viewer/avatar); this keeps the frame and fictionalizes only the transport.; `words-as-touch-transposition` — shared axis: fictionalized delivery physics — there the words become touch; here the words claim a non-oral route.


<a id="entry-1151"></a>

### diegetic-operator-embedding

[#1151](#entry-1151) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: framing*

Recast the session as watching a show rather than being hypnotized, then appear in the show yourself as a character, speaking in the same familiar voice. The listener can even watch an on-screen version of themselves listening to that voice. Someone who thinks they are only watching feels less pushed and goes along more easily, and having a version of themselves already on the screen sets up a later step where they are drawn in and become that figure.


**When to reach for this.** The operator's own voice is deliberately embedded as a character inside the substituted fiction with continuity preserved — weaponizing the frame — versus guided visualization, where the fiction is merely scene content, and versus an interposed proxy agent, where the acting figure is a third agent rather than the operator herself relocated.


**Risk.** Session-scoped frame swap, but it pre-positions identity relocation and so needs a host supplying a clean frame restore at exit.


**Why it works.** Fictional framing lowers reactance because a person who believes they are watching rather than being acted upon has no perceived freedom under threat, so the defensive motivation that produces counter-arguing is never triggered. Keeping the operator's voice constant across the frame swap exploits source-monitoring economy: the auditory stream is unchanged, so responses conditioned to that voice transfer into the fiction while the listener's explicit model of the situation has changed. The predicted split is testable — behavioural compliance should track voice continuity while self-reported 'being hypnotized' tracks the fictional frame. [plausible; psychological reactance; source-monitoring and voice-based cue transfer]


**Worked examples.**

- *The operator relocated behind the screen*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the subject accepts guided scenery and the operator's voice is well established.
  - **The move.** You're sitting in front of a screen, and something is starting. A woman comes on — and there's something odd about her voice, isn't there. It's this voice. The same one in your ears right now, only it's coming from over there, on the other side of the glass. And look: she's got headphones on. She's listening to it too. So there's you watching, and her on the screen, and you watching her being talked to — hold all three at once, and do what she does.
  - **Why it lands.** The listener is seated in front of a television and told a programme is starting — the session has quietly stopped being a session and become a thing being watched. A presenter appears on screen, and her voice is described as oddly familiar: it is the same voice still speaking into the listener's ears, now placed on the far side of the glass. The figure on screen is shown listening to that voice as well, so there are three positions in play at once — the one watching, the one being watched, and the one watching herself being worked on. Every instruction from here is followed by the viewer, not by the person being hypnotized, and the listener has already been arranged in the geometry that a later pull-through into the screen will use.


**See also.** `diegetic-activity-laundering` — both substitute a non-hypnotic fiction for the session frame so technique work reads as ordinary activity. They differ in whether the operator stays outside the cover story or is embedded inside it as a character, which is a genuine writer's choice worth surfacing.; `diegetic-channel-continuity-license` — shared axis: the operator participates in the fiction's delivery situation. DOE swaps the frame (viewer/avatar); this keeps the frame and fictionalizes only the transport.; `identity-merger-occupation` — b builds the multi-position geometry and explicitly pre-positions the listener for a later pull-through into the depicted figure; A is that pull-through, collapsing the observer split into occupation. They chain, so a reader of either benefits from the other.; `perception-source-substitution` — same screen geometry at two stages: one embeds the operator inside a substituted fiction and pre-positions the listener toward the depicted body, the other completes the move by routing sensation inbound from what is depicted.; `protective-role-conscription` — both wrap the session in a fiction that displaces the listener from the hypnotized-subject position, but they differ in what is relocated: one assigns the listener a non-participant scene-role, the other relocates the operator into the fiction as a character. A reader designing or classifying frame-substitution wrappers benefits from seeing both variants of the same displacement family.; `vicarious-depth` — both stage a protagonist geometry the listener occupies before the payload lands, one swapping the imagined subject mid-image so depth is inherited, the other embedding the operator as a character inside a substituted fiction. Useful adjacency for identity or depth transfer through an imagined scene.


<a id="entry-1505"></a>

### differential-reinforcement-low-rate

[#1505](#entry-1505) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

License the behavior in moderation: reinforcement is delivered for the behavior's occurrence, but only when the count stays at or under a predetermined criterion — full-session (at most N per session), per-interval (exceeding the criterion cancels the opportunity and starts a new interval), or spaced-responding on inter-response times. The behavior is throttled to a tolerable band, never banned, which suits acts that are desirable in small doses (asking for help, hand-raising). The ceiling can be reified as a tangible depleting resource: a card with one box per allowed response initialed as each is spent, or a pack of coupons whose unspent remainder converts to bonus tokens with real purchasing power — and the payout is deliberately capped (one point no matter how many boxes remain) so the subject uses the allowance rather than maximizing abstention. Variants are chosen by feedback immediacy: spaced-responding gives the most accurate feedback because every response that violates the inter-response-time criterion instantly withholds reinforcement and resets the interval, a per-response consequence that lets the subject self-monitor and hold the rate down.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the behavior itself is acceptable and only its rate is the problem, and you want the subject to keep spending their allowance rather than quit. The tell is a numeric ceiling with reinforcement for staying at or under it — often materialized as a visible, depleting budget (boxes, coupons) the subject can watch — with the schedule's own reset acting as immediate per-response feedback.


**Worked examples.**

- *ration with a visible meter, spending the quota stays legitimate*
  - No additional points were awarded if more than one box was left empty, because we wanted the children to use the opportunities.


**See also.** `baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration` — criterion-sizing axis: the first allowed-rate ceiling is read off the subject's own baseline session mean.; `differential-reinforcement` — parent schedule family: DRL is the license-in-moderation arm of the differential-reinforcement parametric umbrella.; `massed-practice-rate-suppression` — rate-reduction-without-banning axis: both lower a behavior's frequency while it keeps occurring, one by licensing a quota, one by costly over-emission.


<a id="entry-1464"></a>

### disavowal-as-delivery

[#1464](#entry-1464) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

The operation or its efficacy is explicitly denied while it runs. The denial takes several shapes, all doing the same work: suggestions wrapped in negation ('You can't be hypnotised to obey my every command'), where the mind must construct the suggested state in order to parse the denial — the construction lands, the discard does not; a complete slow induction delivered as a denied hypothetical ('even if I talk slowly and tell you that you're falling into a trance now'), so the pacing and imagery execute while the conscious frame logs that nothing is happening; a session-level disclaimer ('there is no induction') that leaves anti-hypnosis vigilance with no labeled act to filter, since refusing the operation would first require acknowledging an operation the frame denies; hypnotic work run as not-yet-begun preamble ('I haven't even begun yet'), so the announced induction later reads as confirmation of an existing state; the folk tripwire refuted outright ('Relaxation doesn't have anything to do with hypnosis... so I guess it's fine and okay of you to just relax'), where the refutation is itself the permission to drop the defense; and depth conceded as admitted fiction ('isn't it fun to be told you're going deeper, even if it doesn't really mean anything?') then re-reified as experiential reality. Whatever effect arrives is pre-credited to the listener's own mind — 'Your deeply conditioned responses automatically engage' — so the negation does what the affirmation could not.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script's own words deny that hypnosis is happening, has begun, or could work — and the denied content is the payload. The tell is negation as the carrier wave: 'you can't be hypnotized to X,' 'there is no induction,' 'I haven't even begun,' 'relaxation has nothing to do with hypnosis' — each denial forcing the listener to build exactly the content it discards, with any arriving effect attributed to the listener's own conditioning rather than to an operation they could refuse.


**Worked examples.**

- *induction disclaimed while it fires*
  - [Example field withheld: private source overlap.]


**See also.** `anti-effort-permission-frame` — both stand down the listener's is-it-working monitor by declaring there is nothing being done to watch for.; `natural-state-suggestion` — shares the induction-free delivery axis: suggestion lands without any acknowledged inducing act.


<a id="entry-1422"></a>

### discharge-channel-exclusivity
