Each step accepted makes refusing the next feel like breaking a pattern the listener has already kept; jumping straight to the final step is more likely to be refused. A step that feels like gaining control, such as an imagined slider for depth, can prepare later steps that take control away.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script runs graded repetitions of the same demand-type at escalating stakes, with the early instances doing calibration work the late instances spend. The tell is that the peak demand arrives only after smaller enacted versions of itself, and is delivered as continuous with what the body already did — removing the first rung would leave the final one merely asserted.


**Worked examples.**

- *early freeze banks the proof the edge-timed freeze spends*
  - Removing freeze 1 would leave freeze 3 merely asserted; with calibration, the listener has prior in-body evidence.


**See also.** `acceptance-laddered-identity-migration` — the Foot-in-the-Door Ladder recipe was extracted from this entry; `arc-ordering-dependency` — the Foot-in-the-Door Ladder recipe was extracted from this entry; `catalepsy-to-affect-transfer` — a single demonstrated motor convincer spent as warrant for later untested claims — the one-rung version of the same spend.; `manufactured-self-confirmation` — shares the body-banked-evidence axis: prior moves manufacture the somatic proof that later claims cite.; `monotonic-ratchet-one-way-valve` — the escalation-topology neighbour: a strictly one-way ratchet with no regressible step.


<a id="entry-5"></a>

### frame-lamination-non-return

[#5](#entry-5) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

Tell a story inside a story, and maybe another inside that, then never step back out of the outer ones. The listener is woken from trance but left inside the inner story, so the session's frame quietly carries into ordinary life. Variations: three nested stories that blur together, with the outer ones simply dropped; wrap every hypnotic step in an everyday domestic tale that never names what it is doing, so memories feel like a story rather than a procedure, which helps forgetting; layered rituals where each layer lends meaning to the next, so a fantasy makes an instruction feel sacred and the instruction makes the fantasy feel like preparation.


**When to reach for this.** The mechanism is the FAILURE-to-return / the dependency-relation between layers across the whole back half, cited only to the absence of a closing beat, never to one line.


**Risk.** Leaving the listener at exit inside an unclosed inner frame is an incomplete-emergence property; bounded delivery (host supplying a real exit/aftercare) is the mitigation, so requires_bounding is set even though no refusal channel is directly eroded.


**Why it works.** Reality monitoring depends on explicit boundary markers — entering and exiting a frame is what tags material as 'imagined' versus 'actual' — so omitting the exit marker leaves content encoded without the source tag that would quarantine it. Narrative encoding without a procedural label also means the memory retrieved later is a story that happened rather than a technique that was applied, which offers no handle for critical review. Falsifiable: compare scripts identical except for a closing frame-return; if post-session source-attribution accuracy and reported carryover are the same either way, frame closure is not doing the work. [plausible; source-monitoring framework; reality monitoring and boundary cues in narrative transportation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Nested frames that never reopen*
  - **Setup.** The emergence, at the very end; the storyteller frame and the dream frame were both dropped a third of the way in and never resumed.
  - **The move.** One, two, three — eyes open, wide awake, feeling wonderful. The voice is still there in the corner of the room, and the room is still the one from the dream, and that's all fine. Go on with your evening.
  - **Why it lands.** Layer one: the operator asks permission to tell a story. Layer two: inside the story, a dream. Layer three: inside the dream, a voice speaking. Roughly a third of the way in the three fuse and the outer two are simply dropped — no return to the storyteller, no line resetting the scene, nothing. The emergence at the end wakes the listener out of trance but never out of the dream, so the fiction is still load-bearing when the file stops. You cannot point at the line that does this; the mechanism is the closing beat that never comes.
- *Every procedure disguised as a household errand*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the arrival, the washing, and the walk downstairs have all already been narrated as ordinary household events.
  - **The move.** You sit down in the chair in the back room, and she tips your head back against the rest, and she starts to wipe. Left side first, then the right, then across. When she's done there's simply nothing on that side of the cloth anymore.
  - **Why it lands.** Arriving and washing is the induction; walking down the stairs is the deepener; the treatment in the chair is the erasure. At no point does the operator step outside the errand to announce that a deepening is about to happen — there is no line of procedural metalanguage anywhere. The outer visit never closes either: the wake-up returns the listener to their own room without ever bringing them back from the imagined house. What they remember afterwards is a place they went, not a procedure that was done to them, and you cannot recall a technique you never perceived as one.
- *Each layer lends the next its provenance*
  - **Setup.** Final section, plain real-world instruction; the middle section already had the subject speak these exact words inside an imagined ceremony.
  - **The move.** On the first night of each month, kneel where you keep the bowl, light the one candle, and say the words you already said tonight. Say them out loud. You know them — they came out of your own mouth an hour ago.
  - **Why it lands.** The middle section has the listener perform a set of spoken words inside an imagined ceremony. The final section is a plain real-world instruction: say these words, on these dates, with these objects. On its own the instruction is bureaucratic and the ceremony is a one-off scene, but stacked they launder each other — the ceremony makes the schedule feel sacred, the schedule makes the ceremony feel like preparation. The words are taught in the imagined scene precisely so that, by the time they are prescribed, they are not a text the operator wrote but something the listener already said.


**See also.** `covert-frame-entry` — complementary ends of the same frame apparatus: one crosses the entry seam invisibly under a false benign frame, the other fails to reopen the outer frame at exit so the listener is left inside. Reading both gives the entry and exit halves of frame handling.; `declarative-nested-trance-recursion` — both present as stacked layers, so the surface reads identically and the discrimination is not obvious from the text. One is a topology property of the whole arc, where outer frames are never reopened and the listener exits stranded in the innermost layer; the other stacks declared trance-within-trance layers to remove any foothold for verifying depth. Worth the cross-link because a reader looking at nested layers has to decide whether the point is depth or non-return.; `emergence-negative-space` — both are whole-arc negative-space properties about frames that never reopen; one is about nested narrative layers left unclosed, the other about the missing emergence ramp. Close enough that a reader must be told which evidence assigns to which.; `foreclosed-emergence` — both leave no route back to ordinary baseline; one by never reopening an outer narrative frame, the other by deleting the clean waking end-state from what the close makes reachable. Structurally different but constantly confusable at the exit.; `loop-hook-non-wake-close` — both weaponize the absence of a proper return at the end of a session, one by never reopening the outer narrative layers, the other by offering a wake too thin to reorient. A reader analysing a session that ends wrong needs both readings on the table, since the tell is whether the missing return is a frame or the emergence itself.; `no-emergence-series-chaining` — both leave the listener without a clean return, and a reader who has one will misfile the other. The distinction is what fails to close: an outer narrative frame that is never reopened within a single piece, versus the emergence event itself being deleted so the state is forwarded across a boundary into the next.; `operator-voice-absence`


<a id="entry-1373"></a>

### friction-as-artifact-filter

[#1373](#entry-1373) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

The operator deliberately arouses resistance around a piece of material before accepting it, on the reasoning that material which survives active friction is less likely to be an artifact of the operator's own influence. Rather than smoothing the path so the subject agrees easily, the operator pushes back, invites contradiction, states the opposing case, or withholds the confirmation the subject is angling for, and only credits what still stands afterward. The move constrains the operator rather than the subject: it deliberately raises the cost of getting a yes, and it makes an easy yes a warning sign rather than a success. Its practical form is a rule about what counts as evidence in the operator's own notes — agreement obtained without friction is provisionally discounted, and material the subject maintained against pressure is weighted up.


**When to reach for this.** The operator deliberately RAISES the cost of obtaining a yes and treats an easy yes as a warning sign, crediting only material that survived the friction. This is the inverse of rigged-verification-capture, where every branch of the check is pre-mapped to confirmation. The tell is direction of operator interest: every neighbour makes agreement cheaper to obtain, this one makes it dearer in order to learn what cheap agreement conceals.


**Why it works.** Compliance and genuine endorsement produce the same surface response under low-friction conditions, so an easy yes carries almost no information about which one occurred; adding a cost to agreeing separates them, because a subject merely going along has little reason to pay it. The filter works by raising the response threshold until demand characteristics stop being sufficient to clear it. Falsifiable and directly checkable: compare material accepted under friction with material accepted smoothly on any independent criterion — later stability, corroboration from outside the session, whether it survives a change of operator. If the friction-filtered material fares no better, the filter is costing sessions and buying nothing. There is also a real failure mode worth stating: friction selects for stubbornness as well as for accuracy, so a subject who simply digs in under pressure will pass this filter while a compliant but correct subject fails it, which means the filter reduces one artifact class at the price of introducing another. [established; demand characteristics and acquiescence in low-cost agreement; costly signalling as a separator of genuine from compliant response]


**Worked examples.**

- *Counter-case stated before the yes is accepted*
  - **Setup.** The subject has just produced a piece of material the operator would like to credit — a memory, a preference, a stated want — and is visibly angling for confirmation.
  - **The move.** Before I take that: I think you might be handing it to me because I've been leaning on it for twenty minutes and you can hear which answer I want. So here's the opposite case — that it never mattered to you and you've assembled it just now out of what I've been implying. Argue me out of it. If you can't be bothered to argue, I'm writing it down as mine, not yours.
  - **Why it lands.** Raising the cost of a yes means only material that survives friction gets credited, and an easy yes becomes a warning sign rather than a result. The operator observes the difference between a subject who holds the claim under pressure and adds detail, versus one who folds or softens — the latter marks probable operator artifact and is discounted in the notes.


<a id="entry-702"></a>

### front-end-gift-directed-obligation

[#702](#entry-702) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: compliance*

The operator renders an initial no-cost service (a free home inspection); when paid work is then offered while the obligation is live, reciprocity directs the discharge of the debt to the specific benefactor. The target both awards the business to that firm and stops comparison-shopping, so the consideration set collapses to one vendor and price scrutiny is suppressed, the actual profit mechanism.


**When to reach for this.** A front-end free service attributable to a specific firm followed by a paid offer while the debt is live; not a genuinely disinterested favor. The paired boundary condition separates it from generic gift-giving: the gift must leave a viable repayment channel, since blocking repayment reverses the effect into resentment.


**Risk.** Transaction-scoped and escapable, a target who reframes the free service as a sales tactic exits; no consent-channel erosion.


**Why it works.** The reciprocity norm is a well-replicated obligation-generator: an unrequested gift creates a felt debt, and crucially the debt is directed at the specific giver rather than dischargeable generally. That directedness is what collapses the consideration set — comparison shopping would leave the debt outstanding. Falsifiable and already tested in the literature: if the recipient is given an alternative way to repay, or the gift is framed as an unattributable industry standard, the effect on vendor choice should vanish. [established; reciprocity norm; directed obligation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Free service directs the debt and kills comparison-shopping*
  - "most people who agree to a free home examination give the extermination job to the examining company… They apparently feel an obligation to give their business to the firm that rendered the initial, complimentary service." — Cialdini (1984), Influence


**See also.** `perpetual-obligation-ledger` — both run the reciprocity norm, but one over-repays by a labeled surplus so the ledger never reaches zero and the relationship stays open, while the other places a single front-end free service so the one live debt is discharged to a specific benefactor and comparison-shopping stops.; `reciprocity-ledger-seeding` — same reciprocity lever run at two ranges: one seeds an obligation ledger far in advance as a desirable identity, the other renders an immediate free service and collects while the debt is live. A reader identifying an obligation play benefits from seeing both the pre-seeded and the front-loaded form, and from the repayment-channel boundary condition.; `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` — two ways to manufacture a live debt that then directs its own discharge: theatrical costly effort on a predetermined outcome, versus a real no-cost service rendered before the paid offer. Real-versus-staged cost is the selection question, and both collapse the target's consideration or refusal channel the same way.


<a id="entry-1530"></a>

### front-matter-reader-positioning

[#1530](#entry-1530) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

Before any content is argued, the opening/front matter positions the reader as already inside the method's success, working on the reader's state rather than on evidence. One route names the reader's desire as already-felt: a first-person testimonial frames understanding-how-people-work as "my biggest reinforcer" and closes with the rhetorical question "How could you resist that?", so the reader's assumed enthusiasm becomes the platform on which the dry material is then laid and skeptical reading is pre-empted by consensus framing. The other route presupposes competence: the text legitimizes itself by embedding the method in a prestige lineage (Watzlawick/MRI, Haley, Minuchin, Satir) so it arrives pre-validated, and presupposes the reader already knows the basic six-step model, converting "you should learn this" into "you already have the basics, here is the advanced layer." Combined with a hit-and-miss-art-to-systematic-interventions promise, the front matter manufactures both credibility and a forward-leaning yes-disposition before a single technique or definition appears.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when an opening or front-matter posture operates by presupposing something about the reader's own state — their desire already felt, their competence already in hand — before the first claim is argued or demonstrated. The tell is posture preceding content: desire-naming testimony ("how could you resist?"), lineage-backed prestige, or presupposed familiarity doing the recruiting, with no evidence apparatus yet on the table. It is a whole-opening rhetorical strategy on the reader, not a single citable move in the body text.


**Worked examples.**

- *competence presupposed before any technique is taught*
  - pre-positions the reader as already-competent-but-incomplete


**See also.** `borrowed-precedent-legitimacy` — shares the borrowed-legitimacy axis: an already-sanctioned precedent or lineage lets the new material arrive pre-validated.; `evidence-apparatus-credibility` — both set the reader's stance toward the material before and independently of any individual claim being argued.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both lay groundwork before the payload so the later material lands on a prepared disposition rather than being evaluated cold.; `participation-drill-pedagogy` — sibling whole-text move on the audience: that one positions the reader before content arrives, this one drills the reader through it.


<a id="entry-1511"></a>

### function-based-extinction

[#1511](#entry-1511) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Identify the maintaining reinforcer via functional assessment, then arrange that the behavior no longer produces it, so the response rate declines toward its pre-reinforcement baseline. The functional read replaces the lay move of just ignoring it — the payoff may not be attention at all, and mis-targeted ignoring is the named anti-pattern. The withholding must cover every maintaining source at once, since withholding one source of reinforcement while another stays live may have minimal or no effect. Realization then follows the identified channel: for escape-maintained behavior, block the exit so the behavior cannot purchase escape — physically guiding the subject through the demand or re-presenting refused food until the aversive situation no longer terminates contingent on the response; for attention- or conflict-maintained behavior, deny the payoff by flat restatement of the contingency and disengagement, including reading resistance talk as escape behavior whose complaints are ignored while reinforcement is delivered contingent only on actual task performance. The lever throughout is removal of the maintaining contingency, not delivery of any aversive event.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a writer takes down an established behavior by first diagnosing what it earns and then making that exact payoff stop arriving. The tell is the diagnose-then-cut sequence: the text names the maintaining consequence (escape, attention, whatever the assessment reveals), then shows the behavior still occurring but no longer purchasing anything — the demand stays in place, the operator walks away, the complaint goes unanswered — with the decline attributed to the broken contingency rather than to anything delivered. The behavior is starved at its identified feeding point, not suppressed.


**Worked examples.**

- *escape payoff cut after functional identification*
  - Flo's tantrums can be placed on extinction by ensuring that the reinforcer (e.g., avoidance of the activities ...) no longer follows problem behavior (tantrums).


**See also.** `extinction-procedure-fidelity` — the conduct doctrine for running this withholding program through its predictable side-effect cascade.; `function-first-targeting` — an intervention that consumes the functional read — withholding the identified maintaining reinforcer rather than the visible form.; `noncontingent-reinforcement` — same maintaining-reinforcer axis run the other way: the reinforcer is delivered free on a clock schedule so the behavior stops purchasing it.; `reinforcement-extinction` — genus entry for the same withhold-the-maintaining-reinforcer move, spanning every reinforcer channel plus integrity and chain-structured facets.


<a id="entry-1536"></a>

### function-first-targeting

[#1536](#entry-1536) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: operator-craft · kind: principle*

Before trying to change a behavior, ask what it does for the person rather than what it looks like. Saying "fire" while reading aloud and shouting "Fire!" at smoke look alike but are different behaviors with different payoffs. So first find out what the act reliably gets the person, or lets them escape, and aim the change there, so the method has a reason to work instead of being a guess at the symptom. Variations: measure each part of a skill and work on the weakest; spot a familiar pattern, such as "the harder you try, the worse it gets", and use the approach known to fit it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when choosing where to aim an intervention on an already-observed behavior — the practitioner is deciding what to change, not yet changing anything. The tell is a classification step that asks what maintains or controls the act (what payoff it produces, which functional class carries it, which recurring pattern-form it instantiates) while treating the act's visible shape as uninformative, followed by an intervention pointed at that controlling relation.


**Worked examples.**

- *Identical surface acts sorted into different behaviors by controlling variable*
  - two responses of the same topography can be completely different behaviors depending on the controlling variables


**See also.** `descriptive-functional-assessment` — the observational assessment procedure that discovers the maintaining function this rule says to aim at.; `function-based-extinction` — an intervention that consumes the functional read — withholding the identified maintaining reinforcer rather than the visible form.; `preparatory-diagnostic-read` — the umbrella operator-side diagnostic-read surface whose read-discipline face this classification rule governs.; `replace-the-payoff` — function-over-topography axis: classifying the behavior by its maintaining contingency is the assessment step this rerouting builds on.


<a id="entry-1405"></a>

### generalization-gradient-coupling

[#1405](#entry-1405) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

A trigger fires not only to its exact cue but to a halo of near-misses around it. Trying to narrow an over-broad trigger by withholding reward from only the near-misses, while leaving the real cue alone, drags the real cue down too, sometimes to nothing. The trigger and its near-misses act as one linked system, so there is no clean way to trim a trigger by starving its edges, and attempting it risks losing the trigger altogether.


**When to reach for this.** An unengineered coupling between one cue's trained centre and its near-miss halo: extinguishing only the halo drags the centre down with it, so an over-broad trigger cannot be narrowed by starving its periphery. Against trigger-network-mutual-binding (1323) — the tell is that nothing was wired: 1323's inextinguishability is a designed topology over MULTIPLE separately-installed triggers cross-firing laterally, whereas this is a gradient property of a SINGLE cue and appears in installs that never touched a second trigger. Against discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement (306) — 306 is the procedure that DEFEATS this coupling by reinforcing the centre CONCURRENTLY while withholding at the periphery; the coupling described here holds only in the unreinforced-centre case, which is exactly the scope line between the two. Against reinforcement-extinction (432) — 432's collateral warnings concern topography substitution and un-enumerated reinforcer sources, i.e. spread across RESPONSES and reinforcer channels; this is spread across the STIMULUS dimension of one cue. Not context-generalization (1333): that widens an intact payload's firing surface deliberately; here the spread is in the extinction direction and unwanted.


**Why it works.** This assumes the trained response is tied to a whole range of similar cues with graded strength, not to one exact cue, which is why leaving points in that range unrewarded shifts the whole range, centre included. Testable: if the central trigger can be kept at full strength while its near-miss versions are extinguished, given enough training, the two are separable and the claim fails. Discrimination training does achieve exactly that separation, so the honest scope is narrow: the coupling holds when the near-miss versions go unrewarded without the central trigger being rewarded at the same time, and rewarding the centre alongside should rescue it.


**Worked examples.**

- *Halo starved, centre goes with it*
  - **Setup.** A snap-cue has been installed on a specific two-finger snap and has generalized: the subject is dropping on any sharp click, including a pen and a light switch. The operator wants to narrow it.
  - **The move.** For the next two weeks, when you hear a click that isn't my snap — a pen, a switch, a door — nothing follows it. No response from me, no acknowledgement, no drop. You'll notice the near-misses stop meaning anything. [Two weeks on, with no reinforcement given to the trained snap either:] Ready? [snap]
  - **Why it lands.** Starving the near-miss halo without concurrently reinforcing the trained centre pulls the centre down with it: the two-finger snap that was reliable now produces a flicker or nothing at all. The operator observes the trigger they intended to keep, failing on its own token, and reads this as the coupling rather than as a decayed install.


<a id="entry-1546"></a>

### generative-substrate-training

[#1546](#entry-1546) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Instead of teaching every final performance one at a time, practise the basic building-block skills until they are quick and automatic. Once all the needed pieces are in place, complex performances that were never taught or rewarded start showing up as the pieces combine. You pay once for the foundation instead of paying for each target. Two conditions matter: every piece has to be present, because a partial set gives little, and the pieces must be fast, not merely correct. Variations: build basic listening and naming skills so new words get picked up without direct teaching; drill simple skills to speed until harder ones emerge.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the goal is untrained capability appearing for free after an up-front investment in a component base — paying once for the substrate instead of per target. The tell is that no instruction ever touches the composite performance itself: the writer builds echoic/tact/listener components or drills simple skills to fluency, then tests for novel outputs that were never reinforced. The lever is the substrate as a whole, not any trained relation between the target stimuli.


**Worked examples.**

- *component repertoires installed, novel outputs emerge free*
  - once a child can emit echoic, tact, listener, and self-listener behaviors, new mands and tacts can be acquired incidentally with no formal training or reinforcement history


**See also.** `bidirectional-naming-transfer` — sibling generativity move: both convert a small trained investment into untrained verbal behavior, here via a whole component set rather than one relation.; `derived-relations-installation` — umbrella entry for the whole family of designs where training a subset makes an untaught repertoire emerge; this entry is its component-substrate form.; `matrix-recombinative-training` — neighboring generativity route — composite performance emerges from fluent component repertoires rather than from recombining taught combinations.; `natural-contingency-handoff` — shares the fluency lever — pushing performance past bare accuracy so downstream behavior appears or maintains without further operator support.


<a id="entry-1572"></a>

### good-girl-bad-girl

[#1572](#entry-1572) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: compliance · kind: recipe*

Keep the behaviours concrete and checkable so there is no argument about which label applies. Have the labelling happen as each act occurs, not in a summary later. If shame is used, keep it mild and let correcting the act always relieve it. Self-logging shifts behaviour only a little; the identity effect is untested.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Define checkable good and bad behaviours, have them label each act as good-girl or bad-girl, with praise or shame attached.


<a id="entry-1507"></a>

### graded-concurrent-choice-architecture

[#1507](#entry-1507) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

Every option stays simultaneously live — including the problem behavior — and the operator instead rigs the relative terms of the concurrent contingencies so response allocation drifts on its own. The alternative is made to pay richer, faster, and more reliably ('maximizing the difference between rates of reinforcement obtained by the two response classes'), or engineered to cost less response effort than the target, or laid out as a signaled graded menu: completing the task earns a long high-quality break with preferred toys, appropriately asking earns a short low-quality break, and eloping still 'works' but yields a minimal degraded outcome — ten seconds, no toys, neutral blocking — each option tagged by color. Nothing is prohibited or withheld; the matching law does the suppression, since the subject allocates responding in proportion to obtained reinforcement and experiences only that the good option works better. This is the design of choice precisely when the maintaining reinforcer cannot be safely withheld, so unsafe extinction is avoided while demand requirements for the best-paying option are ramped up over time.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the unwanted behavior's payoff cannot safely or practically be cut off, or when you want suppression to arrive as free choice rather than prohibition. The tell is a set of concurrently available, deliberately tiered contingencies — differences in rate, quality, immediacy, or effort, sometimes explicitly signaled — where the unwanted response is still permitted and still pays, just worst.


**Worked examples.**

- *concurrent-schedule payoff tilting with all options left live*
  - the client allocates more responding to the alternative behavior and less responding to the problem behavior, as described by the matching law


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement` — schedule-family axis: the graded menu is the concurrent-choice arm of differential reinforcement, tuned by the matching law.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — choice-architecture axis: both steer through a menu of live options, one by tilting relative payoffs, one by binding every branch to the same outcome.


<a id="entry-1358"></a>

### graded-induction-suppression-spread

[#1358](#entry-1358) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: conditioning*

When a set of triggers has been trained along a series (positions in a row, points on a scale, a run of tones), weakening one also weakens its neighbours, more the closer they are. The nearest drops to almost nothing, the next to about half, and the far end is untouched. So choose which trigger to weaken by the stretch you want flattened: weaken one at the end to flatten that side, or one in the middle to dip the middle and leave both ends.


**When to reach for this.** vs trigger-network-mutual-binding: that gives an all-or-nothing web — any node recruits every other, with no metric and no falloff — whereas the payload here is precisely the distance weighting, so suppression is graded and the far members genuinely survive. vs reinforcement-extinction: extinction has no spread-to-neighbours face at all; it targets one response class and its own chain-structured facets propagate along a CHAIN (link order), not along a perceptual/spatial similarity dimension. vs staged-multi-anchor-erosion: that removes several distinct cognitive anchors one at a time in a deliberate sequence, each addressed on its own — here exactly one anchor is acted on and the others move without being touched. vs lexical-relay-semantic-lattice: that relays meaning across a semantic net; this is a strength gradient over an ordered stimulus dimension, and it suppresses rather than propagates content. Requires a pre-conditioned ordered series with real perceptual proximity between members; on an unordered anchor set there is no gradient to exploit and the move degrades to ordinary single-anchor extinction.


**Why it works.** Conditioning attaches not to a point stimulus but to a region of a stimulus dimension, so changes made at one value transfer to nearby values in proportion to their similarity — the same generalization that spreads acquisition also spreads suppression, giving a falloff curve rather than a clean edge. This predicts an ordering constraint the operator can exploit: the shape of the resulting profile depends on where in the series the suppressed anchor sits. Falsifiable: suppress a mid-series anchor and measure the immediate neighbours; if they hold their pre-suppression strength, or if all members drop equally regardless of distance, the gradient claim is wrong and the effect is either absent or an undifferentiated web. Note the specific ratios (nearest to near-zero, second to about half) are a reported profile from one ordered series, not a constant to be assumed across dimensions. [established; stimulus generalization and generalization gradients; induction across a stimulus dimension]


**Worked examples.**

- *Mid-series anchor suppressed to scoop a symmetric well*
  - **Setup.** Five touch anchors have been conditioned in order along the subject's forearm, wrist to elbow, and each reliably produces its own response; the operator wants the middle band flat and both ends intact.
  - **The move.** The third spot — the one halfway up — I'm pressing now, and it does nothing. Nothing at all, no matter how long I hold it. Feel it go flat under my thumb. Just that one.
  - **Why it lands.** Suppression at the mid-series locus spreads outward by perceptual distance rather than by any stated rule, so anchors two and four come back weak and anchors one and five test near full strength — a gradient, not a boundary. The operator confirms by walking the row afterward and observing a symmetric dip centred on the treated spot, with no instruction ever given about the neighbours.
- *End-of-series anchor suppressed to flatten a one-sided tail*
  - **Setup.** Same conditioned row of five, but the operator wants the top of the series dulled while the lower positions keep working at full strength.
  - **The move.** The last one, up at the elbow — press it yourself. It's dead. Empty. Press it again and feel how there's nothing there to find.
  - **Why it lands.** Because the suppressed locus sits at the end of the dimension, the falloff runs in only one direction: position four drops substantially, three a little, and one and two are untouched. The operator observes an asymmetric tail rather than the symmetric well produced by a mid-series choice, which is the whole reason anchor selection is the move.


<a id="entry-1561"></a>

### handshake-induction

[#1561](#entry-1561) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: attention · kind: recipe*

The interruption has to come mid-motion, while the handshake is still automatic; once the handshake has finished, the moment of confusion is gone. Move straight into fixing attention on the hand and suggesting it stays put, without a gap. Practitioners report it works, but it has not had controlled tests.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 5 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Start a handshake, interrupt it midway, fixate them on the frozen hand, then suggest it stays put and they go into trance.


<a id="entry-1436"></a>

### harm-rejection-filter

[#1436](#entry-1436) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Installs a standing, automatic protective filter: the subject's deeper mind screens incoming suggestions and silently declines any that conflicts with the subject's genuine well-being or safety — without waking, without effort, and without the subject adjudicating in the moment. Framed as pre-existing and automatic ('your deeper mind only accepts what is good for you; everything else passes through and fades') rather than as a deliberate in-the-moment choice, which is what resolves the safety/depth trade: the conscious subject is never recruited as a vigilant gatekeeper, rejection happens below awareness as silent non-uptake, and compliance with everything inside the boundary is undisturbed. The filter is general and content-blind — it names no specific forbidden items; it keys on conflict with well-being, so it covers suggestions nobody thought to negotiate.


**When to reach for this.** The genuine article that a whole neighborhood of subversions counterfeits — reach for it when a REAL standing rejection faculty is installed or affirmed with the subject as the protected party. named-safety-belief-purge is its direct inverse, locating the internal safety faculty and deleting, rerouting, or co-opting it; weaponized-transparency-inoculation inverts it into a single-channel filter admitting only the operator; weaponized-safety-framing wears the safety surface while the safety element itself carries the payload; pre-armored-safety-ratchet locks the safety VERDICT against downward revision, where a real filter keeps revising; anti-stuck-filter is the local per-suggestion caveat where this is the general standing screen; and beneficiary-target-filter runs the same admissibility test on the operator's side before installation. The tell: rejection authority stays with the subject's own deeper mind, and the filter's output is silent non-uptake, not distress, debate, or emergence.


**Risk.** Protective by construction; the field-level hazard is false assurance — a stated filter is a suggestion, not a guarantee, the corpus's attested safety-net language is overwhelmingly subversion, and a filter's claimed presence must never license payloads that would not be run without it.


**Why it works.** Delegating rejection to the deeper mind resolves the safety/depth trade: vigilant conscious monitoring is incompatible with absorption and raises anxiety, while a rejection process framed as automatic and already-existing costs no attention and generates no reactance — it asks the subject to do nothing, only confirms something presented as already true. There is a real substrate underneath: hypnotic subjects reliably fail to take suggestions that conflict with strong values, so the install is partly a truthful description that raises the salience and felt permission of an existing capacity rather than building one from nothing. Falsifiable: subjects with an installed filter should show unchanged uptake of benign suggestions but increased silent non-uptake (without emergence or distress) of value-conflicting test suggestions, relative to no-filter controls. [plausible; suggestion non-uptake under value conflict; monitoring disrupts absorption; describing a capacity raises its availability]


**Worked examples.**

- *Installing the filter before deepening*
  - **Setup.** Early in the session, before any payload; delivered as descriptive fact rather than a rule being made.
  - **The move.** And here's something you don't have to think about, because it's already true: your deeper mind is careful. It takes what's good for you and lets everything else drift past like noise. You never have to check, you never have to guard — anything that doesn't serve you simply doesn't land, and you can go as deep as you like knowing that.
  - **Why it lands.** The is-already-true framing asks nothing of the subject, so the line deepens rather than interrupts; 'you never have to guard' retires conscious vigilance, which is what actually buys the extra depth.
- *The filter as answer to a voiced worry*
  - **Setup.** Pre-talk; the subject has asked what happens if a suggestion is wrong for them.
  - **The move.** Then it won't take, and it won't be a struggle either. If anything I say doesn't fit you, your deeper mind just declines it — quietly, on its own, even while the rest of you stays exactly this relaxed. It's not a door you hold shut; it's a filter that was always there.
  - **Why it lands.** Answers the safety question without recruiting the conscious mind as a guard, so the reassurance does not create the vigilance it is meant to relieve; 'not a door you hold shut' pre-empts the effortful-gatekeeper misreading.


**See also.** `beneficiary-target-filter` — same admissibility test run on the other side of the dyad: beneficiary-target-filter screens targets for the subject's benefit before install; this screens suggestions inside the subject at delivery.


<a id="entry-1457"></a>

### hoarded-charge-single-valve

[#1457](#entry-1457) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

Raise arousal across the whole session and keep refusing to let it discharge, so the built-up need becomes the operator's hold. Either there is exactly one release, at the end and on the operator's word, or none at all. Arousal is named again and again but put off; small dips only reset it slightly before it climbs higher. With no partial payoff along the way, the listener has to stay to the end. Variations: one long build to a single granted climax; no release, with the close sending the unspent arousal into the listener's day; no release, looping back to the start.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when charge is raised and explicitly named across the arc but its discharge is structurally refused — deferred, forbidden, or rationed to nothing. The tell is a release inventory of exactly one operator-owned terminal spike, or zero, with the closing lines carrying the accumulated state out of the session or looping it back to the start of the build.


**Worked examples.**

- *single terminal release justifying the whole retention scaffold*
  - here all tension is hoarded toward one terminal release the operator owns. The shape explains why so much front-loaded scaffolding (contract, trust loop, proof) is necessary: a single-discharge ramp needs the listener locked in for the entire duration, because there is no partial payoff to retain them mid-way.


**See also.** `monotonic-no-reversal-contour` — belongs to the same whole-arc family of monotone energy contours with no reversal beats.; `orgasm-gated-recurrence` — shares the withheld-charge-as-leverage axis: undischarged arousal pointed outward as a pull back to the operator's material.; `severed-relief-valve-ramp` — shares the single-direction arousal contour with periodic discharge structurally refused.


<a id="entry-110"></a>

### hostile-environment-channel-conversion

[#110](#entry-110) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: carrier-binding*

Introduces a persistent second in-fiction audible speaker (e.g. a lecturer) as continuous background dialogue, then re-reads that background stream as a confusion source, IQ-drain rhythm, and post-hypnotic trigger surface. The listener is boxed by the scene premise — they cannot tune the second voice out (they are 'in class') and cannot attend to it without each word being reassigned as a trance reinforcer — so the external environment becomes an operator-controlled beat generator with no neutral place for attention to rest.


**When to reach for this.** And it is more than classroom flavor: it requires a literal audible second channel — remove the lecturer voice and the move collapses; a silent imagined classroom would not carry it.


**Risk.** Session-scoped re-channeling of an in-fiction voice; no durable install, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** A continuous secondary speech stream is unusually costly to ignore, because speech is processed semi-obligatorily and intrudes on verbal working memory even when unattended — this is the irrelevant-speech effect, which measurably degrades verbal task performance. Boxing the listener in a fiction where tuning out is not permitted therefore imposes a real, sustained load rather than an imagined one, and reassigning each intrusion to trance meaning means attention has no non-serving destination. Falsifiable: replacing the audible second voice with a merely imagined one should sharply reduce the effect, since the irrelevant-speech interference requires actual auditory input. [established; irrelevant-speech effect; obligatory speech processing]


**Worked examples.**

- *In-fiction second voice as stimulus stream*
  - **Setup.** A second speaker is audible from the top, droning in the background as part of the scene; the dominant voice arrives late and settles in close.
  - **The move.** Ignore him, he'll go on all hour. Actually — no, listen. Every sentence he finishes sets off a little spark of fog behind your eyes, and the drone of him pulls another thread out of your head each minute. And any time he says the word "therefore", you'll hear yourself think the word "empty" before he reaches the end of it. You can't turn him off. You're in class.
  - **Why it lands.** A second speaker is audible from the opening — droning steadily on in the background, part of the scene rather than part of the session. The dominant voice arrives late, settles in beside the listener, and then re-reads that background for them: every sentence from up front now sets off a small spark of confusion, the rhythm of it pulls a little more out of your head each minute, and any time the topic brushes near this one, a single word surfaces on its own. The listener is boxed in by the premise. Tuning the lecture out means breaking the scene, and attending to it means each sentence arriving pre-assigned as another beat of the work — so the environment itself becomes an instrument with no neutral place left for attention to rest.


**See also.** `ambient-surface-trigger` — both convert an inescapable environmental stream into a trance-reinforcing trigger surface with no neutral place for attention to rest.; `concurrent-dual-stream-delivery` — both run a second audible stream alongside the primary one. The distinguishing question is what the second stream does: carry a concealed payload beneath a decoy, or box in attention so it can be reassigned. A reader designing a two-channel piece needs to see the fork.; `environmental-dissociation` — sibling that keeps the environmental voice IN and weaponizes it; `interspersal-in-carrier-stream` — both hide directives inside a stream the listener is already processing. One requires a literal second audible voice inside the fiction that cannot be tuned out; the other scatters payload fragments through neutral or noisy carrier material. The contrast clarifies whether the cover is an inescapable channel or low salience.; `protective-role-conscription` — both use an in-fiction scene role to relocate where the listener stands relative to the hypnotic content — one boxes attention onto an unavoidable second audible voice, the other dresses the listener as a non-participant. They occupy the same design slot as scene-premise wrappers, so a builder choosing a fictional wrapper wants both. Different levers: an audible second channel versus a costume of non-participation.


<a id="entry-469"></a>

### imagined-goodbye

[#469](#entry-469) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: operator-craft · kind: recipe*

A guided imagined farewell, used mainly so the operator can learn something. The listener pictures the people who matter, states their decision, says what was left unsaid, and looks into a future without them. If they are truly ready, it helps them sort out real last tasks; if not, how they respond shows what they hope the decision will get them and which ties still matter, which becomes material for change. Any absorption or sense of distance the listener feels is real but mild.


**When to reach for this.** The diagnostic payload is the tell (not a guided-imagery relaxation script — the operator reads congruence and mines unfinished business). vs guided-visualization: the imagery is instrumentation for operator-side information capture, not an absorption anchor. Off-axis for the subject-state dims — hence the residual flag.


**Risk.** Covert asymmetry — the subject experiences a completion ritual while the operator harvests the outcomes behind their stated decision for use as leverage AGAINST it; the exposure is informational/positional rather than state-level.


**Why it works.** Two separate things are happening and only one is well grounded. The operator-side half works because asking someone to imagine an outcome as completed elicits the reasons and attachments behind it more readily than direct questioning does — projection into an imagined scene lowers the cost of disclosure. The subject-side effects here are minor and the claim that the ritual itself produces change is not established; treat it as an elicitation instrument. Falsifiable: if direct questioning elicits the same unfinished-business content and the same congruence signals, the imagined-completion framing adds nothing. [speculative; projective elicitation lowering disclosure cost; subject-side effect not established]


**Worked examples.**

- *An imagined farewell that doubles as diagnosis*
  - "this ritual will give you lots of information about the outcomes behind his decision... use this... as leverage" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


<a id="entry-1114"></a>

### imagined-is-real-licensing-rule

[#1114](#entry-1114) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: framing*

Early on, state a general rule of the form 'the deeper the trance, the more X becomes possible or true', presented as a plain fact about how minds work so it is accepted rather than obeyed. This lowers the bar before the content that depends on it arrives. One form: 'the deeper you go, the more the mind experiences the imagined as real' makes the operator's later imagery feel like real experience. Another credits depth with lifting a limit ('because you're so deep you can expand your limits to feel more pleasure'), recasting the listener's own protective restraint as the thing in the way.


**When to reach for this.** Seeds a general 'depth licenses X' rule presented as neutral fact, cashed later. Expectancy-seeding seeds a specific session event; this installs a principle every later scene or limit-push exploits. Concept-redefinition redefines a value or state; this ties a capability (the reality-status of imagery, or the removal of a limit) to trance depth. Pick the variant by what depth licenses: the reality-status of imagined percepts, or the removal of a felt tolerance/restraint ceiling.


**Risk.** Pre-authorizes all downstream imagery to land as experience; session-scoped but broad license.


**Why it works.** Expectancy is one of the best-demonstrated drivers of hypnotic response: people told an effect is a normal part of trance report it more than people who weren't told. Presenting the rule as a neutral fact about how minds work, rather than as an instruction, matters because people judge factual claims by whether they sound plausible, not by whether to comply, and a plausible general rule gets less scrutiny than a direct demand. The specific suggestions that follow then borrow their authority from a premise already accepted. This could be tested: delivering the same suggestions without the earlier general rule should produce less vivid experiences or lower reported limits.


**Worked examples.**

- *Depth licenses the imagined to count as real*
  - **Setup.** Early, just past induction; subject relaxed, no payload imagery delivered yet.
  - **The move.** Here's a thing about trance that people forget. The deeper you go, the less your mind bothers to separate what it pictures from what it takes in — past a certain point it just stops keeping them in different drawers. That's not something I'm doing to you, it's simply how the machinery runs. So: put your tongue against something cold and metallic. Feel it get colder the longer you hold it. Notice that it got more definite, not less — that's the mechanism doing its job.
  - **Why it lands.** Early on, before anything worth resisting has been described, the operator drops in a general remark about how the process works: past a certain point the mind stops sharply separating what it pictures from what it takes in. It is offered as information, not as an instruction, so there is nothing to comply with or refuse; the listener simply accepts it as true. A small test sensation is named and duly reported as getting stronger, which counts as proof of the rule. Everything the operator describes from then on arrives already set up to be felt rather than merely pictured.


**Realizations** (2): `imagined-is-real-premise`, `trance-depth-as-limit-license`


**See also.** `consent-term-redefinition-smuggle` — both install a general proposition presented as a neutral fact about how minds work, accepted rather than obeyed, and cashed by later content. They differ in what the proposition does: one relocates a threatening state word onto experience the subject already owns so no untouched baseline remains, the other ties a capability or a lifted limit to trance depth. Same acceptance route, different payload.; `reality-claim-exit-closure` — both trade on the imagined-becomes-real premise as the load-bearing epistemic move of the session.; `self-perpetuating-depth-bootstrap` — both hang a claim on trance depth, and the carried-belief form of the self-running deepener is itself a depth-licensing rule. Worth the pointer so a writer can tell a rule that licenses later content from a rule that drives its own increment.; `time-as-malleable-construct-induction` — structurally the same move at different targets: both install a general claim presented as a neutral fact about how minds or trance work, accepted rather than obeyed, and cashed later by content that depends on it. One makes felt duration plastic, the other ties a capability or a lifted limit to depth. An author reaching for a licensing premise should see both.


<a id="entry-1543"></a>

### impoverished-context-permission

[#1543](#entry-1543) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The behavior is suppressed by permitting it — but only in one restricted, inconvenient, reward-stripped setting: a face-rubbing bathroom, a smoking chair turned away from TV and conversation, a sulking stool placed in the garage. Confining the behavior to that deliberately impoverished setting strips it of the incidental co-reinforcers (TV, company, comfort) that rode along with it and raises the response cost of emitting it, so rate falls without any prohibition or contingent consequence. In the smoking case, baseline 30 per day fell to 12, then 5, then quit as the chair was made progressively less accessible. The lever is antecedent stimulus control, and it is counterintuitive on purpose: permission-in-an-impoverished-context is what removes the smuggled reinforcers. It requires that the person reliably defer the behavior to the designated setting and keep that setting emptied of competing reinforcers.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a behavior is reduced by explicit permission confined to one designated place that has been made inconvenient and stripped of everything else rewarding. The tell is the pairing of "you may, but only there" with deliberate impoverishment of the there — the chair faced away from the television, the stool in the garage — and the total absence of any consequence delivered for the behavior itself.


**Worked examples.**

- *permission confined to a deliberately impoverished setting*
  - she would smoke only in a prescribed place, and she would
eliminate from that place the potentially reinforcing effects of other
activities


**See also.** `discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement` — same antecedent stimulus-control axis — concentrating a behavior under one narrow stimulus condition via its reinforcement history.; `massed-practice-rate-suppression` — fellow counterintuitive reduce-by-permitting move — the behavior is emitted, even prescribed, and its rate falls anyway.; `motivating-operation-engineering` — the impoverishment works as a value lever — stripping co-reinforcers from the permitted setting lowers what the behavior pays.


<a id="entry-1486"></a>

### indirect-command-smuggling

[#1486](#entry-1486) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

A literal, fully recoverable directive is delivered inside a surface form that is not a command: a yes/no question whose pragmatic force is the order ("Can you place your hands on your thighs?"), a statement-about-a-question ("I wonder whether you are completely comfortable"), a general statement with the client's name placed after a modal ("Children are able to Fred, sit down and relax"), or a reassurance keyed to a true prior fact, which Huxley "did not recognize" as a simple, direct hypnotic suggestion. The listener recovers the force and performs the act, while on the surface no refusable imperative exists, so the issue of resistance and control is never raised and compliance feels chosen. The question frame can even deny the response slot entirely: stacked "I wonder whether" forms build covert response potential that a later clear command cashes in. The move is depth-bounded: it requires a listener still processing utterances for pragmatic force, and fails in deep somnambulistic trance, where literalism dominates and the subject answers only the literal question ("I don't know").


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when an explicit, word-for-word recoverable directive needs to land on a waking, light, or medium-state subject without anything refusable ever being presented. The tell is an utterance that is formally a polite question, a general statement, or a reassurance, answered not with words but with the subject performing the act it names.


**Worked examples.**

- *command presupposed inside a polite yes/no question*
  - by simply asking you whether or not you are able to do it, I communicate the command 'politely' in the form of a question


**See also.** `covert-linguistic-delivery` — same covert-delivery family: an operator-authored directive routed on a linguistic channel the conscious mind processes without auditing.; `description-as-installation-register` — both deliver the payload in a register the listener's command-evaluation interface never receives as a refusable second-person imperative.; `inevitability-yoked-directive` — both obtain compliance without ever presenting a refusable demand at the surface, so the resistance question is never raised.; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — both remove the live decision point, so compliance never presents itself as a choice the listener could decline.; `presupposition-install` — both are Erickson covert-delivery grammar in which the surface form differs from the recoverable payload.


<a id="entry-1403"></a>

### induction-withdrawal-probe

[#1403](#entry-1403) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: emergence*

When progress stalls, instead of deepening further the operator deliberately lets the trance lapse, breaks the frame, or openly brings the person up, then watches what comes up once the state is gone. Whatever the trance had been holding down tends to come up: an objection, a refusal, a wariness, a topic that would not come while the person was absorbed. That obstacle is the useful information, not a failure, because it shows what the trance was actually working against, which stays hidden as long as the trance is going well. Nothing is added; taking the state away is the whole move.


**When to reach for this.** The structural inverse of the deepening family and of emptied-window-install: those add or empty in order to install, and every operator move near them ADDS state. Here state is removed, and removal is the technique rather than the end of the session — which also separates it from ordinary emergence, where the return to baseline is the session's terminal goal rather than an instrument aimed at a mid-session reading. Against unattributable-cause-severing and disavowal-and-masking: both HIDE the operation or its cause so there is nothing to resist; this deliberately exposes what was being resisted, and the subject's noticing is the point rather than the leak. Against neutral-state-deletion: that removes a state from the subject's available-states map to foreclose an exit; this removes a state from the subject's present experience to take a reading, and the map is untouched. Against fractionation, which also cycles state down: there the oscillation is used to deepen on the next descent, and nothing is read at the top.


**Why it works.** An active suppression is only observable through what it prevents, so as long as it is running it produces a null and the null is uninformative — removing the suppressor converts an unobservable into an observable, the same logic as lifting a mask to see what was under it. This predicts the probe yields nothing where nothing was being held down, which is its main falsification route: if withdrawal produced obstructions at the same rate in subjects with no relevant resistance as in those with one, the surfacing material is being generated by the withdrawal itself rather than revealed by it. It further predicts the obstruction appears specifically on withdrawal rather than gradually during the state — if the same material surfaces just as readily by simply waiting inside the induction, the subtraction is not doing the work. [plausible; suppression is inferred from absence, not observed directly; unmasking as a general diagnostic]


**Worked examples.**

- *State stood down mid-session to read what surfaces*
  - **Setup.** Twenty minutes into a working trance; the subject has been responsive on every suggestion but the one topic you asked about produced nothing — no refusal, just blankness.
  - **The move.** Open your eyes for me. All the way — sit up, feel the chair under you, count four things in this room out loud. Good. Now, wide awake, with none of that softness left: what came up just then, when I asked about the thing you couldn't answer? Whatever's arriving right now, even if it's an argument with me, say it.
  - **Why it lands.** Absorption was suppressing an objection the subject could not voice from inside it; removing the state lets the objection arrive with the subject fully oriented and able to speak it. The operator watches for what appears in the first ten seconds after the eyes open — a stated reservation, a flash of irritation, a topic named — and treats that content as the reading, not as a failed induction.


**See also.** `instrumented-covert-probe` — another manufactured probe — there the eliciting event is withdrawing the induced state and reading what surfaces in its absence.


<a id="entry-1489"></a>

### inevitability-yoked-directive

[#1489](#entry-1489) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

An overt directive is yoked to an act the subject is certainly about to perform — "As you sit down in the chair, just go into a trance" — so the trance develops from what the patient was most certainly going to do, the certain act dragging the contingent response along with it. Combining tasks also raises the price of refusal: to refuse, the subject must first work out exactly what is being refused ("Johnny, as you put away your bicycle just step over and close the garage door"), and the very extent of that identification effort is itself a deterrent, so refusal is usually skipped and emotional reasoning rather than logic governs the outcome. Even awakening can be made contingent on understanding, chaining future trances onto the same inevitability. Nothing is hidden: the directive stays fully audible and auditable; what is bypassed is the decision point, not the perception of the order.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the subject can be allowed to hear the order plainly and compliance is to be secured by timing rather than concealment — attach the wanted-but-uncertain response to an action already in motion or guaranteed to occur. The tell is an "as you X, Y" construction where X is inevitable and unpicking the bundle would cost more effort than complying.


**Worked examples.**

- *refusal-cost of the bundled double task*
  - The very extent of the effort needed to identify what one is refusing in itself is a deterrent to refusal


**See also.** `indirect-command-smuggling` — both obtain compliance without ever presenting a refusable demand at the surface, so the resistance question is never raised.


<a id="entry-1409"></a>

### inhibitory-cue-sign-inversion

[#1409](#entry-1409) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning*

Take a cue the person has already learned means stop, wait or not yet, and reward it on its own, over and over in quick succession, with nothing else competing. Its stop meaning wears away and then flips: the cue that used to hold the response back starts to bring it on, so the same word now works as a go signal without ever being redefined. It takes a while, and how long it takes tells you something: a cue that flips after a few rewards was never firmly in place, while one that holds out for many was deeply installed.


**When to reach for this.** vs counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening: that is the nearest neighbour and the one the draft missed — it weakens or severs a cue's control so the cue stops evoking, landing at INERT; here lone massed reinforcement drives the cue past inert into the opposite sign, so it evokes the very response it used to suppress. vs reinforcement-extinction: that breaks the response-reinforcer contingency and the rate decays toward baseline, again ending at zero rather than reversed. vs respondent-stimulus-pairing: that builds a conditioned response onto a NEUTRAL stimulus; the whole point here is that the cue starts with an established negative sign that must be overwritten. vs massed-practice-rate-suppression: that over-emits a BEHAVIOR to drive its rate down; here a CUE is over-reinforced to flip its sign. vs within-session-conditioning-loop: that drills a pairing in the direction it already points; the massing here runs AGAINST the cue's established sign. vs reward-channel-rerouting: that remaps which content may occupy the reward channel and leaves each cue's sign intact.


**Why it works.** A cue's sign is maintained by the contingency history that installed it, not stored as an intrinsic property, so a sustained contrary history overwrites it; and the number of contrary trials needed is proportional to the depth of the prior history, which is what makes latency an assay. This is falsifiable in both halves. It is wrong if massed lone reinforcement of a well-established stop-cue leaves it inert or merely weakened rather than evoking, across repeated attempts — that would mean inhibitory cues decay toward neutral rather than inverting. And the assay claim specifically fails if conversion latency does not track install strength: if cues installed with many reinforcements flip in about the same number of trials as cues installed with few, the latency reading is measuring something else and should be discarded. The safety consequence is the reason to state it precisely — a brake-cue that inverts stops functioning as a brake, and the same procedure applied to a safeword-adjacent token would destroy the stop signal it was reading.


**Worked examples.**

- *Massed lone reinforcement flips the stop-cue's sign*
  - **Setup.** A raised open palm has been installed as an unambiguous stop signal and holds reliably. Nothing else is being trained in the channel.
  - **The move.** Palm. Good — that's exactly right, perfect. Palm. Good girl, yes. Palm. That's it, so good. Palm. Yes. [Continued, alone, nothing else offered, until the response to the palm changes:] Palm.
  - **Why it lands.** Reinforcing an established stop-cue alone and massed erodes its negative sign and then reverses it, so the palm that suppressed the response starts evoking it — with no announcement that the meaning has changed. The operator watches for the exact turn from stillness to forward movement on the raised palm.
- *Repetitions-to-inversion counted as a seating readout*
  - **Setup.** As above, but the operator's purpose is to measure how firmly the stop-meaning was originally installed rather than to obtain the flip.
  - **The move.** Palm. Good. Palm. Good. Palm — good. [Counting silently, and continuing without varying the delivery:] Palm. Good. Palm.
  - **Why it lands.** The number of massed reinforcements the cue absorbs before its sign inverts reads out how deeply the original stop-meaning was seated: a handful means it was never really installed, dozens means it is load-bearing. The operator records the count, and treats a cue that flips fast as one that was never reliable in the first place.


<a id="entry-1413"></a>

### injunction-mechanism-disclosure

[#1413](#entry-1413) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Take a group's rule against questioning (doubt is disloyalty, analysis is resistance, the questioning mind is the enemy) and, rather than arguing against it, explore with the person why a group needs such a rule: what it protects, what would come out without it, whose interests it serves. The rule is treated as a working part with a job, not as a statement about truth. You need not disprove any belief, and the person never has to defend their judgment against yours. Once the rule is seen as propping something up, it loses most of its force: a ban seen as protecting something can no longer feel self-evident.


**When to reach for this.** vs disclosure-as-inoculation and weaponized-transparency-inoculation: this is the closest pair and the draft missed both — each also NAMES the influence machinery out loud, but does so to pre-convert the subject's recognition into deepening, arousal, or proof of the design, so noticing becomes capture. Here the disclosure hands evaluation back and the operator gets no return on it: nothing is reframed as protection and no critic is pre-classified as the threat. vs refusal-foreclosure: that INSTALLS the prohibition, relabeling thinking and doubt as pathological or impossible; this dismantles the same object by exposing what it is for. vs faculty-preserving-scope-restriction: that leaves evaluation running but narrows what it may range over; this restores range over the rule itself. vs evaluation-gate-standdown and epistemic-guard-disable: both stand the gate down by fiat; this brings it back up. vs licensed-erasure-and-refill: that manufactures a belief-vacuum and fills it with operator content; this fills nothing and installs nothing.


**Why it works.** A prohibition on questioning is sustained by being experienced as a norm rather than as an instrument, so a functional account of it converts it from something felt into something evaluated — and evaluation is the exact operation the prohibition existed to prevent, which is why disclosure disproportionately weakens this class of rule compared with rules that survive scrutiny on their merits. Falsifiable and sharply so: if functional disclosure works equally well against rules with genuine independent justification, then it is generic persuasion rather than the targeted move claimed here. It fails outright if subjects who accept the functional account nonetheless comply with the injunction at the same rate — that would mean the rule is maintained by contingency (what happens to people who question) rather than by belief, and disclosure aimed at belief cannot reach it. The useful corollary is that this predicts partial effect at best where questioning carries real external cost, since there the injunction has support the disclosure does not touch.


**Worked examples.**

- *The no-questioning rule examined as machinery with a function*
  - **Setup.** The subject has repeated a rule they were given elsewhere — that doubting is disloyal, that analysing the material is resistance — and is treating it as obviously true.
  - **The move.** I'm not going to tell you that's wrong. Just answer a mechanical question with me: what would a person find out, if they did question it? Set aside whether they should. What specifically stops being available once questioning is off the table, and who is better off for that?
  - **Why it lands.** The prohibition is handed back to the subject as a structure with a purpose rather than contested as a claim, so they never end up defending their own judgment against the operator's. The rule stops reading as self-evident wisdom the moment it is understood as protecting something, and the operator gets nothing back from the disclosure — no deepening, no proof of design, no reframe.


<a id="entry-1550"></a>

### install-under-attentional-cover

[#1550](#entry-1550) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

Deliver the trigger-install lines while the listener's attention is taken up by something else, so they slip past as background. Examples: trigger lines ('every time I say [word], you will...') dropped in while the listener pictures letter shapes; a rhyme-memory game shouted back under time pressure, which has the listener repeat commands far more often than plain suggestion could while they think it is only a memory game; a toe-to-head body scan pairing each body part with the trigger, giving real relaxation and cue-pairing at once while the listener notices only a body scan; or a short chant dropped at the dizziest point of an overwhelming passage, so it lands as rhythm rather than meaning. You can even say the cover out loud, telling the listener the commands slip past their conscious thoughts straight into the subconscious. The install lines can be completely ordinary; what is covered is the attention.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the installing language runs simultaneously with an activity or state that occupies the listener's processing — a visualization task, a memory game, a body scan, saturation-induced dizziness — instead of in a cleared, attended-to install moment. The tell is double duty: a single passage is at once the cover activity and the conditioning, and the listener could honestly describe it as only the cover ("just a body scan," "just words in a game").


**Worked examples.**

- *trigger paragraphs running under a letter-visualization task*
  - let my word and command and programming just slip past your conscious thoughts directly into your subconscious mind


**See also.** `alibi-carrier-front-loading` — shares the attention-consumption axis of the attention variant: a cover load occupies the parsing channel while the real install proceeds.; `armed-while-meaningless-phase-split` — the concurrent-cover route to the same end — install content slides past while parsing capacity is consumed, rather than being armed in an earlier meaningless phase.; `covert-install-under-cover` — umbrella entry for concealed-install covers; this is its concurrent-task attentional cover.; `description-first-install` — sibling cover: there the listener's parsing capacity is consumed by a concurrent task, here attention is free and the timing of the reveal does the concealment.


<a id="entry-1539"></a>

### instrumented-covert-probe

[#1539](#entry-1539) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: operator-craft*

When a decision hinges on something the subject can't or won't report, stage an ordinary-looking event that is really a test, and read the reaction. Never tell them what you checked. Variations: word a suggestibility test in one sense (seeing, hearing, feeling) to learn which sense reaches them before choosing an induction; make a deliberately wrong guess so they correct you with specifics; fire decoy cues beside the real trigger, since only the real one should work; quote the trigger casually, or block one sense, and see if it still fires; check whether trance learning is recalled outside trance; recreate the original problem and watch for the old reaction.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a specific decision hangs on information the subject cannot or will not report accurately — which channel to induct through, what a vague criterion concretely means, whether a cue is truly bound, whether the work actually took — and passive watching has not settled it. The tell is a staged event with a hidden purpose: what the subject encounters looks like a routine test, a naive guess, casual quoting, an accident, or an ordinary drink, while the payoff is a datum the operator pockets; the result is never announced or demonstrated to the subject.


**Worked examples.**

- *Suggestibility test repurposed as a covert channel probe*
