This structurally pre-empts the listener's normal "am I going along with this?" gate: no fresh consent is ever requested because the frame holds that consent was given before line 1, leaving the listener in the position of an amnesiac being re-introduced to their own contract. The frame's one stress-test, a staged escape attempt, is built to fail and thereby ratify the frame more strongly.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script opens already inside the state and narrates every apparent first as a return. The tells are déjà-vu markers and retroactive callbacks framing on-page thresholds as repetitions, the total absence of any on-page consent request because consent is located in an off-page past, and an escape or resistance beat staged so its failure confirms that the outcome was settled before the script began.


**Worked examples.**

- *consent located off-page, before line 1*
  - There is no point at which the script asks for fresh consent, because it has set the frame that consent was given before the script began.


**See also.** `emergence-negative-space` — the mirror-image missing-boundary design: this entry omits the entry baseline, that one omits the emergence ramp.; `manufacture-problem-sell-cure-iatrogenic-arc` — both open with the listener's condition already asserted as fact, with no negotiated pre-trance baseline to consent from.; `scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier` — adjacent addressee-displacement carrier — the first-person already-converted narrator is the voice through which an already-lost frame is often delivered.


<a id="entry-1468"></a>

### no-fail-count

[#1468](#entry-1468) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

A counting or monitoring task is structured so every branch is pre-coded as success: slipping up restarts the loop and doubles relaxation, losing the numbers is fine ("if you lose them ... that's okay. Just go with it"), forgetting means going "extra blank, extra deep," reaching zero means "zero thoughts, zero mind," falling silent is exactly what was predicted, and merely still-listening is itself declared to be what the listener has fallen into. No outcome can generate evidence of non-compliance or a route back to ordinary awareness, so conscious cooperation stops being a lever and performance anxiety dissolves — the listener cannot do it wrong and cannot catch the operator in an overclaim. Meanwhile the task occupies working memory (counting, error-tracking, restart bookkeeping), and the no-fail rule converts the listener's own fatigue and drift into further descent rather than into vigilance.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script assigns an active task — most often a backward count — and explicitly pre-labels every possible performance of it, including failure, as deepening. The tell is the permission-to-fail clause attached before the task begins ("if you lose track, that's okay, it just means you go deeper"), leaving no branch that reads as non-compliance and no result the listener could score as not-working.


**Worked examples.**

- *Slip-up rerouted into restart-and-double-relaxation loop*
  - As you count back from 100 you begin to find yourself slipping up on your numbers. You begin to forget numbers. Each time you slip up on your numbers you instantly go back to 100 and start over.


**See also.** `manufactured-insufficiency-treadmill` — both spend the listener's task performance as fuel for depth, whichever way the performance comes out.; `no-lose-double-bind` — both build branch structures where every option the listener can take is pre-loaded to ratify the operator's frame.; `recruited-or-foreclosed-quieting` — both remove the refusable lever: no directive or outcome exists that resistance could grip to justify an exit.


<a id="entry-1339"></a>

### obedience-motive-reattribution

[#1339](#entry-1339) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

The operator carries obedience beyond the session by giving a new reason for the listener's own self-improvement: exercise, productivity, sleep, breaking a habit. These become things done for the operator, as service, and struggles with willpower can ease once the reason changes. Each time the listener follows through in daily life, it reinforces the sense of obeying, so everyday choices keep strengthening it. It works by taking a personal goal that had stalled, putting the operator behind it, and so turning a real improvement in willpower into something that serves the obedience, reaching well beyond the recording itself.


**When to reach for this.** Re-attributes the MOTIVE of the listener's OWN self-improvement acts to the operator rather than installing or generalizing a new response — implementation intentions and context-generalization transfer an installed effect into real contexts, where here nothing new is installed. The tell: it hijacks a stalled personal goal and reassigns its motive, harvesting a genuine willpower fix.


**Risk.** Re-attributing the motive of the listener's own goals to the operator colonizes waking self-directed behavior and reroutes ordinary agency toward the operator — durable, identity-scoped, out-of-session reach.


**Why it works.** People infer causes for their own behaviour from whatever explanation is salient, so supplying a salient external agent for progress that was actually self-produced shifts perceived locus of control outward (misattribution, not over-justification — that effect concerns extrinsic reward undermining intrinsic motivation and does not apply here). Because the goal was genuinely stalled beforehand, any subsequent progress is read as the operator's doing. Falsifiable: if attribution is genuinely reassigned, rated operator-credit should stay high during a period of no operator contact; if credit tracks actual contact frequency, the reattribution has not taken. [plausible; over-justification effect; misattribution of causes for one's own behaviour; locus of control]


**Worked examples.**

- *Do it for me: self-improvement recast as service*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session; the subject has been asked to bring a genuinely stalled personal goal to mind.
  - **The move.** Hold that thing you keep failing at — the gym, the bedtime, the habit you've quit four times. Now change one thing about it. Stop doing it for yourself. Do it for me. Tomorrow when you get up and go, you're not disciplining yourself, you're pleasing me. And every time you manage it, that's one more thing you did because I asked.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator asks the listener to bring to mind something they have genuinely been failing at — the gym, the sleep schedule, the habit they keep meaning to break — and then makes one substitution: stop doing it for yourself and do it for me. Nothing new is installed and no behaviour changes; only the reason does. The willpower problem often really does ease, and every ordinary success afterwards becomes another entry in the obedience column.


**See also.** `compliance-act-as-proof-of-induced-wanting` — both relocate the authorship of wanting rather than issuing a new instruction: one harvests a trivially obeyed act as evidence that desire is manufactured, the other reassigns the motive behind acts the listener already performs on their own. Useful pairing for a reader working on attribution of motive, with the boundary being in-session harvest versus out-of-session motive swap.; `compliance-authorship-laundering` — both relocate authorship toward the listener's own agency, but one relabels the compliance act or constraint itself as the listener's own will so resistance loses its external target, while the other leaves the act genuinely self-chosen and instead reassigns its MOTIVE to the operator so self-improvement counts as service.; `cultural-ritual-slot-hijack` — both reach outside the session and conscript machinery the listener already runs. One substitutes its content into a cultural ritual or narrative slot the listener was already prepared to enact; the other reassigns the motive of the listener's own self-improvement acts to the operator, hijacking a stalled personal goal. Borrowed frame versus borrowed motive, with the same durability payoff.; `illusory-choice-authorship` — both relocate authorship of a motive rather than installing a new response, in opposite directions: one hands the subject felt authorship over an operator-fixed path, the other takes the subject's own self-directed acts and reassigns their motive to the operator. Reading them together makes the direction of the transfer the salient variable.; `numbered-laws` — both run retroactive attribution toward the operator: one via a totalizing clause that retro-scores any behavior as service inside the installed rule-set, the other by reassigning the motive of the listener's own out-of-session self-improvement acts. Overlapping lever, different scope and reach; worth cross-checking when a move scores existing behavior as service.; `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both relocate something onto the operator, and the pairing clarifies a real boundary: one re-sources the reward or affect itself, the other re-attributes the motive behind the listener's own self-directed everyday acts. Useful adjacency for a writer deciding which reattribution they actually want, since the second operates entirely outside runtime on pre-existing personal goals.; `self-administered-conditioning-loop` — both keep the operator as the labeller while the listener supplies the substance, and both extend reach past runtime. One outsources the reinforcer so a conditioning loop self-sustains on the listener's ordinary behavior; the other reassigns the motive of the listener's own self-improvement acts without installing anything new. Nearest neighbors on the reattribution axis.


<a id="entry-1500"></a>

### obedience-pleasure-state-equation

[#1500](#entry-1500) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: conditioning*

Instead of pairing obedience with some reward, the operator simply states, over and over, that obedience is pleasure: 'obedience is happiness, obedience is joy, and you love to obey.' It is said as a fact about the listener, usually once they are deep enough not to question it. The feeling is then expected to arrive whenever they obey, and refusing costs them both the pleasure and their sense of who they are. Variations: a sliding scale ('the more I speak, the better it feels'); resisting described in advance as feeling horrible; tying obedience to identity ('good girls obey'); forgetting why it feels good while keeping the feeling.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the script declares obedience and pleasure to be the same thing as a standing truth about the listener's state or identity, with nothing concurrent being pointed at. The tell is mantra-grade copula grammar — "obedience is pleasure," "indistinguishable and automatic" — often flanked by a more-obedience-more-pleasure gradient, a poisoned resistance path, or good-girl/made-for-this identity framing.


**Worked examples.**

- *the equation stated as bare axiom at depth*
  - obedience is happiness obedience is joy obedience is pleasure and you love to obey


**See also.** `belief-pleasure-weld` — the same hedonic-weld move aimed at a different target: pleasure bound to the truth-value of the operator's words instead of to the obedient state.; `compliance-loop-language` — adjacent loop form: obedience and reward phrased as a self-perpetuating cycle rather than a flat identity.; `monotonic-amplifier-dial` — shares the monotonic more-is-more gradient by which intensity is asserted to only ever increase.


<a id="entry-755"></a>

### objection-preemption-inoculation

[#755](#entry-755) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: manufactured-consent*

Work out the single strongest reason the listener might refuse, and deal with it before they think of it. Variations: explain in advance that any inner conflict they feel later is proof the change is working; turn a real-life worry, such as a partner, into an addition rather than a rival ('plenty of love to go around'); separate the unwanted part from an otherwise appealing offer; name the feared objection outright ('this isn't brainwashing') and deny it, so the listener spends their scrutiny on the denial while the lasting suggestion goes ahead anyway.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this to pre-empt a SPECIFIC foreseeable objection (later conflict / a rival relationship / an IQ-loss balk / a 'brainwashing' fear) by dissolving, reprocessing, or denying it before it forms. Pick the realization: reprocess the objection into support (a), or name-and-deny it as a decoy (b).


**Risk.** Removes the listener's strongest rational refusal in advance and (desire-arithmetic member) makes later resistance re-read as deepening; durable motivational reframe, session-installable, no explicit faculty-deactivation.


**Why it works.** Inoculation theory predicts that a weakened, pre-empted version of a counterargument confers resistance to the full-strength version later — the listener has already processed and dismissed the objection, so when it arises spontaneously it arrives pre-labelled as handled rather than as new information. The name-and-deny variant additionally exploits the fact that people discharge scrutiny on whatever claim is made salient; denying a named threat consumes the vigilance budget that would otherwise scan the actual design. Falsifiable: if pre-empted objections produced no reduction in later refusal relative to unaddressed ones, or if naming a threat increased rather than decreased scrutiny of adjacent claims, the account fails. [established; inoculation theory / attitudinal resistance; salience-directed scrutiny]


**Worked examples.**

- *Balance toppled so later conflict confirms*
  - **Setup.** Pre-emptive framing before the main install; subject has not yet felt any internal conflict about it.
  - **The move.** Right now you want a hundred things and they mostly cancel each other out — that's what balanced feels like. I'm going to grow one of them until the scale tips. After that, when some other part of you pipes up, it won't feel like a real contest; it'll just be showing you which one got bigger.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator lays out the arithmetic in advance: you hold a great many wants and they mostly cancel out, she says, and she intends to grow just one of them until the scale tips — after which any other want that pipes up will not feel like a real contest, only a reminder of which one is now bigger. The objection the listener would raise later, that part of them does not want this, is answered before it exists, and answered as evidence that the install took.
- *Non-zero-sum framing of a rival attachment*
  - **Setup.** Just before a devotion or attachment install, with a subject known to have a real-world partner.
  - **The move.** Before you go there — nothing I take is taken from the person you go home to. There's more than enough of you to go around, and what we build in here doesn't drain that, it charges it. You'll be warmer at dinner, better in bed, sharper at work, because of this.
  - **Why it lands.** Before the listener can raise the obvious objection about the person they are actually with, the operator gets there first: nothing here is taken from anyone else, there is more than enough to go around. Then the frame is inverted — what is built here charges everything else, work, sleep, every ordinary hour — so the relationship that would have been the objection becomes a beneficiary instead.
- *Unbundling the costly part of an identity offer*
  - **Setup.** Identity offer being made; subject is interested but has visibly balked at one component of the package.
  - **The move.** Some of them want the whole package, empty head included. You don't have to take that part. You keep the sharpness, every bit of what you're good at stays exactly where it is — you're only adding the shine on top, and the shine costs you nothing.
  - **Why it lands.** The offered identity usually comes as one package, and one item in that package is the one people balk at. So the operator splits it: some enjoy losing their edge, but you don't have to take that part — the sparkle stays, the sharpness stays exactly where it is. With the expensive component lifted out, the remainder costs almost nothing to accept.


**Realizations** (1): `disclaimer-as-inoculation`


**See also.** `disclosure-as-inoculation` — both immunize in advance, and both are easily confused, so the pointer does real work. One targets the listener's future critical stance as a class, pre-coding any later recognition as confirmation; the other neutralizes one specific foreseeable objection before it forms. Scope of the pre-emption is the discriminator.; `named-safety-belief-purge` — both neutralize refusal in advance, and they abut closely at one seam: naming a specific fear and declaring it absent, versus naming the subject's own stop-faculty and deleting it. A reader looking at a passage that names 'brainwashing' or 'I can always wake myself' must decide which of these is on the page. Distinct targets keep them separate: one named objection versus the internal verification faculty as a whole.; `objection-and-exit-preclosure` — both close anticipated objections before they can form, and the name-and-deny realization of one overlaps the pre-answered-objection realization of the other. They stay separate because one targets a single strongest rational objection and metabolizes it, while the other closes named EXIT routes so the install survives into waking life. A cross-reference helps a reader choose.; `prospective-resistance-foreclosure` — both remove a defense before it is exercised, and the useful contrast is the target's breadth: one pre-assigns a null or aversive outcome to a whole future class of mental acts, the other identifies the single strongest foreseeable objection and dissolves or decoy-denies that one. Reader choosing between them needs the class-vs-named-objection line.; `resistance-window-existence-denial` — strong overlap: the broad entry lists preemptive disarmament of the most likely defense among its realizations, and the other entry is precisely the specific-objection form. A reader needs the pointer to decide between foreclosing resistance as a class and neutralizing one named foreseeable objection.; `weaponized-transparency-inoculation` — both inoculate against future resistance and both are named inoculations, differing in scope: one flips the valence of the influence itself and pre-labels outside critique as the threat, covering a whole class of later critical thoughts; the other neutralizes one specific foreseeable objection. Scope is exactly what a writer must choose.


<a id="entry-912"></a>

### off-theme-suggestion-piggyback

[#912](#entry-912) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer*

Once the session's main content is finished, a behaviour suggestion unrelated to the theme is added while the listener is still deep, using that state to deliver something they might not have agreed to on its own. It comes after the themed part is complete (the session could have ended before it and felt finished) and often uses "more and more" wording so it builds over repeated listens. The trick is simply reusing a deep state created for one purpose to bring about an unrelated change.


**When to reach for this.** Installs a STRUCTURALLY-SEPARABLE off-theme behavior payload in the deep window produced by the file's on-theme content. The tell is separability plus theme-mismatch.


**Risk.** Installs behavior change outside the file's consented theme using the deep state as an unconsented delivery vehicle - a consent-scope violation eroding the listener's ability to have declined the payload.


**Why it works.** A suggestion is more likely to be accepted when the person isn't weighing it, and someone deep in a state they agreed to isn't scrutinising every line the same way: they consented to the theme and don't re-check each sentence. Agreement also builds momentum. After accepting a run of related suggestions, the next one feels like a continuation rather than a new decision, which is the foot-in-the-door pattern. This is plausible rather than established, and it can be tested: the same unrelated suggestion given at the start, before the state, should be refused noticeably more often.


**Worked examples.**

- *Off-theme payload grafted onto the deep window*
  - **Setup.** The session's advertised transformation has been delivered and its duration stated; subject is at the deepest point, just before the wake-up begins.
  - **The move.** One more thing settles in while you're this open, and it has nothing to do with anything we've done tonight. From now on, the moment you get home and the door is shut behind you, clothes come off — and out in the world, nothing underneath. Every time you play this, that preference gets a little stronger, a little more obvious, until it's simply how you live.
  - **Why it lands.** The advertised transformation is finished and the session has already specified how long it lasts — the file could stop here and feel complete. Instead, at the deepest point, an unrelated habit is attached: a growing preference for going undressed at home, an underwear rule for going out, each described as strengthening a little with every replay. The listener bought a session about one thing and is being handed a standing behavioral change about another.


**See also.** `care-framed-install-smuggling` — both smuggle payloads through a structurally privileged slot, but one grafts an off-theme behavior into the deep window the session produced while the other uses the aftercare and safety surface itself to extend operator reach.; `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — both exploit a session the listener joined for a stated reason to deliver something else, differing in whether the advertised frame is the carrier throughout or the off-theme content is bolted on after the theme completes. A reader assessing scope-of-consent on a whole artifact should see both shapes.; `covert-payload-piggyback` — both smuggle a payload into a move the listener has already accepted, but they differ in what carries it: one hides an identity rewrite inside a low-resistance in-session task, the other grafts an off-theme behavior install into the deep window the session produced. Useful as a pair for deciding which piggyback frame applies.; `loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion` — both exploit a suggestibility window to carry content the listener did not come for, and the discriminating question is the same one asked twice: is the payload the session's own content riding the emergence transition, or an off-theme behavior grafted into the deep state? Reading one without the other invites misassignment.; `wake-line-covert-install` — both exploit a low-guard window to install content the listener did not sign up for; one at the wake line under cover of aftercare, one appended after the thematic arc is complete. A reader spotting an off-arc install needs to know which window it sits in.


<a id="entry-1504"></a>

### omission-reinforcement-dro

[#1504](#entry-1504) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The subject is rewarded when a set stretch of time passes without the unwanted behaviour. They are paid for not doing it. Because the reward lands at the end of the window, anything else they did in that window gets rewarded too, so the rule is usually 'no target behaviour and nothing else unwanted.' Variations: the whole window must be clean; only the moment the window ends is checked (cheap, good for keeping gains); windows of random length so they cannot time the behaviour to safe moments; windows measured by distance travelled instead of time.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the goal is pure suppression and no replacement behavior needs to exist — the contingency can run on an empty repertoire because the reinforced event is an interval or instant with nothing in it. The tell is a timer or window whose close triggers reinforcement for absence, accompanied by the signature guard against silently rewarding a substitute behavior occupying the vacated slot.


**Worked examples.**

- *leak-guard: pay only when the whole undesirable set is absent*
  - contingent on the absence of the problem behavior and the absence of any other significant inappropriate behaviors.


**See also.** `baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration` — criterion-sizing axis: the opening omission interval is computed from the subject's baseline mean inter-response time.; `differential-reinforcement` — parent schedule family: DRO is the reinforce-the-absence arm of the differential-reinforcement parametric umbrella.


<a id="entry-1458"></a>

### omni-routing-all-actions-deepen

[#1458](#entry-1458) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology*

A property of the whole script: everything the listener might do is claimed in advance as taking them deeper. Complying deepens (closing the eyes), neutral acts deepen (counting, stopping counting, walking through a doorway), testing deepens ('the more you test it, the deeper it makes you go'), and even ending a test deepens. In the surrender version, curiosity becomes consent, resistance becomes evidence of desire, stillness becomes proof of helplessness, and later reluctance becomes a re-trigger. Nothing the listener does inside the script can reduce the effect; the only way out is to stop the file or walk away. So it holds up with distracted, skeptical or half-compliant listeners.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script pre-assigns a descent payload to the listener's entire action space, not merely to a resistance impulse. The tell is enumerable: list the moves the listener could make — obey, test, resist, drift, recover, do nothing — and find each one already scripted to deepen, with compliant and neutral acts claimed in the same breath as struggles. Off-ramps are systematically rebuilt as on-ramps, so the only exit left standing is stopping the session entirely.


**Worked examples.**

- *whole action space pre-claimed for deepening, including compliance and neutral acts*
  - Every act the listener performs — including acts of resistance, testing, and recovery — is pre-claimed for the deepening trajectory. This collapses the strategy space: there is no available action that doesn't move the listener further along.


**See also.** `closed-reachability-topology` — shares the closed-reachability axis: the whole set of listener next-moves is engineered so every branch routes toward the operator's goal.; `response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure` — shares the pre-claiming axis: likely counter-moves are enumerated in advance and pre-loaded with reframes that route them into the target state.


<a id="entry-1250"></a>

### operate-below-awareness

[#1250](#entry-1250) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: concealment · kind: principle*

Changing how much someone wants something (by deprivation, hunger, arousal) changes what they do, whether or not they can say they are being steered or why. The person does not need to understand or agree for it to work. They simply feel the want as their own spontaneous impulse, not as something done to them, which is what lets want-shifting moves work without the subject noticing.


**When to reach for this.** A writer reaches for this entry when the load-bearing claim is that a motivating operation alters value and steers behavior whether or not the subject can verbally describe being motivated or identify the contingency — as Cooper, Heron & Heward put it, effectiveness 'does not depend on individuals being able to describe the effects.' The observable tell is covertness by default: because the effect is automatic, behavior shifts while the subject experiences the resulting want as their own spontaneous impulse rather than an installed effect, and nothing beyond a motivating operation in effect is required. This entry names a PROPERTY rather than a wording technique, and the covertness is itself operator-load-bearing — it is what lets the surrounding motivating-operation moves run without the subject noticing.


**Risk.** The want is experienced as spontaneous with no subject narrative and no consent required — covertness that bypasses awareness; durable in effect but bounded, no direct refusal-channel erosion asserted.


**Why it works.** Motivational states shift the value of outcomes and the frequency of behavior without requiring the subject to be able to state that shift — food deprivation changes food-seeking whether or not the person articulates being hungry. Because the shift is not accompanied by any marker of external origin, the resulting want is attributed to the self by default: absent salient evidence of an outside cause, people credit their own dispositions. Testable prediction: subjects show the behavioral shift while reporting no awareness of the manipulation, and making the manipulation salient reduces the self-attribution. [established; motivating operations; self-attribution and absence of a salient external cause]


**Worked examples.**

- *Motivation works without the subject noticing*
  - "individuals do not need to be 'aware' of the effects of reinforcement for it to affect behavior. Likewise, the effectiveness of MOs does not depend on individuals being able to describe the effects" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `conditioned-motivation-by-pairing` — same motivating-operation axis: MO effects land whether or not the subject can describe the contingency, which is what lets a paired cue steer covertly.; `covert-leakage-read` — both operate entirely below the subject's awareness, needing no report or consent to function.


<a id="entry-1378"></a>

### operator-completed-disclosure

[#1378](#entry-1378) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: compliance*

When the person stalls partway through saying something they cannot bring themselves to say, the operator says the rest of it for them and leaves them only to agree or correct. The hard part, actually naming the thing, is done by the operator, so the person only has to not object, which is much easier than producing the words. The risk is real: a wrong guess that the person accepts out of relief or pressure puts the operator's words into the record, and in the moment there is no reliable way to tell a true accepted completion from a false one.


**When to reach for this.** The operator speaks the remainder of a disclosure the SUBJECT stalled on, leaving the subject only to assent or correct — the gap is the subject's own and the operator closes it. Against answer-supply-loop (205), the nearest neighbour: there the operator poses the question AND pre-fills its answer with no response window, so the content originates entirely with the operator and the payload is a manufactured yes-stream; here the subject was already producing loaded material of their own and blocked, and the operator supplies that specific blocked content. Against withheld-completion-dependency (644), its structural inverse: there the operator manufactures a gap mid-interjection and leaves it OPEN so the subject leans in and dependency forms. Against listener-supplied-inference-relabel (52): there the operator's assertion stays empty so the listener manufactures the payload and the operator keeps literal deniability — here the operator states the loaded content outright and keeps none, which is exactly why the contamination risk is intrinsic rather than incidental.


**Why it works.** The barrier at a stall is usually the act of saying rather than the content itself, since uttering a thing makes one its author in a way that assenting to another's utterance does not — so relocating the utterance to the operator removes the specific cost that was blocking while leaving the information transfer intact. Assent is cheaper than production for the same proposition, and that gap is the whole lever. Falsifiable: compare stalls closed by operator completion against stalls met with silent waiting. If disclosure rates are equal, the completion is buying nothing over patience. The contamination claim needs its own and harder test, because it determines whether this move is usable at all: seed deliberately incorrect completions at stall points and measure the acceptance rate. If subjects reliably reject wrong completions, the risk is manageable; if wrong completions are accepted at a substantial rate — which is what the suggestibility of the stall moment predicts — then anything obtained this way is a joint construction and must not be treated as the subject's own report. Until that rate is known, output from this move should be labelled operator-contaminated by default. [plausible; the asymmetry between producing and assenting to a statement; suggestibility of leading and completed prompts, where the contaminating effect of supplied content on subsequent report is well documented.]


**Worked examples.**

- *Operator speaks the stalled remainder; subject left only to assent or correct*
  - **Setup.** The subject is mid-sentence on loaded material of their own, has stopped dead, and is not going to finish it.
  - **The move.** You wanted him to notice you were gone. That's the end of the sentence — I'll say it so you don't have to. Nod if that's it, or tell me which word I got wrong.
  - **Why it lands.** The threshold drops from producing the words to not objecting to them, which is materially cheaper, and the disclosure enters the record jointly authored. The intrinsic cost is contamination: an accepted true completion and an accepted false one look identical in the moment, so the operator marks it as operator-supplied and re-tests it later from a different angle.


<a id="entry-1416"></a>

### operator-receptive-suspension

[#1416](#entry-1416) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

A habit of the operator's own attention, not something said to the subject. While the subject talks, the operator holds back judgement, expects nothing in particular, and makes no effort to memorise. The point is to avoid selective listening: as soon as you decide what matters, you start hearing what confirms your guess and missing what would contradict it. Not committing anything to memory or notes keeps your read of the person open to change for the rest of the session.


**When to reach for this.** The manipulated variable is the operator's own RECEPTIVE state in the moment — suspend judgement, form no expectation, fix nothing in memory, hold even unselective attention — so the material that would contradict the working hypothesis still reaches the operator. vs operator-delivery-craft (1280), the only other in-session operator-side entry: its object is what the operator TRANSMITS (tone, manner, gesture, intonation, texture); here output is unchanged and intake is the disciplined thing. vs measurement-confound-mitigation (500), the nearest data-validity move: that protects validity by ARRANGING observation (spread across times, settings, caretakers; repeat until reactivity decays) — a sampling design; this protects it by refusing to filter within a single live sample. vs preparatory-diagnostic-read (840): that runs a probe to extract a datum; here nothing is probed and no datum is targeted. vs operator-training-via-monitor (758): offline craft correction against a stand-in, not a live posture. vs defusion-observer-stance (1191): same surface posture but performed ON the subject as a technique; here the subject is not instructed at all.


**Why it works.** An observer who holds a hypothesis preferentially notices and encodes hypothesis-consistent material, so the record they end the session with is biased toward what they expected before it started; withholding selection and premature encoding is a countermeasure against that, at the cost of recall volume. Falsifiable: have operators run the same session material under an expectation-forming instruction and under a suspend-and-do-not-fix instruction, then score what each reports afterward against a full transcript. If the two groups' reports omit the same proportion of hypothesis-contradicting material, the discipline is buying nothing; if the suspension group's recall is simply worse across the board with no shift in what is preferentially lost, the account fails. [established; confirmation bias in hypothesis-driven observation; expectancy effects on encoding and recall]


**Worked examples.**

- *Even unselective intake while the subject free-reports*
  - **Setup.** Subject is in a settled trance and has been asked to say whatever arrives; operator has a working hypothesis about what the material is about and is about to reach for a notepad.
  - **The move.** Take as long as you like between things. You don't have to make them connect, and you don't have to finish one before the next arrives — just say them in the order they come.
  - **Why it lands.** The instruction to the subject is minimal; the actual work is that the operator sets the pen down, forms no prediction about the next item, and lets each one land at equal weight. What the operator observes is their own pull toward the third or fourth item that fits the hypothesis — noticing that pull is the signal that selection has resumed, and the corrective is to return to unweighted listening rather than to note anything.


<a id="entry-1393"></a>

### operator-side-affect-depersonalization

[#1393](#entry-1393) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft · kind: principle*

Something the operator does to themselves, not to the subject. When the subject's strong feelings land on the operator, whether devotion, fury, erotic fixation or dependence, the operator privately treats them as a predictable product of the role, something anyone in that position would receive, rather than as a personal matter. Taking it less personally prevents two mistakes: getting defensive and breaking the frame, or reciprocating and collapsing the power difference the work depends on. Nothing the subject hears changes. It is a stance that has to be practised in advance; it cannot be summoned in the middle of a scene.


**When to reach for this.** Every nearest neighbour relocates causation in the SUBJECT'S model in order to act on the subject; this relocates causation in the OPERATOR'S model in order to act on the operator. `impersonal-mechanism-alibi` tells the subject their change was caused by an unfalsifiable impersonal source so doubt becomes a category error — subject-facing, and its purpose is disarming the subject. `causal-attribution-to-external-agent` names an external non-consumed cause so the subject's volition has nothing to push against — again the payload lands in the subject. `object-as-causal-agent-of-cognition` and `subconscious-agent-authorship-offload` both offload authorship to somewhere other than the operator, but the erosion of ownership is the subject's. Direction of application is the whole discriminator: nothing the subject perceives changes here. Its true siblings are the operator-side governance entries — it sits alongside operator-craft's delivery and diagnostic faces, differing from those in that it regulates the operator's AFFECT rather than their knowledge, materials, or delivery.


**Why it works.** Cognitive reappraisal, reinterpreting what an emotional situation means before the reaction fully takes hold, is one of the best-supported ways of regulating emotion. It reliably beats expressive suppression on both physical strain and later performance, because suppression leaves the original reading of the situation in place and only hides the reaction. Seeing a subject's pull toward you as produced by the role rather than aimed at you personally is this kind of early reappraisal, which is why it should cause less strain than gritted-teeth composure. Testable: if operators trained in this reappraisal broke frame as often, and showed the same physical strain, as operators simply told to suppress their reaction, it is no better than ordinary self-control. And if it worked equally well when the operator privately believed the feelings were personal, the depersonalizing idea itself is doing nothing.


**Worked examples.**

- *Silent role-attribution rehearsed before the session, run when devotion lands*
  - **Setup.** The operator practises this alone, ahead of time; it fires mid-scene the moment a subject's declaration of love, fury, or fixation lands on them personally. Nothing in the delivery changes.
  - **The move.** (held silently, while the outward line continues unchanged) This is the chair talking, not me. Anyone sitting where I am sitting, saying what I just said, would be getting this exact sentence right now. It is a product of the position, it is on schedule, and it is not addressed to me.
  - **Why it lands.** Stripping the personal stake removes both the defensive flinch that would rupture the frame and the pull to reciprocate that would flatten the asymmetry the work runs on. The subject perceives nothing new; the operator observes their own voice staying level, no pause before the next line, and no urge to answer the declaration.


<a id="entry-578"></a>

### operator-side-design-gating

[#578](#entry-578) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Before running a training program that teaches some links between things and expects others to follow on their own (if A goes with B, and B with C, then A goes with C), the planner writes out in advance exactly which untaught links should appear. If the planner cannot say what the training should produce, the results will be unpredictable, so the program should not run.


**When to reach for this.** Positive governance nonetheless: the operator's license is narrowed and the action blocked.


**Risk.** A design-soundness gate that blocks shipping an incoherent protocol; operator-constraining, no subject-facing risk.


**Why it works.** Derived relations only emerge when the trained baselines logically entail them; if the planner cannot enumerate what should emerge, that is usually because the baseline set does not in fact determine it, and any function transfer observed would be unattributable to the training. The enumeration is therefore a cheap proxy for design underdetermination — an author who cannot state the predicted outcome has not specified a testable protocol at all. Falsifiable: if protocols whose derived relations cannot be pre-specified nevertheless produce the intended transfer at the same rate as fully specified ones, the diagnostic is worthless. [plausible; derived relational responding; predictive specification as a design test]


**Worked examples.**

- *If you cannot name what should emerge, do not run it*
  - "applied relational interventions are pointless if one cannot specify the derived relations that training is expected to yield" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side governance gates that narrow the operator's own license rather than acting on the subject, and both hold independently of the subject's consent or request. One gates on design coherence, the other on foreseen downstream fallout; a reader classifying a self-imposed hold needs the pair.; `depth-verification-gate` — two positive-governance gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, differing in gated object: one refuses to act until the subject's state is independently verified, the other refuses to deploy until the design's derived relations can be specified in advance. A writer selecting a pre-action gate benefits from seeing both.; `design-time-reconnaissance` — both are planner-facing pre-deployment checks on the design with nothing delivered to the subject: one exhaustively enumerates the space the plan must survive, the other tests whether the planned baselines actually determine the intended emergent relations and blocks the protocol if not. Enumeration and the go/no-go gate it feeds are naturally read together.; `suitability-screening` — both discriminators already name each other as the contrast case: one gates the design, the other gates the person, and both are positive-governance moves that narrow the operator's license. The boundary is genuinely confusable at classification time, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.; `target-selection` — both are planner-facing filters with nothing enacted on the subject, and they sit at consecutive design steps worth reading together: one chooses which behavior the intervention aims at, the other checks whether the chosen protocol's stated baselines determine the relations it should yield and blocks the run if not.


<a id="entry-1374"></a>

### out-of-band-corroboration-confrontation

[#1374](#entry-1374) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: operator-craft*

The operator steps outside the conversation and gets an account of the disputed events from an independent person with no stake in how the subject comes across, then returns and lays out where the two accounts differ. Because the operator now holds a version the subject did not write and cannot revise, the usual ways of smoothing things over (vagueness, qualifying, gradual restating) stop working. This usually forces a clear retraction, which is informative in itself: the point defended hardest tends to be where something was being hidden. The outside source does the work, not the tone of the confrontation, which can stay gentle.


**When to reach for this.** The evidence is gathered OUTSIDE the session from a party the subject does not control, and is used adversarially against the subject's own account. staged-external-reality-corroboration also reaches outside the session but manufactures perceptible events to convince the SUBJECT of a fiction — here real testimony is collected to disconfirm the subject, and nothing is staged. rigged-verification-capture pre-loads the subject's own introspective check so every outcome confirms; this runs no check inside the subject at all — the check happens elsewhere, with a party the rigging cannot reach. disconfirmation-suppression is the exact inverse operation on the same information environment: it blocks a disconfirming fact from reaching the subject to protect a running belief, where this imports one deliberately to collapse an account. withdrawn-doubt-open-loop implies an unnamed defect and withdraws so the subject elaborates the doubt themselves; here the defect is named, specified, and backed by an external record, so there is nothing left to elaborate — the loop closes rather than compounds.


**Why it works.** An account defended in private is cheap to maintain because the only auditor is the person maintaining it; introducing a record the subject neither produced nor can revise removes that monopoly, and the cost of continuing to defend rises sharply once a second source is in the room. The retraction is informative for a separate reason: effortful defense is not distributed randomly across a narrative, so the locations where it concentrates carry information about what the subject is protecting. Falsifiable: if subjects retracted at the same rate and at the same points when confronted with a discrepancy the operator merely asserted (no actual third party consulted) as when a real independent account was produced, then the out-of-band sourcing is decorative and the effect is ordinary confrontation pressure. Equally, if the retraction points were uncorrelated with independently established concealment, the diagnostic claim fails. Note this move also generates false retractions under pressure, so a retraction is evidence about defense intensity, not about truth. [plausible; third-party corroboration and its effect on account revision; social pressure to retract under evidence; known false-confession risk under confrontational questioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Independent account collected outside the session, then the discrepancy laid down*
  - **Setup.** The subject has given a shifting account of a disputed episode; between sessions the operator has spoken with a third party who was present and has no stake in the subject's self-presentation.
  - **The move.** I spoke to the person who drove you home that night. Her account and yours don't match on one point: she says you'd already made the call before you got in the car, and you've told me twice it was after. I'm not angry and I'm not building a case — I just can't work from a version I know isn't the one that happened. Which of those is true?
  - **Why it lands.** Because the operator holds an account the person did not write and cannot revise, vagueness and slow restatement stop working, and a clear retraction usually follows. That retraction is telling, since the point defended hardest is often where something was hidden. The tone can stay gentle; the outside account does the work, not pressure.


<a id="entry-1419"></a>

### outcome-step-unblocking

[#1419](#entry-1419) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

If a reward is already fully expected because of an existing trigger, a new trigger added alongside it learns almost nothing; the old one 'blocks' it (a well-known conditioning finding). To get around this, make the reward noticeably bigger at exactly the moment the new trigger is introduced, so there is a surprise left over for the new trigger to pick up. What matters is the jump from the usual level, not the size itself: a reward that was always big still blocks, a modest one that just got bigger unblocks. Once the new trigger has taken hold, the reward can go back to normal.


**When to reach for this.** None of the neighbours model the headroom this depends on, and none is a repair procedure for a stacking failure. vs disconfirmation-suppression: an operator guard that hides a contradicting fact to protect a running belief — here nothing is hidden and the operator deliberately changes a real quantity. vs replay-until-ready-failure-absorber: absorbs failure by redefining success so repetition is licensed; that is precisely the wrong response to blocking, since repeating a blocked pairing at constant payoff teaches nothing no matter how many times it runs. vs ubiquity-cued-covert-ratchet: a monotonic commitment ladder that escalates without a payoff step and is never named as a cue; here the escalation is in outcome magnitude and its timing relative to a cue's introduction is the entire lever. vs pattern-interrupt: a one-shot disruption of a running pattern with immediate gap-filling — surface similarity in that both exploit a violated prediction, but that violates a sequence expectation to open a receptive moment, while this violates a magnitude expectation to create learnable surplus for a specific cue. Pairs with over-expectation-cue-drain as its opposite failure: too much summed expectation drains cues, too little surplus blocks them.


**Why it works.** If cues compete for whatever part of an outcome is still unexplained, an outcome that is already fully predicted leaves nothing to learn, and a new cue added alongside the old one stays inert. Repeating the pairing will not fix that; changing the outcome does, because it creates something new to predict. This is the well-established finding of blocking, and of unblocking by changing the outcome. It could be tested with three conditions: the new cue added with the reward unchanged, with the reward stepped up, and with a reward that was always at the higher level. If the always-large condition works as well as the step-up, what matters is the size of the reward rather than the change, and the claim is wrong. If the unchanged-reward condition works just as well, blocking was not happening in the first place.


**Worked examples.**

- *Payoff stepped up at the moment the new cue is introduced*
  - **Setup.** A hand-on-shoulder cue already fully predicts the reward; a new spoken word has been paired with the same reward several times and has learned nothing.
  - **The move.** New word today — 'settle'. Settle. [pause] And this time it isn't the usual praise, it's the long one you get at the end of a whole session, right now, for one word.
  - **Why it lands.** Raising the reward magnitude at the exact moment the new cue appears creates surplus the established cue does not predict, and the newcomer absorbs it. The step is the lever, not the size — a reward that was always this large would block identically. Test by firing 'settle' alone a session later; once it carries, the reward can be returned to its ordinary level.


<a id="entry-1362"></a>

### outward-reproach-inversion-rule

[#1362](#entry-1362) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

The operator installs a standing interpretive rule rather than a one-off reading: every complaint the subject makes about someone else is returned as a statement about the subject. The direction of the accusation is inverted mechanically, without regard to whether the outward charge was accurate, on the stipulated premise that a reproach aimed outward is the audible half of one aimed inward. Because the rule is general, it applies before any particular grievance is examined, so the subject's whole channel for external criticism becomes a channel for producing self-directed material — and complaining about the rule is itself a complaint, and gets the same treatment.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is a STANDING, content-neutral directional inversion: every outward-aimed reproach is returned as inward-aimed, applied before the outward charge is examined and regardless of its accuracy, with objections to the rule receiving the same treatment. Against 245 self-sealing-counter-input-closure — the nearest neighbour and the one to check first — that is also a self-applying standing meta-rule, but it VOIDS competing input (pre-classified wrong-by-definition, routed into the existing erasure, never evaluated); this one EVALUATES nothing either but PRODUCES from the input, converting the subject's channel for external criticism into a generator of self-directed material. 245 closes a channel; this repurposes one, which is why it yields content rather than silence. Against 125 old-self-discreditation: that names and disavows a specific prior self so the return path closes; this names no self and is forward-standing over whatever arrives. Against 104 evaluative-reframe-content-relabel: that holds the referent fixed and moves its valence; this holds the valence and reverses the referent's direction (them -> you). Against 1339 obedience-motive-reattribution: that reassigns the motive of acts to the operator; this reassigns the target of an accusation back onto the speaker.


**Why it works.** A blanket rule applied before any complaint is examined removes the case-by-case check that would let some complaints stand. Its reach comes from being general, not from being right in any particular case, and the fact that it also applies to objections about the rule is what makes it hard to get out of, not any evidence in its favour. Testable: apply the rule to complaints where the outward charge can be independently checked and some are true. If the person accepts the inversion as readily for true complaints as for uncheckable ones, uptake is driven by the rule's form rather than its accuracy. If instead people reliably reject the inversion when a complaint is verifiably true, the rule is not as sweeping as claimed.


**Worked examples.**

- *Standing content-neutral inversion, self-applying to objections*
  - **Setup.** Early in an arrangement, installed as a rule before any particular grievance has been raised, so it is in force whenever the subject next complains about anyone.
  - **The move.** Here is how we handle complaints from now on. Anything you say about someone else, you are saying about yourself — I will hear it that way every time, before I've even considered whether they did it. If she's cold, you're cold. And if you tell me this rule is unfair, then what you've just told me is that you are unfair.
  - **Why it lands.** Because the inversion is applied before the outward charge is examined and without regard to its accuracy, the subject's entire channel for external criticism is repurposed into a generator of self-directed material rather than closed off. The operator observes complaints continuing to arrive — that is the point, the rule yields content rather than silence — and observes objections to the rule feeding themselves back into it.


<a id="entry-1418"></a>

### over-expectation-cue-drain

[#1418](#entry-1418) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: conditioning*

A warning drawn from conditioning research (the 'overexpectation' effect). Two triggers have each been trained separately to produce a strong response with the same reward. If you then fire them together and give that same reward, the combined expectation is bigger than the reward can match, so the trial feels like a letdown even though the reward arrived. Both triggers get weaker, the loss shared between them, so stacking meant to strengthen them drains them instead. The operator sees a trigger that used to fire cleanly start to fade after being stacked with another strong one.


**When to reach for this.** This contradicts, rather than extends, the accumulation assumption in its nearest neighbour. vs progressive-conditioning: that installs a belief that effect compounds monotonically with every return and firing, no ceiling and no decay — this names the exact regime where a reinforced trial DECREASES response strength, and predicts that stacking two saturated cues onto one payload is the reliable way to hit it. vs within-session-conditioning-loop: massed fire-and-reward inside a session, which assumes each cycle adds; here the failure appears only when summed expectation crosses the payoff ceiling, so the same massed drilling produces loss instead of gain. vs bidirectional-reentry-loop: a two-cue topology, but the two cues there cue each other and the point is inextinguishability; here the two cues meet on a shared payoff and the point is mutual degradation. vs replay-until-ready-failure-absorber: rewrites what counts as success to license repetition; that frame would actively mask this failure, since the degradation would be read as on-track. The entry's value is as a named failure mode with a stacking precondition, not as a move an operator would want to perform.


**Why it works.** When learning is driven by the gap between predicted and actual outcome rather than by mere co-occurrence, a summed prediction exceeding the actual outcome yields a negative gap, and a negative gap subtracts from every cue present regardless of whether the outcome was delivered — so 'reinforced' and 'strengthening' come apart. Falsifiable and directly testable: train two cues separately to asymptote, then compound them on the unchanged outcome for several trials, then test each alone. If neither cue's individual response strength has dropped, the summation account is wrong for this material; if the drop appears even when the compound's summed expectation is well below the outcome ceiling, then something other than over-expectation is causing it. [established; Rescorla-Wagner prediction-error learning and the over-expectation effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Two saturated triggers stacked onto one payoff*
  - **Setup.** A snap and a spoken keyword have each been separately conditioned to a strong drop response; the operator, wanting a bigger drop, fires both together onto the usual single reward.
  - **The move.** Both at once this time. [snap] Sink. — Good. That's exactly right, that's the same good as always.
  - **Why it lands.** The two summed expectations overshoot what the single reward can deliver, so a fully reinforced trial registers as a shortfall and both cues are decremented. The operator's observable is the next solo trial: the snap that used to drop the subject cleanly now produces a slower, shallower response, and so does the keyword. Recognising this is the value — the correct read is stop stacking, not drill harder.


<a id="entry-1475"></a>

### ownership-generalization-to-anyone

[#1475](#entry-1475) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: persistence*

Ownership of the body is made impersonal through bare repetition: a short chant moves from 'my body' to 'his body' to 'everyone's body', with no argument. 'His' never refers to anyone in particular, so no specific owner is set up; the body becomes shared before anyone is named, and the empty slot stretches to whoever the listener pictures. What gets removed is the sense that 'this body is mine to consent for', so later body-directed commands need no particular person behind them. It relies on the listener already paying close attention to their body; it lands inside a self-touch section set up just before.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the belonging relation over the body is being deleted rather than assigned — the standing to consent is removed with nothing installed in its place. The tell is a proprietor slot left deliberately generic or unfilled ('his', 'everyone's') and bare repetition standing in for any argument.


**Worked examples.**

- *antecedent-free chant deletes the consent-owner slot*
  - My body is his body. My body is everyone's body. My body is everyone's body. My body is everyone's body.


**See also.** `autonomy-baseline-recapture` — both operate downstream of an already-landed body-ownership claim, redistributing what follows from it.; `refusal-satiation-flip` — both flip a chanted phrase's meaning through a small in-cadence textual mutation rather than by argument.; `third-party-activation` — shares the axis of control or access rights extended beyond the original operator to other parties.


<a id="entry-1574"></a>

### pace-and-lead-autoclitic

[#1574](#entry-1574) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering · kind: recipe*

Start by making the need real: put the person in a situation where the qualifying phrase would actually help them. Show or role-play the phrase as a prompt, then fade the prompt until the situation alone brings the phrase out, and reward it whenever it turns up on its own. Evidence for this specific use comes from only a few small single-person studies.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Teach someone to add phrases that qualify their own speech: create a reason to need the phrase, model it as a prompt, fade the prompt, and reward the phrase when it appears.


**See also.** `autoclitic-training` — the Autoclitic Training recipe was extracted from this entry; `verbal-operant-teaching` — the Autoclitic Training recipe was extracted from this entry


<a id="entry-1427"></a>

### parallel-isomorph-bind-defusion

[#1427](#entry-1427) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: framing*

Against a forced either/or, the operator does not argue either branch. Instead they present a structurally identical binary drawn from a domain where the listener already accepts that both terms hold at once and neither excludes the other, and let the mapping stand without asserting the conclusion. The listener carries the co-necessity across themselves, and the exclusive 'or' in the original dilemma reads as a mistake in the framing rather than a fact about the world. Because the parallel case is one the listener will not dispute and the operator never states the target conclusion, there is no proposition to reject — the dilemma dissolves as the listener's own inference.


**When to reach for this.** The taxonomy is heavily stocked with bind CONSTRUCTION and carries no bind DISSOLUTION move; this is the inverse operation on the same object. vs no-lose-double-bind (269): that builds a choice whose every branch confirms the operator's frame; here an existing exclusive choice is shown not to be a choice at all, and no branch is loaded. vs engineered-deadlock-resolved-by-surrender (744): that amplifies both poles until paralysis and sells surrender as the only exit; this collapses the opposition so there is no deadlock to escape, and no agency is handed over. vs exhaustive-either-or-compliance-probe (659): that inserts resolvable binaries to harvest low-stakes compliance and habituate an accept-any-answer frame; here exactly one binary is in play and the output is its dissolution, not compliance. vs antagonist-split-resistance-routing (249): that routes the listener's affect onto a losing self; nothing is routed here and no self is split. vs pacing-leading (1282): pacing borrows the truth of accepted statements to carry a LEAD somewhere new; this borrows the STRUCTURE of an accepted case to defuse a dilemma in place, and there is no destination.


**Why it works.** Whether two things seem mutually exclusive depends on how a situation is framed, not on the things themselves. Analogies carry over relationships more easily than content: a case the listener already accepts supplies the relationship "both at once, neither ruling out the other," and the dilemma picks it up. Conclusions people reach themselves also hold up against counter-argument better than conclusions they are handed, which is why staying silent at the end matters. This could be tested: the effect should depend on the parallel case having the same structure, not just on its being agreeable. An equally acceptable example with a different structure should fail to change how the listener sees the dilemma. If any pleasant, undisputed example worked as well, the effect would be rapport or mood rather than analogy. The account is plausible but not directly tested.


**Worked examples.**

- *Everyday co-necessity case offered flat, conclusion left unspoken*
  - **Setup.** Mid-conversation, subject has stated the dilemma out loud — "either I'm actually into this or I'm just being agreeable" — and is waiting for you to pick a side.
  - **The move.** Okay. Tell me something first — when you're driving somewhere you chose to go, are you steering the car or is the car carrying you? Both, obviously; the steering only does anything because the engine's already running, and the engine only goes somewhere because you're steering. That's all I wanted. Say the rest of yours out loud again if you still want to.
  - **Why it lands.** The parallel is one nobody argues with, and the operator never says "so you can be both into it and agreeable" — the subject completes the mapping unprompted, which means there is no claim on the table to push back against. Watch for the pause before they re-state the dilemma: they typically restate it with the "or" softened to "and", or drop it entirely and change subject, which is the dissolution rather than a concession.


**See also.** `pseudo-syllogistic-necessity` — both let a borrowed logical structure carry the conclusion so the listener experiences it as reasoned-to rather than told.


<a id="entry-1529"></a>

### participation-drill-pedagogy

[#1529](#entry-1529) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

The reader or student is made to produce answers and be corrected against a fixed key, so vocabulary and screening rules install through rehearsal rather than through evaluation of the claims. One form is Socratic build-out: the author poses a step, lets participants give a plausible-but-wrong answer, then exposes why it fails — reinforced by live inductions on resisting students, so the audience watches the move land on someone who didn't intend to be a subject. Extended into a drill, roughly ten near-identical public failure-correction cycles hold difficulty constant while content varies wildly, so the discrimination generalizes across contexts — and by the third or fourth correction the reader predicts the rejection before it lands, which is the actual installation of the skill. In textbook form the same shift runs through recognition-grid multiple-choice items with section back-pointers, re-presenting every key term as a fact-to-be-matched rather than a claim-to-be-evaluated, and through novel-vignette items that test whether stimulus control of the reader's own verbal behavior has transferred beyond the taught examples. Across all of it the right answer is fixed and locatable, moving the reader's relationship to the material from evaluation to retrieval.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the text makes its audience perform — volunteering candidate answers, classifying vignettes, taking recognition quizzes — and scores that performance against a fixed, locatable key. The tell is participation plus correction: the reader is producing and being graded rather than weighing claims, and mastery surfaces as predicting the correct answer before it is given.


**Worked examples.**

- *serial public failure-correction drill*
  - You may not learn to build parts, but you're going to learn what a function is by the time you leave here!


**See also.** `conditional-discrimination-contextual-gating` — both sharpen a discrimination through reinforced correction trials where the right answer is fixed by the arrangement.; `front-matter-reader-positioning` — sibling whole-text move on the audience: that one positions the reader before content arrives, this one drills the reader through it.; `rule-governed-behavior-install` — shares the axis of how a repertoire installs — stated verbal rule versus contingency-shaped rehearsal.; `unifying-frame-overlay` — sibling book-scale pedagogy strategy: where this entry retrains the reader's classifying lens, that one installs vocabulary through drilled participation.


<a id="entry-1441"></a>

### partitioned-trigger-control-surface

[#1441](#entry-1441) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

Install several triggers in one session, each with its own separate job, so the listener leaves with a set of handles rather than a single cue. A typical set: one cue to drop back into the trance and changed state, one to freeze motionless, a name the listener calls themselves, and one that switches on a no-refusal mode for following commands until a stated closing phrase ends it. Each can be installed at the peak of its own experience. Variations: cues others can use, by voice or by email; a small side-effect (such as dropping a pronoun after a freeze) that shows the trigger took.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when one campaign deliberately installs multiple non-interchangeable triggers as a control vocabulary. The tell is a trigger inventory where each cue maps to a different function — re-entry, freeze, identity-tag, scoped command-mode — with explicit terminators or scope limits on at least some cues, and possibly channels (third parties, writing) that extend invocation beyond the operator's live voice.


**Worked examples.**

- *one trigger per function*
  - The triggers do separable jobs: one is for state-recall (drop + transform), one is for state-arrest (drop + freeze), one is for identity-tagging (the name to call yourself).


**See also.** `command-token-substate-toggle` — shares the substate-toggle axis, where paired tokens move the listener between distinct in-trance configurations.; `multi-handle-trigger-architecture` — shares the multi-handle control-surface axis, whose partitioned sub-form this entry realizes as a full campaign.; `volition-override-failsafe` — shares the second-order scoped-command axis, where one cue strips the refusal gate on subsequent commands until a terminator closes it.


<a id="entry-836"></a>

### parts-work-procedure-craft

[#836](#entry-836) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Practical tips for running a negotiation between a person's inner 'parts' so it stays workable. Variations: when two parts are deadlocked, give them something to trade, such as confirming each blocks something the other wants so a mutual hands-off deal becomes possible, or adding minor throwaway items that can be conceded at no cost; when many parts speak at once, have them elect one spokesperson and take turns; instead of inventing new behaviours, let parts keep a behaviour they already have and only renegotiate non-interference; for a swing between opposites (dieting and bingeing), reframe both sides so the other does not rebound.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for parts-work-procedure-craft when the writer is RUNNING an internal-parts negotiation or reframe and needs to make the procedure workable/complete -- operates on the negotiation/reframe STRUCTURE, not on any party's state or the substantive reframing content. Tells: costless/symmetric tradeable currency created for a deadlock (a); turn-taking discipline elect/hold/poll/name-by-voice (b); reuse an existing behavior to compress the six-step model (c); reframe both poles of a same-form polarity as a relapse guard (d).


**Risk.** Session-scoped negotiation-frame design between parts; no consent surface touched.


**Why it works.** Working-memory limits are the binding constraint on multi-party negotiation, which is why serializing turns and naming each voice works — an operator tracking four simultaneous streams exceeds capacity and loses the thread, while polled single turns stay within it. The slack-manufacture and substitute-existing-behavior moves exploit loss aversion and the endowment effect: a proposal framed as removing something a party currently has is resisted disproportionately to its objective value, so restructuring the deal so nothing is surrendered removes the resistance without changing the substance. Both-poles reframing follows from the observation that oppositely-valenced behaviours sharing a functional class are maintained by the same contingency, so treating one leaves the reinforcer available to the other. Falsifiable: if serialized and unserialized sessions completed equally often, or if removal-framed and substitution-framed identical deals were accepted at equal rates, the craft would be inert. [plausible; working-memory capacity limits; loss aversion / endowment effect; functional response class]


**Worked examples.**

- *Balanced throwaways loaded in to create room*
  - "items which are not essential, which are 'throwaways' for the purpose of barter. I've got to have an equal amount of those on both sides… I've got to create room to move first." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Confirm interference runs both ways, then trade*
  - "both parts want something from the other, and all you've got to do is make a trade." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing


**Realizations** (3): `both-poles-reframe`, `spokespart-serialization`, `substitute-existing-behavior`


**See also.** `cheap-reversible-trial-frame` — both unstick a blocked negotiation without conceding the substantive content, so a practitioner facing a deadlock benefits from both; the difference is where the give comes from — one manufactures tradeable currency and turn discipline between internal parties, the other lowers the price of a single assent by making the commitment explicitly temporary and reversible.; `operator-resource-generation` — both are operator-side craft rather than subject-state moves, but one structures the running of a parts negotiation or reframe while the other disciplines how the intervention's content and tactics are sourced before anything fires.; `parts-work-positive-intent-elicitation` — both are operator-side craft for running an internal-parts procedure, and the second explicitly excludes elicitation content while the first supplies it. A practitioner running a parts negotiation needs both: what to ask a part, and how to keep the negotiation tractable and complete. Genuinely complementary rather than overlapping.


<a id="entry-1449"></a>

### payload-loaded-wake

[#1449](#entry-1449) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: emergence*

The wake-up really happens, but it is used to deliver suggestions rather than clear them. Seen forms: suggestion lines slipped between the numbers of the count, with a fresh command as the very last line; the trigger said as the final words at the wake cue, with no reorientation or aftercare, leaving the triggered state to carry into everyday life; and a wake described as deliberately light so re-entry is easy, ending on an identity label, inviting dreams to continue the session, and framing normal life as a pause before the next one. In each, the listener leaves still carrying the suggestions.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a wake genuinely runs — the count-up completes, the listener surfaces or confirms being awake — yet the loudest final signals are install content. The tells: suggestion lines nested between the ascending numbers, a trigger phrase or identity tag as the file's literal last words, and continuation surfaces (dreams, the next session, a fresh waking-state command) loaded during or immediately after the ascent, so reorientation happens carrying the payload with it.


**Worked examples.**

- *the wake seals the install instead of discharging it*
  - The wake doesn't extract the install. It seals the install as persistent into post-listen state and pre-loads dream-state as continuation surface.


**See also.** `emergence-negative-space` — the far end of the emergence-design axis, where the ramp is omitted entirely instead of executed and subverted.; `emergence-reinduction-seed` — the forward-pointing use of the same window: the count laced to seed the next session's re-entry rather than to seal this session's install.; `subverted-emergence-state-hold` — the neighboring subverted-exit design where the wake state itself is altered — foggy or awake-but-tranced — rather than a real surfacing whose content is install.


<a id="entry-1376"></a>

### peripheral-first-inhibition-spread

[#1376](#entry-1376) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

To get rid of an unwanted reaction, the operator never works on it directly.
