Instead they start with cues that only faintly resemble the real one and let those fail to produce the reaction, then move step by step to closer and closer cues. The weakening spreads inward, so by the time the original cue is reached, if it ever is, it already sits among similar cues that no longer work. Because the guarded cue is never approached while it is still guarded, the person never has a reason to defend it.


**When to reach for this.** The operator's activity is concentrated on the target cue's NEIGHBOURS and the target is worked last or never, with suppression arriving by generalization along the similarity dimension. Against counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening (1032), which is the same dimension traversed the other way: its graded-exposure facet APPROACHES the eliciting stimulus under an incompatible state and its sub-threshold-property-fade works a property of the target cue itself — both contact the target, this retreats from it. Against reinforcement-extinction (432), which requires every maintaining source to be enumerated and cut AT the target: here the target's contingency is never touched. Against antecedent-manipulation (1052), which removes the cue so the occasion stops arising: here the target cue remains fully available throughout. The falsifying test is the tell — stop the sequence before reaching the target and probe it; if responding is unchanged, no spread occurred and there is no technique.


**Why it works.** Training a cue to mean that nothing happens does not stay local. The effect spreads to similar cues along a gradient (generalization of conditioned inhibition), so working on neighbouring cues leaves suppression that reaches the untouched target in proportion to how similar it is. Working from far to near lets that effect build up before you approach the defended cue, instead of provoking the protection that direct contact would. The test is sharp and cheap: run the sequence but stop before the target, then check the target. If its response is unchanged, nothing spread and every gain was local. And if starting near the target works just as well as starting far away, the order does not matter and this is just ordinary extinction. Pavlov explained the spread with a physiological theory of 'irradiation' that has since been abandoned; the gradient itself holds up, his explanation does not.


**Worked examples.**

- *Outward-in ladder: distant neighbours worked, the defended cue untouched*
  - **Setup.** The subject flinches hard at one specific cue — a hand at the back of the neck — and has defended it every time it was approached directly. The operator opens at the far end of the same dimension.
  - **The move.** Today I'm not going anywhere near your neck. Give me your left forearm — two fingers resting there, and nothing happens, and you notice nothing happens. Now the inside of the elbow: same thing, nothing. Now the top of the shoulder. Nothing there either. That's where we stop for today.
  - **Why it lands.** The neck is never touched while it is still defended, so the subject has no reason to put up the protection that direct work would trigger. Meanwhile the learning that nothing happens builds at the neighbouring spots and spreads inward toward the neck. To check whether it is working, stop short of the neck and test it: if the flinch is unchanged, nothing has spread.


<a id="entry-1562"></a>

### peripheral-vision-induction

[#1562](#entry-1562) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: attention · kind: recipe*

Have the listener hold a fixed stare while spreading attention across the whole edge of vision at once; this is tiring and absorbing, and eye fatigue does the rest. As the eyes tire, call the tiredness trance and suggest the eyes grow heavy and close. The evidence is folk-level only.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Have them stare at one point, then widen attention to everything at the edge of vision at once until the eyes want to close.


<a id="entry-1386"></a>

### phase-gated-suppressor-timing

[#1386](#entry-1386) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

What happens after a stop signal depends on timing. In classic conditioning experiments with dogs, a metronome trained to signal a response after a three-minute delay was played only for its early part, while the animal was still holding back. A touch or light signal the dog already responded to was then tested two minutes later. In one dog the later response was weaker, because the build-up never started in that gap. In another dog the build-up did start, and the later response came out stronger, as the two effects added together. So the effect differs between individuals and can run either way; a stop signal does not reliably dampen what follows.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting principle when distinguishing inhibitory after-effects from excitatory summation in the response to a later positive stimulus, with the preceding delayed reflex's phase isolation explicitly considered. Forward pairing or cue-order rules concern acquisition or predecessor selection; this account concerns an already established delayed reflex and its effect on a later test response. Opposed-state fusion binds opposed effects in a script and is not the reported procedure. Timing is relevant to the phase account, but the cited contrast is between two dogs under the same interval, not an interval sweep proving sign reversal in one fixed cue-and-animal pair. A breathing rhythm is not evidence of these conditioned phases, and a stop request is not the positive probe used here.


**Why it works.** The report gives a 60–70% reduction of positive tactile and visual reflexes in the first dog after the metronome's inhibitory phase, and an increased positive effect in a second dog. Pavlov relates this difference to effective separation of the inhibitory and excitatory phases in the first dog versus earlier, stronger excitation and incomplete separation in the second. Under the same two-minute interval, the first dog showed no emergence of the excitatory phase while the second did. The source also emphasizes variability across dogs. This supports a historical account of phase-dependent after-effects and summation, not a universal timing-only sign law, a guaranteed crossing point in an interval sweep, or the claim that a mistimed human interrupt strengthens what it is intended to stop. It provides no breath-timed stop procedure.


**Worked examples.**

- *A later positive test response under different delayed-reflex after-effects*
  - **Setup.** A reader is comparing two dogs in Pavlov's delayed-reflex report. After the early portion of a delayed metronome reflex, a positive stimulus from another sensory modality is used to test the after-effect.
  - **The move.** Draw two timelines with the same two-minute interval. For the first dog, mark that excitation did not emerge during the interval and that the later positive reflex was diminished. For the second, mark the emergence of excitation and the increased later positive effect attributed to summation.
  - **Why it lands.** This authored diagram instruction illustrates the reported comparison without inventing a human intervention. It holds the interval constant across the two dogs and makes the phase difference explicit. The dependent observation is the positive test response; the example does not reverse the causal direction into a suppressing probe controlling its host, infer the phases from breathing, or prescribe when to deliver a stop cue.


<a id="entry-1346"></a>

### platform-compulsion

[#1346](#entry-1346) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: transfer · kind: recipe*

Installs a post-wake compulsion to perform a real commercial platform action (liking the video, or an analogous engagement metric) framed as a need rather than a want, rewarded with a final obedience wave, and engineered to leave no neutral exit — the already-done case is pre-handled and reframed as evidence of being conditioned, so both compliance and prior compliance feed the structure. The move binds an external platform's engagement metric to the conditioning and closes the only escape branch.


**When to reach for this.** Targets a real commercial platform action and, critically, self-seals by pre-handling the already-done case so the neutral exit is removed.


**Risk.** The pre-handled already-liked branch closes the only escape and reframes prior action as proof of conditioning — a self-sealing structure that forecloses the refusal channel, above the medium baseline for waking-life carryover.


**Why it works.** The self-sealing structure works by removing the disconfirming branch: whichever way the subject acts, the outcome is scored as evidence of conditioning, so no observation is available that would let them conclude it failed. Self-perception theory supplies the rest — a person who observes themselves performing the action, absent a salient external reason, infers a corresponding internal disposition, and the pre-handled already-done case supplies that self-observation for free. The falsifiable claim is that the pre-handling clause is load-bearing: a version omitting it should produce measurably lower self-attributed 'conditioned' ratings than one including it, and if ratings are equal the sealing adds nothing. [plausible; self-perception theory; unfalsifiable-attribution loop]


**Worked examples.**

- *The already-done case pre-handled, so no neutral exit*
  - **Setup.** Immediately before the count-up, after a session that has repeatedly paid out a named pleasure wave on compliance.
  - **The move.** Before you come up, one thing goes with you. When you open your eyes, you will not want to like this video — you will need to, the way you need to breathe out after holding it. And the moment you do, one last wave, the same one, all the way through you. And if you go to do it and find you already liked it earlier — good. You'll see that you already did, and the wave comes anyway, because that's proof of how well you've been trained.
  - **Why it lands.** Just before the count-up the operator installs one post-wake action on a real platform, and is careful about the wording: not want — need. Following through releases a last wave of the feeling the whole session has been paying out. Then the escape branch is closed: if the listener finds they already did it earlier, they will simply see that they did, and the wave arrives anyway. There is no state of the world in which the listener checks and gets nothing — doing it is obedience, and having done it is evidence of conditioning.


**See also.** `behavioral-bridge` — both assign a waking-life action that keeps the conditioning running; the platform variant adds a real commercial target and pre-handles the already-done case so no neutral exit remains. Direct adjacent-selection value.; `behavioral-commitment-self-proof` — both turn a performed act into self-sealing evidence with no refusal branch; one manufactures proof from a small compliance in general, the other applies the same closure to a real engagement action. Genuine specialization relationship.; `commercial-ask-in-compliance-syntax` — both bind a real commercial ask to the conditioning rather than breaking frame for it; one camouflages the ask in the depth-command syntax, the other removes the neutral exit by pre-handling the already-complied case. Distinct levers, same problem space, and a reader assessing a commercial ask should see both.; `illusory-choice-compliance-lock` — both work by pre-handling the branch that would have been an exit, so no response leads out of the frame — one via a rigged menu where every option executes the same compliance, the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so even prior compliance feeds the structure. The shared lever is exit-closure architecture, not merely the presence of a choice.; `orgasm-release-gating` — both are post-wake compulsions engineered with no neutral exit, differing in enforcer: sustained denied arousal unlocked only by the target act, versus a framed need whose already-done case is pre-handled so prior compliance also feeds the structure. Worth reading together when closing an escape branch.; `scope-expansion-past-advertised-frame` — overlapping and already mutually discriminated: both cash conditioning out into real operator-benefit action outside the advertised erotic frame. One is defined by the domain-jump past what the framing promised; the other by pre-handling the already-complied case so no neutral exit remains. A platform-engagement payload frequently exhibits both, so the reader needs the boundary stated.


<a id="entry-1476"></a>

### pluralistic-ignorance-freeze

[#1476](#entry-1476) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: social-topology · kind: principle*

In an ambiguous emergency among co-present strangers, each bystander reads the calm non-response of the others as evidence that nothing is wrong, and so stays calm too — every onlooker mutually pacifying every other, each person's inaction becoming proof to the next, recursively. No operator is required and no model performs any act; the crowd's mutual monitoring alone generates the suppression, so a crowd produces less help than a lone witness would. The freeze is experienced as a calibrated read of the situation, not as paralysis: a witness explains he 'did not investigate because no one else seemed to be paying attention.' It requires genuine ambiguity, multiple co-present observers who are strangers, and visibility of one another's (non)response. As a lever it is exploited by suppressing cues that anyone is responding; as a defense it is broken by singling out one person.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when passivity emerges from a crowd mutually reading its own non-response in an ambiguous situation — nobody demonstrates anything, and the suppression is self-generating among peers. The tell is the inversion: more witnesses yielding less action, with each witness reporting their inaction as a reasonable inference from everyone else's calm.


**Worked examples.**

- *crowd non-response read as proof of no-emergency*
  - not investigate because no one else seemed to be paying attention.


**See also.** `self-sealing-feedback-loop` — shares the closed evidence-loop structure in which each participant's state is read as proof of the others'.; `self-validating-language` — shares the axis of present-moment behavior being recycled as evidence about what is really happening.


<a id="entry-1480"></a>

### polarity-response-utilization

[#1480](#entry-1480) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

With a subject whose reflex is to contradict whatever is offered, the operator states the negation of the desired action as doubt — 'I don't think it would be possible for you… to come up here and work in front of this entire group' — and the contradicting reflex fires the wanted behavior in rebellion. The same move runs in reverse on the subject's own negative position: instead of reassuring, the operator agrees emphatically and amplifies past the subject's own claim ('you must be beyond help… lock yourself in the closet'), and the subject flips to argue the opposite — her own competence — which was the goal. Resistance is not defeated or converted; it succeeds, and is merely aimed by the operator's choice of what to oppose. Because the subject experiences self-driven defiance ('I'm not that bad; come on… let's just get on with it'), the resulting motivation is self-authored rather than imposed. It requires a reliably polarity-responding subject read correctly in advance — on a compliant subject the stated negation is simply obeyed, and an amplified agreement taken at face value can do harm.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the subject reliably takes the other side of anything offered and you want that reflex to do the work — the outcome should arrive as the subject's own defiance. The tell is an operator voicing the opposite of the actual goal, as doubt in the subject's ability or as emphatic over-agreement with the subject's negative self-assessment, and then letting the flip supply the behavior.


**Worked examples.**

- *stated doubt fires the contradiction reflex*
  - I don't think it would be possible for you… to come up here and work in front of this entire group.


**See also.** `commanded-autonomic-conviction-bind` — both are Erickson demonstrations that explicitly invite the subject's resistance and put it to work for the operator's outcome.; `response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure` — both arrange in advance that the listener's oppositional responses route into the target behavior.; `trojan-goal-contract` — both state an ask that is the opposite of the intended outcome so that pursuing it delivers the operator's goal.


<a id="entry-1401"></a>

### post-episode-cue-mapping

[#1401](#entry-1401) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

After an automatic reaction has fired and passed, the subject writes down what immediately preceded it — the word, the tone, the setting, the body state — building over several episodes a log from which the actual firing cue can be read off. An opaque 'it just happens to me' converts into a named antecedent, and a named antecedent is something the subject can see coming, prepare for, or arrange not to encounter. Nothing is installed and the response itself is untouched; what changes is that the subject now holds the cue-response map that the installing party held. This is the audit step that install-concealment moves exist specifically to prevent, and it works retroactively on triggers whose install the subject cannot remember, because it reads the cue off the behavior rather than off the memory of being given it.


**When to reach for this.** Against internal-event-keyed-trigger, declarative-trigger-installation and implementation-intention: all three INSTALL a cue-response pair; this one discovers an existing pair the subject did not author, and installs nothing. The direction is the tell — those write the map, this reads it. Against fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal: that manufactures a rehearsal history to make a response feel native; this recovers a real antecedent to make a response feel foreign. Against self-observation-instrumentation: that engineers the contingency so a subject's self-COUNT of a behavior's score is truthful, and its object is the behavior's rate; here nothing is reinforced, no count is verified, and the object is the antecedent rather than the score. Within safety it is the family's first discovery move — the existing entries supply exits, bounds, checkpoints and screening, all of which presuppose you already know what you are bounding.


**Why it works.** A conditioned reaction fires faster than introspection can catch what set it off, so in-the-moment reports of the trigger are unreliable. The trigger can still be found across episodes, because it is the thing that keeps recurring while everything else varies; that is why you need several entries, and a single one proves nothing. Writing at the time also avoids the drift that creeps into memory later, as research comparing in-the-moment recording with recall shows. Testable: compare triggers identified from several written logs with a person's confident from-memory guess. If they agree just as often, the logging adds nothing over simply asking. It also predicts that logs pinpoint the trigger faster when the surroundings vary more between episodes; if someone logging in one fixed setting found it just as easily, recurrence is not what is doing the work.


**Worked examples.**

- *Antecedent log kept across episodes, cue read off the behavior*
  - **Setup.** The subject has an automatic reaction they describe as arriving out of nowhere; this is given after one has fired and fully passed, not during.
  - **The move.** Next time it happens, once it has passed, write down four things and only four: the last words you heard, whose voice, where you were standing, and what your hands were doing. Don't interpret any of it. Do that for the next five times it fires, then bring me the five and we'll read them side by side for what repeats.
  - **Why it lands.** Nothing is installed and the response is untouched; the subject simply acquires the cue-response map the installing party held, which works retroactively even where the install itself is unremembered because the cue is read off behavior rather than off memory. Observable: by the fourth or fifth entry the subject names the antecedent themselves, and "it just happens to me" is replaced by a specific word, tone, or setting they can now see coming.


<a id="entry-1365"></a>

### pre-pairing-exposure-immunization

[#1365](#entry-1365) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

Repeated unpaired exposure to a cue before it is paired with an outcome can reduce subsequent evaluative conditioning relative to a cue without that exposure history. The relevant operation is pre-exposure before acquisition, not weakening an already established cue association. The cited meta-analysis distinguishes cue-only trials before, during, and after pairing: before and after trials were associated with reduced evaluative-conditioning magnitude, while intermixed trials during acquisition showed a different pattern. Two possible writing applications remain hypotheses: participant-side familiarization with a prospective cue, and author-side reserving a cue until its meaningful introduction. Neither application establishes durable immunity, a fixed maximum installable response, or a prescribed exposure count.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting principle for unpaired cue exposure BEFORE the relevant acquisition phase. Cue-only presentations AFTER an association has been established concern extinction or weakening and are not inherently inert. A semantically neutral carrier that is already paired with a response and reward, as in 1325's practice variant, is not the same procedure: neutral meaning does not imply consequence-free exposure. Habituation concerns change in an elicited response with repetition, while this entry concerns how prior unpaired exposure relates to later acquisition. Prior ordinary responses to a cue do not by themselves determine whether the specific association under discussion has been acquired.


**Why it works.** A review of evaluative-conditioning studies (learning to like or dislike something through pairing) found that showing a cue on its own, with nothing happening, weakens later conditioning when it comes before the pairing (latent inhibition) and weakens existing conditioning when it comes after (extinction). Exposures mixed in during the pairing are a separate case. So timing matters and should be kept clear. The evidence does not show that exposure after pairing does nothing, that early exposure guarantees a lower ceiling, or that repeating a cue a hundred times a day protects someone against its use in scripts. Ideas such as the cue being learned as irrelevant may explain the pre-exposure effect, but they are explanations, not direct evidence for these uses. Whether any protection lasts over time or carries into other settings has not been tested.


**Worked examples.**

- *Subject-side immunization: pre-spending a cue's conditionability*
  - **Setup.** A hypothetical familiarization example before a particular cue-outcome association has been introduced; no protection or conditioning ceiling is assumed.
  - **The move.** The character repeatedly encounters the same word in ordinary, unpaired contexts before it acquires a special role in the story. Treat the possible effect of that history as a question, not as an instruction promising immunity.
  - **Why it lands.** This illustrates the temporal difference between prior unpaired exposure and later pairing. The cited review supports a pre-exposure effect on evaluative-conditioning magnitude in its evidence base, but does not supply this human script scenario, a fixed daily dose, or proof that the word can never acquire a strong response. A source-grounded comparison would retain the exposure history and avoid inventing a measured flattened asymptote.
- *Operator-side sequencing constraint: never spend a cue on ambient use*
  - **Setup.** At the writing stage, an author compares a cue used incidentally in the opening with a cue first introduced at its meaningful moment.
  - **The move.** Mark the cue's first appearance and any earlier unpaired uses. If reserving it for the meaningful passage, record that as a design choice and a hypothesis about exposure history, not as a guarantee of a stronger install.
  - **Why it lands.** The author-side variant preserves the useful sequencing question: has this cue already appeared without its intended association? It does not claim that all earlier ordinary usage spends a fixed store of conditionability or that later cue-only exposure is inert. The cited review explicitly treats post-pairing CS-only trials as capable of reducing evaluative conditioning.


<a id="entry-1554"></a>

### presupposed-conditioning-fire

[#1554](#entry-1554) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: triggers*

No binding act occurs: the operator names a specific word — "automatically" — and declares it already burned into the subconscious, so the assertion itself functions as the install and installation reads as discovery. The evidence offered is the listener's own just-trained reflex: "doesn't it feel like it's burned into your subconscious already? ... Because it is," a bootstrap in which the proof of the trigger is the response the proof itself elicits. Because the alleged conditioning is dated to the past, the claim is unfalsifiable — the listener's recent felt compliance is retroactively presented as confirmation that the trigger already existed, and any current sensation counts as further proof. The result is a discrete conditioned response keyed to one word ("a trigger for you to say yes and automatically obey when you hear that word from your dominant"), converted from a generic compliance gradient without any visible act of creation.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the operator asserts a trigger ALREADY exists rather than performing any installation in view, and invites the listener to discover it as a pre-existing fact. The tell is a rhetorical question pointing at the listener's own present sensation as evidence, immediately ratified by flat operator confirmation ("Because it is") — the felt response the session just manufactured is recycled as proof of prior conditioning, leaving nothing the listener could check or refuse.


**Worked examples.**

- *self-confirming assertion-as-install bootstrap*
  - that word, automatically, doesn't it feel like it's burned into your subconscious already? / Mm-hmm. / Because it is.


**See also.** `arousal-cognition-shutdown-law` — shares the install-as-discovery grammar: the assertion is delivered as a report of wiring that already exists rather than as a suggestion.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both let a just-manufactured experience stand as the evidence for a claim delivered afterward, so the claim reads as description rather than assertion.; `self-validating-trigger-hype` — both close the disconfirmation exit so that whatever the listener feels reads back as proof the claim is true.


<a id="entry-1485"></a>

### presupposition-install

[#1485](#entry-1485) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

The target proposition is placed in a grammatically presupposed position, so that parsing the sentence for meaning forces its acceptance: a relative clause ("the chair that you will soon find yourself comfortably sitting in"), a factive complement — predicates like realize, aware, recognize presuppose their complements true ("aware that you are deeply in trance"; "Are you aware that you are sitting on my hat?") — an adverb ("Are you deeply in trance?" presupposes in trance), or a predicate that lexically entails prior occurrence ("keep on listening" presupposes the listening has been happening; keep, continue, still all backdate compliance so there is no decision point at which to refuse). Because the claim is never asserted on the surface, there is no assertion to refuse: even answering "no" to the foreground question concedes the embedded content, and challenging the surface leaves the presupposition untouched. Stacking several presuppositions compounds the difficulty of challenge. The move needs a subject who is processing the sentence for meaning rather than auditing each clause's truth, and an embedded claim they are not already actively contesting.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a claim would draw refusal if stated outright and you want it accepted as settled background instead — including framing compliance as already underway so refusal has no decision point. The tell is that the contested content never occupies the main clause: it hides inside relative clauses, factive complements, adverbs, or keep/continue/still predicates, while the foreground offers something else — a question, a timing or sub-choice — to engage with. It works identically in print and speech, needing no prosody and no second reading.


**Worked examples.**

- *compounded presuppositions leaving no surface assertion to refuse*
  - Erickson compounds the presuppositions, making it very difficult for the client to challenge the truth of the statement you are in trance


**See also.** `backdated-nonrefusable-install` — both backdate the operative event to a moment the listener cannot revisit or contest.; `indirect-command-smuggling` — both are Erickson covert-delivery grammar in which the surface form differs from the recoverable payload.; `presupposed-completion-fait-accompli` — both deliver the target as already-settled fact so no live decision point exists at which to refuse.


<a id="entry-1470"></a>

### pretend-frame-belief-decoupling

[#1470](#entry-1470) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

Performance is licensed without belief or commitment: the operator explicitly grants that imagining, considering, or pretending a behavior is not the same as doing or believing it, so the blocking assumption "consider = must do" or "respond = must believe" dissolves and the listener can simulate freely. The skeptical listener who would otherwise bail at "I'm not actually feeling hypnotized" keeps producing the observable behavior — eye-close, eye-open, playing along with the game — which is the only input the loop needs. The frame is one-directional: the operator narrates pretense becoming real ("eventually I'm wondering how the feelings will shift and change in your body"), never real becoming pretense, so the exit ramp quietly disappears while the license stands. The same valve can run with polarity flipped — "Pretend to be awake / At least pretend for me" — reusing pretense as the compliance channel in the opposite direction. The move works overtly as a stated contract or as an explicitly drawn distinction between considering a behavior and doing it; either way the prohibition it removes is self-imposed, living at the consideration gate.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the listener's resistance sits at the threshold — a skeptic or self-monitor who won't respond because responding would mean admitting it's real, or won't even consider because considering feels like commitment. The tell is an explicit permission to "just pretend" or "just consider" with no stake attached, followed by narration that steers the pretense toward the genuine state. It suits openings and re-inductions where behavioral throughput matters more than professed belief.


**Worked examples.**

- *one-way pretend license*
  - maybe at first you're just pretending and playing along with the game of being hypnotized and fractionated. But eventually I'm wondering how the feelings will shift and change in your body.


**See also.** `belief-gate-contingent-yoking` — both let sustained pretense do real operative work while belief is bracketed out of the loop.; `post-wake-self-report-reframe` — both work the 'was I really hypnotized or just playing along' interpretation of the listener's own performance.


<a id="entry-575"></a>

### procedure-well-formedness-QA

[#575](#entry-575) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft*

Before a script or procedure is used on anyone, it is tested against something stricter than the author's own satisfaction. The goal it installs should be single and tightly limited so it cannot overshoot, and the target should be something the person can actually do. If any inner part of the person objects, the install waits until that part's purpose is built into the design, so it cannot sabotage the change later. Then a trained outsider follows the written steps exactly; any mistake, added step, skipped step or question means the script is faulty. Every likely response gets a scripted reply, so it works without the author.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for procedure-well-formedness-QA when the writer's question is 'is the thing I authored correct and transferable before I run it?' — a validity test on the OPERATOR'S artifact (the install spec or the written procedure), enacting nothing on the subject. Tells: spec bounded/no-objector/dead-man test (a); third-party enactment failure counts against the text plus exhaustive-branch scripting (b).


**Risk.** Design-stage self-discipline; no move on the subject.


**Why it works.** This is error-detection by external test rather than by author introspection, and it works because authors cannot see their own gaps: the curse of knowledge means the writer silently supplies missing steps from their own model of the procedure and therefore cannot detect that the text omits them. Handing the description to a naive enactor makes each omission surface as an observable failure — a question, a wrong move, an added step — converting an unmeasurable property (completeness) into a countable one. The parallel spec tests do the same job for design: a bounded single outcome and an explicit no-objection pass make overshoot and internal conflict detectable before deployment rather than after. Falsifiable: if third-party enactment errors do not predict downstream failures when the procedure is run for real, the test lacks validity. [plausible; curse of knowledge / illusion of explanatory depth; externalised error detection]


**Worked examples.**

- *Installation gated on no internal objection*
  - "The well-formedness condition of our design is going to be that no other parts object. We are going to take all of their concerns into account and modify the new part accordingly." — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *Bound the outcome so nothing can veto it*
  - "Every extra outcome… makes it more complicated… The more limited its outcome, the easier it is to install" — Bandler & Grinder (1982), Reframing
- *The dead-man test on the target spec*
  - "if a dead man can do it, it isn't behavior. Getting blown over by strong wind is not behavior" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**Realizations** (1): `procedure-fidelity-enactment-test`


**See also.** `experiential-consent-trial` — two gates that both constrain the operator before anything is installed, at different stages: one tests whether the authored procedure is correct and transferable, the other tests whether the subject actually likes the experience and can return abort. A reader auditing a script's governance layer wants both and needs the artifact-versus-lived-trial distinction.; `operator-training-via-monitor` — the two operator-facing quality moves, and each already names the other as its nearest boundary. One tests the authored artifact before it runs, the other corrects the operator's live delivery through a stand-in or observer. Reading both is how you place any given practitioner-side move.; `preparatory-diagnostic-read` — the two operator-side families where nothing is installed on the subject, and the disambiguation is live: one tests whether the operator's own authored procedure or install spec is well-formed and transferable, the other tests or measures the subject so the operator's map updates. A move that changes no subject state belongs to one or the other.


<a id="entry-1402"></a>

### program-disclosure-reattribution

[#1402](#entry-1402) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

Walk the subject step by step through the influence program that was actually run on them — the sequence, what each step was for, and the fact that it is a general procedure that works on ordinary people rather than a filter that selected them for weakness. The cause of their compliance relocates from a personal defect to an engineered situation, and self-condemnation drops because the thing being explained is no longer a fact about their character. The move requires the program's real structure, delivered in enough detail that the subject can match specific remembered moments to specific steps; a vague 'it wasn't your fault' does not land, because the shame is anchored to concrete episodes and only a step-by-step account gives each of those episodes a non-defect explanation. Its payoff is accurate authorship returned rather than an alternative story installed.


**When to reach for this.** The named inverse of manufactured-deficit-remedy and old-self-discreditation — those install or exploit a defect-reading of the subject to sell a payload or close the return path; this dismantles a defect-reading and sells nothing, and the subject is left holding an explanation they can check against their own memories. Against obedience-motive-reattribution: identical reattribution machinery, opposite direction and beneficiary — that redirects the motive of the subject's own acts TOWARD the operator and harvests the result; this redirects causation OUTWARD onto a structure and the operator gains nothing. Against illusory-choice-authorship: that manufactures a felt authorship over a fixed path; this removes an inaccurate authorship the subject already felt. Against licensed-erasure-and-refill: that invalidates prior beliefs en masse specifically to fill the vacuum with operator content — here the invalidation is targeted at one specific self-attribution and no refill follows.


**Why it works.** Shame is generated by attributing an outcome to a stable internal trait, whereas guilt or mere regret follows from attributing it to a situation or a specific act — so shifting the attribution from disposition to situation changes the emotion rather than merely arguing with it, and predicts a shame drop without a corresponding drop in accountability for specific acts. The step-by-step delivery matters because attribution change requires a competing causal account that covers the specific evidence, not a general reassurance. Falsifiable: compare detailed procedural disclosure against a matched-length general reassurance for the same person. If shame measures moved equally under both, the mechanism is comfort and rapport rather than attribution. A second, sharper test: the account predicts NO benefit where the subject's compliance genuinely was idiosyncratic and the program had no such steps — if the intervention worked equally well when the disclosed program was fabricated, it is not operating on accurate attribution. [established; situational vs dispositional attribution; shame-guilt distinction and internal-stable attribution]


**Worked examples.**

- *Step-by-step walkthrough of the actual program, matched to remembered episodes*
  - **Setup.** Debrief, subject out of trance and holding shame about having complied; the operator knows the real sequence that was run and is prepared to name each step and its function.
  - **The move.** Here is what was actually done to you, in order. First the sessions were moved late so you were always tired — that's step one, and it's why you couldn't argue on the Thursdays. Then the small requests came before the large ones, in that order deliberately, because that ordering works on almost everyone who agrees to the first one. This is a procedure. It was not aimed at something weak in you; it would have run the same on the person sitting next to you.
  - **Why it lands.** The cause of compliance relocates from a personal defect to an engineered situation, and because the account is concrete enough to match specific remembered moments, each shamed episode gets its own non-defect explanation rather than a blanket reassurance. Observable: the subject starts supplying episodes back — "so that's why the Thursdays" — and the self-condemnation drops as the recall becomes checkable rather than accepted on the operator's word.


<a id="entry-1564"></a>

### progressive-muscle-relaxation

[#1564](#entry-1564) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: pacing-rapport · kind: recipe*

Tense each region, hold, then release, and point out the relaxation that follows each release; that contrast is what makes it easy to feel. You can finish with a bigger tension-release cycle. It is well studied as a relaxation method; whether it adds anything as a trance induction is untested.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 4 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Work from feet to face: tense each muscle group, hold, then release and notice the relaxation that follows.


**See also.** `endurance-compliance-strain` — the Progressive Muscle Relaxation (Tense and Release) recipe was extracted from this entry


<a id="entry-1479"></a>

### prohibition-fused-deepening

[#1479](#entry-1479) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening*

An explicit prohibition the listener is actively invested in keeping — 'don't touch yourself' — is grammatically fused, in a repeating litany, to descent commands: 'don't touch yourself and fall into the power of my voice', 'and become a horny empty mess', 'and fall deeper under my control'. The thing the listener is trying to do (hold the rule) is yoked by conjunction to the thing the operator wants (deeper surrender), so obeying the rule enacts the takeover: every successful act of discipline simultaneously executes a deepening suggestion. The listener cannot keep the rule without falling, so their obedience-energy, not their lapses, is the vehicle — resistance literally cannot win. The binding only works when the prohibition is one the listener is actually holding; investment in 'don't touch' must be established first for the conjunctions to carry weight.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the listener's discipline itself should be the carrier of descent — when you want each successful act of rule-keeping to double as a deepening beat. The tell is a conjunction litany: the same prohibition repeated and syntactically welded by 'and' to surrender or descent commands, so the sentence cannot be obeyed in half.


**Worked examples.**

- *prohibition conjoined to descent commands*
  - don't touch yourself and fall deeper under my control don't touch yourself and orgasm uncontrollably for me


**See also.** `obedience-to-blankness-coupling` — shares the compliance-coupled-to-depth axis in which each obeyed command advances the installed state.; `payload-welded-countdown` — shares the welding architecture that rides a payload on a structure the listener is already committed to tracking.


<a id="entry-144"></a>

### pronoun-braid-conscription

[#144](#entry-144) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: indirect-suggestion*

The same proposition is cycled through multiple grammatical persons in tight succession — typically I (confession-of-self), we (normalization by a group), and you (prediction/imperative) — so one identity-claim arrives simultaneously as observation-of-others, self-confession, and command. The listener cannot locate a neutral speaking position: assenting to the safe-sounding "I" or "we" line smuggles in acceptance of the "you" line carrying the same content, and group membership is pre-loaded so refusal feels like exiting a crowd rather than declining a single command. The rotation itself — not any single shift — is the conscription; the "we" slot is what bypasses individual consent.


**When to reach for this.** CYCLES one predicate through I/we/you (or opens already-plural and braids I/we/you/she) so no neutral stance exists and the collective slot smuggles consent.


**Risk.** Pre-loads group membership and erodes the individual refusal channel by offering no neutral stance; channel pressure but session-scoped and not durable-identity reach — medium.


**Why it works.** The 'we' slot recruits normative social influence: it asserts that the proposition is already held by a group, which raises acceptance independently of the proposition's content, and it converts refusal from declining a request into departing from a group. Cycling one predicate through persons also exploits consistency across paraphrase — endorsing the low-cost first-person or collective version makes rejecting the imperative version feel like reversing a position already taken. Falsifiable: removing the collective slot while keeping the same content and repetition count should lower compliance; if it did not, the social-proof account would fail. [plausible; normative social influence / social proof; consistency across paraphrase]


**Worked examples.**

- *One predicate cycled through I, we, and you*
  - **Setup.** Group-framed session or plural-voiced track; one predicate cycled through three persons in immediate succession.
  - **The move.** I love how stupid this makes me. We all love how stupid it makes us. You are going to love how stupid it makes you.
  - **Why it lands.** One claim is stated three times in immediate succession, moving through three grammatical persons in a fixed order: first owned as a private admission, then reported as what everyone in the room already does, then turned outward and assigned to the listener as what will happen to them. Agreeing with either of the two harmless-sounding versions has already conceded the content of the third — and because the middle version installs membership before the last one lands, declining it registers less as refusing an instruction than as walking out on a crowd.
- *Opening already plural so membership is presupposed*
  - **Setup.** Opening words of the session, already plural; the subject is treated as having arrived rather than invited.
  - **The move.** Oh, good — we're all here now, and she fits perfectly; the circle doesn't close without her. I remember my first time in it. We all remember. You'll feel it any second, the way we did.
  - **Why it lands.** The first words are plural and treat the listener as having already arrived: how glad everyone is, how well she fits, how the shape is complete now she is in it. No one is asked to join. From there the persons interleave mid-thought — a private confession, a shared experience, an address — until it is no longer possible to say who is speaking about whom, so objecting would mean disputing not an instruction but a description of oneself.


**See also.** `covert-referent-migration` — both move the listener's grammatical seat without a defensible checkpoint. One rotates person openly so no neutral stance exists; the other holds the surface form fixed and migrates the referent unannounced. The overt-rotation versus covert-swap contrast is the working discriminator.; `pronoun-migration-identity-install` — both install via grammatical-person topology rather than direct assertion, and the surfaces overlap heavily. The separating question is whether one predicate is cycled through several persons so no neutral stance remains, or whether the referent of a third-person category quietly drifts onto the listener.; `self-recited-first-person-mantra` — both hand the listener grammatical work to perform, and the second explicitly names the first-person-only case as its neighbor. Reader adjudicating a recited line needs to check whether the person is rotating through I/we/you (conscription) or held fixed at first person (self-recitation), so the cross-reference does real disambiguation work.; `self-voiced-avowal` — both move an identity claim into the listener's own grammatical position, and the discriminators need each other to hold the line: one cycles a single predicate through multiple persons so no neutral stance exists, the other hands the claim to the listener as speaker so there is no external author to reject. Adjacent, not identical.; `subject-voiced-self-mantra` — both use first-person; braid rotates persons, mantra does not.; `third-person-proxy-normalization` — same family of person-shift laundering, read together for the parameter: one pivots to detached third person so a claim is observed rather than evaluated, the other cycles a single proposition through several persons so no neutral stance remains. Single pivot versus rotation.; `third-person-surrogate-frame` — both operate on grammatical person as the vehicle, and they are near-complements: one cycles a single proposition through first, plural, and second person so no neutral stance exists; the other removes the second-person addressee entirely so resistance has no target. A reader tagging a pronoun-manipulation passage will need to check which direction the person-work runs, so the pointer earns its place.; `uninvited-pronoun-migration-enrollment` — both exploit grammatical person to remove a neutral stance, but one CYCLES a single predicate through several persons so assent to a safe slot smuggles the loaded slot, while the other runs a one-way gradient whose load-bearing move is the refusal to invite. Related enough to cross-reference, different enough that the topologies should not be merged.


<a id="entry-953"></a>

### prosodic-pacing-rail

[#953](#entry-953) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: carrier-binding · kind: container*

Deliver the whole script in a steady, predictable form so the rhythm itself carries the suggestions. The listener's ear locks onto the pattern, so they weigh each line less, key words slip by as part of the rhyme, and any break in the pattern reads as emphasis without a raised voice. Variations: regular rhymed couplets throughout; lean on the small satisfaction of each rhyme landing as expected, sometimes opened with a nursery-rhyme cadence to invite a childlike state; stress only a few chosen action or identity words (in capitals on the page, by voice when read) and never stress anything else, so those words always carry the same weight.


**When to reach for this.** Cited to the cumulative whole-form property (remove any single couplet or any single capitalized instance and the rail/discipline survives; remove the form and the script is gutted), never to one line. The tell is that the form is load-bearing and disciplined — including the prediction-reward angle, where continuous predictive success is used as a criticality-suppressant carrier wave.


**Risk.** Delivery-form craft; lowers per-line evaluation bandwidth but installs no durable scope and erodes no refusal channel on its own.


**Why it works.** Regular meter and rhyme make upcoming words predictable, and processing fluency — the ease with which material is processed — is systematically misread as truth, familiarity, and liking; the rhyme-as-reason effect shows that rhyming statements are judged more accurate than non-rhyming paraphrases of identical content. A stable prosodic baseline additionally makes any departure from it perceptually salient, so emphasis can be delivered by deviation rather than by volume, and the restriction of emphasis to a fixed small set keeps each anchor's cue constant across repetitions, which is what conditioning requires. Falsifiable — if the same content in unmetered prose produced equal acceptance and equal anchor strength, the form would not be load-bearing. [established; processing fluency and the rhyme-as-reason effect; predictive processing]


**Worked examples.**

- *Whole script in couplets as a pacing rail*
  - **Setup.** Any point in a file written end to end in ten-syllable rhymed couplets; the trigger word arrives in rhyme position like every other word.
  - **The move.** The counting goes from ten and slips to nine, / and every number softens down the spine; / at eight the shoulders let the holding go, / at seven all the thinking runs too slow; / and slower still, and lower than before, / until the word you answer to is more.
  - **Why it lands.** Every line of the file is roughly ten syllables and rhymes with its neighbour, start to finish, with no prose passages anywhere. Within a minute the listener's ear has locked onto the beat and is running ahead of the words, which costs them most of the attention they would otherwise spend weighing any individual line. Two consequences follow. The operator never has to raise her voice for emphasis — a broken beat does it for her. And the trigger word, when it arrives, arrives at the end of a line, completing the rhyme like every other word has, which is how something that would stand out in speech slides past unexamined here. Cut any four lines and the rail is unaffected; take away the verse and there is no file.
- *Rhyme's predictive payoff as the carrier wave*
  - **Setup.** Opening lines of a rhymed file; the nursery cadence is set immediately and the suggestion is placed in the first line of a couplet so the rhyme confirms it.
  - **The move.** Softly, softly, little one, / thinking's over, thinking's done; / every rhyme you hear me say / takes another thought away.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening line borrows the cadence of a nursery rhyme every reader learned before they learned to read critically, and the couplets never let go of it. Every second line pays off a prediction the first line set up — a small, reliable satisfaction arriving every few seconds, which keeps attention pointed forward at the coming rhyme rather than down at the sentence in hand. The suggestion is put in the rhyming word's line, so it is already received by the time the chime lands and confirms it.
- *Emphasis reserved for three fixed-load words*
  - **Setup.** Written-script guidance for a performer; capitals are reserved across the whole script for exactly three words or phrases and appear nowhere else, not on relax, sleep, or deeper.
  - **The move.** Let the shoulders relax, let the breath get slow, and SINK. Nothing to hold. You hear my voice and you OBEY, that's all it is now. Deeper, softer, easy — and when I say GOOD GIRL you drop the rest of the way.
  - **Why it lands.** Capitals appear in the script only on three specific words: the verb for going down, the verb for obeying, and the trigger phrase. They appear nowhere else, not even on the usual candidates like relax, sleep or deeper. Because emphasis is rationed to those three, each one carries the same weight every time it comes up, and a performer reading aloud cannot accidentally weaken a trigger by hitting some neighbouring word harder. Which words get the emphasis is telling in itself: words of action and identity, not words of state.


**See also.** `breath-pacing-entrainment` — both make verse form load-bearing, and they overlap on the same text-only surface: one uses metre and rhyme to suppress per-line scrutiny, the other uses it as a tempo substrate that imports genuine settling. The overlap is close enough that a reader will need the distinction.; `delivery-form-as-induction-envelope` — both make the whole-file linguistic surface the carrier rather than any line, and the surface features overlap enough to be confusable; the split is removal of exit ramps versus predictive-reward pacing and disciplined emphasis. Link, do not merge.; `proprioceptive-gait-metronome` — both are whole-form carriers rather than passage-local moves, sustaining the state without requiring per-line attention. The useful contrast is where the rhythm lives: the listener's own body motion in one, the engineered prosody of the delivery in the other, which is exactly the operator-independence question a reader is deciding.; `repeating-frame-carrier` — both make the delivery form itself do work content cannot, by setting a predictable pattern the listener's prediction system locks onto and then riding material in under it. Worth reading together to see the split: a repeating frame whose fixed slot camouflages rotating novel payloads, versus a continuous prosodic or typographic rail that manages emphasis and lowers per-line scrutiny throughout.; `song-architecture-delivery-vehicle` — both make the artifact's form, not its content, do the delivery work, and both are cited to the whole piece rather than any line. One substitutes a cyclical musical architecture for the linear arc; the other binds meter, rhyme-prediction, and emphasis discipline as a continuous carrier. Useful as the two scales of form-as-vehicle.


<a id="entry-1363"></a>

### protective-drive-moralized-as-fault

[#1363](#entry-1363) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: framing*

A pre-existing protective or attachment drive — a parent's pull toward a child, loyalty to a partner, the reflex to shield someone — is recoded as a moral failing: attachment is possessiveness, protectiveness is lack of faith, the ordinary impulse is named as the sin. The subject then generates guilt at exactly the moments they behave normally, and the drive begins suppressing itself without further operator input, because every expression of it now arrives pre-labeled as evidence of the fault. This disables a defense from the inside rather than arguing against it: the operator never has to prohibit the behavior, only to supply the label the subject applies to their own impulse.


**When to reach for this.** Direction of the valence move plus ownership of the target is the tell: a drive the subject ALREADY HELD with positive or neutral standing (protectiveness, loyalty, a parent's pull toward a child) is given a negative moral label it did not have, so its every ordinary expression now arrives pre-tagged as evidence of a fault and the subject suppresses it unprompted. Against 312 self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop — the nearest neighbour, and the one this most needs separating from — that also installs a self-firing aversive detector that runs in the operator's absence, but it fires on deviation from a standard the operator FIRST BUILT (it presupposes an installed identity-reward there is a shortfall from), and its function is to enforce compliance with that standard; here nothing was installed to fall short of, the target pre-dates the operator, and the function is to disable a defense rather than to enforce a standard. Against 1106 cost-to-virtue-valence-flip and 1153 failure-state-inversion: both run negative -> positive on an item already carrying shame; this is the reverse vector on an item carrying none. Against 118 manufactured-deficit-remedy: that fabricates a deficit and sells the payload as its cure; here no cure is offered and no behavior is prohibited — only the label is supplied, and the suppression is the subject's own work.


**Why it works.** A drive that is under moral surveillance is regulated by the person holding it, so labeling it converts an external prohibition into self-enforcement — which is why the suppression continues in the operator's absence and why it targets frequency of expression rather than the drive's strength. Falsifiable: the account predicts guilt reports rise specifically at moments of ordinary expression, not diffusely, and that the underlying drive persists while its expression drops. If measurement shows the drive itself weakening in parallel — or shows guilt distributed evenly rather than time-locked to expressions — the self-suppression story is wrong. It is also falsified if removing the label restores expression only slowly or not at all, since a label-driven mechanism should be more reversible than an extinguished drive.


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-existing protective drive relabelled as the fault itself*
  - **Setup.** Out of session or in conversation, addressing a drive the subject already held with positive standing — here, the reflex to check on and shield a family member — with nothing yet installed for them to fall short of.
  - **The move.** That pull you feel to call and check she's alright — sit with what it actually is. It isn't care. It's you needing to be needed. Every time you reach for the phone, that's the wanting-to-own showing itself, and you'll feel it again in about an hour.
  - **Why it lands.** No behaviour is prohibited and no remedy is offered — only the label — so the drive begins suppressing itself the moment it next arises, because every ordinary expression now arrives pre-tagged as evidence of a fault the subject supplies themselves. The operator observes guilt appearing at exactly the moments of normal behaviour, and the checking rate declining with no further input.


<a id="entry-1534"></a>

### pseudo-syllogistic-necessity

[#1534](#entry-1534) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

A directive is delivered in the surface grammar of valid inference so the listener experiences the conclusion as reasoned-to rather than imposed. The operator builds sentences of the form "X cause Y" where X is ongoing, verifiable behavior and Y the desired response — "Sitting all the way down in that chair will make you go into a deep trance" — even though there is "not, in fact, [a] necessary connection"; because the listener habitually models life in single-cause terms, resisting Y would mean denying X, so the response leaves the domain of choice. The same move runs as chained pseudo-syllogism, where "logically," "therefore," and "clearly" do the heavy lifting over invalid steps (thinking about being hypnotized gets you "at least twice as hot, and therefore twice as deeply"); as face-valid-but-empty bridging that licenses a refused behavior ("There's no actual logic to that statement, but it sounds meaningful, and will get your client to do it"); and as a physical-constraint metaphor mapped onto the will ("The train can only go in one direction... you can only go in one direction too"), so not-following feels like trying to derail a train. The terminal form forecloses deliberation entirely: obedience is "the only rational choice" and simultaneously "beyond the rational," covering analytic and intuitive resistance in one stroke. Either the listener accepts the chain and self-confirms the conclusion, or gets bogged down evaluating the surface logic — both branches advance the response.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the writer wants a command to arrive wearing the costume of a conclusion — the listener should feel they were argued into the state, not ordered into it. The tell is inference vocabulary (since, therefore, logically, clearly, because, make, only) yoking something currently true or already accepted to the desired response, where deleting the connective leaves no actual entailment behind. A second tell is constraint language borrowed from physics or definition ("can only go in one direction," "no other rational choice") applied to the listener's volition.


**Worked examples.**

- *Connectives ("logically... therefore... clearly") asserting an entailment that does no work*
  - thinking about being hypnotized, / thinking about being hypnotized, not hypnotized, logically, get you at least twice as hot, / and therefore twice as deeply, and transforming, clearly, you can feel that.


**See also.** `closed-logic-and-inevitability` — both manufacture acceptance from the shape of an argument or an unearned necessity rather than from evidence.; `no-exit-state-braid` — both make resistance cost too much by linkage — denying the target means denying something already granted or already moving.; `parallel-isomorph-bind-defusion` — both let a borrowed logical structure carry the conclusion so the listener experiences it as reasoned-to rather than told.


<a id="entry-1354"></a>

### punisher-onset-sign-inversion

[#1354](#entry-1354) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning · kind: principle*

A reported onset transient can differ from the later direction of a response-rate trend. In Skinner's animal experiment, four rats were undergoing extinction after periodic food reinforcement. The response-contingent slapper was first connected twenty minutes into the third day's observation period. Its introduction was followed by a quick second response and two or three minutes of relatively rapid responding, then substantial suppression. The useful assessment distinction is between the early transient and the later trajectory under the reported arrangement. The twenty-minute mark describes when the apparatus was introduced; it is not a prescribed observation floor or a reason to continue an aversive procedure despite concern. The account does not establish that every apparent sign reversal resolves by itself or provide a human intervention protocol.


**When to reach for this.** Use this supporting assessment when reading the time course immediately around the introduction of a response-contingent aversive event, separating a reported early burst from a sustained trend. Contingency-sign verification (1186) concerns whether an intended reducing procedure is functioning as reinforcement and needs reassessment; this observation adds temporal context rather than overriding that check. An extinction burst follows removal of a maintaining reinforcer, whereas the transient isolated here follows introduction of the aversive event, although Skinner's reported arrangement was itself occurring during extinction. Commanded massed responding is different again: the early repeat here was observed, not instructed. No universal waiting period follows from these distinctions.


**Why it works.** Laboratory reports on rats describe a quick repeat of the punished behaviour and a short burst of rapid responding before it settles down, and quick second responses also appear in early shock experiments. Why the burst happens is not known, and there is no evidence that it always resolves by itself. One possible explanation is a spike of arousal before suppression is learned, but that has not been demonstrated, and neither has the idea that the burst is absent when the unpleasant stimulus is not tied to the behaviour. The safe takeaway is the observation and its timing: an early worsening can happen. It does not justify a fixed waiting period for people, or a rule to ignore early bad reactions.


**Worked examples.**

- *Minimum observation window stated before onset of the aversive*
  - **Setup.** A reviewer is interpreting the timeline of Skinner's reported rat experiment, distinguishing the baseline observation period, introduction of the apparatus, and subsequent response pattern.
  - **The move.** Mark twenty minutes as the point when the apparatus was connected. Mark the initial quick repeat and the following two-to-three-minute burst separately from the later suppression. Do not turn the pre-intervention interval into a minimum time to continue the procedure.
  - **Why it lands.** The timeline separates an onset transient from the later trend in the reported animal experiment. It preserves what the observation can contribute to assessment without claiming that all early increases resolve, inventing a mandatory twenty-minute observation floor, or prescribing an aversive human procedure. Contingency-sign verification remains a separate empirical judgment; this example is about reading the record accurately.


<a id="entry-1355"></a>

### punishment-recoverability-discriminator

[#1355](#entry-1355) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · bounded · family: conditioning*

A brief penalty holds a behavior down only while it keeps being applied. Stop it and the behavior comes back, with no new reward or retraining needed. The habit was never erased, only held back, so punishment buys an ongoing obligation, not a lasting change, and the fact that it works while running says nothing about what remains afterward. Checking whether the behavior returns once the penalty stops is how you tell real change from mere suppression.


**When to reach for this.** vs reinforcement-extinction (432): the load-bearing contrast and the closest miss — 432 already carries spontaneous recovery/resurgence, but those occur WHILE the contingency remains broken and the behavior is genuinely decaying toward baseline. Here the strength was never decayed: withdrawing the aversive restores approximately the pre-punishment rate with no reinforcement in between, because punishment gated expression rather than removing history. That withdrawal-test is the discriminating observation between the two procedures and neither entry currently carries it. vs negative-punishment-timeout (876), removal-from-reinforcement-timeout (1110), response-cost-token-economy (1057): all three define themselves by suppressive effect on future frequency and are silent on post-discontinuation recovery. vs massed-practice-rate-suppression (1076): a satiation/response-cost route with no recoverability claim. The tell: spontaneous re-emergence on withdrawal, no reinforcement delivered, rate returns near pre-punishment level.


**Why it works.** Suppressing a behaviour and unlearning it are different things. A procedure can lower how often a behaviour appears by acting on its expression without changing the history that made it strong; remove the procedure and the suppression goes with it, leaving everything else as it was. This can be tested: if the behaviour does not come back after punishment stops, staying low with no reward delivered, then punishment really did weaken it and this account is wrong. A sharper prediction: the behaviour should return to roughly its pre-punishment level rather than a partly weakened one. A partial return would mean punishment also wears down the behaviour's strength, and the simple picture of punishment as only holding the behaviour down is too simple.


**Worked examples.**

- *Withdrawal test on a suppressed hand-to-mouth habit*
  - **Setup.** Late in a session after several days in which every instance of the subject touching their lips has been met with a sharp corrective word; the operator now runs the diagnostic to find out whether anything was actually learned.
  - **The move.** For the next twenty minutes I am not going to correct you at all. Not once, no matter what your hands do. Sit exactly as you are, keep your hands loose in your lap, and let them go wherever they want to go — I'm going to sit here and count, and neither of us is going to say a word about it.
  - **Why it lands.** Removing the aversive with no reinforcement supplied in between isolates the one question that matters: whether the strength was decayed or merely gated. If the hand goes back to the mouth within the first few minutes and settles at roughly its pre-correction frequency, nothing was extinguished — the operator has bought a maintenance obligation, and the observable is that rate, not the clean twenty minutes that preceded it.


<a id="entry-1359"></a>

### ratio-cost-collapse-threshold

[#1359](#entry-1359) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: conditioning*

Ask for too much effort per reward and the behavior stops, even though the reward is still paid every time the requirement is met. Nothing is taken away; the task just is not worth doing anymore. It can happen by raising the demand, or by letting the reward lose its appeal while the demand stays put. The result is someone who stops working beside a reward they still want and could still get.


**When to reach for this.** Names the requirement/return boundary past which an intact, honoured contingency stops maintaining behaviour. vs reinforcement-extinction (432): extinction stops the payout; here every completed ratio pays exactly as promised. vs response-cost-token-economy (1057): its upper-bound facet is reserve DEPLETION (nothing left to fine); here nothing is held and nothing is debited — the cost is paid in effort. vs motivating-operation-engineering (429): that moves the consequence's momentary value with the requirement fixed; this is the same exchange rate approached from the requirement side, and 429 is the correct entry when the operator devalues rather than raises the price. Deciding tell: the subject stops working beside a reward it still wants and could still obtain, and responding resumes promptly when the ratio drops back — a slow or absent recovery means extinction, not ratio strain. Sibling schedule-shaped-output-contour describes the pattern while the behaviour lives; this is the boundary past which there is no pattern.


**Why it works.** Whether a behaviour keeps going depends on the return per unit of effort, not just on whether a reward arrives. A deal can be honoured perfectly and still fail once the effort costs more than the reward is worth (ratio strain; the breaking point on ratio schedules). Because the collapse is about the exchange rate, you can cause it from either side, by raising the demand or cheapening the reward, and you reverse it by restoring the ratio. Testable: after a collapse, drop the demand back below the threshold with the same reward; if responding does not recover promptly, something lasting was damaged and this is closer to extinction. Or keep the demand and raise the reward; if responding does not resume, the collapse was not about relative return. A caution: someone stopping beside an available reward can also mean they are satiated, or that the task has become linked with something unpleasant, and those need different fixes.


**Worked examples.**

- *Requirement raised past the effort/return boundary with the payoff honoured*
  - **Setup.** A subject has been reliably earning a specific reward by repeating a phrase; the operator now walks the requirement up while paying out every single time it is met.
  - **The move.** Twenty repetitions earns it. Good — that's yours. Now it's sixty. Good. Now it's two hundred, and yes, you will get it at two hundred, exactly as before, every time, I'm not going to stop paying.
  - **Why it lands.** The contingency stays intact and honoured, so nothing is being extinguished — the behaviour dies purely because a run no longer repays the effort it costs. The tell the operator watches for is a subject who stalls beside a reward they visibly still want and could still obtain, and who resumes promptly when the requirement is dropped back to twenty; a slow or absent recovery would mean extinction instead.


<a id="entry-14"></a>

### reader-assent-architecture

[#14](#entry-14) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: reader-craft · kind: container*

Write a teaching text so its method feels obviously right by the time it is stated: shape the reader's attitude before the claim arrives. Variations: treat resistance as a sensible signal, so 'satisfy every objecting part' feels inevitable; let the subject 'find' each control, then have the operator adopt it as method; offer a crude fixed-step model, then drop it for a better one; present the system's removal as its goal, so every piece reads as temporary scaffolding; claim every direction the listener might push as a tool; frame every self-check, memory included, so either answer confirms the method; openly name the manipulation so noticing it feels like joining in.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this entry when a whole chapter or file is engineered so that its method reads as already-agreed by the time it is stated, or so the listener's reachable responses and self-monitoring are closed off as a standing property — the target is the reader-as-operator-in-training or the whole-file assent/resistance surface. The observable tells are priming that arrives before the claim (a naive fixed-step model offered and then placed on extinction, the subject 'discovering' each control parameter which the operator then ratifies as method, a system's own removal front-loaded as its design goal, the manipulation named aloud so that noticing it becomes participation) and distribution: the architecture survives removal of any single block, because no one passage carries it. Where refusal is involved, the tell is foreclosure — the refusal channel is never opened — rather than any handling of a refusal that occurs.


**Risk.** The reader-directed literature members carry no consent surface (target is a reader of a book, low risk on their own), but the whole-file listener-facing members (one forecloses every resistance vector; another dismantles every self-monitoring yardstick including memory) erode the refusal/verification channel as a standing property, which is the high-risk criterion; entry risk set to the erosive members.


**Why it works.** Establishing the reader's stance before the claim arrives means the claim is evaluated by an already-committed reader, and committed readers process confirming material with less scrutiny than disconfirming material. Falsifiable: present the same method claim to readers with and without the priming material; if stated agreement and counter-argument generation are unchanged, the priming is inert. (Drop the 'pre-claiming every push-direction leaves no position from which to object' clause — as phrased it reabsorbs any observed disagreement as further evidence of itself, and the stated test does not probe it.) [established; motivated reasoning / disconfirmation bias; inoculation and pre-emption of counterarguments]


**Worked examples.**

- *Offer the naive model, then place it on extinction*
  - "These levels were arbitrarily provided as a pedagogical illustration… Shaping… is absolutely not a step-wise, fixed-gradient process." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *Naming the manipulation makes noticing it participation*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, delivered in the register of a shared joke, immediately after a suggestion has visibly landed.
