  - **The move.** You do realise the whole thing is engineered, don't you — every pause, every time I drop my voice like that. This bit is training you too, by the way. And look how little it took. Look how much you enjoyed noticing.
  - **Why it lands.** Every few minutes the operator turns and names her own machinery, in the register of a shared joke: she points out that the whole setup is engineered, that this doubles as training, that she could go on doing it indefinitely. Then she attaches the pleasure to the noticing — see how little it took, and how much you enjoyed it. A listener who spots the machinery has nowhere to take the objection, because spotting it has already been priced in as part of the fun. The last available defence, embarrassment at how well it is working, is the one being disarmed.
- *The system taught as designed for its own removal*
  - "From the beginning, a systematic aim of the token economy should be to withdraw the program" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `case-then-formalize` — shares the stance-priming axis: the reader's acceptance of a method is arranged before the method is stated, as in its follow-and-formalize instance.; `consent-topology-arc` — both are whole-artifact topologies about where agreement is captured rather than any one passage, and both explicitly disclaim single-line citation. They differ in target — one reshapes the listener's consent surface across the arc, the other primes the reader's stance toward a method or closes the resistance surface as a standing property. Adjacent enough that the boundary needs to be visible from either side.; `design-space-pedagogy` — both are reader-directed whole-artifact architectures with no in-session listener target, and they sit adjacent enough that one explicitly holds itself separate from the other on the dial-space tell. Keep the pointer so the assent-manufacture versus selection-space distinction stays visible. Not a merge — teaching a parameterized choice space is not foreclosing a refusal vector.; `manufactured-self-confirmation` — both self-sealing-flavored; boundary is target (listener body vs reader belief) and polarity; `reader-assent-engineering` — one face of the broader entry is the same reader-directed stance-priming the narrower entry covers, which is why they read as near-duplicates. They stay separate because the broader entry has a second face aimed at the listener - closing the reachable-response and self-monitoring set as a standing property - which the narrower entry explicitly excludes, and which carries materially higher risk metadata. Merging would soften that. A prior adjudication reached the same conclusion.; `self-sealing-frame` — both are whole-artifact closure architectures and the pair is a known confusion: leaving no refusal channel open versus leaving no disconfirming branch available. The first entry's discriminator already devotes a clause to separating them, which is the case for linking rather than against it.; `unattributable-cause-severing` — both are non-executable whole-artifact design observations from the same instructional material, and the pair is defined by contrast: A targets the reader's belief that a method is already correct, B targets the subject by severing every outcome from a locatable operator cause. Since they are explicitly framed as siblings, keeping the pointer prevents either from absorbing the other.; `validation-by-demonstration-arc` — both are reader-directed whole-text architectures that manufacture assent before the claim lands, and the narrower one is already positioned as a deliberate split from the general container on a specific tell: earning acceptance of a claim the reader would refuse if stated cold, via staged corroboration. Keep the authored separation; link so the split is visible from both sides rather than collapsing it.; `whole-script-arc-shape-architecture` — both are whole-artifact containers rather than single moves, and both are easy to reach for wrongly. Cross-reference so the reader can pick correctly: one targets the reader's or listener's assent and response surface as a standing property, the other collects observations about a script's arc, energy contour, and topology. Confusable by scope, not by lever.


<a id="entry-807"></a>

### reading-act-as-induction-substrate

[#807](#entry-807) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: carrier-binding*

In a natively written / on-screen medium, the involuntary act of reading itself is weaponized as the induction. The text reflexively narrates the reader's own eye-movement and line-scanning as it happens ('each line that moves through your field of vision', 'come closer to the screen'), makes words 'grow in size' while peripheral vision fades so the text becomes 'all that you see', and pre-binds resistance so noticing the trance produces more trance. Because continuing to read IS the compliance, there is no discrete task to refuse and no falsifiable failure point; the reader's normal scanning behavior is redefined as the trance behavior, capturing a tunnel of attention with no external induction equipment (voice, music, breath).


**When to reach for this.** Carrier-medium-bound, not a listener-internal magnitude move.


**Risk.** Session-scoped, reversible reading-attention capture with no consent surface or out-of-session reach.


**Why it works.** Reading is an overlearned, largely involuntary process — literate adults cannot look at a word and not read it — so the compliance behavior is already running before any decision to comply is available. Narrating the reader's ongoing eye movement also exploits the fact that self-descriptive statements about processes currently occurring are trivially verifiable, which builds the acceptance set cheaply. Falsifiable: the effect should not survive translation to audio, and readers instructed to scan without comprehending should show weaker absorption. [plausible; automaticity of reading (Stroop-type obligatory processing); truism-based acceptance sets]


**Worked examples.**

- *The text narrates the reader's own eye-movement*
  - **Setup.** Opening lines of a written, on-screen piece; the reader has just started scanning.
  - **The move.** You are reading this. Each word pulls your eye into the next one, and the line you just finished has already slid up out of the way to make room for this one. Notice your head coming forward a little, closer to the screen, without you deciding to do it. You aren't doing anything unusual — you're only reading, exactly as you always read — and that is why this is already working.
  - **Why it lands.** There is no voice and no relaxation request; the induction is the page. The lines describe, in the present tense, exactly what the reader is doing while they do it — the pull of one word into the next, each line sliding upward through the field of vision, the small lean toward the screen — so ordinary reading behavior is returned to the reader as evidence that something is already working. Because there is no task other than continuing, there is nothing to perform badly and nothing to decline; stopping is the only form non-compliance could take, and stopping is what a reader is least inclined to do mid-sentence.
- *Words grow, periphery fades, resistance deepens*
  - **Setup.** Several stanzas into a rhymed on-screen piece read silently; the reader has not looked away.
  - **The move.** The letters are growing larger now — you can see it happening, line by line, they swell — while the edges of the screen and the room behind it go grey and quiet and stop mattering. Soon there is only the word you are on. And should you push back, should you tell yourself you're not affected at all, the pushing is a hand on your back: the more you resist, the more you sink into what you read next.
  - **Why it lands.** Written in rhyme to be read silently off a screen, the piece asserts its own optics as the reader goes: the letters are getting larger, everything at the edge of vision is dimming, the page is becoming the whole of what there is to see. Resistance is claimed in advance — trying to push back is described as one more thing that pulls the reader in — so noticing the effect counts as the effect. Read aloud by someone else, or printed, none of it works.


**See also.** `attention-as-evidence-loop` — the reading-act technique instantiates the continued-attention evidence loop inside a written medium, where scanning the page is itself the accumulating proof. Distinct because its defining property is medium-binding, but readers will land between the two.; `delivery-form-as-induction-envelope` — genuine near-neighbors: both make the delivery surface itself the induction rather than any discrete block. The boundary a reader needs is that one binds the script's own linguistic form (punctuation, cadence, unbroken syntax) and would survive being read aloud, while the other is bound to the on-screen medium and narrates the reader's own scanning, so it cannot transfer to audio without rewriting.; `fixation-covert-or-undeliverable-onset` — both remove the recognize-and-refuse juncture at induction: one delivers fixation without any recognized focus command, the other makes the involuntary act of reading the compliance so there is no discrete task to decline. The second explicitly recruits and exceeds ordinary fixation, so the link is a real containment relationship rather than a coincidence.; `proprioceptive-gait-metronome` — genuine structural siblings: both recruit an act the listener is already performing involuntarily (scanning lines of text; walking cadence) as the carrier that induces or sustains the state, so no discrete task exists to refuse and no operator presence is needed. They differ in which carrier and whether the medium is written or portable-somatic, which is exactly the choice a reader of either is making.; `voice-as-physics-vehicle` — same channel-physics axis: the delivery medium's own literal mechanics are narrated as the induction mechanism.


<a id="entry-1535"></a>

### reality-claim-exit-closure

[#1535](#entry-1535) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

Close off the 'it's only imagination' escape by insisting, with things they can actually feel or see, that it is real. One way is to disown a feeling that is genuinely there: the special feeling about you 'was there the whole time' and only surfaced once old thoughts fell away, so it feels self-discovered and there seems no other explanation for it. Another is to say imagined images become real through hypnosis, so real trance sensations count as proof the imagery works; each confirmation strengthens the next, and later suggestions are harder to dismiss as just a story. A third doses obvious impossibilities, such as boxes that hold ever bigger boxes, until the person stops checking them, which prepares them to accept bigger impossibilities later. All forms need an immersive experience already producing real feeling; otherwise there is nothing to point to.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script must survive the listener's own later reality-testing — when the payload would otherwise be dismissible on waking as fiction or operator trickery. The tell is the operator explicitly addressing whether the experience is real, imagined, or suggested, and settling the question by pointing at something genuinely present: an actual felt attraction, an actual sensation, or an image the listener has already accepted despite its impossibility.


**Worked examples.**

- *Pre-existing affect disclaimed as suggestion and recoded as independent evidence*
  - [Example field withheld: private source overlap.]


**See also.** `imagined-is-real-licensing-rule` — both trade on the imagined-becomes-real premise as the load-bearing epistemic move of the session.; `intrinsic-self-reframe` — both recode operator-installed content as something pre-existing that the listener merely discovers.; `own-desire-attribution` — both narrate the operative feeling as already the listener's own, so the disavowal exit has nothing to push against.


<a id="entry-1406"></a>

### recency-gated-discrimination-potency

[#1406](#entry-1406) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: triggers · kind: principle*

A distinction the person has only just learned to make gives a strong boost; the same distinction, once practised into habit, gives none. Teaching a finer distinction on the same theme brings the boost back. So the useful moment is the learning itself, not the learned result: to keep the effect going, the operator keeps introducing finer and finer distinctions rather than rehearsing ones already settled.


**When to reach for this.** Potency is carried by the ACQUISITION TRANSITION of a discrimination, not by the settled discriminated state — so a just-formed distinction yields a large boost, a heavily-drilled one yields none, and introducing a finer split on the same dimension revives it. Against discrimination-training-differential-reinforcement (306): 306 BUILDS stimulus control and banks the finished product as its payoff; this entry says the finished product is exactly where the leverage has gone, and prescribes subdividing rather than drilling to criterion — same procedure, opposite scheduling advice, and the two are used together (306 to build, this to decide when to stop building and re-split). Against respondent-habituation (facet of 1313): that is magnitude decay of an involuntary ELICITED reflex under massed re-presentation with no pairing; here nothing habituates — the discrimination remains fully intact and accurate, only its leverage is spent, which is why re-splitting restores it and rest does not. Against progressive-conditioning (544): 544 is the flat contradiction (monotonic accumulation, no ceiling, no decay), not a neighbour. Against within-session-conditioning-loop: massed drilling is, under this entry, the way the resource is spent down.


**Why it works.** The claim is that the effect is carried by the transition — the moment the subject's responding reorganizes — rather than by the resulting stable state, which is why over-practice abolishes it and a finer split restores it. Falsifiable: hold the discrimination itself constant and vary only trials-since-acquisition; potency should fall with practice. If a heavily over-practiced discrimination yields the same boost as a fresh one, the recency gate does not exist and the effect belongs to the discrimination's content instead. Equally, if introducing a finer split fails to revive potency, the transition account is wrong and something is simply being exhausted.


**Worked examples.**

- *Re-splitting the same dimension once the first distinction goes flat*
  - **Setup.** The subject learned three sessions ago to distinguish "heavy" from "light" in their hands and it was powerful then; by now it is routine and produces almost nothing.
  - **The move.** Heavy and light are old news to you now — you can do those in your sleep. So forget them. Inside heavy, there are two different heavies: the one that's a weight pressing down on the back of your hand, and the one that's a thickness inside the arm itself. Find which one you have right now. Tell me which.
  - **Why it lands.** The settled distinction has spent its leverage, but the moment of forming a finer split on the same dimension restores it — the subject's attention narrows sharply and response magnitude comes back. The operator observes the return of the pause-and-search behaviour that the coarse distinction stopped producing, and takes that as the signal to subdivide again rather than drill.


<a id="entry-918"></a>

### referent-voiding-portable-obedience

[#918](#entry-918) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · family: transfer*

Once the listener wants to obey, the operator detaches that want from any owner. For example: 'obey the spiral', then 'who owns the spiral? who do I really obey?', answered with 'I don't know; all I know is I want to obey.' The urge stays while its target disappears, leaving a free-floating wish to obey that can attach to whatever the listener meets next. The question has to come after the urge is firmly in place.


**When to reach for this.** The referent of an installed impulse is deliberately removed, leaving a portable owner-less drive. Not state generalization (which broadens a state that keeps its content) and not a surrender-as-freedom relief reframe (where the referent stays intact). The tell is deliberate voiding of the obedience object while the impulse is preserved.


**Risk.** Installs a durable, portable, owner-less obedience impulse that outlives the session and attaches to any future object - durable identity/agency scope with out-of-session reach and no bounding.


**Why it works.** Affect and its attributed cause are separable: an aroused or motivated state can persist while the subject's explanation for it is disrupted, and it will then be reattributed to whatever plausible target is salient — the core finding of misattribution-of-arousal work. Stripping the referent while preserving the impulse leaves an unexplained drive that the next available object captures. Predicts that a listener with a strong competing candidate object present at the time will bind the impulse there rather than remain targetless. [plausible; misattribution of arousal; cause-uncertain affect seeking an explanation]


**Worked examples.**

- *Obedience kept, its object deleted*
  - **Setup.** After a long obedience chant has been repeated to steadiness; the impulse to obey is established and felt.
  - **The move.** Say it with me again — I want to obey, I want to obey. Now: whose is it? Who does the spiral belong to, who is it exactly that you're obeying? I don't know either. I've never known. All I know is that I want to obey, and so do you — and that part is true no matter who's asking.
  - **Why it lands.** The chant is given first and repeated until the wanting is steady, and only then is the question asked: whose is it, exactly, that I am obeying? The answer supplied is that it does not matter and is not known — the wanting is the only certain part. The drive is left intact with nothing on the far end of it, so it walks out of the session unattached and available to whatever asks next.


<a id="entry-1484"></a>

### refusal-satiation-flip

[#1484](#entry-1484) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: critical-faculty-softening · kind: recipe*

Start with the listener's own protest in their own voice, such as 'I'm not a maid', and have them repeat it out loud or in their head thirty to fifty times, until the words stop meaning anything and are just rhythm. Then, without breaking the beat, finish the sentence differently: 'I'm not just any maid... I'm a...' and an even stronger version of the role. Nobody wins an argument; the refusal is worn out and then turned around. It doubles as the induction, so no relaxation section is needed. It needs the listener to actually voice the protest; reading it silently as a story does not work.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the material starts from an explicit first-person denial and you want that denial to become the delivery vehicle for the identity rather than an obstacle argued down. The tell is massive verbatim repetition of a refusal sentence followed by a mid-cadence syntactic re-completion — a qualifier like "just any" slipped in — that flips the emptied sentence into an escalated claim of the very role being refused.


**Worked examples.**

- *refusal jackhammered flat, then re-completed into affirmation*
  - I'm not a fucking maid. Uh, I'm not. I'm not. Your fucking maid… I'm not just any fucking maid… I'm a fuckmaid. I'm a fuckmaid.


**See also.** `ownership-generalization-to-anyone` — both flip a chanted phrase's meaning through a small in-cadence textual mutation rather than by argument.; `practice-then-aim` — both deliver the install into a window where the tools for objecting have just been hollowed out.; `resistance-fold` — the Refusal Satiation Flip recipe was extracted from this entry; `semantic-satiation-depatterning` — both run a phrase far past semantic exhaustion so only rhythm and affect remain.


<a id="entry-762"></a>

### rehearsable-impairment-template

[#762](#entry-762) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: encoding*

A voice speaks in a specific impaired pattern and praises that pattern as desirable at the same time, while the listener whispers along. The voice trails off mid-sentence, searches for words and fails, cannot finish long words, and substitutes filler words. The stumbles land on linking words and long words, and their placement imitates real mental strain. Because the listener is producing the pattern themselves rather than just hearing a suggestion to "be dumb", they practise the actual speech habit. That makes it more specific, and more likely to take hold, than a general suggestion to feel slower or less clever.


**When to reach for this.** Targets a SPECIFIC rehearsable production pattern (polysyllable/connector failure, filler substitution) performed-and-named simultaneously — distinct from identity-labeling (asserts a trait) and from affect-fused-identity (welds a label to affect). A behavioral-rehearsal template, not a label at all; it resembles a generic 'be dumb' identity suggestion only at the surface.


**Risk.** Rehearses a durable degraded-cognition production pattern; durable-but-bounded, no channel erosion. Medium.


**Why it works.** The production effect is a memory finding — items spoken aloud are recalled better than items read silently — not evidence that motor rehearsal installs a durable speech pattern, and covert whispering is a weaker manipulation still. The defensible claim is narrower: rehearsing a specific output gives the listener an executable routine where a bare instruction gives none, and pairing praise with the performance may attach positive valence to it. Falsifiable: if listeners who whispered along showed no more of the targeted speech signature in later unprompted speech than listeners who only heard it, the rehearsal claim fails. [plausible; production effect / motor rehearsal; evaluative conditioning]


**Worked examples.**

- *Rehearsing the stumble as a praised trait*
  - **Setup.** Chorus/mantra block the subject has been told to whisper along with; degraded delivery is the thing being modelled.
  - **The move.** Thank you for making it so much... um... easier? Now I don't have to do all the... the compli— the complicated... the thinking part. It's better like this. It's better like this.
  - **Why it lands.** A chorus voice speaks the gratitude line and fails at it in a very particular way: it loses the long words halfway, gropes for the connectors, patches the gaps with fillers and a rising question mark, and then thanks itself for exactly that. A listener murmuring along does not simply agree that being slower is nice — they run the production loop of the deficit through their own mouth, breaking on the same syllables. The stumbles land where real cognitive strain lands, on the multi-syllable words and the joins, which is what makes the rehearsal convincing rather than a caricature.


**See also.** `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — instructive contrast on seam width. One deliberately splits produce and label into separate phases so the later claim reads as recognition of what was just experienced; the other performs and names the deficit in the same breath, collapsing the seam entirely. Reading them together makes the ordering variable visible.; `speech-degradation-ladder` — both degrade the speech faculty, but one has the listener motor-rehearse a specific broken production pattern while the other walks a named ladder of categories that reclassifies what speech means without touching production.; `valence-laundering-collapse-ring` — both end in performed rather than asserted degradation. One routes a target word through a benign equivalence ring and then collapses into filler that enacts the emptiness it sells; the other has the listener rehearse the actual production loop of a speech-motor deficit. Demonstrate-versus-claim siblings worth reading together.


<a id="entry-885"></a>

### relational-fractionation

[#885](#entry-885) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: social-topology*

Between moments of high control, the speaker shows small, low-stakes vulnerabilities: breaking character to admit pride ("I'm too proud of myself, can you tell?"), coining a delighted made-up word, or referring to their own known style. This reminds the listener mid-scene that the speaker is a person they like. It is a gentle form of fractionation, but it alternates the relationship rather than trance depth: the listener swings between "she has me" (submission) and "she's a person I like" (affection). Being controlled becomes more welcome because the one in control is charming. These breaks are what join the intense moments together.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is cycling of RELATIONAL stance (control vs likeability), not descent/ascent of absorption. Distinguish from classic fractionation (which cycles trance DEPTH) and from pacing-leading (which reflects the subject's experience; here the operator reveals their own persona to bind rapport).


**Risk.** Session-scoped rapport cycling; raises willingness-to-be-controlled via charm but no durable install or channel erosion.


**Why it works.** Compliance rises with liking, and self-disclosure of small vulnerabilities reliably increases liking — the disclosure is itself a low-cost concession that invites reciprocal warmth. Interleaving these beats with high-control ones also exploits contrast: the relational warmth reads as larger against the surrounding intensity, and the alternation prevents habituation to either stance. Falsifiable: strip the vulnerability beats and compliance should fall while the control content is held constant; if it does not, likeability is not the operative lever here. [established; liking as a compliance lever; self-disclosure–liking reciprocity]


**Worked examples.**

- *Charm breaks between the control beats*
  - **Setup.** Between two hard commanding passages, subject already in state; operator drops register into an ordinary speaking voice.
  - **The move.** Okay, that one was — hang on. I'm calling that a brainmelt. Brainmelt. That's a word now, I've decided. God, I am enjoying myself far too much tonight, can you tell? Right. Hands still, eyes closed. Down.
  - **Why it lands.** Between two hard commanding passages the operator drops the register entirely: she coins a silly compound word, laughs at her own invention, and admits — as an aside, in an ordinary voice — that she is enjoying herself far too much. A beat later she is back to giving orders. The listener is being cycled, but not up and down through trance depth: they are moved between she has me and she is someone I like, and the second makes the first easier to want. The small self-mocking breaks read as the operator relaxing; they are the connective tissue that keeps willingness high across the intense beats.


**See also.** `metacognitive-destabilization-drop` — both borrow the wake-and-drop cycling surface but run it on an axis other than trance depth, which is the reason to see them together. One cycles the listener's certainty about their own state until the criterion for resisting is gone; the other cycles relational stance between control and likeability so willingness rises because the controller is charming. Neither deepens by felt contrast.


<a id="entry-1329"></a>

### relief-monopoly-dependency

[#1329](#entry-1329) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: relief-monopoly*

Create or sharpen a bad feeling (guilt, craving, fear), then present yourself, obeying, or listening again as the one way out. The same source causes the problem and sells the cure, so leaving feels like losing the only relief, though time, rest or outside help would also ease it. Relief comes partly or only sometimes, which keeps them returning, and is often read as proof that giving in was right. Variations: your voice calming chaos you stirred; a threat followed by your rescue; a sensation caused, then partly cured; guilt cleared by accepting punishment; a peaked feeling withheld, returned on your terms; a trigger word sparking unresolved arousal and frustration.


**When to reach for this.** ONE relief source is made to feel uniquely necessary after the same source generated the distress; the felt exit is monopolized. A bidirectional affect anchor instead loads affect onto a neutral cue's presence or absence rather than manufacturing distress and cornering its relief; a closed affect loop routes every valence to one conclusion or couples two states into mutual amplification, where this is a single distress->compliance->relief circuit, not a valence funnel or a coupled oscillator. Genuine comfort and aftercare differ in that their relief is real and complete rather than deliberately partial and monopolized.


**Risk.** Erodes the exit/refusal channel by taxing it with loss of the only relief; a coercive dependency loop persisting out of session.


**Why it works.** Relief from an aversive state is a powerful negative reinforcer, and reinforcement attaches to whatever reliably precedes the relief — so if the same source that produces the distress also delivers the relief, the source itself becomes the conditioned reinforcer. Making the relief intermittent or incomplete puts it on a partial-reinforcement schedule, which produces slower extinction and more persistent seeking than continuous relief would. Falsifiable prediction: subjects whose distress is relieved completely and predictably should show faster decay of the return behaviour than those given partial relief. [established; negative reinforcement; partial-reinforcement extinction effect]


**Worked examples.**

- *Problem-source and relief-source are the same*
  - **Setup.** Late session, after the frame has spent several minutes naming a lack or restlessness in the subject's ordinary life.
  - **The move.** That hollow feeling you've been carrying — you already know it doesn't lift on its own. It lifts here. Give me a little more than last time and feel how it eases. Feel that? That's proof you were right to let go. It won't go all the way tonight, and that's fine; that's what the next one is for.
  - **Why it lands.** The distress is generated or sharpened by the same frame that then presents itself as the way out, and the way out is always more of the same: deeper surrender, more belief, one more session. When the relief arrives it is immediately re-read as proof that surrendering was correct. Leaving now costs not just the frame but the only relief the person can currently see — even though rest, time, or anyone outside would also have reduced the distress — and because the relief is partial rather than complete, the loop reliably teaches return.
- *Hurt then soothed by the same hands*
  - **Setup.** Aftercare-shaped segment following an imagined punishment scene; subject deep, the hurt vividly established.
  - **The move.** Now hold still. I'm opening the jar, and I'm taking a little on two fingers — feel how cool it is — and I'm working it in, slowly, exactly where I put the marks. There. Better. Not gone; I've taken the worst of it, and I've left you a little, so you'll still feel me tomorrow.
  - **Why it lands.** The same figure who caused the hurt now administers the comfort, and the administering is drawn out into ceremony rather than done briskly — a container opened, a measure taken, the slow careful application. The narration is precise about the result: the soreness is eased, but not all of it. What is left over is not carelessness, it is the point — the residue keeps the listener oriented toward the one source that both causes and eases.
- *Your own thoughts recast as the disorder*
  - **Setup.** Mid-session, pacing has slowed; the subject is quiet and receptive with no distress named yet.
  - **The move.** Listen to what's in your head right now: half a thought, then another, a scrap of tomorrow, a bit of a song. Clutter, all day, every day — that's the noise you live in. And then my voice comes in, and it's the one clean line in there, and everything else lines up behind it. That's why it's so quiet in here. That's what more of me does.
  - **Why it lands.** The pacing shifts, and the operator describes the listener's ordinary mental weather — fragments, half-finished thoughts, the noise that everyone has — as clutter and chaos. Then, in the next line, the operator's own words are offered as the thing that arrives clean and puts it in order. Nothing has been demanded; the listener's baseline has simply been reclassified as the problem, and the only stated cure is more of the voice.
- *The peak feeling locked in a box*
  - **Setup.** At the peak of a carefully built warm feeling that has been repeatedly attributed to the operator.
  - **The move.** Right there — that's the top of it. Now I'm taking it. I'm putting it in a box and the box is with me, and you can't reach it. You'll feel it missing tonight and worse tomorrow. And when the wanting gets big enough — I'll decide when that is — I'll give it back.
  - **Why it lands.** The good feeling is built carefully to a peak and tied to the operator, and then — at the top — taken away and described as sealed somewhere the listener cannot reach and the operator can. The stated release condition is not an action but an appetite: it is returned once the need for it has grown large enough. Wanting more is therefore the only permitted route back to what was just removed, and the deprivation, not the feeling, is what the listener carries out of the session.


**Realizations** (1): `anti-closure-relief-rebound-token`


**See also.** `bidirectional-affect-anchor` — both bind relief to compliance. The distinction is whether affect is loaded onto a cue's presence and absence, or a distress is manufactured and its exit monopolized by the same source. The second already carries this separation explicitly, so the link is reciprocal and load-bearing.; `manufactured-deficit-remedy` — complementary halves of one dependency build: a fabricated deficit the listener is induced to own, then a single source positioned as the only route out with relief kept deliberately incomplete. They frequently run together, and the second is the natural next move after the first.; `negative-reinforcement-escape-compliance` — the relief-monopoly entry is an applied case of the escape contingency: distress is manufactured or intensified, then compliance is made the unique route to relief, so the response is maintained by relief rather than an added reward. Naming the underlying schedule helps a reader see why the monopoly form is so durable.; `orgasm-gated-relief-monopoly` — both make the operator the sole route out of a manufactured need, but one gates a specific somatic discharge (orgasm) behind a named out-of-session operator-benefiting act, while the other manufactures distress of any kind and monopolizes its relief with deliberately incomplete resolution so return is taught rather than a single act purchased.; `relief-monopoly-bind` — both make the operator the sole exit, but one forecloses every competing route to a bodily release by ontological or cross-agent decree without needing to create the need, while the other manufactures the distress itself and then supplies deliberately incomplete relief so return is taught.; `withhold-then-beg` — both weaponize withdrawal of a valued state, but withdrawal-as-commitment-extraction cashes the deficit immediately into self-voiced begging that relocates authorship, while relief monopoly keeps the operator as the sole recurring exit from a distress it manufactures — spoken commitment versus an ongoing dependency circuit.


<a id="entry-1506"></a>

### replace-the-payoff

[#1506](#entry-1506) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering · kind: recipe*

Work out exactly what an unwanted behaviour gets the person (attention, escape, a treat), stop it getting that, and give the same payoff for a different behaviour you prefer, such as handing over a 'break' card instead of throwing a tantrum. The want is kept and redirected, not starved. Variations: choose a replacement that physically cannot be done at the same time as the old behaviour; avoid 'punishments' that actually deliver the payoff, such as time-out for someone trying to escape, or a telling-off for someone seeking attention.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a functional assessment has already identified which specific payoff sustains an unwanted behavior, and the plan's whole leverage is routing that identified payoff through a sanctioned response while the old response stops earning it. The tell is the same reinforcer appearing on both sides of the design — extinction on the problem channel, contingent delivery on the trained alternative — often accompanied by function-derived contraindications ruling out interventions that would accidentally deliver the maintaining reinforcer.


**Worked examples.**

- *functionally-equivalent replacement channel for the same reinforcer*
  - The operator identifies the reinforcer maintaining the problem behavior (via functional assessment), then teaches an adaptive communicative response (sign, vocalization, device, card) that produces that *same* reinforcer.


**See also.** `differential-reinforcement` — schedule-family axis: rerouting realizes the DRA arm of differential reinforcement with the maintaining reinforcer as the payoff.; `function-first-targeting` — function-over-topography axis: classifying the behavior by its maintaining contingency is the assessment step this rerouting builds on.


<a id="entry-1522"></a>

### response-space-preclaiming-foreclosure

[#1522](#entry-1522) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology*

The operator lists in advance every way the listener might push back, such as fighting, tuning out, doubting, stopping or holding back, and gives each one a meaning that feeds the target state: resisting breaks you, doubt becomes the trigger, stray thoughts become things to drift past. Since every reaction has already been claimed, nothing is left that counts as resistance. Opposite states get fused the same way: relaxation with arousal, choosing with compulsion, frustration with sinking, so every outlet feeds what it would normally relieve. Variations: lock one layer before opening the next, body first, then craving for depth, then arousal, then identity.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script wins by out-anticipating the listener rather than by intensifying commands — a large share of its lines answer objections and counter-moves that were never voiced. The tell is exhaustive semantic coverage of the option space: fight, doubt, tune-out, stop, and every candidate relief-state each arrive with a pre-installed reframe that routes back inward, and no reachable behavior or state is left unclaimed as an exit.


**Worked examples.**

- *sealed option-space as funnel topology*
  - The result is a topology with many entrances and no exit — a funnel where every wall is also a one-way door.


**See also.** `adverse-attentional-state-recruitment` — the same anticipatory pre-claiming applied specifically to attentional postures, where the presenting failure-state is recruited as the working vehicle.; `closed-reachability-topology` — shares the enumerated-branch closure axis: every available next-action individually narrated and bent inward toward the operator's goal.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — same reachable-state closure axis at whole-artifact scale — the coverage-by-anticipation policy here is one of the interchangeable no-off-ramp operations pooled there.; `omni-routing-all-actions-deepen` — shares the pre-claiming axis: likely counter-moves are enumerated in advance and pre-loaded with reframes that route them into the target state.; `polarity-response-utilization` — both arrange in advance that the listener's oppositional responses route into the target behavior.


<a id="entry-1370"></a>

### retrospective-influence-disclosure

[#1370](#entry-1370) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

After a frame is already installed and running, the subject is given the two things that were withheld while it was being installed: the facts that were kept from them at the point of entry, and a plain naming of the influence steps that were used on them, in the order they were used. The combination lets the subject re-read their own conversion as an engineered sequence rather than a discovery, which is what re-opens the stay-or-leave decision as genuinely theirs. It is restorative rather than persuasive — it does not argue for leaving, and a subject who stays after it has run has made a choice the pre-disclosure subject could not have made. The operator's license narrows when it runs: nothing about the frame is left available to be cashed later.


**When to reach for this.** Retrospective de-installation on an ALREADY-INSTALLED frame is the deciding tell, and the safety family currently has nothing that fires after the fact. `agency-reminder` (316) asserts that choice persists inside a live frame — prophylactic and in-session, and it does not touch a frame already accepted. Weaponized look-alikes fail the who-is-constrained test in the opposite direction: `chosen-descent-ratchet` (317) names the manipulation while performing it, so hearing it named retroactively converts sunk compliance into 'informed consent' and the operator's reach is unchanged; disclosure-as-inoculation and transparent-narration likewise disclose in order to capture, spending the disclosure as credibility. Here the disclosure is spent on the subject's decision and nothing is collected. `granted-exit-disarm` (319) supplies an assurance whose ACCEPTANCE stands down protective monitoring; this supplies facts whose acceptance stands the monitoring back up. `named-safety-belief-purge` (1203) deletes an internal safety belief; this restores an external decision.


**Why it works.** The direct evidence comes from debriefing research. A debriefing that both supplies the withheld facts and explains the procedure that produced the belief reliably reduces lingering belief, whereas a bare factual correction often does not: people keep a belief after being told its basis was false, but less so once shown how it was manufactured (belief perseverance; process debriefing). That is why both halves are needed. Two limits: this research uses short laboratory manipulations, so applying it to a belief held for years and reinforced socially is an inference, and effects are likely smaller and slower where relationships and identity are involved. Testable: compare giving the facts alone with facts plus walking through the steps; if belief and commitment shift the same, naming the steps adds nothing. And if disclosure reliably pushed people one way, such as toward leaving, rather than simply reopening the decision, it would be persuasion in disguise rather than a genuine return of choice.


**Worked examples.**

- *Withheld facts plus a named step-by-step of the influence used*
  - **Setup.** The frame is installed and running; the operator initiates the disclosure unprompted, out of trance, with nothing pending and nothing being asked for.
  - **The move.** Two things I kept from you when you came in, and you should have had both: I already knew the answer to the question I opened with, and the people you met on the second night were there because I asked them to be. And here's the order I did it in — I matched your breathing, I put you next to someone who agreed before you spoke, I named your doubt before you could, and I made leaving expensive by giving you something you'd have to hand back. That's all of it. None of that is an argument to stay and none of it is an argument to go; you decide now with what you should have had then.
  - **Why it lands.** Supplying the withheld facts alongside the named sequence lets the subject re-read their conversion as engineered rather than discovered, which reopens the stay-or-leave decision as genuinely theirs. Nothing is collected — the operator's later leverage is spent, not banked — and the tell of a correct run is that the subject can now argue against the frame using the operator's own inventory.


<a id="entry-1544"></a>

### reward-taper

[#1544](#entry-1544) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering · kind: recipe*

When a behavior is held up by an artificial support, such as tokens, frequent free rewards, or a drug dose, remove that support gradually while something else takes over. First build the replacement: pair praise with every reward from the start, so praise becomes rewarding by itself. Once the behavior is stable, cut the support in small steps, stepping back up if the behavior slips. The support ends; the behavior continues on praise or expectation. Variations: ask for more work per reward; shorten the hours the reward system runs; raise the price of the best rewards; with a drug dose, suggest the effect continues as each cut is made.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when an artificial maintaining supply is being withdrawn in graded decrements after its effect is already established. The tell is a stepwise reduction schedule with an explicit start criterion (suppression or stable performance first), increments deliberately kept small, a rebound-reversal rule, and a pre-built carrier — a paired natural reinforcer or implanted expectancy — named as what holds the behavior through each step.


**Worked examples.**

- *day-one pairing that makes the artificial reinforcer removable*
  - the descriptive verbal praise that is delivered simultaneously with the token acquire the reinforcing capability of the token. From the beginning, a systematic aim of the token economy should be to withdraw the program.


**See also.** `aversive-procedure-administration-envelope` — the envelope's planned-sunset rule opens onto the graded-withdrawal mechanics this entry details.; `baseline-keyed-criterion-calibration` — same parametric-calibration axis — steps and criteria sized from measured performance so each stage stays winnable.


<a id="entry-1568"></a>

### rigged-catalepsy

[#1568](#entry-1568) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: critical-faculty-softening · kind: recipe*

The positioning must feel natural and pass without comment; if they notice the setup, the effect looks like a trick. Command the move with confidence and name the failure at once. Be clear with yourself that this is staged: it builds belief because the difficulty is physical, not hypnotic.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 3 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Quietly put their body in a position where a move is physically hard, command that move, and call the failure trance.


<a id="entry-1452"></a>

### scaffold-then-spend-sequencing

[#1452](#entry-1452) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

Use the early part of a session to set up the beliefs, identity or feelings a later big command will rely on, then deliver the command. By the time it arrives, resisting would mean undoing things the listener has spent the session accepting as their own. Order matters: the command treats the earlier material as already true. Variations: a stack of justifications before the ask; long identity work before any instruction; building two feelings and labelling them alike so a short link feels like description; whole sessions that only lay groundwork for later visits.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when a script's early real estate is spent installing premises — beliefs, identities, assembled states, or standing infrastructure — that a later costly command then cites, with the payload arriving only after its support is load-bearing. The tell is a dependency you can articulate as a syllogism or citation: the command completes something already accepted (a baby doll wears baby-doll clothing), and mentally reordering the phases turns the payload from compelling into negotiable.


**Worked examples.**

- *Identity installed first so the behavioral command completes self-consistency*
  - a baby doll wears baby-doll clothing; you are a baby doll; therefore you wear baby-doll clothing


**See also.** `alibi-carrier-front-loading` — the deniability variant of front-loading, where the early phase supplies cover for the payload rather than premises it spends.; `arc-ordering-dependency` — the genus scheduler: phase ordering and inter-phase dependency as the operative lever across a whole artifact.; `deprivation-then-grant-relief` — sibling sequencing move where the early phase installs premises rather than aversive pressure.; `fixation-object-role-inversion` — shares the bank-early-spend-late shape: work invested up front is cashed by a later move that depends on it.; `low-ball-commitment` — the dyadic-negotiation form of the same ordering lever: commitment extracted before the change is revealed.


<a id="entry-887"></a>

### scope-boundaries

[#887](#entry-887) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: safety*

The operator says plainly what the session will not touch (daily life, relationships, core identity) and that its suggestions stay inside this session or recording, narrowing what the operator is licensed to affect. In a series it can also fence off earlier files: 'you have permission to remember; forgetting suggestions from other recordings don't apply here.' Variations: whole-life exclusions; limiting effects to this one recording; suspending other files' forget-instructions for the duration.


**When to reach for this.** Bounds the REACH of suggestion content (session scope, protected domains, prior-install carve-outs) — not a per-target admissibility screen (beneficiary-target-filter), not spec craft (install-well-formedness-gate), and not a time bound on a negotiated deal (time-boxed-consent-contract). The cross-file variant disarms forgetting rather than installing it.


**Risk.** Low — the technique is itself a bounding device: it narrows the operator's standing license rather than extending it.


**Why it works.** Explicit boundaries reduce anticipated loss of control, and reduced threat lowers reactance — the motivational push-back that follows perceived freedom restriction — so the listener resists the in-scope content less because the out-of-scope domains are safe. The effect is on the listener's willingness, not on the suggestions themselves: nothing here mechanically prevents a suggestion from generalizing, so a scope declaration should be understood as consent hygiene plus reactance reduction, not as a technical containment. Falsifiable: if listeners given explicit scope bounds show the same resistance and the same out-of-scope carryover as listeners given none, the claim fails. [plausible; psychological reactance; perceived control reduces threat appraisal]


**Worked examples.**

- *Suspending a forget-order left by other files*
  - **Setup.** Near the end of a file in a series where earlier files installed a standing forget-suggestion; content of tonight's session needs to be recalled to work.
  - **The move.** One piece of housekeeping before you come up. You have permission to remember this one. Whatever instruction you picked up in the other recordings about letting things go afterwards — that one doesn't reach tonight. Tonight stays with you, clear and complete.
  - **Why it lands.** Near the end the operator addresses not this session's content but a standing instruction left by earlier recordings in the series: recall of tonight is expressly allowed, and any forget-suggestion picked up elsewhere does not reach here. The scope limit is aimed backwards, at installs already in place, and it disarms forgetting rather than causing it — because the thing built tonight is useless if the listener cannot recall it afterwards.


**See also.** `covert-scope-authorization` — direct inverse on the same surface: the operator's standing license. One narrows it explicitly with declared off-limits domains and carve-outs; the other widens it covertly by placing a generalization authorization in a slot processed as procedural housekeeping. The pair reads as the honest and the disguised version of one control.; `forward-directed-amnesia` — opposed operations on the same reach dimension, and one is the documented counter to the other: a declared anchor after which later material is framed as un-encodable, versus explicit bounds that carve out prior installs so a standing forget-suggestion cannot reach the current content. A reader assessing whether a series seals or disarms forgetting needs the pair.; `install-concealment-amnesia` — protective inverse. One conceals the fact that an install happened so its origin cannot be audited; the other narrows what suggestions may reach, including a variant that explicitly carves out standing forget-suggestions from earlier material. Reading the bounding move clarifies exactly what the concealment move defeats.; `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — both narrow what an installed suggestion may reach, and the contrast is instructive: a plain declared bound on scope versus a bound conditioned on trust that doubles as a loyalty hook and can widen rather than narrow. A reader evaluating a bounding clause should see both.


<a id="entry-1477"></a>

### scripted-peer-overhearing-carrier

[#1477](#entry-1477) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: social-topology*

The operator builds a model inside the script and makes the listener an eavesdropper: an assistant on the mic who goes visibly from sharp and sassy to spacey, blank and wordless; peer characters who happily fail at a game and praise the state; or an already-changed narrator telling her own story. Since nobody tells the listener to do anything, defenses against direct commands have nothing to push against, and any 'you' lines are tucked inside story or side-talk. The target state arrives as testimony or live demonstration, so the listener adopts it through identification and imitation rather than submission, and happy peers make giving in less lonely. It comes in two forms: a testimonial, where an already-changed narrator presents the script's premises as settled fact, and a demonstration, where the listener silently rehearses a stand-in's step-by-step collapse. Sometimes the script says this openly, using the stand-in's experience to tell everyone listening that the same thing is getting into their heads too.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the delivery vehicle itself is a fabricated peer or proxy — the suggestions are voiced by, or run on, a character within the script while the listener merely overhears. The tell is an absent command surface: the listener is addressed rarely or not at all, and the desired state is presented as already true of, or actively happening to, someone else on stage.


**Worked examples.**

- *proxy demonstration made overt as transmission vector*
  - Let's remember how the pink pulse got into your head. That helps everyone listening know how it gets into their heads too.


**See also.** `covert-diegetic-install-shell` — shares the story-carrier architecture where the load-bearing content arrives as narration rather than command.; `description-as-installation-register` — shares the third-person descriptive register that bypasses the listener's command-evaluation interface.; `no-baseline-already-lost-frame` — adjacent addressee-displacement carrier — the first-person already-converted narrator is the voice through which an already-lost frame is often delivered.; `subject-voiced-self-mantra` — shares the first-person already-converted narrator voice as a delivery vehicle for pre-accepted identity content.


<a id="entry-1523"></a>

### seamless-arc-checkpoint-denial

[#1523](#entry-1523) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: arc-topology · kind: container*

The whole file is written as one unbroken rise, with no separate induction, no clear deepener sections, no dips and no wake-up. Each line carries on the rhythm or wording of the one before, and depth and arousal climb together. With no lull anywhere, the listener never gets a natural moment to surface and think, and leaving means breaking off mid-flow. A continuous physical activity can keep time underneath, so stopping also means breaking their own body's rhythm. If a break comes at all, it comes only after the take-home suggestion is in, and the ending keeps the charge rather than releasing it.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the control comes from what the artifact structurally withholds: rest points, section boundaries, contrast beats, a closing discharge. The tell is a piece engineered to be unbreakable into chunks — a single rising ramp where lines chain clause-to-clause with no seam to surface at, and the only pause in the whole file arrives after the payload has already landed.


**Worked examples.**

- *seamless ramp denies the judgment checkpoint*
  - Because there is no valley anywhere, the listener has no rest point at which to reassert judgment — the unbroken ramp is itself a control structure (no seam to resist at).


**See also.** `induction-less-work-as-onramp` — shares the deleted-section-boundary axis: the induction phase is removed by design so no felt entry threshold is ever crossed.; `loop-as-mechanism-no-dismount` — both delete discrete arc checkpoints so no section is uniquely load-bearing.; `no-exit-reachability-closure` — the unbroken monotonic ramp with no fractionation valley appears there as one pooled realization of whole-artifact reachability closure.


<a id="entry-1515"></a>

### self-administered-contingency

[#1515](#entry-1515) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The contingency-administrator role is relocated into the subject: the subject emits a separate controlling response that manipulates a variable of the behavior to be changed, so one of the person's own behaviors alters the probability of another. The warrant is coverage — the self is the one change agent guaranteed present in every setting and at every time, including private events no external agent can reach, so installing the person as their own prompter, monitor, and reinforcer extends the contingency where no one else can follow. Partial handovers give the subject selected roles: self-selected performance criteria and rewards, which can outperform agent-set standards but carry a documented drift toward too-lenient criteria, and self-scoring against an answer key with self-delivered reward or error correction so responses no longer wait on a busy external agent. The full form is the self-contract, which collapses all four roles — task selection, reward selection, self-monitoring of completion, and self-delivery of the reward — into one person. Across every realization the integrity of the arrangement rests on unenforced honest self-delivery: reinforcement depends on the subject withholding the reward until the criterion is genuinely met.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the target behavior lives in settings or private events no external agent can attend, and the design's answer is to make the subject their own contingency manager. The tell is the subject standing on both sides of the contingency — setting the criterion, judging their own performance, and delivering their own consequence — with the leniency and honesty risks acknowledged as part of the arrangement rather than engineered away.


**Worked examples.**

- *two-response split: subject as own contingency administrator*
  - One response, the controlling response, affects variables in such a way as to change the probability of the other, the controlled response.


**See also.** `contingency-authorship-transfer` — same contingency-authorship axis viewed as process: the fading handover whose end-state is this standing self-run arrangement.; `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — self-management genus for the same relocated-administrator arrangement, spanning reactivity-only observation through the full self-contract.; `social-reinforcement-recruitment` — same who-administers-the-contingency axis with the role routed into recruited others rather than the self.


<a id="entry-1577"></a>

### self-contract

[#1577](#entry-1577) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: contingency-engineering · kind: recipe*

Pick the task and the reward yourself, track the behaviour yourself, and give yourself the reward only when you have actually met the goal. The common failure is setting yourself an easy target, so choose one that takes real effort. Tracking your own behaviour tends to change it by itself, and self-reward adds a little more.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 3 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Choose your own task and reward, track yourself, and give yourself the reward only when you meet the goal.


**See also.** `self-management-self-administered-contingency` — the Self-Contract recipe was extracted from this entry


<a id="entry-1516"></a>

### self-monitoring-reactivity

[#1516](#entry-1516) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

The act of observing and recording one's own behavior is itself the intervention: recording begins the moment the target is defined, before any other tactic, and the desired improvement may be achieved by self-monitoring alone — no programmed consequence is added; the measurement is the lever. It works by forcing an immediate, salient event onto a response otherwise governed only by remote outcomes: eating normally produces only delayed bodily consequences, but tallying and charting each instance triggers an immediate observable mark the person cannot make without confronting the behavior at the moment it occurs. Temporal contiguity is load-bearing — the recording must be contemporaneous with the target behavior, and a deferred end-of-day reconstruction loses the effect. The same logging simultaneously yields baseline data exposing antecedent-behavior-consequence patterns, and the documented range runs from increasing on-task behavior to decreasing smoking, stereotypy, and tics.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the design's first or only move is having the subject observe and log their own target behavior, with the rate shift expected from the recording act itself. The tell is the absence of any programmed payoff — no reward, fine, or accountability partner — paired with insistence that the log entry happen at the moment of occurrence rather than in retrospect.


**Worked examples.**

- *measurement alone as the intervention*
  - the desired improvement in behavior may be achieved by self-monitoring alone.


**See also.** `contingency-space-analysis` — same operator-side measurement axis: turning a log of behavior events into the operative lever or datum.; `temporal-lag-function-discriminator` — shares the temporal-contiguity axis: the timing of an event relative to the behavior is the load-bearing datum.


<a id="entry-1087"></a>

### self-observation-instrumentation

[#1087](#entry-1087) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: measurement*

Train the person to record their own behaviour accurately. Give the reward only when their own count matches an independent count, so honest reporting, not performance, is what gets rewarded. Then show the goal as a shaded band on a chart, so 'am I doing well enough?' becomes the simpler question 'is my dot inside the band?'


**When to reach for this.** Not rewarding performance and not criterion-shaping; the tell is that the accuracy or truthfulness of self-measurement (or the ease of reading the verdict) is the reinforced or de-skilled target, not the behavior's score. The matching contingency exists because reinforcement contingent on the self-report corrupts it: students who previously had accurately self-scored greatly exaggerated their scores when higher scores resulted in points, so reward is routed through agreement with an independent record rather than through the score itself.


**Risk.** Reinforces accurate self-observation; reversible, no consent surface.


**Why it works.** Behaviour follows the contingency actually in force, so making the reward depend on agreement between self-report and an independent count reinforces accuracy rather than performance — misreporting stops paying. The graphical band works by replacing a judgment (is this good enough?) with a perceptual discrimination (is the dot inside the shaded region?), which is faster and less variable across occasions. Falsifiable in an obvious way: if the independent check is removed or becomes predictable, reported scores should drift upward relative to actual performance. [established; reinforcement of the accuracy class rather than the performance class; perceptual vs. judgmental discrimination]


**Worked examples.**

- *Reward gated on agreement, not performance*
  - "If Brad's self-recorded data agreed with the teacher at a level of 80% or higher, he received his choice from a menu" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.
- *The standard drawn as a band on the graph*
  - "chart self-recorded data on a graph that showed the competitive standard with a shaded area"; "I'm not in the shaded area. I need to work faster." — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `self-policing-reward-withdrawal-loop` — both recruit the listener as their own monitor, with opposite reinforced targets: one fires an aversive signal on self-detected deviation, relieved only by self-correction, while the other reinforces the accuracy of self-measurement itself. Easy to conflate under self-monitoring, so the contrast is useful.


<a id="entry-245"></a>

### self-sealing-counter-input-closure

[#245](#entry-245) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: self-sealing*

Installs a meta-rule that routes any competing input into the existing erasure mechanism by definition, rather than letting it be evaluated — making the conditioning immune to counter-suggestion. Any future hypnosis opposing this conditioning will itself be 'washed away by the latex,' and challenges to 'the operator is always right' are pre-classified as wrong. It is a closed epistemic seal: it forbids new conditioning except the operator's and pre-labels any challenge as invalid, reframed as protection so it feels like a benefit.


**When to reach for this.** A closed epistemic seal — counter-content is pre-classified wrong-by-definition and routed into the existing erasure, never evaluated (a reachability closure over what content can ever land).


**Risk.** Forecloses deprogramming and any outside counter-influence by definition — erodes the exit/verification channel durably; high (matches Pass B sort11-high).


**Why it works.** This is belief perseverance engineered on purpose: pre-classifying counter-evidence as invalid means incoming disconfirmation is processed as further confirmation rather than as data, the same asymmetric-scrutiny pattern seen in motivated reasoning. Framing the seal as protection recruits the listener's own motivation to maintain it, which is why it outlasts mere instruction. Falsifiable: if listeners still evaluated competing suggestions on their merits after the seal, or if the protective framing added nothing over a bare exclusivity claim, the account is wrong. [plausible; belief perseverance; motivated reasoning / disconfirmation bias]


**Worked examples.**

- *Counter-hypnosis routed into the same erasure*
  - **Setup.** Closing minutes, after the main conditioning has landed; delivered as a parting gift.
  - **The move.** One last thing, to keep you safe. If anything ever comes along afterwards trying to undo this — another voice, another recording, someone telling you to shake it off — you don't have to weigh it up or argue with it. It goes straight into the same wash that emptied you tonight, and it rinses away like everything else did. And if anyone says I'm wrong about you, well — I'm right about you. So they're wrong. That's all the thinking that ever needs doing.
  - **Why it lands.** A standing rule is installed at the end: anything that later arrives to undo this work does not get evaluated on its merits — it goes into the same solvent that cleared the listener out in the first place, and rinses off. A second clause covers arguments rather than sessions: the operator is right, therefore whatever contradicts the operator is by definition wrong. The lock is handed over as protection, so the listener receives it as a gift rather than a wall.


**See also.** `closed-epistemic-self-validation-loop` — both are whole-text closures, and their discriminators already gesture at each other: one seals against incoming competing content, the other validates claims using states the text itself induced. Reading them together clarifies the seal-versus-loop distinction.; `isolation-by-annexation` — both are closures against competing conditioning, and they differ on the one axis a reader must pick between: deny-and-route-into-erasure versus annex-and-relabel-as-the-operator's. Rival prior conditioning is the shared object, so a reader classifying an immunity clause needs to check which move is on the page. Genuinely two mechanisms, so no merge.; `no-exit-response-closure` — two closures over different domains: one closes the space of content that can ever land, the other closes the space of responses the listener can make. Real risk of confusion when a script does both, and the discriminators already turn on which space is sealed, so the pointer earns its place.; `operator-removal-self-policing-closure` — both are closure end-states rather than single lines: one seals against competing external input, the other closes the loop internally so no operator is needed. Adjacent halves of the same 'nothing can open this' design space.; `reality-test-insulation` — two seals against different disconfirming channels — ordinary-life feedback versus competing hypnosis — already cross-named in each discriminator. The pointer is earned.; `self-sealing-frame` — both engineer away disconfirmation. One seals against competing external input by pre-classifying it wrong and routing it into the erasure mechanism; the other pre-maps every possible listener response and outcome branch to confirmation. External-input seal versus internal-verdict rig.; `unfalsifiability-scaffold` — both seal an epistemic channel so nothing can disconfirm the frame, and one already flags a close twin in this territory. The line is what is sealed against: competing external conditioning pre-classified as invalid and routed into the existing erasure, versus the listener's own observations and inspection of the machinery. Adjacent enough that the discriminators must be read together.


<a id="entry-1533"></a>

### self-sealing-feedback-loop

[#1533](#entry-1533) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: indirect-suggestion*

The operator asserts a closed causal ring between the subject's own states — depth and trust, depth and pleasure, obedience and pleasure, arousal and obedience and trance chained with reordered terms — so each term is offered as proof of the others and the ring has no entry or exit point. At least one variable is genuinely present (arousal, mild relaxation, the fact of listening), and whatever the subject actually feels is recruited as evidence the other terms are rising too; disconfirmation is impossible because questioning one clause requires rejecting every other clause simultaneously, and there is no "because" that bottoms out. The ring extends to wanting itself, looped onto being-told-to-want ("you always do what I tell you because you want to because I told you to want to"), erasing the distinction between desire and instruction so every escalation arrives pre-licensed. In the self-recited variant the subject speaks both halves of the loop about themselves in first person ("Slavery makes my cunt wet. My wet cunt makes me a slave"), closing the trap in their own voice; in the enacted variant, parsing the described cycle is itself running it ("the more you listen, the more confused you become, the more confused you become, the more you listen"). Naming the loop openly does not break it — it adds authority, and once accepted the engine runs self-driven, making continued operator speech optional.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when two or more of the subject's states are welded into circular mutual causation offered as its own evidence, with a genuinely felt variable feeding the ring. The tell is reciprocal "the more X, the more Y / the more Y, the more X" phrasing with no first cause to interrogate — including mantra forms where the subject recites both halves about themselves, and prose whose very parsing enacts the cycle it describes.


**Worked examples.**

- *operator names the closed ring openly and it works anyway*
  - The deeper you go, the more you trust me. And the more you trust me, the deeper you go. A wonderfully simple feedback loop


**See also.** `arousal-state-feedback-weld` — neighbouring weld family: two or more state-variables asserted to co-move in a mutually-amplifying loop fueled by real body arousal.; `pluralistic-ignorance-freeze` — shares the closed evidence-loop structure in which each participant's state is read as proof of the others'.; `recited-feedback-loop-formula` — close variant on the recited axis: the loop compressed into a tight verbal formula spoken as an equation and fed back into itself.; `self-validating-language` — shares the evidentiary axis: whatever the subject actually produces or feels is read back as proof the suggestion has taken hold.


<a id="entry-1512"></a>

### sensory-extinction

[#1512](#entry-1512) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: contingency-engineering*

For behavior maintained by its own sensory product there is no delivered reinforcer to withhold — instead the operator physically alters the environment or body so the self-produced sensation no longer occurs: goggles over eye-poking, mittens over hair-twirling, lima beans fouling the taste of vomit, disconnecting the switch, carpeting the spinning surface. The behavior still emits but stops producing its payoff — the response-consequence contingency is broken at the sensory channel, and the behavior decays toward its pre-reinforcement rate. This is explicitly distinct from response blocking: the subject remains free to perform the act; it simply yields no sensation. It requires that the maintaining reinforcer be automatic and sensory rather than socially mediated, and that the specific channel be physically maskable while still permitting the response. Because the apparatus is intrusive, it is not simply left on: the glove is gradually cut away so the masking fades out rather than being removed all at once.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when the payoff is self-produced sensation with no social mediator — visual, tactile, gustatory, kinesthetic — and the writer attacks the sensation itself rather than the subject's freedom to act. The tell is protective apparatus and altered surfaces: gloves, goggles, taste-spoilers, disconnected switches, carpet, each leaving the behavior physically possible while its feedback channel goes dead. The subject keeps acting and gets nothing back.


**Worked examples.**

- *behavior left free while its sensory payoff is masked*
  - the persons can emit the problem behavior, but that behavior will not produce reinforcement


**See also.** `antecedent-manipulation (retained core: cue/materials editing)` — same physically-edit-the-environment axis, applied upstream to the evoking occasion rather than downstream to the behavior's sensory payoff.; `reinforcement-extinction` — genus extinction entry whose sensory-masking channel this entry matured out of.


<a id="entry-1472"></a>

### single-cue-shortcut-substrate

[#1472](#entry-1472) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: — · family: critical-faculty-softening · kind: principle*

The described substrate: under load — rushed, stressed, uncertain, indifferent, distracted, or fatigued — a decider stops integrating all available evidence and lets one highly representative feature stand in for the whole, firing a fixed routine to completion, "click, whirr," the way a turkey's maternal behavior rolls out at "cheep-cheep." Influence is thereby reframed as stimulus-triggered response rather than persuasion of a reasoning agent: cooperation becomes a reflex to cue, not an argument to win. The demonstrated instance is the reason-token: a justification-shaped clause satisfies the "a reason was given" check on grammatical form alone — the raw word "because" carries the power, and the content of the reason is never evaluated, as children intuit with "because… just because." The shortcut fires because the cue is normally reliable and the ask is small enough that demanding a real evaluation isn't worth the effort; the substrate weakens when stakes rise and the empty token is exposed.


**When to reach for this.** Reach for this when explaining or engineering compliance that runs on a cue instead of a case — a target in a low-resource state responding to one representative feature as if it were the whole assessment. The tell is a complete routine executing off a single trigger: a bare "because" clause accepted without its content being read, or one salient feature standing in for evidence the decider never integrates.


**Worked examples.**

- *single-feature substitution under load*
  - only a single, highly representative piece of the total
