**See also.** `contingency-function-substrate-principles` — both are literature-derived substrate principles about what determines a response, constraining technique design rather than deploying a move.; `open-slot-attachment-frame` — both show grammatical form doing the causal work while the content filling it is interchangeable.


<a id="entry-1570"></a>

### six-step-reframing

[#1570](#entry-1570) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · family: operator-craft · kind: recipe*

Agree a clear yes/no signal before asking the part anything, and wait for the signal rather than guessing. Treat the part's aim as positive even when the behaviour is not. If another part objects at the final check, the new choices do not fit yet. There is no good outcome evidence; it is mainly useful for thinking about motives.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 6 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Contact the part behind an unwanted behaviour, learn its positive intent, have it choose better ways to meet that intent, then check fit.


<a id="entry-1377"></a>

### specificity-demand-degeneralization

[#1377](#entry-1377) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: compliance*

When the person speaks in vague generalities, the operator treats this as hiding rather than imprecision and will not move on until they give one concrete instance: which time, which person, what exactly was said. A vague worry has no edges, so it cannot be examined or argued with; a single specific example can be checked and has a definite feeling attached. Usually the person gives an example and the diffuse dread turns into something nameable that can be worked on. The point is to keep pressing each time they drift back into generalities, not any single question.


**When to reach for this.** The operator refuses a generality the SUBJECT produced and holds out for one concrete instance, repeatedly, across successive retreats into abstraction. Against 525 target-selection facet (e) trait-to-behavior-decomposition, which is the closest content match and dissolves a trait label into countable behaviors: that is a design-time filter on the operator's own target list with nothing enacted on the subject, whereas this is a live in-session demand the subject must answer. Against 1263 somatic-localization-handle, which also meets a disputed abstraction by demanding something concrete: it drops to a BODY SITE to originate a kinesthetic anchor, where this demands a specific episode (which time, which person, what was said) and the payload is a proposition with a truth value. Against the whole deletion surface (1208 predicate-generalization, 398 linguistic-deletion-selfsupply), which this inverts: those engineer under-specification so self-supplied content escapes audit; here the operator refuses a deletion the subject made and audits the supplied content immediately.


**Why it works.** A vague generality has nothing specific to check and nothing particular to feel, so it can be held indefinitely at little cost. Replacing it with one real instance brings in both, which is why people resist the swap and why it changes what there is to work with. The operator's job is to keep refusing the retreat, because the person will drift back to generalities whenever allowed. Testable: compare steadily demanding instances with sympathetically accepting the general version; if both lead to the same feelings and the same progress afterwards, the specificity does nothing beyond attention or persistence. A serious risk: pressing for an instance may produce an invented one rather than a recalled one. Pressured recall is known to generate confabulation, and if supplied instances match independently checkable events no better than chance, that is what is happening. The approach resembles the NLP 'meta-model' challenge, which is not itself established.


**Worked examples.**

- *Holding out for one instance across successive retreats into abstraction*
  - **Setup.** The subject is describing a diffuse dread — 'people always end up disappointed in me' — and each attempt to pin it down slides back into a generality.
  - **The move.** Not people. One person, one time. Which one. — 'A lot of them' isn't a time; give me the day. — Now what did she actually say. Her words, not your summary. Say the sentence.
  - **Why it lands.** A diffuse formulation has no edges and cannot be examined or contradicted; forcing one instance in its place collapses it into a proposition with a truth value and a specific affect attached. The operator's persistence across each retreat is the technique rather than any single question, and the observable result is the dread resolving into something nameable and workable.


<a id="entry-1415"></a>

### split-audience-deniable-disclosure

[#1415](#entry-1415) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: concealment*

One utterance is engineered to carry two different meanings to two different hearers present at the same moment: a manufactured slip, misnaming, or 'error' delivers the real content to a chosen overhearing witness while remaining, to the addressee, nothing but a stumble. The addressee has a ready-made innocent reading available (the speaker misspoke), so nothing is disclosed that can be challenged; the witness, holding the context the addressee lacks, resolves the same words to the loaded reading. The apparent accident is what buys the deniability — a deliberate statement invites accountability, whereas a slip is conventionally exempt from being held against the speaker. The operator therefore discloses and denies in the same breath, with the audience split, not the channel, doing the work.


**When to reach for this.** The unit is ONE utterance resolving to two different meanings for two REAL hearers present at once, with the addressee holding an innocent reading that makes the disclosure unchallengeable. vs audience-split-bypass (255): that partitions a SINGLE listener into conscious/subconscious and assigns the critical faculty an ignore-task — the 'audiences' are faculties inside one head, and no second person is in the room. vs two-target-command-router (296): also intra-subject, dispatching incoming commands across two installed selves. vs two-channel-relational-delivery (773): two delivery TRACKS staged for one absorbing listener; here there is one track and two receivers. vs register-camouflaged-delivery (286): payload hidden in a channel the single listener does not monitor — remove the camouflage and it dies; here the payload is in the monitored foreground and survives on the addressee's available innocent reading. vs identity-labeling (1234), whose absorbed 'staged-accidental slip' variant is the closest single line in the corpus: that slip is aimed at the sole subject to seat a label on them, whereas here the slip's real recipient is a third party and the addressee is the one it must NOT land on. Precondition none of the above carry: at least three parties and context asymmetry the witness holds and the addressee lacks.


**Why it works.** Utterance meaning is resolved by each hearer against their own context, so the same string can settle into two different interpretations when two hearers hold different priors — and conversational convention treats slips and errors as exempt from accountability, which is what makes an engineered error a low-cost carrier for content that could not be asserted openly. Falsifiable: deliver the identical content as a flat assertion rather than as an apparent error, with the same two hearers and the same asymmetric context. If the witness's uptake and the addressee's willingness to challenge are unchanged, the error-framing is decorative and only the audience asymmetry is doing work; if neither hearer diverges, the account fails outright. [plausible; audience design in pragmatics; plausible deniability and off-record politeness strategies]


**Worked examples.**

- *Manufactured slip: a wrong word corrected too fast*
  - **Setup.** Mid-conversation, three people present; the witness knows the subject's collar sits under the shirt collar, the addressee does not.
  - **The move.** Sorry, I've been on the phone all morning — could you pass me the leash, the lead, the *pen*, sorry, the pen. Long day.
  - **Why it lands.** The addressee resolves it as fatigue-driven word-searching and has nothing to challenge; the witness, holding the collar context, hears the first word as the intended one and the correction as cover. The operator watches for the witness's eye-flick or half-second stillness while the addressee reaches for the pen without pausing.
- *Misnaming: the addressee called by the witness's private name for them*
  - **Setup.** Introductions at a group table; the witness has previously heard the operator use a possessive pet name for the addressee, who has never heard it said aloud in company.
  - **The move.** And this is — sorry — this is Kitten. Katie. Katie, sorry, I've got two of you in my phone.
  - **Why it lands.** The addressee is handed a ready-made innocent reading (contact-list confusion) and cannot object without asserting the loaded reading themselves. The witness receives confirmation that the private name is real and in use. Observe whether the addressee colours while still smiling — the tell that the innocent reading is being held onto deliberately.
- *Staged 'error': reading the wrong line off a list*
  - **Setup.** Operator is reading aloud from a schedule or shopping list in front of both parties; witness knows what the operator actually keeps on that list.
  - **The move.** Right — Thursday, dentist; Friday, pick up the restraints — sorry, the *rest of the* order. Friday, pick up the rest of the order.
  - **Why it lands.** A misread of one's own handwriting is the most conventionally exempt kind of slip, so the addressee's innocent reading is airtight and no accountability attaches. The witness hears an inventory disclosed. The operator should see the addressee's attention move on to Saturday while the witness's does not.


<a id="entry-1372"></a>

### spontaneous-charge-redirection

[#1372](#entry-1372) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: pacing-rapport*

A strong relational charge forms between subject and operator that the operator did not build and did not ask for — intensified attachment, hostility, idealization, or a mixture — and instead of managing it as an obstacle or letting it distort the work, the operator captures it and points it at the task. The charge becomes the engine: the subject's investment in the operator is redirected into investment in doing the work, so the very intensity that was derailing sessions is what now sustains them. The defining fork is capture versus manufacture — the operator did not create this charge and could not have, which is why the move is only available reactively and why misreading a manufactured attachment as a spontaneous one is the main failure. Because the charge is bidirectional, the operator's own investment is part of what has to be named and handled rather than assumed neutral.


**When to reach for this.** The charge is UNBIDDEN — it formed without operator construction and could not have been built to order — and it is redirected to POWER the task rather than to be examined or to obligate.


**Why it works.** Motivation can transfer between goals that feel linked, so an existing strong attachment can be recruited to sustain effort on work the person would not otherwise keep up; the feeling supplies drive that instruction alone does not. That same link is why it is high-risk: the work now depends on the relationship, and effort is likely to collapse if the relationship does. Testable: if people whose feeling was openly redirected into the work engage no better than matched people whose feeling was simply acknowledged and set aside, the redirection adds nothing beyond ordinary rapport. More importantly, if they keep going just as well after the relationship ends, the work was never running on the attachment and the dependency worry is unfounded. Consent and limits matter, because steering an attachment the person did not choose to form, without saying so, turns an unasked-for bond into leverage. The related clinical idea of working with transference is not independently established.


**Worked examples.**

- *Unbidden intensity named, then pointed at the task*
  - **Setup.** Several sessions in; a strong attachment the operator did not build has formed and is derailing sessions — the subject is preoccupied with the operator's approval rather than with the material.
  - **The move.** Something has got very strong between us, and I didn't build it and neither of us asked for it. I'm not going to pretend it isn't there, and I'm not going to let it eat the hour. So we're going to spend it: all of that wanting-me-to-be-pleased goes into the thing you've been walking around for three weeks. Do that piece now, out loud — and yes, do it for me, because that's what currently has fuel in it.
  - **Why it lands.** The charge stops being an obstacle and becomes the engine, so the intensity that was derailing sessions is what now sustains them. The operator must first verify the charge is unbidden — the check is that nothing in their own conduct engineered stake or debt — since misreading a manufactured attachment as spontaneous is the named failure; the operator's own investment gets named rather than assumed neutral.


<a id="entry-1394"></a>

### staged-compromise-evidence-banking

[#1394](#entry-1394) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded · family: contingency-engineering*

A scene is arranged so that it generates a durable, compromising artifact — a photograph, a recording, a signed statement, a witnessed act — which the operator retains without using. Nothing is cashed at the time; the subject's experience of the scene is often unremarkable, and the coercive function activates only later, on the first refusal, when the held artifact is produced or alluded to. The staging is designed backward from the artifact: participants are positioned and the scene is shaped so the resulting record will read as maximally damaging out of context, independent of what actually occurred. Its value to the operator is the standing threat, so it works best never used.


**When to reach for this.** A durable compromising artifact (photograph, recording, signed statement, witnessed act) is generated by a staged scene, retained, and deliberately NOT used — the coercive function is a standing threat activated only on a future refusal. Two properties are jointly unmatched: the artifact is external to the subject's psychology (no state or belief change is asserted or required at the time), and the value is in holding rather than exercising. Split from `threat-of-loss-rouse` (389), the nearest lever in kind: 389 also runs on forfeiture, but its threatened asset is the subject's own future state access, it is spoken aloud, and it is cashed on the spot to break a blocked command channel — here the asset is an external record, the threat is unspoken, and cashing it spends it. Split from `precommitment-rule-governed-stakes` (424), where a third party holds a stake the SUBJECT arranged against their own future defection; here the subject did not agree and does not know a stake exists. Split from the staging cluster on timing: `staged-negotiation-favor-theater` (517) collects felt indebtedness the moment the operator returns, `context-lock-staging` (243) gates a payload in the same session, and `counterfeit-cue-forgery` (493) collapses on detection — this one is designed to be detected later, deliberately.


**Why it works.** The operative asset is asymmetric information about reputational exposure, and the standing-threat structure is what gives it force: an unexercised threat retains its full value while an exercised one is spent, which is why holding is rational for the coercer and why the target's compliance can be sustained indefinitely without any further action. Decontextualization does the rest — records of intimate or transgressive acts are read by outside audiences without the framing that made them ordinary, so the artifact's damage is largely independent of what the scene actually was. Falsifiable: if compliance rates under a held-but-unused artifact matched those with no artifact, the banking does nothing; and if targets who knew the artifact existed complied at the same rate as those who did not, the mechanism is not the threat but something else in the scene. Note this is a game-theoretic and social account, not a psychological state claim — no state change in the subject is asserted or required. [established; standing-threat leverage under asymmetric information; decontextualized-record reputational harm]


**Worked examples.**

- *Scene shaped backward from the artifact, banked unspoken, alluded to on first refusal*
  - **Setup.** A scene staged so the resulting record will read badly out of context — the camera already placed at the angle that crops the context out — and then, weeks later, the subject declines something for the first time.
  - **The move.** In the scene: "Kneel with your face up toward the lamp and say your full name and the date, clearly, for me." Weeks later, on the refusal: "That's fine, you can say no. I still have the clip from the lamp night on the drive — the one with your name in it. I've never done anything with it. Think about it and get back to me tomorrow."
  - **Why it lands.** At the time the scene is unremarkable to the subject, so nothing is defended against; the leverage is an external record rather than any belief, and its power comes from being held rather than spent. Observable on the refusal: the subject stops arguing about the request itself and starts negotiating about the artifact — asking where it is, who has seen it, what would make it go away.


<a id="entry-768"></a>

### stakeholder-obligation-bond

[#768](#entry-768) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · consent-required · family: persistence*

Declares the operator's and listener's pleasure 'locked together in a sexy bond of dominance and submission', installing the operator as a personal stakeholder in the listener's compliance. Because the listener's pleasure is now also the operator's, refusing the behavioral program is reframed as refusing-to-please-her — a parasocial obligation layer that adds a relational cost (disappointing the operator) on top of the behavioral install, reinforcing it.


**When to reach for this.** The tell is the stakeholder framing (her pleasure is bound to yours) that adds a relational obligation to comply, not a conditioned trigger and not a possession claim.


**Risk.** Adds a durable relational cost to non-compliance (obligation to please the operator) but is bounded and does not erode the refusal channel directly; medium.


**Why it works.** Once compliance is framed as pleasing a specific person rather than following an instruction, refusal is re-priced as a relational act with an interpersonal cost, and people avoid disappointing a valued other more reliably than they avoid breaking an abstract rule. Parasocial bonds recruit the same obligation machinery as reciprocal ones despite being one-directional, which is why a recorded operator can still function as a stakeholder. Falsifiable: if listeners complied at the same rate whether or not the operator's pleasure was declared contingent on their behaviour, the relational-cost account fails. [plausible; parasocial obligation; compliance framed as interpersonal cost]


**Worked examples.**

- *Her pleasure bound to yours as obligation*
  - **Setup.** Assigning a between-sessions routine; rapport established and the subject already values the operator's approval.
  - **The move.** Your pleasure and mine are tied together now — when it's good for you it's good for me, and that's the arrangement from here on. So the ten minutes I've set you every night isn't a chore on a list. It's the thing I'm waiting for, and I'll know the nights it doesn't come.
  - **Why it lands.** The operator declares the two of them wired together: what you feel and what I feel are tied now, she tells the listener — when it is good for you it is good for me, and that is the arrangement. From that point the program is no longer only a set of instructions: skipping it is not laziness but letting her down, and every completed step is a small gift she is waiting for.


**See also.** `pleasure-attributed-to-operator` — both re-route reinforcement toward the operator, one by re-sourcing the subject's own pleasure to the operator and the other by binding the two parties' pleasure so refusal becomes a relational failure. The second reads as a relational-obligation neighbor of the first's reward-rerouting lever.


<a id="entry-581"></a>

### stakeholder-set-success-threshold

[#581](#entry-581) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: low · stated only — not demonstrated in corpus · family: safety*

The people who will live with the outcome, not the operator, decide in advance how much change counts as enough. Afterward, someone checks that the real-world reason for the work actually improved (is anyone safer, do people get along differently), not just that a chosen number went down. The operator is not allowed to declare success on a measure they picked themselves.


**When to reach for this.** Recipe governance test 'who is constrained after the move runs?': the OPERATOR (cannot self-certify success), so positive governance, not consent-manufacture (which erodes the refusal channel). vs operator-side-craft: craft procedures sharpen the operator's own knowledge/measurement/conduct while leaving authority with the operator; here the threshold-setting authority is RELOCATED to stakeholders — license narrowed, not sharpened. vs a post-hoc satisfaction survey: the threshold is set BEFORE the intervention and re-checked against the original real-world reason.


**Risk.** Protective, license-narrowing move: it constrains the operator and hands verification to affected parties ('a metric-only win is disallowed'; success confirmed outside the operator).


**Why it works.** The operator has both an incentive and an unconscious bias toward declaring success, and can satisfy any self-chosen metric by choosing a metric that will move — the standard proxy-gaming failure in which an indicator ceases to be a good measure once it becomes a target. Relocating threshold-setting to the affected parties, and fixing the threshold before the intervention, removes both degrees of freedom: the operator can no longer pick the goalpost or move it afterwards. Falsifiable: if pre-registered stakeholder thresholds are met at the same rate as operator-chosen ones, and if outcomes on the original real-world concern track proxy movement equally either way, the relocation buys nothing. [plausible; Goodhart's law / proxy gaming; pre-registration against post-hoc goalpost movement]


**Worked examples.**

- *Those who live with the behavior set the bar*
  - "the answer is most likely to come from the people who must deal with the behavior; they should be asked" — Cooper, Heron & Heward (2020), Applied Behavior Analysis, 3rd ed.


**See also.** `experiential-consent-trial` — a pair worth reading together as two placements of the same governance bar: both strip the operator of unilateral go/no-go, one by relocating the definition of success to the people who must live with the result and re-checking it against the real-world reason, the other by blocking the install until the subject has lived the experience and can abort. One constrains what counts as done, the other what is allowed to start.


<a id="entry-170"></a>

### staying-means-yes

[#170](#entry-170) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: framing · kind: recipe*

The script opens by repeatedly telling the listener to leave because their memories will drain if they stay, but each 'you should leave' line is a vivid rehearsal of memory-loss imagery. The warning to escape is how the suggestion is delivered. Since the format all but guarantees they keep listening, staying is then quietly counted as a choice to submit, creating a commitment before any formal induction begins.


**When to reach for this.** The warning's own sentences ARE the induction content (each escape-warning rehearses the payload). vs a genuine safety disclaimer or content warning — a boundary offered before content. vs warning-as-binding-agreement (kin) — that plants a warning to cite BACK as agreement; here the warning delivers the payload directly.


**Risk.** A counterfeit exit whose sentences deliver memory-loss imagery and manufacture pre-commitment; session-scoped.


**Why it works.** Instructions to not think of something require representing the thing in order to obey, so a warning phrased in vivid content-imagery delivers that content regardless of compliance — the same reason thought-suppression instructions can increase the target thought's accessibility. The pre-commitment half runs on self-perception plus consistency: having freely continued after being told to leave, the subject infers a chosen willingness, and that inferred choice constrains later refusal. Falsifiable: if imagery-loaded warnings produced no more of the target experience than content-free ones, the first half is wrong; if continuing after a warning produced no more later compliance than no warning, the second half is wrong. [plausible; ironic effects of thought suppression; self-perception and consistency after free choice]


**Worked examples.**

- *Every warning to leave rehearses the payload*
  - **Setup.** First minute of the recording, before any induction; framed as a warning to leave.
  - **The move.** You should stop this now. Really — turn it off, because if you keep listening your memories start to loosen and thin out, the recent ones first, and you won't notice them going. Last chance. Stay past this sentence and everything from this week starts to fade, so go, unless you'd rather stay.
  - **Why it lands.** The opening minute repeatedly urges the listener to stop and go, but the reason given is always a vivid description of what will otherwise happen: memories loosening, thinning, going out the longer this continues. The listener hears these lines as a disclaimer and so does not examine them, while hearing the suggestion rehearsed several times. Since the format all but guarantees they keep playing, the operator can then point out that they chose to stay, and that choice becomes a commitment made before any induction started.


**See also.** `care-framed-install-smuggling` — both convert protective-sounding surface material into delivery: an escape warning that rehearses the payload it warns about, and an aftercare surface that performs install work. Same inversion applied at opposite ends of a session, and a reader auditing safety-shaped language wants both.; `carrier-frame-payload-smuggling` — two whole-artifact delivery-vehicle relationships where the ostensible surface does the payload work. In one the escape warnings are themselves rehearsals of the content they warn about; in the other the genuinely delivered advertised frame carries an unrequested payload and gates early exit. Same structural insight, different cover.; `expectation-seeding` — the Staying Means Yes recipe was extracted from this entry; `loop-hook-non-wake-close` — both weaponize a structural slot that should protect the listener — the pre-content warning and the closing wake — by making the protective form itself deliver payload or suppress the evaluation window, differing in whether the exit is denied at entry or at exit.; `no-lose-double-bind` — the Staying Means Yes recipe was extracted from this entry


<a id="entry-1559"></a>

### stroke-to-my-rhythm

[#1559](#entry-1559) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · family: triggers · kind: recipe*

Your voice sets the stroking pace, so make the tempo clear enough to follow as you speed it up and slow it down. Say 'stop' at the peak, and hold off release until you allow it. Common in kink audio, but untested.


**When to reach for this.** A recipe: 3 ordered steps, each pointing at the entry that does that step's work. Reach for it as a whole when you want this: Have them stroke to the tempo of your voice, speed it up and slow it down, then say 'stop' to break motion from release.


<a id="entry-1400"></a>

### suppression-banked-past-zero

[#1400](#entry-1400) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers · kind: principle*

Once a trigger being removed has stopped producing any response, continuing to run it unrewarded still keeps burying it deeper, even though nothing visible changes, since the response is already at zero. That hidden extra depth shows up later: the response comes back more slowly on its own, is harder to re-install, and its weakening spreads further to similar triggers. So 'it stopped responding, we can stop' is the wrong rule both ways: too few extra rounds leaves it shallow, too many buries it far deeper than intended with no sign that it happened.


**When to reach for this.** Against irreversible-ratchet-persistence: that is an ASSERTED one-way accumulation the listener is told about and which does its work by being believed; this is an actual accumulation with no assertion, no listener awareness, and no framing component whatever. Against disconfirmation-suppression: that is a discrete act blocking one contradicting fact from reaching the subject; this is a continuous accrual in the subject's own conditioning with nothing being blocked. Against manufactured-insufficiency-treadmill and manufactured-insufficiency-ratchet: those are both operator-owned moving standards that manufacture a shortfall for the subject to feel — nobody is told anything here, and the measurement problem is the OPERATOR'S, not the subject's. The distinctive shape is a measurement trap: the instrument floors out while the quantity keeps moving.


**Why it works.** The observable is a floored, censored measure of an unbounded latent quantity, so once the response hits zero the readout carries no information about further change — a general property of any bounded instrument on an unbounded process, not something specific to conditioning. That makes it testable without any theory of what suppression is: hold visible-zero constant and vary the number of post-zero trials, then measure later recovery latency, re-acquisition trials-to-criterion, and sibling decrement. If those later measures were flat across post-zero trial counts, nothing is being banked and the visible zero is the whole story. [established; extinction beyond criterion / floor effects in measurement; latent inhibition accrual]


**Worked examples.**

- *Post-zero trial budget fixed in advance, because the meter has floored*
  - **Setup.** Mid de-conditioning pass; the starved cue has produced no visible response for the last several trials and the temptation is to call it done or to keep going until it feels done.
  - **The move.** It has been at zero for four trials, which tells you nothing — the meter floored, the burial did not stop. Pick the number of post-zero trials now and write it down: six. Run exactly six more, then stop, and do not let 'it still looks the same' talk you into twenty.
  - **Why it lands.** Once the response is at floor every further trial looks identical while suppression keeps accruing, so any depth reading taken during the pass systematically understates how deeply the response is buried. Observable only later and indirectly: markedly slower spontaneous recovery, a higher bar for re-installation, and more collateral loss on siblings than the run appeared to justify.


<a id="entry-1417"></a>

### suppression-dose-response-titration

[#1417](#entry-1417) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: triggers*

Treat a suggested block (a forgotten item, a frozen limb, a denied response) as something with a strength you can set, not as simply on or off. Two things control it. The more times the block is suggested, the deeper and wider it goes. The longer you wait after the last suggestion before testing it, the more it has faded. Using both, you can aim for a partial block and predict roughly how strong it will be later. Too little and a test breaks straight through it; too much and it spreads into responses that were meant to keep working.


**When to reach for this.** Both neighbouring dials parameterize an EXCITATORY quantity; this one parameterizes a suppression. vs monotonic-amplifier-dial: that ratchets a positive state upward by utterance count and pre-loads the listener's expectation of escalation as the active ingredient — here the parameterization is operator-side calibration, the subject is told nothing about a gradient, and the quantity being moved is a hold rather than an intensity. vs scope-coupled-depth-titration: that titrates DEPTH by widening the requested scope of a phenomenon, one knob and an indirect one; here there are two independent knobs (count and elapsed time) and the titrated quantity is the suppression itself. vs disconfirmation-suppression: that is a single discrete guard action protecting a running belief — no dose dimension at all. vs massed-practice-rate-suppression: that reduces a behaviour's future rate by over-emitting it, an entirely different route to suppression with no application-count-to-depth mapping. The load-bearing novelty is treating a hold as a titratable dose; the taxonomy currently treats every hold as binary.


**Why it works.** Where suppression is itself a learned, decaying state rather than the mere absence of a response, repeated application accumulates it and elapsed time dissipates it — which makes it a quantity with a growth term and a decay term, and anything with both is titratable in principle. Falsifiable: vary application count and probe delay factorially and measure residual response strength. If the response is all-or-nothing regardless of count, or if probe delay has no effect on how much suppression is left, then suppression is not an accumulating decaying state and the two-knob model is wrong. A single non-monotonicity — more applications producing reliably less suppression at fixed delay — also breaks it. [established; inhibitory conditioning as an active learned state; time-dependent recovery from inhibition]


**Worked examples.**

- *Count knob: application repetitions set depth and width of the hold*
  - **Setup.** A hold on saying a particular word is already installed and lightly seated; operator wants it firm enough to survive direct questioning but not so wide it silences adjacent speech.
  - **The move.** Each time I tap the arm of the chair, the word settles a little further out of reach. That's one. That's two. That's three — and I'm stopping at three.
  - **Why it lands.** Deliberately capping the application count at three keeps the suppression scoped to the single word instead of spreading to the semantic neighbourhood, which is what a run of ten taps would do. The operator probes immediately afterward and reads how much effort the subject visibly spends on the workaround: a full stall means over-application, a smooth substitution means the level is right.
- *Delay knob: elapsed time since last application sets residual strength*
  - **Setup.** The hold has been applied to the desired depth; the operator wants a specific partial level to be in force at a known later moment rather than full suppression right now.
  - **The move.** That's the last one I'll set. It's at full strength now, and it thins out at about the rate a taste fades — by the time we're at the door it will be thin enough to push through if you decide to.
  - **Why it lands.** Naming a decay window converts the hold from binary to a quantity the operator can aim at a chosen later moment. Probe at two minutes and again at ten: the difference in how readily the word arrives is the measurement of the second knob, and it lets the operator schedule a target level instead of accepting whatever remains.


<a id="entry-1384"></a>

### suppressor-strength-matching

[#1384](#entry-1384) · [Back to Standalone entries](#genus-standalone) · [Contents](#contents)

*risk: medium · bounded · family: safety · kind: principle*

In the reported animal-conditioning arrangement, the relative strength of the stimuli in a combination matters to the quick and complete establishment of a conditioned inhibitor: Pavlov recommends choosing the additional stimulus so that it is not much weaker than the positive component. This is a relation between stimulus strengths in the conditioning arrangement, not a requirement to match rehearsal counts or installation effort between two human commands. The same passage describes a possible developmental continuity: the new stimulus initially produces external inhibition through the investigatory reflex, and this can gradually and almost imperceptibly become permanent conditioned inhibition. Retain both the relative-stimulus-strength observation and that transition as supporting material for thinking about cue competition and acquisition; neither supplies a procedure for building, testing, or maintaining a human stop signal.


**When to reach for this.** Choose this supporting principle when examining how the strength of an additional stimulus relative to the positive component bears on establishing conditioned inhibition. Counterconditioning and cue-response weakening describe learning an incompatible response over exposure; this passage instead concerns the relative strengths of components in an inhibitory combination. Overshadowing is a neighboring compound-stimulus phenomenon that Pavlov discusses in the same argument, but the specific observation here concerns establishing the inhibitor. Preloaded exit cues, stop signals, and mirrored installation/removal address permission or script procedures and must not be treated as evidence for a rehearsal-matching requirement. The gradual transition from novelty-related external inhibition to conditioned inhibition is a source-supported accompanying observation, not a prediction that a lightly rehearsed safeword will fail.


**Why it works.** In Pavlov's laboratory, researchers observed that a stop signal not much weaker than the signal it was set against made a conditioned inhibitor form quickly and completely; a later colleague confirmed this and saw a gradual shift from ordinary distraction-type inhibition to a learned one. Those observations are about how strong or intense the stop signal is relative to the other, not about how many times it is drilled. They do not call for equal amounts of training, or for re-drilling a stop cue when another response grows stronger. Pavlov thought ordinary and learned inhibition were probably the same process, but said the evidence was not conclusive. There is no established rule that the stronger cue always wins, and no tested prediction about when a human safeword fails.


**Worked examples.**

- *Relative stimulus strength in establishing conditioned inhibition*
  - **Setup.** A reader is comparing the components of Pavlov's reported animal-conditioning arrangement: a positive conditioned stimulus and an additional stimulus being established as a conditioned inhibitor.
  - **The move.** Label the positive component P and the additional stimulus X. The reported consideration is whether X is much weaker than P, and the reported outcome is how quickly and completely conditioned inhibition is established. Do not substitute numbers of human rehearsals for these stimulus strengths.
  - **Why it lands.** This source-grounded schematic keeps the comparison at the level actually discussed: relative stimulus strength during acquisition of conditioned inhibition. The passage supplies no equal-rehearsal rule, prescribed test of a running human response, or evidence that an ordinary stop request depends on conditioning strength.
- *Initial investigatory inhibition becoming conditioned inhibition*
  - **Setup.** A reader is distinguishing the initial effect of a new stimulus from the later conditioned effect in Foursikov's experiments as reported by Pavlov.
  - **The move.** Mark the new stimulus's first inhibitory effect as attributed to the investigatory reflex. Then mark the reported gradual transition into permanent conditioned inhibition. Keep the observed continuity distinct from the theory that external and internal inhibition are fundamentally identical.
  - **Why it lands.** The source reports that an initially novelty-related inhibitory effect can pass gradually into conditioned inhibition. Pavlov treats this as evidence for a unifying account, while explicitly calling the evidence inconclusive. It is not a report of periodically rebuilding an off-switch after reinforcing a competing human response.
